domainSummaries:
[converter] The 29 mW AGBM-01/AGBM-02 idle gap is NOT the "VIN approaches VOUT" hypothesis — with 2xAA (3.2 V fresh alkaline, ~2.5 V eneloop) VIN never reaches VOUT3 = 3.336 V, so the LTC3527 always boosts. The gap is structural: the LTC3527 makes ONE Burst Mode decision for BOTH channels ("both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition"), so the ~0.7 mA 5 V rail is forced into fixed-frequency 1.2 MHz PWM whenever the ~37 mA 3.3 V rail is loaded — worth ~6 mW off the datasheet's own burst-vs-fixed curves — plus ~2.3 mW of extra conduction loss and ~2.7 mW of active Iq (500 uA from VOUT vs 2x11 uA for the TPS63802); the residual ~18 mW is 1.2 MHz switching/core loss I cannot separate from published data. The two biggest actionable levers are outside the IC: PTC1 (0805L075SLYR, R up to 160 mOhm post-reflow) carries the entire ~480 mA in-use input current and its 0.47 A hold current at 60 C is already BELOW the peak in-use draw — the same-family 0805L150SLYR is a drop-in that saves ~12 mW in use (~17 mW overclocked) and removes a real nuisance-trip risk; and VOUT3 is wired to the LTC3527's WEAK channel 2 (0.50/0.60 Ohm switches, 400 mA limit) while the light 5 V rail sits on the strong channel 1 (0.30/0.40 Ohm, 800 mA) — swapping them is a zero-BOM-cost schematic/PCB change worth 6-16 mW and it removes a brownout that the ClockxControl otherwise causes at low battery.
  anchors: RAIL VOLTAGES (computed, not assumed): LTC3527 V_FB = 1.20 V typ (1.176-1.224 V), from the datasheet Electrical Characteristics. VOUT5 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/560k) = 5.014 V. VOUT3 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/1.00M) = 3.336 V. AGBM-02 for comparison: TPS63802 V_FB = 500 mV, VOUT5 = 0.5 x (1+820k/91k) = 5.006 V, VOUT3 = 0.5 x (1+510k/91k) = 3.302 V. FSEL = GND -> f_sw = 1.2 MHz (0.9/1.2/1.5 MHz min/typ/max).

BATTERY: MouseBiteLabs' Required-Parts wiki states all AGBM-0X testing was done with eneloop pro NiMH, so the measured 170/141 mW are at a NiMH pack voltage, not 3.2 V alkaline. I use V_pack = 2.50 V at idle and 2.45 V at heavy load (2 x 1.25/1.22 V per cell). ESTIMATE; the design envelope is 1.8-3.2 V. Everything below scales as 1/V_pack.

INPUT CURRENT (derived): idle 170 mW / 2.50 V = 68 mA. In use 410 mW / 2.55 V = 161 mA (FP ITA, min brightness) up to 1175 mW / 2.45 V = 480 mA (Hispeedido IPS, max brightness + Everdrive + max volume). All of this flows through F1 and PTC1 (netlist: BT1+ -> F1 -> VBATT -> PTC1 -> VCC -> L1/L2 + U5 VIN/VIN1/VIN2; SW1 is NOT in the power path, it only gates /EN).

VOUT5 LOAD: at idle the only DC load is DL1 (green power LED) through R25 = 3.3 k, plus IC quiescent -> ~0.7 mA, P5 ~3.5 mW. ESTIMATE (LED Vf not verified). In use, the max-vs-min-brightness delta of 1175-568 = 607 mW at the battery is essentially all backlight -> ~88 mA on VOUT5 at max brightness, ~10 mA at min.

VOUT3 LOAD: back-solved from AGBM-02. 141 mW in, minus ~4.4 mW for its 5 V converter, = 136.6 mW into the 3.3 V TPS63802; at 90% (Fig 10-5, VI=2.5 V, VO=3.3 V) that is 123 mW out = 37 mA at 3.336 V. ESTIMATE. In use: 135 mA (min brightness) to ~180 mA (max brightness with audio). I use 150 mA as the typical in-use anchor.

CLOCKxCONTROL: +12 mA on VDD3 (module V+ lands on P1 pad S1 = VDD3, fed from VOUT3 through U18 TPS22917, 1:1 current) and +40-60 mA of extra core current. The AGB core and SRAM are on VDD2 = 2.5 V from U8 NCV8164, an LDO whose input is VOUT3, so an LDO passes that current 1:1 back to VOUT3. Central case +50 mA -> VOUT3 goes 150 -> 212 mA in use, 37 -> 49 mA at idle. FLAG: insideGadgets publish 40-60 mA as a console-level figure, not a per-rail one; if part of it is actually on VDD3 or VDD35 the split changes but the VOUT3 total does not, because every one of those rails is fed from VOUT3.

CONDUCTION-LOSS MODEL (CCM boost, VIN 2.45 V, VOUT3 3.336 V, L 4.7 uH, f 1.2 MHz): D = 1 - 2.45/3.336 = 0.2656. dI_pp = VIN*D/(L*f) = 0.6507/5.64 = 0.1154 A. I_L,avg = Iout/(1-D). I_rms^2 = I_avg^2 + dI^2/12. Effective switch resistance ch2 = 0.2656 x 0.50 + 0.7344 x 0.60 = 0.5734 Ohm; ch1 = 0.2656 x 0.30 + 0.7344 x 0.40 = 0.3734 Ohm; inductor DCR 0.120 Ohm. CCM is valid for the 3.3 V channel at >= ~42 mA out; the 5 V channel at light backlight is in DCM and I do not quote CCM numbers there.

[linear-rails] VOUT3 computes to exactly 3.336 V from the LTC3527's 1.20 V feedback reference and the R23/R55 = 1.78 M/1.00 M divider, which makes both LDOs 74.87% efficient (2.5/3.336 x 30/30.03) — an arithmetic match to MouseBiteLabs' own "roughly 75% efficient" statement about the audio supply, which confirms the whole model. U8 therefore throws away 25.1% of every milliwatt the CPU core draws: 25.2 mW at 1x (27.4 mW referred to the battery, 16% of the 170 mW idle figure) rising to ~40 mW at 1.75x (43.7 mW at the battery), of which ~15 mW is new heat created by the overclock. The real lever is replacing U8 with a switcher: a buck from VOUT3 (TPS62840, D = 0.75, comfortably viable, ~93% from Fig 18) wins 21 mW at 1x / 34 mW at 1.75x, and a buck-boost straight off VCC (TPS63900/TPS63802, skipping the boost entirely) wins 25 mW / 39 mW — but both are blocked by a detail nobody counts: U8's PGOOD output is the enable for U4 and U18 and none of the candidate switchers has one, so this is a schematic change, not a part swap. The cheap partial win — lowering VOUT3 by one resistor — is real but small at 4-10 mW, and there is no drop-in LDO worth anything at all (0.1 mW).
  anchors: RAIL VOLTAGES (computed, not assumed). LTC3527 datasheet EC table: "Feedback Voltage FB1, FB2 | 1.176 | 1.20 | 1.224 V" and pin description "The output voltage can be adjusted from 1.6V to 5.25V by VOUT1 = 1.2[1 + R1/R2]". With R23 = 1.78 M / R55 = 1.00 M: VOUT3 = 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V. Cross-check on the other channel, R21 = 1.78 M / R22 = 560 k: VOUT5 = 1.20 x 4.17857 = 5.014 V — a sane 5 V rail, which confirms the 1.20 V reference reading. Worst case with the +/-2% FB spec and +/-1% resistors, VOUT3 spans 3.228-3.447 V. VDD2 = VAUD = 2.500 V from the NCV8164 ordering table: "NCV8164ASN250T1G | 2.5 V | MP | With Active Output Discharge | TSOP-5 (Pb-Free)".

CURRENTS. There is no published per-rail measurement of the AGB CPU's 2.5 V core current. I looked: the Zekfoo/AGZ circuit-level GBA redesign publishes switching frequencies but no rail currents, and the GBAtemp current-draw threads are system-level only. The only anchor is MouseBiteLabs' own annotation on the AGBM-01 root schematic, placed directly above U8 at (111.76, 90.42) under the heading "2.5V Supply": "2.5V @ ~30mA", part of a block headed "Rough estimates (rounded up)". The same block gives "3.3V@~10mA (no cart)", "3.3V@~20mA", "3.3V@~50mA (Everdrive)", "5.0V @ ~130mA", and next to U4 at (241.3, 138.68): "~100mW" — which matches MBL's public statement that audio is "something like 50 to 100 mW at max volume". So I take I_VDD2(1x) = 30 mA and I_VAUD(max) = 40 mA (100 mW / 2.5 V); I_VAUD(idle) I estimate at ~5 mA, which is my own number chosen to close the idle budget below, not a measured or published one.

BOOST EFFICIENCY (used to refer rail savings back to the battery). MODE = GND and FSEL = GND on this board; the LTC3527 datasheet says "MODE = Low: Automatic Burst Mode operation" and "sets the switching frequency to 1.2MHz if the FSEL pin is below 0.35V". The applicable curve is therefore G05, "Efficiency vs Load Current and VIN for VOUT2 = 3.3V at 1.2MHz", BURST traces: at VIN = 2.4 V and 10-100 mA these sit at 92-94%. I use eta_boost = 0.92.

IDLE RECONCILIATION (this is what validates the 30 mA). VOUT3 draw at idle = U8 input 3.336 x 30.03 mA = 100.2 mW, plus VDD3 at 10 mA (no cart) x 3.336 = 33.4 mW through U18 (TPS22917 Ron ~100 mOhm at 3.3 V, so 6 mV drop at 60 mA — VDD3 = VOUT3 for all practical purposes), plus U4 input at ~5 mA = 16.7 mW, plus the R23+R55 = 2.78 M divider at 1.2 uA = 4 uW. Total 150.3 mW at VOUT3. Divided by 0.92 = 163 mW at the battery. Measured AGBM-01 idle is 170 mW, leaving 7 mW for the LTC3527's own quiescent (12 uA Burst measured on VOUT), three TPS3840 supervisors, the VOUT5 standby loop and the pull-up network. That closes to within 4%, so MBL's ~30 mA is credible.

OVERCLOCK MODEL (this one is modelled, not measured — treat with the confidence I assign it). CPU dynamic power scales with clock; the core and the SRAM are both on VDD2, and SRAM active current also scales with access rate. Model I_VDD2(f) = I_static + 1.75 x I_dyn with I_static + I_dyn = 30 mA at 1x: 100% dynamic gives 52.5 mA (delta 22.5), 80% gives 48.0 mA (delta 18.0), 60% gives 43.5 mA (delta 13.5). I use 48 mA / delta 18 mA as the central case, range 44-53 mA. Cross-check against insideGadgets, verbatim from the product page: "Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more." Both of those are stated as additional current the *console* draws, i.e. at the battery, for GBA/GBC/DMG generically — NOT per-rail, and I am not silently treating them as such. At a 2xAA pack around 2.9 V, 40-60 mA is 116-174 mW extra at the battery = ~107-160 mW extra at the rails. My VDD2 delta accounts for 18 mA x 3.336 = 60 mW of that; the balance has to be CPU I/O switching on VDD3 (address/data bus, LCD, cart) plus the cart itself, which is where you would expect it. Consistent, but not independently confirmed. Note where the module's own 12 mA lands: its V+ is on P1 pad S1 = VDD3, so it costs 12 mA x 3.336 = 40.0 mW at VOUT3 (43.5 mW at the battery) and passes through the TPS22917 load switch — it never touches U8.

ENVELOPE CHECK. All savings I quote below are 4-40 mW against a 170 mW idle and a 410-1175 mW in-use envelope. The biggest single number in this domain (39 mW for a buck-boost off VCC at 1.75x) is 23% of idle and 3.3% of the 1175 mW peak. Nothing here is a factor-of-two change.

[battery-path] The whole series path from the pack to the boost is two 0805 parts — F1 (2 A fuse, 0.080 Ω max) and PTC1 (0.75 A LoRho PPTC, 0.040 Ω min / 0.160 Ω max) — for 0.120–0.240 Ω total; board copper adds only ~6 mΩ and SW1 carries no load current at all (verified from the netlist: VBATT→PTC1→VCC goes straight to U5, the switch only drives an enable network drawing ~170 µA). That series R costs 10–20 mW at a typical 700 mW in-use draw and 68–135 mW at the overclocked low-battery peak; a one-part drop-in swap of PTC1 to 0805L150SLYR recovers 2–8 mW typical / 14–53 mW at peak, and a lower-R fuse or a 0 Ω build option in F1 adds another 3–17 mW. The bigger finding is not efficiency but stability: PTC1's hold current derates to 0.62 A at 40 °C and 0.47 A at 60 °C (Littelfuse table), while the ClockxControl pushes peak input current to roughly 0.70–0.78 A at a partly discharged pack — the fitted PPTC sits inside its own indeterminate hold/trip band and will heat, add resistance, and can latch off. Two correctness problems: both PCB footprints carry a stale Value "0467001.NR" which is a 0603 1 A fuse (wrong size, wrong function, no resettable protection), and D1 sits on the wrong side of F1 so its reverse-battery fault current never passes through the fuse.
  anchors: Pack voltage: 2 x AA, 3.2 V fresh to ~1.8 V at end of life. Energizer E91 datasheet gives nominal internal resistance 150-300 mohm per cell fresh (https://data.energizer.com/pdfs/e91.pdf), so pack ESR 0.30-0.60 ohm — 2 to 5x the entire board-side series resistance, which bounds how much of the total loss I can address.

Input currents used, all derived as P_system / V_pack:
- Idle 170 mW (MouseBiteLabs wiki, board under review): 57 mA at 3.0 V, 71 mA at 2.4 V, 85 mA at 2.0 V. I use 71 mA as the self-consistent idle anchor.
- Typical in-use 700 mW: 292 mA at 2.4 V. This is my "typical in-use operating point" for benefit_mw.
- Max in-use 1175 mW (Hispeedido IPS, max brightness/volume, Everdrive): 490 mA at 2.4 V, 588 mA at 2.0 V, 653 mA at 1.8 V. This is where the 550 mA figure in the brief comes from.
- ClockxControl adder: insideGadgets state "about 12 mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60 mA more" (fetched from the local capture of the product page). The figure is AMBIGUOUS about which rail — it is almost certainly system-level current measured on a stock console, not per-rail on this board. I priced both readings: (A) system-level at ~3 V = 36 mW + 120-180 mW = 156-216 mW extra; (B) per-rail, 12 mA on VDD3 (3.3 V) = 40 mW plus 50 mA of extra CPU core current on VDD2, which is an LDO from VOUT3 so it costs 50 mA x 3.34 V = 167 mW at the converter output, total ~207 mW, /0.88 boost efficiency = ~235 mW at the battery. Both land in +150 to +240 mW system power. I use +235 mW.
  => typical in-use overclocked = 935 mW = 390 mA at 2.4 V (this is benefit_mw_overclocked).
  => worst case overclocked = 1175 + 235 = 1410 mW = 588 mA at 2.4 V, 705 mA at 2.0 V, 783 mA at 1.8 V. I use 750 mA as the "overclocked low battery" peak.

SW1 current, computed from the netlist: the SW node drives R3 5.1k + R4 33k (38.1k), R58 5.1k + R63 100k (105.1k), R11 1k + R24 100k (101k), R12 100k, and Q3's emitter. At 3.0 V that is 79 + 28.5 + 30 + up to 30 uA = ~140-170 uA total.

Board copper: 4-layer, 35 um (1 oz) on all layers per the stackup block in the .kicad_pcb, so R_sheet = 1.72e-8 / 35e-6 = 0.491 mohm/square. I ran a scanline integral over the In2.Cu VCC fill polygons (script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Game-Boy-Enhance-desalvage/d4943806-0aca-58a2-867c-47f254d93b45/scratchpad/strip.py): 3.59 mohm for the full 21.3 mm run from the PTC1 area down to L1, which is the worst case and ignores the parallel B.Cu pour.

Component resistances all from datasheets (see per-finding sources), not from memory:
- F0805B2R00FSTR: 0.080 ohm max (measured at 10% of rated current, 25 C), 220 mV max drop at 2 A. The implied hot resistance at 2 A is 0.110 ohm, i.e. +0.069 ohm/W of self-heating; at 750 mA the device dissipates 45 mW so the rise is ~3 mohm. Cold R is therefore a good model across the whole operating range.
- 0805L075SLYR: R_min 0.040, R_1max 0.160 ohm.
- 0805L150SLYR: R_min 0.015, R_1max 0.065 ohm.
CAVEAT stated once here and applied throughout: R_1max is a 20 C figure. A PPTC operating at an appreciable fraction of I_hold self-heats and its resistance rises above R_1max. Every high-current loss number below is therefore a LOWER BOUND for the fitted 0.75 A part, and the understatement is much larger for it than for the 1.5 A part.

[passives] The passive selection on this board is much better than the "no dielectric in the schematic" worry suggests: the schematic Source fields resolve to real MPNs, and they are conservative parts — 25 V X5R for the 22 uF/10 uF bulk, 16 V and 50 V X7R for the 1 uF/0.1 uF decoupling, C0G for the 15 pF feed-forward, and case-B tantalum (not MLCC) for the 100 uF audio caps. I fetched and digitised the manufacturers' own DC-bias curves: the only significant deration is C21 (22 uF 25 V X5R 0805 -> 10.7 uF at 5.014 V, 49 % of nominal) and the 10 uF 0603s (-26 % at 2.5 V, -39 % at 3.34 V); the 1 uF X7R loses 3 % at 2.5 V and the 0.1 uF loses nothing. None of that breaks a datasheet requirement, so the derating story is a "check and move on", not a lever. The real findings are elsewhere: three assembly/correctness defects (polarized tantalums on a symmetric MLCC land with no polarity silk; CP1 used as a bidirectional AC coupler with 0 V DC bias; the SRAM and the ClockxControl's VDD3 tap both have no local bypass at all), and one honest efficiency lever worth 3-11 mW (L1/L2 DCR) that needs a PCB revision to collect. Total realistic energy recoverable in this domain is roughly 4-12 mW against a 792-1420 mW overclocked in-use budget, i.e. under 1 %. The EM chokes and beads carry no current and are worth exactly 0 mW.
  anchors: RAIL VOLTAGES (computed, not assumed). LTC3527 VFB = 1.20 V typ (1.176/1.224 limits), datasheet p.3. VOUT5 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/560k) = 1.20 x 4.1786 = 5.014 V. VOUT3 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/1.00M) = 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V. VDD2 = VAUD = 2.500 V (NCV8164ASN250). VDD3 = VOUT3 through TPS22917 = ~3.33 V. FSEL=GND -> 1.2 MHz; MODE=GND -> automatic Burst Mode.

BATTERY / INPUT CURRENT. 2xAA; I use VCC = 2.4 V as the mid-discharge operating point (context gives 1.8-3.2 V). Idle 170 mW -> 70.8 mA in. Funnyplaying-ITA max-use 792 mW -> 330 mA in. Hispeedido max-use 1175 mW -> 490 mA in.

CHANNEL SPLIT (ESTIMATE, flagged). From the netlist, ch1/VOUT5 feeds only U11 -> VDD5 -> cart pad S2 and FFC pin 34 (VSHA, the LCD analog supply) plus the two indicator LEDs (R25 3.3k gives (5.014-2.0)/3300 = 0.91 mA). ch2/VOUT3 feeds both NCV8164 LDOs and U18 -> VDD3. The brightness-dependent swing (568 -> 1175 mW on Hispeedido) is the backlight, which reaches the screen kit through VSHA on ch1. I therefore assume ch1:ch2 = 40:60 of input current at 792 mW and 45:55 at 1175 mW. This is the weakest number in the analysis; it is settleable in 5 minutes by putting a current probe on TP13 (VOUT5) and TP16 (VOUT3).

CLOCKXCONTROL LOAD. Verified from the fork's netlist: the module's V+ lands on P1 pad S1, which is net VDD3 (switched 3.336 V from U18). insideGadgets quote ~12 mA for the module plus 40-60 mA more when overclocked. FLAG: their 40-60 mA is quoted as system-level, not per-rail. I place it on VDD2 (CPU core, 2.5 V) because CPU dynamic power is what scales with clock; because VDD2 is an LDO from VOUT3, VOUT3 current is the same either way, so the inductor arithmetic below is insensitive to that assumption (only U8's dissipation changes). Delta-I(VOUT3) = 12 + 50 = 62 mA -> delta-P(VOUT3) = 62 mA x 3.336 V = 207 mW -> at ~85 % boost efficiency, 244 mW at the battery -> delta-I(L2) = 244/2.4 = 101 mA.

RESULTING INDUCTOR CURRENTS. 792 mW: I(L1) = 132 mA, I(L2) = 198 mA; +overclock I(L2) = 299 mA. 1175 mW: I(L1) = 220 mA, I(L2) = 270 mA; +overclock I(L2) = 371 mA. Peak inductor current adds half the ripple: D = 1 - 2.4/3.336 = 0.281, dIL = 2.4 x 0.281/(4.7uH x 1.2MHz) = 120 mA, so Ipk(L2) worst case = 371 + 60 = 431 mA against the LSXND3030's 1.02 A Isat - comfortable at 2.4 V, tighter at 1.8 V end-of-life.

CPU DYNAMIC CURRENT (ESTIMATE, used only for the VDD2 impedance target). Taking insideGadgets' 50 mA of extra draw as CPU dynamic current for a 0.75x clock increase gives I_core(4.194 MHz) ~ 67 mA and I_core(7.34 MHz) ~ 117 mA on VDD2. No verified AGB core-current datum exists; this is an inference from their published figure.

EFFECTIVE CAPACITANCE (digitised from the manufacturers' own published DC-bias charts; each curve read off the datasheet page by pixel-mapping the plot axes, +/-1 % reading error).
- Murata GRM21BR61E226ME44L, 22 uF 25 V X5R 0805, 2.0 x 1.25 x 1.25 mm (C1, C21, C42): 0 V +0.2 % = 22.0 uF; 2.4 V -18.6 % = 17.9 uF; 3.336 V -32.1 % = 14.9 uF; 5.014 V -51.5 % = 10.7 uF.
- Murata GRM188R61E106KA73J, 10 uF 25 V X5R 0603, 1.6 x 0.8 x 0.8 mm (C2, C12, C23, C37, C59, C60, C68): 2.4 V -24.6 % = 7.54 uF; 2.5 V -26.1 % = 7.39 uF; 3.336 V -38.9 % = 6.11 uF; 5.0 V -56.8 % = 4.32 uF.
- 1 uF 16 V X7R 0603 (BOM part KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU; curve taken from the same-class Murata GRM188R71C105KA12): 2.5 V -3.2 % = 0.968 uF; 3.336 V -12.5 % = 0.875 uF.
- 0.1 uF X7R 0603 (BOM part KEMET C0603C104K5RACTU, 50 V; curve taken from the 16 V Murata GRM188R71C104KA01, which is the pessimistic case): +0.7 % at 2.5 V, 0.0 % at 3.336 V, -0.7 % at 5.014 V - i.e. flat.
- C40/C41 15 pF are KEMET C0603C150J5GACTU, C0G/NP0 50 V: no voltage coefficient by construction.
- C61/C80 3300 pF are KEMET C0603C332K5RACTU, X7R 50 V: flat at these biases by the same argument as the 0.1 uF.

RAIL TOTALS AFTER DERATING. VOUT5: C21 10.66 + C72 0.099 = 10.76 uF effective (nominal 22.1, i.e. 49 %). VOUT3: C42 14.94 + C2 6.11 + C23 6.11 + C22 0.875 = 28.0 uF effective (nominal 43, 65 %). VCC: C37 7.54 uF (nominal 10). VDD2: C60 7.39 + 4 x 0.968 + 5 x 0.1007 = 11.76 uF effective. VAUD: C59 7.39 + 3 x 0.968 = 10.29 uF. VDD3: 3 x 0.875 + 4 x 0.100 = 3.03 uF. LTC3527 requires COUT >= 4.7 uF for loop stability and NCV8164 requires >= 1 uF with no minimum ESR, so every rail passes with margin.

PHYSICAL PLACEMENT (from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb, pad centres computed from footprint origin + rotation). U1 VDD2 pins: 44 (74.34, -49.62), 65 (72.34, -61.52), 115 (51.84, -53.62), 117 (51.84, -52.62). Nearest VDD2 caps: pin 44 -> C15 0.1u at 2.6 mm, C46 1u at 4.5 mm; pin 65 -> C16 at 2.4 mm, C48 at 3.6 mm; pins 115/117 -> C45/C47 1u at 2.5-2.7 mm, C52/C53 0.1u at 3.1-3.7 mm. U2 (SRAM) VDD2 pins: 12 (81.31, -58.05) nearest cap 9.9 mm; 16 (81.31, -56.05) nearest 8.0 mm; 37 outer (95.10, -58.05) and CY62157 third-column (100.31, -58.05) nearest C8 at 9.9 / 7.1 mm. P1 pad S1 (VDD3, the ClockxControl tap) at (96.90, -35.20): nearest VDD3 capacitor is C69 at 43.5 mm, and its source U18 is at (29.47, -27.30), 68 mm away. Both VDD2 and VDD3 do have In2.Cu plane pours (VDD3 zone spans x 23.6-98.1, y -52.2 to -26.6; VDD2 zone x 16.8-101.8, y -63.2 to -31.6) over a solid In1.Cu ground plane, which is what keeps these distances survivable.

[ics-quiescent] The whole supporting-IC and discrete population accounts for only ~7.4 mW of the 170 mW idle (4.4%); 96% of idle is the salvaged AGB CPU/SRAM, the two NCV8164 LDOs, the audio chain and LTC3527 conversion loss — none of it in this domain. Within that 7.4 mW the picture is very lopsided: the green power LED DL1 with its 3.3k series resistor burns 4.66 mW at VOUT5 (5.8 mW at the battery), and the brownout-latch bias around Q1/Q3/Q10 burns another 0.93 mW straight off VBATT; everything else — three nanopower supervisors (300 nA each), three load switches (0.5 uA each, 13-230 uW conduction loss), the MIC1553 (correctly held in <1 uA shutdown), the whole HC/LVC logic block, and RA1 — together add under 0.35 mW. Six resistor-value changes plus one LED swap, all drop-in on existing land patterns, recover ~6.2 mW at the battery (3.7% of idle, ~12% of the ClockxControl's 50 mW standing overhead) and cut the post-brownout latched-off battery drain from 6.9 mW to 0.79 mW. Separately I found three defects worth reporting regardless of efficiency: R3/R4/R64 disagree between schematic and PCB, Q10A's NDC7002N gate threshold (2.5 V max) is above the VBATT gate drive it must latch on, and the obvious Schmitt upgrade for U16 (SN74HC7002) is NOT pin-compatible with SN74HC02 — verified from both datasheets.
  anchors: Rails: VBATT = SW = 2.4 V (the prompt's anchor; a fresh alkaline pack is ~3.0-3.2 V and all VBATT-side divider currents scale linearly with it). VOUT5 = 5.0 V and VOUT3 = 3.34 V, taken as given from the context pack (consistent with R21/R22 = 1.78M/560k and R23/R55 = 1.78M/1M against a 1.20 V feedback reference; I could not fetch the LTC3527 datasheet — analog.com and mouser both refused the connection — so the 1.20 V VFB is inferred, not verified). VDD2 = VAUD = 2.5 V, VDD3 = 3.34 V.

Currents I derived rather than measured, with basis:
- Latch bias 387 uA: computed from the netlist topology (Q10B gate=/EN, source=GND, drain=Q1-C; Q3 PNP emitter=SW, base via R15 10k from Q1-C, collector=Q10A-G; Q1 NPN base via R16 10k from Q10A-G) with Vbe(sat)=0.65 V and Vce(sat)=0.05 V. In the RUN state /EN is high, so Q10B is on, Q1-C is low, Q3 is on and Q1 is on — the latch sits armed and biased, not dormant. Ie(Q3) = 1.70V/10k (base) + 2.35V/100k (R17) + 1.70V/10k (R16) = 363.5 uA, plus R12 = 23.5 uA.
- DL1 current 0.932 mA: solved iteratively against the Wurth 150060VS75000 forward I-V curve, which I digitised from the vector data in the datasheet PDF (axes 0-4.0 V x 0-35 mA; extracted points (0.106 mA, 1.801 V), (1.006 mA, 1.925 V), (2.006 mA, 1.964 V), (8.00 mA, 2.045 V), (20 mA, ~2.09 V) — the 20 mA value falls inside the datasheet's own 2.0 V min / 2.4 V max spec, which validates the digitisation). I = (5.0 - 1.92 - 0.005)/3300 = 0.932 mA.
- All pull-up/pull-down/divider currents: from the schematic values in the KiCad files, at the rail each net actually sits on. Pull-ups that carry NO static current in the run state, and which I therefore excluded from the inventory after checking the schematic: R9 (parallels D2, carries only U3's 300 nA -> 49 nW), R13 and R8 (pull-ups on open-drain PGOOD outputs that are high in normal operation), R6 (cart IRQ input), R7 (only conducts if Q8 is on, i.e. VCNT5 asserted -> 0 or 112 uW), R67 (both ends at VDD3 when U12 is on), R68 (drives only TP12, no DC path), R70/R71 (touch pads, FETs off), R29 (PGOOD1 high-Z), R18/R66/R10 (gate nets only), R2/R5/R35 (CPU inputs; R35 is the one exception and could carry 33 uA if the CPU drives its SC pin low - unverifiable, flagged).
- Boost referral: I could not fetch the LTC3527 datasheet, so battery-referred figures use an ASSUMED boost efficiency of 80% at these light loads. All "at the rail" numbers are hard; divide-by-0.80 numbers carry that assumption. At 85% the savings shrink ~6%; at 75% they grow ~7%.
- VDD5 and VDD3 load currents: not measurable from the files. I bounded them (12/30/50/100 mA cases shown per finding) rather than guessing a single value.
- ClockxControl: 12 mA on VDD3 = 40.1 mW at VOUT3 = 50.1 mW at the battery. insideGadgets' additional "40-60 mA when overclocked" is almost certainly system-level CPU dynamic current landing on VDD2 (LDO from VOUT3), not on VDD3 through U18 — I have NOT assumed it flows through U18.

[audio] The audio chain is a 1-bit PWM reconstruction path, not an analogue one: the AGB CPU's SO1/SO2 PWM outputs are re-buffered by U9 onto the 2.5 V VAUD rail (so VAUD is the DAC's full-scale reference, which is why it gets its own low-noise LDO), filtered by a textbook 4th-order Butterworth Sallen-Key at 15.84 kHz built from U7's four sections, attenuated by VR2, and amplified by U6 at a gain of only 0.2. The single biggest thing in this domain is a correctness bug that is also the biggest efficiency lever: U7 is a TLV9364QPWRQ1, whose datasheet minimum supply is 4.5 V and whose input common-mode ceiling is (V+)-2 V — it is being run at 2.5 V with its inputs at 1.25 V, and its rated 2.6 mA/amplifier quiescent is ~10.4 mA, roughly 80% of the whole audio chain's ~12.75 mA standing current. Swapping it for the pin-identical TLV9064IPWR (1.8-5.5 V, RRIO, 538 µA/amp) is a drop-in that both fixes the violation and wins back ~31 mW at the battery — about 18% of AGBM-01's 170 mW idle, and roughly 12-16% of what the ClockxControl costs. Everything else in the domain is either quality-only (worth ~0 mW) or large-but-invasive (a class-D speaker amp is worth ~48 mW at MouseBiteLabs' own max-volume operating point but needs a schematic and PCB redesign and puts a 250 kHz switcher 1.3 mm from the ClockxControl window).
  anchors: RAILS. VAUD = 2.5 V from U4 NCV8164ASN250T1G, ±2% over load and temperature (onsemi datasheet Electrical Characteristics), i.e. 2.45-2.55 V. VOUT3 = 3.34 V per the context pack. Battery-side numbers are computed as I_load x 3.34 V / eta_boost with eta_boost ASSUMED = 0.90 for the LTC3527 at this load; I did not read the LTC3527 efficiency curve, so treat the 0.90 as an assumption (at 0.85 every battery-side figure below is 6% larger; at 0.92 it is 2% smaller).

STANDING (volume-independent) VAUD CURRENT, itemised:
  U7 TLV9364, 4 x 2.6 mA (SBOSA67B IQ per amplifier)                     = 10.40 mA  [see caveat]
  U6 LM4853 IDD, 1.8 mA typ at VDD=2.7 V (SNAS155E); ~1.75 mA at 2.5 V   =  1.80 mA
  U9 SN74LVC2G34: ICC max 10 uA (SCES359J) + PWM drive (below)           =  0.20 mA
  R45/R46 and R49/R50 mid-rail bias dividers, 2 x (2.5 V / 200 k)        =  0.025 mA
  R14 100 k (conducts only in speaker mode, jack switch closed)          =  0.025 mA
  R37 100 k (conducts whenever VDD5 present and Q6 is on)                =  0.025 mA
  VR2 10 k dual pot track, 2 x (1.25 V / 10 k) — see finding vr2-dc-bias =  0.25 mA
  U4 NCV8164 own IQ, 30 uA typ (drawn on the VOUT3 side)                 =  0.03 mA
  TOTAL                                                                  ~ 12.75 mA
  -> 12.75 mA x 3.34 V = 42.6 mW at VOUT3 -> / 0.90 = 47.3 mW at the battery WITH THE VOLUME AT ZERO.

U9 PWM-DRIVE ESTIMATE (the 0.20 mA above): at the 32.768 kHz carrier the 1 uF coupling caps C25/C29 are effectively shorts (|Zc| = 4.9 Ohm), so U9 drives R42/R51 = 7.5 k with a +/-1.25 V square wave: P = 1.25^2/7500 = 0.21 mW per channel, 0.42 mW for two = 0.17 mA at 2.5 V. Dynamic CV^2f is negligible (Cpd 14 pF at 2.5 V x 2.5^2 x 32.8 kHz = 2.9 uW).

RECONCILIATION AGAINST MOUSEBITELABS' "50 to 100 mW at max volume". The 47.3 mW quiescent floor computed above IS essentially their 50 mW lower bound. Taking their 100 mW upper bound: 100 mW x 0.90 / 3.34 V = 26.9 mA total; minus the 12.75 mA quiescent leaves 14.2 mA of class-AB output-stage current. For a BTL class-AB stage the supply current equals the rectified load current, I_avg = (2/pi)(Vp/RL), so Vp = 14.2 mA x (pi/2) x 8 Ohm = 0.178 V peak differential, i.e. Pout = 0.178^2/(2 x 8) = 2.0 mW into the 8 Ohm speaker. That is a completely realistic max-volume PROGRAM AVERAGE (game audio has 10-15 dB crest factor), so the model closes against their measurement. All output-stage arithmetic below uses this 14.2 mA / 2.0 mW operating point as the "max volume" anchor.

GAIN STRUCTURE / MAX CAPABILITY (from the schematic + LM4853 datasheet). PWM full scale = VAUD = 2.5 Vpp, so a full-scale recovered sine is 1.25 Vpk = 0.884 Vrms at the filter output. LM4853 is inverting with Ri = R30/R31 = 100 k and Rf = R56/R57 = 20 k, so SE gain = 0.2 per channel and BTL AVD = 2 x Rf/Ri = 0.4 per input (L and R are summed internally in BTL mode, so a correlated mono signal sees 0.8). Max speaker output = 0.8 x 0.884 = 0.707 Vrms differential = 62 mW into 8 Ohm (I_avg would be 79.6 mA, 199 mW at VAUD — far above MBL's figure, confirming their number is program-average not sine). Max headphone output = 0.2 x 0.884 = 0.177 Vrms into 32 Ohm = 0.98 mW/channel, which is only ~4% of the LM4853's 25 mW/32 Ohm capability at 2.7 V — a deliberate and good choice for THD and noise.

SPEAKER: 23 mm, 8 Ohm, 0.5 W (standard GBA/GBC replacement part, multiple retail sources).

FILTER (computed from the schematic values, unity-gain Sallen-Key, f0 = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(R1R2C1C2)), Q = sqrt(R1R2C1C2)/(C2(R1+R2))):
  stage 1 (U7C right / U7D left): R=7.5k & 20k, Cfb=1000p, Cgnd=680p -> f0 = 15.76 kHz, Q = 0.540
  stage 2 (U7A right / U7B left): R=5.1k & 18k, Cfb=3300p, Cgnd=330p -> f0 = 15.92 kHz, Q = 1.312
  Textbook 4th-order Butterworth Qs are 0.5412 and 1.3065 — this is an exact Butterworth alignment at fc = 15.84 kHz. It is a RECONSTRUCTION filter for the PWM, not an anti-alias filter.

INPUT/OUTPUT CORNERS: C25/C29 (1 uF) into R45||R46 = 50 k -> 3.18 Hz. C55/C56 (1 uF) into R30/R31 = 100 k -> 1.59 Hz. CP2/CP3 (100 uF) into 32 Ohm -> 49.7 Hz (99.5 Hz into 16 Ohm). CP1 (100 uF) into 8 Ohm -> 199 Hz.

CLOCKXCONTROL COUPLING: audio quiescent current is clock-independent, so every mW figure below is the same at 1x and 1.75x except for second-order changes in boost efficiency. The one real clock coupling is the PWM carrier frequency (see finding clockxcontrol-underclock-pwm-carrier).

[clockxcontrol] The single most important answer is negative in a good way: the VDD2 LDO is not the bottleneck. U8 (NCV8164ASN250T1G, TSOP-5) is rated 300 mA with a 350 mA minimum current limit and 158 °C/W θJA; my worst-case VDD2 draw at 1.75x is ~82 mA, giving 68.6 mW of dissipation and an 11 °C junction rise — roughly 3.5x current margin and 4x thermal margin. The real constrained node is one level up: VOUT3 is fed by LTC3527 **converter 2**, the 400 mA-switch channel, and it carries VDD2, VAUD and VDD3 (all logic, all cart, all audio), while the 800 mA channel drives only the screen rail. Converter 2's guaranteed capability at 3.336 V is ~220 mA at VIN 2.4 V and ~178 mA at the 2.0 V supervisor cutoff; my worst-case 1.75x estimate is 150–207 mA, so the overclock consumes most of the remaining margin on nearly-flat cells. The biggest efficiency lever the overclock creates is U8 itself: it burns exactly (3.336−2.500) = 0.836 V × I_VDD2, which is 25.1 mW at 1x idle and 43.9–68.6 mW at 1.75x — replacing it with a ~89 %-efficient buck wins back 21 mW typical and 49 mW at 1.75x in a game, about a third of the whole overclock cost. Everything else in my domain is small: the depopulation of C3 and C4 is worth ~4.9 mW at the battery at 1.75x (and ECO-6's stated reason for removing C4 is wrong — C4 is still tied to CK2 through R41), and the 73.5 mm CLK run is electrically fine for timing but is referenced to a patchwork of five different In2.Cu power islands, which is worth fixing while the ECO is still on paper.
  anchors: RAIL VOLTAGES (computed, not assumed). LTC3527 VFB = 1.176/1.20/1.224 V (datasheet 35271fc p.4). VOUT3 = 1.20 × (1 + 1.78M/1.00M) = 3.336 V. VOUT5 = 1.20 × (1 + 1.78M/560k) = 5.014 V. VDD2 = 2.500 V (NCV8164ASN250T1G). VDD3 = VOUT3 − I×Rds(on,U18) = 3.336 − 0.012×0.090 = 3.335 V.

BATTERY VOLTAGE. MouseBiteLabs' wiki states the power figures were taken "at 2.4V (NiMH)" with a Fluke 117 measuring current, power = V×I. So 170 mW idle = 70.8 mA of battery current. Low-battery cutoff: U3 is a TPS3840DL20, and TI's TPS3840 datasheet gives fixed VIT− options from 1.6 V to 4.9 V in 0.1 V steps, so DL20 = 2.0 V, measured on VFILT (= VBATT − one 1SS355 drop). So the board never runs below VCC ≈ 2.0 V.

I_VDD2 AT 1x — DERIVED, NOT MEASURED. This is the load-bearing estimate and everything downstream inherits its error bars. Method: AGBM-01 idle = 170 mW at the battery ("idle, no game, no screen"). Assume LTC3527 efficiency 87 % (datasheet claims up to 94 %; at ~70 mA in / 2.4 V this is a reasonable mid-figure) → 148 mW delivered to the four rails. Subtract VOUT5, which with no screen is only DL1 through R25 3.3 k: (5.014 − ~2.0 V LED)/3300 = 0.91 mA → ~5 mW, plus load-switch/supervisor µA → 6 mW. The two 2.5 V LDOs pass current 1:1, so their input power is 3.336/2.500 = 1.334× their output power. That gives 142 = 1.334·(P_VDD2 + P_VAUD) + P_VDD3. Taking P_VAUD = 12.5 mW (5 mA: LM4853 IDD 2.4 mA typ per its datasheet, plus TLV9364 + SN74LVC2G34 + 4×100 k dividers) and P_VDD3 = 26 mW (8 mA: CPU I/O, U15, U16, six 100 k pull-ups that carry no DC when the buttons are up) → P_VDD2 = 74.4 mW → **I_VDD2(1x, idle) ≈ 30 mA**. Sensitivity: sweeping boost efficiency 82–90 % and the VAUD/VDD3 allocations ±60 % moves this only between 23 and 34 mA, so I use 30 ± 6 mA. In-use (game running) I scale to ~47 mA (1.55×), which is a guess with no measurement behind it.

OVERCLOCK SCALING. CMOS dynamic power ∝ f, and at the AGB's process node room-temperature leakage is a few percent of dynamic, so I scale the dynamic part of VDD2 and VDD3 by 1.75 and treat leakage as fixed: I_VDD2(1.75x) = 1.75 × 30 = 52.5 mA idle, ~82 mA in a game. The GBA service manual (§2.4) confirms the CPU multiplies the 4.194304 MHz input by 4 in GBA mode, so 7.34 MHz in = 29.36 MHz core.

CROSS-CHECK AGAINST insideGadgets. My model predicts the console's extra battery draw at 1.75x = ΔI_VDD2 22.5 mA × 3.336 V (the LDO passes it 1:1 to VOUT3) = 75.1 mW, /0.88 = 85.3 mW; plus VDD3 I/O dynamic ~3.6 mA → 12.0 mW → 13.6 mW; plus the clock net's own C·V²·f 1.2 mW. Total ≈ 100 mW = **42 mA at 2.4 V**, rising to ~63 mA if in-use base current is 1.5× idle. insideGadgets publish 40–60 mA. The two agree, which is the main reason I trust the 30 mA anchor.

TRACE ELECTRICALS (computed from the board's own stackup: F.Cu 0.035 / prepreg 0.100 / In1.Cu / core 0.840 / In2.Cu / prepreg 0.100 / B.Cu, εr 4.5). A 0.25 mm track 0.1 mm over a plane: Hammerstad gives εeff = 3.477, Z0 = 42.0 Ω, 6.22 ps/mm, and C = √εeff/(c·Z0) = 0.148 pF/mm. So CXC_CLK's 73.5 mm = 10.9 pF, the existing CK1 copper's 22.9 mm = 3.4 pF.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. No public datasheet exists for the AGB CPU, so its XIN input capacitance, input threshold type and which rail its oscillator block runs from are all unknown; I assume 5 pF and VDD3 and say so at each use. insideGadgets publish no schematic, supply range or output drive strength for the ClockxControl, so its edge rate (I assume 2 ns) and whether it has an internal regulator are unverified. Cartridge current (especially an Everdrive) is unverified. All of these are flagged in the individual findings.

[thermal-emc-layout] Nothing on this board is thermally stressed — the hottest junction I can compute is the LTC3527 at roughly +10 to +16 °C over internal ambient, and the two NCV8164 LDOs sit at +12 °C and +4 °C, all with >60 °C of margin to their limits; the ClockxControl covers no dissipating part and is a non-event thermally. The real limits at 1.75x are elsewhere: PTC1 (0805L075, Ihold derates to 0.63 A at 40 °C) is already at its derated hold current at end-of-battery with max backlight and goes over it once the overclock adds 40-60 mA, so the board nuisance-trips before anything gets hot; and the 73.5 mm ClockxControl clock run is referenced to GND for only 5.9 mm of its length, changing reference-plane net 15 times and crossing 5 plane slots. The VDD2 rail itself is a non-issue for DC drop (7.4 mΩ of In2 plane from U8 to the CPU core pins, under 1 mV at any plausible current) — I am reporting that as a finding so nobody spends effort on it. The most serious things I found are not upgrades at all but breaks the ECO-5 fork introduced: U2 pin 37 (RAM VCC) is on an isolated VDD2 copper island with no via to the plane, C8's VDD2 terminal is unrouted, and a removed via has open-circuited Net-(Q5B-G).
  anchors: RAIL VOLTAGES (computed, not assumed). LTC3527 FB reference = 1.200 V (datasheet 35271fc, Electrical Characteristics; also confirms TJMAX 125 °C, thetaJA 68 °C/W, FSEL=0V -> 1.2 MHz, MODE=0V -> Burst Mode). VOUT5 = 1.200 x (1 + 1.78M/560k) = 5.014 V. VOUT3 = 1.200 x (1 + 1.78M/1.00M) = 3.336 V. VDD2 = VAUD = 2.500 V (NCV8164ASN250 fixed). VDD3 = VOUT3 less U18 Ron drop = 3.33 V.

BATTERY CURRENT. Context gives 1.8-3.2 V pack and 410-1175 mW in use. Typical in-use point used throughout: 800 mW at 2.4 V = 333 mA. Worst-case point: 1175 mW at 1.9 V = 618 mA; add the ClockxControl's own 12 mA on VDD3 (= 12 mA x 3.336 V / (0.88 boost x 0.95 series) = 48 mW = 25 mA at 1.9 V) and insideGadgets' published +40-60 mA when overclocked, giving ~700 mA. NOTE, per instruction: insideGadgets' wording ("Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more") reads as 12 mA of module current plus 40-60 mA of extra CONSOLE current; I treat the 40-60 mA as battery-side, and the cross-check below supports that.

VDD2 CURRENT (estimated - basis stated). (a) The measured Hispeedido min-brightness / OEM cart / muted case is 568 mW at the battery. Taking CPU+SRAM as ~40% of that = 227 mW, referred through the boost (assumed eta 0.88, unverified at this operating point; datasheet claims up to 94% peak) and the U8 LDO (2.500/3.336 = 74.9%) gives 227 x 0.88 x 0.749 = 150 mW at VDD2 = 60 mA. (b) Cross-check: scaling 60 mA to 1.75x with ~70% of it dynamic gives 0.3x60 + 0.7x60x1.75 = 91 mA, i.e. +31 mA = +78 mW at VDD2, which referred back to the battery is 78/(0.749x0.88) = 118 mW = 47 mA at 2.5 V - squarely inside insideGadgets' published 40-60 mA. The two derivations agree, so I use I_VDD2 = 60 mA at 1x and 90 mA at 1.75x. Both are estimates.

VAUD CURRENT. MouseBiteLabs states audio draws 50-100 mW at max volume through a "roughly 75% efficient" supply - that 75% is exactly U4's 2.500/3.336 = 74.9% LDO ratio, so the VAUD-side load is 37-75 mW = 15-30 mA.

COPPER. Stackup from the board file: 1.2 mm, 35 um (1 oz) on all four layers, F.Cu-In1 0.1 mm prepreg, In1-In2 0.84 mm core, In2-B.Cu 0.1 mm prepreg, FR4 er 4.5. Sheet resistance = 1.72e-8 / 35e-6 = 0.491 mOhm/square. Via resistance (0.3 mm drill, 1.2 mm long, 25 um plating assumed - IPC Class 2 minimum, not verified for this fab) = 1.72e-8 x 1.2e-3 / (pi x 0.3e-3 x 25e-6) = 0.88 mOhm.

INTERNAL AMBIENT. All junction temperatures below are quoted as a rise; I assume 45 °C inside a closed AGB shell in use (estimate, no airflow, no measurement available).

findings.title: PTC1 carries the whole input current and its post-reflow resistance is up to 160 mOhm; the same-family 0805L150SLYR is a drop-in at 15-65 mOhm
findings.current_part: PTC1 = Littelfuse 0805L075SLYR, LoRho 0805L SL series PPTC. Verified from the Littelfuse LoRho datasheet table: Ihold 0.75 A, Itrip 1.50 A, Vmax 6 V, Imax 50 A, Pd 0.6 W, R_min 0.040 Ohm, R_1max 0.160 Ohm (R_1max is defined as the maximum resistance at 20 C measured one hour after tripping OR after 260 C reflow, i.e. it is the relevant bound for a soldered board). Package A = 2.00-2.20 mm, B = 1.20-1.50 mm, C = 0.40-0.75 mm; solder pad layout F/G/H = 1.00/1.20/1.50 mm. Digi-Key's page for the same part independently lists 40 mOhm initial / 160 mOhm post-trip. Board netlist confirms PTC1 pad1 = VBATT, pad2 = VCC, and VCC feeds C37, L1, L2 and U5 VIN/VIN1/VIN2 — i.e. 100% of converter input current passes through it.
findings.proposal: Littelfuse 0805L150SLYR, same LoRho 0805L SL series, same datasheet, same 0805 body (A 2.00-2.20, B 1.20-1.50, C 0.40-0.75 mm) and the SAME recommended solder pad layout (F/G/H = 1.00/1.20/1.50 mm), so it drops onto the existing Fuse_0805_2012Metric land with no PCB change. Specs: Ihold 1.50 A, Itrip 3.00 A, Vmax 6 V, Imax 50 A, Pd 0.6 W, R_min 0.015 Ohm, R_1max 0.065 Ohm. Conservative middle option if you want to keep the trip point lower: 0805L110SLYR, Ihold 1.10 A, R_min 0.030 / R_1max 0.130 Ohm.
findings.benefit: Only the resistance bounds are published, so I give the range and a central value. Series resistance drops from 0.040-0.160 Ohm to 0.015-0.065 Ohm; central estimate 0.080 -> 0.030 Ohm (2x R_min, which is where reflowed parts typically land). At the max in-use input current of 480 mA (1175 mW / 2.45 V): loss now = 0.480^2 x 0.080 = 18.4 mW, after = 0.480^2 x 0.030 = 6.9 mW, SAVING 11.5 mW. Bounds: best case 0.480^2 x (0.040-0.015) = 5.8 mW, worst case 0.480^2 x (0.160-0.065) = 21.9 mW. With the ClockxControl at 1.75x the extra 62 mA on VOUT3 = 207 mW of rail power = ~232 mW at VCC at 89% = +97 mA of input current, so 577 mA: saving = 0.577^2 x 0.050 = 16.6 mW (range 8.3-31.6 mW). At idle (68 mA) the saving is 0.068^2 x 0.050 = 0.23 mW — nil. This is an in-use-only lever, but at 12-17 mW out of a 1175 mW budget it is ~1.4% of total system power and it is a two-cent part change.
findings.risk: Raises the trip point from 1.50 A to 3.00 A, so PTC1 no longer catches faults between 1.5 and 3.0 A. What it still protects: a hard short on the VCC node. That is fine because (a) F1 upstream is a 2 A Accu-Guard whose 5-second fusing current is 4.00 A, still above the new PTC trip point, and (b) the LTC3527 cannot itself draw more than its two switch limits (800 mA + 400 mA peak inductor current, folded back to 500/350 mA when VOUT < 1 V), so the converter can never present a 1.5-3.0 A load. The 0805L150SLYR is 0.15 mm taller at worst (C max 0.75 vs 0.75 — identical per the LoRho table), so no height risk. If you want to keep more fault sensitivity, take 0805L110SLYR instead and accept ~7 mW instead of ~12 mW.
findings.verify_reason: I fetched the Littelfuse LoRho datasheet myself (mouser.com/pdfdocs/Littelfuse_LoRho_PTC.pdf, 4 pages, extracted with pypdf) and every quoted number is exact: '0805L075SL YR -G 0.75 1.50 6 50 0.6 8.00 0.20 0.040 0.160' and '0805L150SL YR -K 1.50 3.00 6 50 0.6 8.00 0.50 0.015 0.065'; 0805L110SL is 1.10/1.80/0.030/0.130. Dimension table rows for all three read '2.00 2.20 1.20 1.50 0.40 0.75 ... 1.00 1.20 1.50', so body and recommended pad layout are identical and the swap IS a drop-in on Bucketmouse:Fuse_0805_2012Metric. I re-parsed the fork PCB: PTC1 pad1=VBATT, pad2=VCC, and VCC carries C37/L1/L2/U5 VIN,VIN1,VIN2, so 100% of converter input current does pass through it. 0805L150SLYR is in production and stocked (LCSC $0.1201; Farnell 3130 pcs). FOUR CORRECTIONS. (1) The '2x R_min central estimate' is invented. The datasheet defines only 'R min = Minimum resistance of device in initial (un-soldered) state' and 'R 1max = Maximum resistance at 20C measured one hour after tripping or reflow soldering'. There is no typical and no post-reflow minimum, so 0.080->0.030 Ohm is not a datasheet-backed pair; the honest statement is that the delta lies between (0.040-0.015)=0.025 and (0.160-0.065)=0.095 Ohm. (2) Wrong input current basis: MouseBiteLabs' own wiki states 'These measurements were made using a benchtop supply providing 2.4V', not 2.45 V, so 1175 mW/2.4 V = 490 mA, not 480 mA. Redone: 0.490^2 x 0.050 = 12.0 mW central, bounds 0.490^2 x 0.025 = 6.0 mW to 0.490^2 x 0.095 = 22.8 mW. (3) The overclocked 577 mA inherits the double-count flagged under clockxcontrol-converter-tax; insideGadgets' sentence is 'when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more', i.e. a console-level figure with no stated measurement node. If it is battery-side, input goes 490->~540 mA and the saving is 0.540^2 x 0.050 = 14.6 mW, not 16.6 mW. (4) The risk section's foldback numbers are wrong: the LTC3527 Operation section reads 'Peak switch current is limited to approximately 900mA for converter 1 and 500mA for converter 2 ... If VOUT1 or VOUT2 falls below 1V, its respective current limit is cut in half' (i.e. ~450/250 mA, not 500/350 mA; the 800/400 mA figures are the EC-table guaranteed minimums). The conclusion that the converter cannot present a 1.5-3.0 A load is unaffected. Also 'it is ~1.4% of total system power' overstates: 12.0/1175 = 1.0%. The F1 backstop claim is correct (Accu-Guard II table: F0805B2R00 fusing current 4.00 A within 5 s). Verdict: direction and drop-in status stand; the point estimate does not. Measure the installed PTC with a milliohm meter before quoting any number.

findings.title: PTC1's hold current at 60 C (0.47 A) is BELOW the measured peak in-use input current (0.48 A), and the ClockxControl pushes the draw to ~0.58 A
findings.current_part: PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR. Littelfuse LoRho datasheet temperature rerating table for 0805L075SLYR, hold current in A: -40 C 1.24, -20 C 1.07, 0 C 0.94, 20 C 0.75, 40 C 0.62, 60 C 0.47, 70 C 0.37, 85 C 0.23. Trip current 1.50 A at 20 C, maximum time-to-trip 8.00 s at 0.20 A above... (datasheet column: 8.00 s at the stated test current).
findings.proposal: Littelfuse 0805L150SLYR (drop-in, see finding ptc1-lorho-1a5-swap). Its rerating table: 20 C 1.50 A, 40 C 1.25 A, 60 C 0.93 A, 70 C 0.74 A, 85 C 0.50 A. Note that 0805L110SLYR is NOT a clean fix on this axis: its 85 C hold current is 0.21 A, actually worse than the 075SL's 0.23 A, per the same table.
findings.benefit: This is a reliability fix, not an efficiency one, so benefit_mw = 0. The arithmetic: MouseBiteLabs' own maximum measured in-use draw is 1175 mW; at a 2.45 V eneloop pack that is 480 mA, all of it through PTC1. The 0805L075SLYR holds 0.62 A at 40 C and 0.47 A at 60 C. A GBA shell with a Hispeedido IPS backlight at max brightness will sit well above 25 C internally, so the operating margin is between 1.29x (40 C) and 0.98x (60 C) — i.e. at 60 C the part is already at or past its hold current before any modification. Add the ClockxControl: +62 mA on VOUT3 = 207 mW of rail power = ~232 mW at VCC at 89% converter efficiency = +97 mA of input current, giving 577 mA. Margin then falls to 1.07x at 40 C and 0.81x at 60 C — i.e. guaranteed to be in the trip region at 60 C. A tripped PPTC latches (it stays hot and high-resistance until power is removed), so the failure mode is the console dying mid-game and not restarting until the batteries are pulled. With 0805L150SLYR the margin at 577 mA becomes 2.6x at 20 C, 2.17x at 40 C and 1.61x at 60 C.
findings.risk: Same as the efficiency finding: higher trip threshold. I have NOT measured the actual internal temperature at PTC1 — the 40 C and 60 C rows are the honest bracket, and if the real internal temperature is only 30 C the current part is marginal rather than failing. Also note the 480 mA figure assumes a 2.45 V pack; with a nearly flat pack at 2.0 V the same 1175 mW would be 588 mA, making the margin worse still.
findings.verify_reason: The rerating table is exactly as quoted - I read it off the datasheet I fetched: '0805L075SL YR 1.24 1.07 0.94 0.75 0.62 0.47 0.37 0.23' and '0805L150SL YR 2.37 2.07 1.80 1.50 1.25 0.93 0.74 0.50' against the header 'Ambient Operation Temperature -40C -20C 0C 20C 40C 60C 70C 85C'. The observation that 0805L110SL is WORSE at 85 C (0.21 A) than 0805L075SL (0.23 A) is correct and is a good catch. But the load-bearing inference is wrong. (1) The finding conflates I_hold with I_trip. The datasheet's own definitions: 'I hold = Hold current: maximum current device will pass without tripping in 20C still air' and 'I trip = Trip current: minimum current at which the device will trip in 20C still air'. Between the two the behaviour is indeterminate; exceeding I_hold is NOT the same as tripping. Rerating I_trip by the same factor as I_hold gives 1.50 x (0.47/0.75) = 0.94 A at 60 C and 1.50 x (0.62/0.75) = 1.24 A at 40 C. A 490 mA (or even 577 mA) load is roughly half the 60 C trip current. So 'at 60 C the part is already at or past its hold current' is true but 'guaranteed to be in the trip region at 60 C' is FALSE. The correct claim is much weaker: above I_hold the part is no longer guaranteed not to trip, and the failure is possible rather than certain. (2) The datasheet columns are misquoted: the header is 'Maximum Time-To-Trip: Current (A) / Time (Sec.)' and the 0805L075SL row is 8.00 A at 0.20 s, not '8.00 s at 0.20 A'. (3) 480 mA should be 490 mA (2.4 V bench-supply basis per the MouseBiteLabs wiki). (4) 577 mA depends on the rail-side reading of insideGadgets' console-level figure (see clockxcontrol-converter-tax); on a battery-side reading it is ~540 mA. (5) The 40 C / 60 C internal temperature bracket is asserted, not measured - the finding says so. Net: the underlying concern (PTC1 has thin margin and the 1.5 A part restores it at no footprint cost) survives; the 'guaranteed to trip / console dies mid-game' framing does not.

findings.title: The LTC3527 makes one Burst Mode decision for both channels, so the ~0.7 mA 5 V rail is forced into 1.2 MHz PWM — this is the single largest identified piece of the 29 mW AGBM-01/02 gap
findings.current_part: U5 = LTC3527, MODE pin (3) tied to GND per the board netlist, so automatic Burst Mode is selected. Datasheet, Burst Mode Operation section, verbatim: "To realize the efficiency benefits of Burst Mode operation, both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition, if they are both enabled." and "Once the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 have left Burst Mode operation and returned to normal operation, they will remain there until both output loads are reduced below the burst threshold current." Burst Mode Threshold Current vs VIN for VOUT1 = VOUT2 = 3.3 V (Fig. G14, 2.2 MHz) reads ~16 mA (converter 1) / ~18 mA (converter 2) leave-burst at VIN 2.4 V; at the board's 1.2 MHz the per-cycle energy is ~1.8x higher so the threshold scales up to roughly 30 mA — the datasheet publishes no 1.2 MHz threshold curve, so that is my extrapolation.
findings.proposal: No drop-in fix exists inside the LTC3527 — the shared-burst behaviour is architectural. It is fixed only by the AGBM-02 transplant (finding agbm02-converter-transplant), where each TPS63802 makes its own PFM decision. Partial mitigation: see l2-3u3-raise-burst-threshold.
findings.benefit: Quantified off the datasheet's own curves. VOUT5 idle load ~0.7 mA -> P_out = 5.014 V x 0.7 mA = 3.5 mW. From Fig. G07 (VOUT1 = 5 V, 1.2 MHz), the VIN = 2.4 V BURST curve at 0.7 mA reads ~84%, the VIN = 2.4 V FIXED curve at 0.7 mA reads ~33%. Burst: 3.5/0.84 = 4.2 mW in, 0.7 mW loss. Fixed: 3.5/0.33 = 10.6 mW in, 7.1 mW loss. Delta = 6.4 mW, i.e. 22% of the whole 29 mW AGBM-01/AGBM-02 idle gap, spent switching a 4.7 uH inductor at 1.2 MHz to deliver 3.5 mW. Accounting for the rest of the 29 mW: ch2 conduction loss at the 37 mA idle point is I_rms^2 x (0.5734 + 0.120) = 0.0604^2 x 0.6934 = 2.5 mW versus ~0.2 mW for a TPS63802 with 18-43 mOhm switches and a 22 mOhm inductor, so ~2.3 mW; the LTC3527's active quiescent current is 500 uA typ / 900 uA max measured into VOUT (5.014 V) = 2.5 mW at the output = ~2.8 mW reflected to the input versus 2 x 11 uA x 2.5 V = 0.055 mW for two TPS63802s, so ~2.7 mW (partly already inside the efficiency curves, so do not simply add it). Identified total ~9-11 mW of 29 mW; the residual ~18 mW is 1.2 MHz gate-drive, switching and ferrite core loss in two 3x3x1.5 mm drums versus 2 MHz PFM with 0.47 uH metal-composite parts, which is not separable from published data. CRITICAL for this fork: the ClockxControl's own 12 mA lands on VDD3, which is fed from VOUT3, so idle VOUT3 goes 37 -> 49 mA. That takes the 3.3 V channel unambiguously above the leave-burst threshold at ALL times, permanently locking the 5 V channel into fixed-frequency operation. ECO-6 therefore costs ~6 mW of converter loss on top of the 40 mW its 12 mA actually consumes.
findings.risk: No change proposed, so no risk. The 84%/33% efficiency reads are eyeballed off a log-x graph and are good to maybe +/-4 points; that puts the 6.4 mW figure in a 5-8 mW band. My 0.7 mA VOUT5 idle load is an estimate from R25 = 3.3 k and the green LED — if it is really 2 mA the delta grows to ~7.6 mW, if it is 0.2 mA it shrinks to ~2 mW.
findings.verify_reason: The MECHANISM is confirmed verbatim from the datasheet I fetched and text-extracted. Operation section: 'To realize the efficiency benefits of Burst Mode operation, both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition, if they are both enabled' and 'Once the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 have left Burst Mode operation and returned to normal operation, they will remain there until both output loads are reduced below the burst threshold current.' Also 'When the MODE pin is high, LTC3527/LTC3527-1 feature continuous PWM fixed frequency operation', so MODE=GND (netlist: U5 pin 3 MODE -> GND) does select automatic Burst. The graph attributions are right: I rendered page 4 at 250 dpi and Fig. G07 is titled 'Efficiency vs Load Current and VIN for VOUT1 = 5V at 1.2MHz', and the netlist confirms pin 5 VOUT1 -> VOUT5, so it is the correct curve. I re-read G07 at 0.7 mA myself: BURST 2.4 V ~82% (they said 84), FIXED 2.4 V ~30-35% (they said 33) - within graph-reading error. Their arithmetic reproduces: 5.014 x 0.7 mA = 3.51 mW; 3.51/0.82 - 3.51/0.33 = 4.3 - 10.6 = -6.3 mW. I also confirmed on page 5 that Fig. G14 ('Burst Mode Threshold Current vs VIN for VOUT1 = VOUT2 = 3.3V') is explicitly annotated '2.2MHz OPERATION' and that no 1.2 MHz threshold curve is published anywhere, so the 1.8x extrapolation to ~30 mA is honestly flagged as an extrapolation. Note 3 confirms the 500 uA/900 uA active Iq is 'measured into the VOUT pin since the supply current is bootstrapped to the output', so reflecting it to the input is the right treatment. WHAT DOES NOT HOLD: the whole argument turns on VOUT3 idling at ~37 mA, above the extrapolated ~30 mA leave-burst threshold, and that 37 mA figure has no stated source. It appears to be back-derived from AGBM-02's measured 141 mW idle assuming ~91% converter efficiency, which makes the reasoning partly circular - the number derived from the gap is then used to explain the gap. If VOUT3 idles below ~30 mA the entire 6 mW disappears. Separately, my own estimate of the VOUT5 idle load from the netlist is ~0.9-1.1 mA, not 0.7 mA (R25 3.3 k with green DL1 at ~2 V Vf from 5.014 V alone is 0.91 mA, plus the R10/DL2 branch and U11/U14/U17 quiescent), which pushes the delta to ~6.5 mW - immaterial. Verdict: mechanism CONFIRMED, magnitude unproven; treat the 6.4 mW as a hypothesis to measure by putting a scope on SW1, not as an accounted-for piece of the 29 mW.

findings.title: The heavy 3.3 V rail is on the LTC3527's WEAK channel 2 (0.50/0.60 Ohm, 400 mA) and the near-idle 5 V rail is on the strong channel 1 (0.30/0.40 Ohm, 800 mA) — swapping them is free in BOM terms
findings.current_part: Board netlist (pinout.py U5): pin 5 VOUT1 -> VOUT5, pin 6 SW1 -> L1; pin 8 VOUT2 -> VOUT3, pin 7 SW2 -> L2. LTC3527 datasheet Electrical Characteristics: NMOS on-resistance SW1 0.30 Ohm, SW2 0.50 Ohm; PMOS on-resistance SW1 0.40 Ohm, SW2 0.60 Ohm; NMOS current limit SW1 800 mA (min), SW2 400 mA (min). Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2 (Fig. G11) at VOUT = 3.3 V reads ~200 mA at VIN 1.8 V, ~280 mA at VIN 2.4 V, peaking ~390 mA near VIN 3.0 V. Converter 1 (Fig. G10) at VOUT = 3.3 V reads roughly double throughout.
findings.proposal: Re-map the two channels at U5: VOUT3 to VOUT1/SW1 (with L1 and C42), VOUT5 to VOUT2/SW2 (with L2 and C21), and move FB1/FB2, SHDN1/SHDN2 and PGOOD1/PGOOD2 with them so the existing sequencing is preserved (today: /EN -> SHDN2 starts the 3.3 V channel, PGOOD2 -> /PG_3V3 enables the LDOs, /PG_2V5 -> SHDN1 starts the 5 V channel, PGOOD1 -> /~RESET). No component values change; R21/R22 stay with the 5 V rail and R23/R55 with the 3.3 V rail, and C40/C41 follow their dividers. Zero BOM cost, zero extra parts.
findings.benefit: Using the CCM model in measured_anchors. At the typical in-use point (VOUT3 = 150 mA, VIN 2.45 V): I_L,avg = 0.150/0.7344 = 0.2042 A, I_rms^2 = 0.2042^2 + 0.1154^2/12 = 0.042823 A^2. On channel 2 the total series R is 0.5734 + 0.120 = 0.6934 Ohm -> 29.7 mW. On channel 1 it is 0.3734 + 0.120 = 0.4934 Ohm -> 21.1 mW. Saving 8.6 mW. With the ClockxControl at 1.75x (VOUT3 = 212 mA): I_L,avg = 0.2887 A, I_rms^2 = 0.084434 -> 58.6 mW on ch2 vs 41.7 mW on ch1, saving 16.9 mW. Penalty on the 5 V rail, which moves to channel 2: at max brightness (88 mA, D = 1 - 2.45/5.014 = 0.5114, dI = 0.2221 A, I_rms^2 = 0.036548) the loss goes 0.036548 x 0.4689 = 17.1 mW to 0.036548 x 0.6689 = 24.4 mW, i.e. +7.3 mW; at min brightness (10 mA) the 5 V channel is in DCM and the penalty is under ~1 mW. NET: 8.6 - (1 to 7) = 2-8 mW without the overclock, 16.9 - (1 to 7) = 10-16 mW with it. I quote the mid of the overclocked band. Second, larger benefit: it moves the heavy rail off the 400 mA current limit — see finding converter2-current-limit-vs-overclock.
findings.risk: Needs a schematic edit plus a PCB revision: L1/L2 stay on the same land patterns but SW1/SW2, VOUT1/VOUT2, FB1/FB2, SHDN1/SHDN2 and PGOOD1/PGOOD2 all re-route around a QFN-16 whose pads are 0.3048 x 0.8128 mm on a 0.5 mm pitch in a very congested area. The 5 V channel on converter 2 must still deliver ~88 mA: Fig. G11 shows converter 2 at VOUT = 5 V reaching roughly 130 mA at VIN 2.4 V and ~90 mA at VIN 1.8 V, so at end-of-discharge with a max-brightness screen the 5 V rail would be at its ceiling. If your screen kit draws more than ~90 mA on VSHA this swap trades one ceiling for another — verify your screen's 5 V current before committing. Efficiency numbers are conduction-only (they exclude switching and core loss, which are essentially unchanged by the swap), so they are a lower bound on the benefit but also do not capture any second-order penalty.
findings.verify_reason: Every device number checks out against the datasheet I fetched: 'NMOS Switch On-Resistance, SW1 0.30 / SW2 0.50', 'PMOS Switch On-Resistance, SW1 0.40 / SW2 0.60', 'NMOS Current Limit, SW1 800 mA / SW2 400 mA' (both marked as guaranteed minimums). The channel assignment is confirmed from my own pinout dump (pin 5 VOUT1 -> VOUT5, pin 6 SW1 -> L1, pin 8 VOUT2 -> VOUT3, pin 7 SW2 -> L2), so the heavy rail IS on the weak channel. The sequencing chain is confirmed exactly as described (pin 12 SHDN2 <- /EN, pin 13 PGOOD2 -> /PG_3V3 which is U8's EN, U8 PGOOD -> /PG_2V5 -> pin 1 SHDN1, pin 16 PGOOD1 -> /~RESET). The conduction arithmetic reproduces exactly: D = 1-2.45/3.336 = 0.2656, duty-weighted R = 0.2656x0.50+0.7344x0.60 = 0.5734 (ch2) and 0.3734 (ch1); I_L,avg = 0.2042 A, dI_pp = 2.45x0.2656/(4.7uH x 1.2MHz) = 0.1154 A, I_rms^2 = 0.042823 A^2; 29.7 mW vs 21.1 mW. PROBLEMS. (1) Both operating currents are unsourced guesses and they do not reconcile with the measurement they are supposed to sit inside. Taking their own numbers: 5 V rail 441 mW at ~88% = 501 mW in, 3.3 V rail 500 mW at ~90% = 556 mW in, plus ~35 mW of PTC+fuse loss = ~1092 mW, against the measured 1175 mW - a 7% shortfall. The split is a construction, not a measurement. (2) Wrong VIN: the wiki says measurements were taken at a 2.4 V bench supply. (3) The 5 V-side penalty is materially understated. I read Fig. G11 (Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2) off the rendered page: the VOUT = 5 V trace is a near-straight line reading roughly 140 mA at VIN 2.4 V and ~115 mA at VIN 2.0 V. VIN 2.0 V is the board's real floor (U3 = TPS3840DL20, VIT- = 2.0 V, drives /EN -> SHDN2). So moving an 88 mA screen rail onto converter 2 leaves only ~25% margin at cutoff, on a load figure that is itself a guess. The swap does not remove a ceiling, it moves it onto a rail whose current nobody has measured. (4) The overclocked +16.9 mW inherits the possible double-count in the 212 mA figure. (5) 'Zero BOM cost' is technically true but the change is a full re-route of eight nets around a 0.5 mm-pitch QFN-16 in the densest area of a 4-layer board - the finding says this in the risk field, but the title 'free in BOM terms' oversells it. Corrected: ~2-8 mW stock (I quote 4 as the midpoint) and ~8-14 mW overclocked, contingent on unmeasured rail currents, and only worth doing if you first measure the 5 V screen current and confirm it stays under ~90 mA.

findings.title: With the ClockxControl at 1.75x, VOUT3 demands ~212 mA — more than LTC3527 converter 2 can deliver at VIN 1.8 V, so the console browns out before the batteries are flat
findings.current_part: U5 converter 2 (VOUT2 -> VOUT3): NMOS current limit 400 mA minimum (spec is a MIN, tested over -40 to 85 C), NMOS 0.50 Ohm, PMOS 0.60 Ohm. Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2 (datasheet Fig. G11), VOUT = 3.3 V curve: ~200 mA at VIN 1.8 V, ~230 mA at VIN 2.0 V, ~280 mA at VIN 2.4 V. The datasheet front page also states the part delivers only "3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells" — 200 mA is converter 2's rating for exactly this application.
findings.proposal: Either (a) move VOUT3 to converter 1 per finding ltc3527-channel-assignment-backwards, which raises the limit to 800 mA and roughly doubles the Fig. G10 ceiling; or (b) transplant the AGBM-02 converter, whose TPS63802 has a 4 A minimum boost-mode peak current limit and delivers ~1.5 A at VIN 1.8 V (Fig. 10-2); or (c) gate the ClockxControl down from 1.75x when the low-battery flag asserts.
findings.benefit: Reliability, not power, so benefit_mw = 0. The arithmetic at end-of-discharge, VIN = 1.8 V, VOUT3 = 3.336 V: D = 1 - 1.8/3.336 = 0.4604; I_L,avg = 0.212/0.5396 = 0.393 A; dI_pp = 1.8 x 0.4604/(4.7u x 1.2M) = 0.147 A; I_peak = 0.393 + 0.0735 = 0.466 A. That is 17% ABOVE the 400 mA minimum current limit, and it agrees independently with Fig. G11, which shows converter 2 topping out near 200 mA of output at VIN 1.8 V against a 212 mA demand. When the limit is hit, VOUT3 sags, the NCV8164 feeding VDD2 drops out of regulation, and the AGB core browns out. Without the overclock the demand is 150 mA against the same ~200 mA ceiling — a 33% margin, which is why the stock board works. So the overclock converts a comfortable margin into a deficit and shortens usable battery life by cutting off the bottom of the discharge curve. Note this is independent of, and worse than, the input-side PTC trip risk.
findings.risk: Fig. G11 is read off a graph at a single VOUT (3.3 V, versus the board's 3.336 V) and I extrapolated the 200 mA reading at VIN 1.8 V; the 400 mA current limit is a guaranteed minimum so typical parts will do better. My 212 mA figure rests on the +50 mA central estimate of insideGadgets' 40-60 mA — at +40 mA the demand is 202 mA and it is a coin flip; at +60 mA it is 222 mA and the deficit is clear. Measure VOUT3 current with the module fitted at 1.75x before deciding how urgent this is.
findings.verify_reason: The device facts are right. Front-page bullet verbatim: 'Delivers 3.3V at 200mA/100mA from one Alkaline/NiMH Cell, or 3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells' - so 200 mA is indeed converter 2's headline rating for this application. EC table: 'NMOS Current Limit, SW2 [l] 400 mA' with the [l] over-temperature marker, i.e. a guaranteed minimum. Fig. G11 exists with a 0-500 mA axis. BUT THE SCENARIO IS OUTSIDE THE BOARD'S OPERATING RANGE. VIN = 1.8 V never occurs: U3 is a TPS3840DL20 whose VDD is /VFILT (~VBATT via R9 100k and D2) and whose open-drain output is /EN, which drives U5 pin 12 SHDN2. I fetched TI's TPS3840 datasheet and the orderable table reads 'TPS3840DL20 ... 2.0 0.100', i.e. VIT- = 2.0 V with 100 mV hysteresis. The converter is shut down below VBATT ~2.0 V, so the entire end-of-discharge arithmetic is done ~200 mV below where the board still runs. REDONE AT THE REAL FLOOR (VIN 2.0 V, VOUT3 3.336 V, 212 mA): D = 1-2.0/3.336 = 0.4005; I_L,avg = 0.212/0.5995 = 0.354 A; dI_pp = 2.0x0.4005/(4.7uH x 1.2MHz) = 0.142 A; I_peak = 0.425 A. That is 6% over the 400 mA guaranteed minimum, but I also rendered Fig. G17 (Current Limit vs Temperature) and converter 2's TYPICAL limit reads ~0.61 A at 25 C (converter 1 ~1.21 A), so a typical part has ~44% headroom on peak current. My own read of G11 at VIN 2.0 V on the VOUT = 3.3 V trace is ~225-240 mA against a 212 mA demand - roughly 10% margin: genuinely tight, worth flagging, but not the 'browns out before the batteries are flat' the title claims. Additionally the 212 mA rests on a 150 mA base (unsourced) plus 62 mA that may be double-counted (see clockxcontrol-converter-tax); on the battery-side reading the demand is ~190 mA and the margin is ~20%. Verdict: real concern, wrong voltage, overstated severity. Proposal (c) - back the clock off when the low-battery flag asserts - is the cheap correct mitigation and survives.

findings.title: Transplanting AGBM-02's twin TPS63802 converter into AGBM-01 is worth the measured 29 mW at idle and ~26 mW in use, and the inductor land pattern is already identical
findings.current_part: U5 = LTC3527 in Bucketmouse:QFN-16_UD, 16 pads of 0.3048 x 0.8128 mm on a 0.5 mm pitch at +/-1.4478 mm plus a 1.5494 mm square exposed pad, at (26.9, -39.9). L1/L2 = Taiyo Yuden LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG, 4.7 uH +/-20%, DCR 0.12 Ohm typ / 0.144 max, Isat 1.02 A, 3.0 x 3.0 x 1.5 mm, in footprint Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering (pads 1.65 x 2.0 mm at +/-1.175 mm). LTC3527EUD is listed out of stock at Digi-Key with a 2026-04 lead time and $1.81-$4.52 depending on source; the AGBM-01 README carries its own note that "This part has been going in and out of stock at various places for the past few months."
findings.proposal: Two TI TPS63802 (VSON-10 DLA, 2 x 2 mm, pads 0.25 mm wide on a 0.5 mm pitch at x = -0.9 / +0.55...0.75 mm), exactly as AGBM-02 does it: U5 -> VOUT5 with R59 820k / R60 91k, U13 -> VOUT3 with R72 510k / R73 91k (V_FB = 500 mV, and the datasheet requires the low-side resistor <= 100 kOhm, which the board's existing 560 k and 1 M do NOT satisfy so they must change). L1/L2 -> Samsung CIGT201610EHR47MNE, 0.47 uH +/-20%, DCR 18 mOhm typ / 22 max, Isat 5.5 A min, Irms 4.8 A min, 2.0 x 1.6 x 1.0 mm. Add one 10 uF 0603 (a second VIN cap, AGBM-02's C57) and one 22 uF 0805 (AGBM-02's C58 on VOUT5). Delete C40/C41 — AGBM-02 has no feed-forward caps on its FB nets. MODE (pin 2) to GND on both, exactly as AGBM-02 does, which is what enables the per-device PFM.
findings.benefit: Idle: this is the measured 29 mW (170 -> 141 mW), a 17% cut, with the whole downstream identical. In use, from the two datasheets' own curves at VIN 2.45 V / VOUT 3.3 V and 212 mA out (the overclocked point): LTC3527 Fig. G05 reads ~88% at the 2.4 V trace, TPS63802 Fig. 10-5 reads ~91% at the 2.5 V trace. P_out = 3.336 x 0.212 = 707 mW, so P_in goes 707/0.88 = 803 mW to 707/0.91 = 777 mW, saving 26 mW. Without the overclock (150 mA), 500 mW out, 568 -> 550 mW in, saving 18 mW. Conduction loss alone tells a much larger story (LTC3527 ch2 58.6 mW vs TPS63802 boost R_eff = 0.2656 x 0.018 + 0.7344 x 0.043 = 0.0364 Ohm plus 0.022 Ohm DCR, about 7 mW), but the TPS63802 pays much of that back in switching and core loss with 0.66 A p-p of ripple at 2.1 MHz, so I quote the curve-based numbers, not the conduction-only ones. Secondary wins: converter 2's 400 mA ceiling disappears (TPS63802 peak current limit is 4 A minimum in boost, 3.8 A in buck); the part is buck-boost so it stays in regulation with fresh 3.2 V alkalines above VOUT3; each device has its own 11 uA PFM decision so the 5 V rail is never dragged out of power-save; and sourcing improves markedly (TPS63802DLAR is widely stocked at roughly $0.62-$1.74 versus the LTC3527's $1.81-$4.52 and backorder).
findings.risk: This is a full PCB revision of the converter block: the QFN-16 3x3 land and the VSON-10 2x2 land share nothing, and you need two ICs where one sat, in a 4-layer 1.0 mm board inside a GBA shell where the ClockxControl now also occupies 18.65 x 12.00 mm at board centre. AGBM-02 places its two converters and two inductors at (22.75,-44.55)/(27.5,-37.55) and (22.25,-41.05)/(27.5,-34.2), which is a different arrangement from AGBM-01's (26.9,-39.9) and (29.5,-45)/(29.5,-34.8) — so this is a re-layout, not a patch. The one genuinely free part: both boards use the identical Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering land, so the 4.7 uH -> 0.47 uH change is purely a value change. Also note VOUT3 becomes 3.302 V instead of 3.336 V, a 1% drop that slightly reduces the VDD2 LDO's headroom (still ~800 mV, far above the NCV8164's dropout). Practical verdict: if you are already respinning the board for the ClockxControl, do this; if not, take the channel swap and the PTC instead.
findings.verify_reason: Most of the design detail is verified. From the TPS63802 datasheet I fetched: Iq into VIN 11 uA typ, VFB 500 mV, 'The low-side resistor R2 (between FB and GND) must not exceed 100 kOhm', boost RDS(on) low-side 18 mOhm / high-side 43 mOhm, Peak Current Limit Boost 4 A min / 5 typ / 5.75 max, Buck 3.8 A, boost fSW 2.1 MHz. I parsed AGBM-02's own files: R59 820k / R60 91k (VOUT5 = 0.5x(1+820/91) = 5.005 V), R72 510k / R73 91k (VOUT3 = 3.302 V), C57 10u 0603, C58 22u 0805, U5 pin 2 MODE -> GND, and no feed-forward capacitors on either FB net - all as claimed. AGBM-02's README gives the inductor as 'CIGT201610EHR47MNE' and the Samsung spec sheet I fetched confirms 0.47 uH +/-20%, DCR 18 typ / 22 max mOhm, Isat 5.5 A, Irms 4.8 A, 2.0x1.6x1.0 mm. The AGBM-01 inductor is confirmed as LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG (0.12/0.144 Ohm, Isat 1.02 A, 3.0x3.0x1.5, 'Mass Production (Preferred)') from Taiyo Yuden's own page, and BOTH boards use the identical Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering land (pads 1.65x2.0 mm at +/-1.175 mm in both PCBs), so the L change really is value-only. THREE ERRORS. (1) PACKAGE SIZE WRONG. The TPS63802 DLA is not 2x2 mm. Its Device Information table reads 'BODY SIZE (NOM) 3.0 mm x 2.0 mm' and the DLA0010A mechanical drawing gives 2.9-3.1 x 1.9-2.1 mm. Two of them are ~12 mm^2 of body against the LTC3527 QFN-16's 9 mm^2, so the transplant makes the converter block bigger, not smaller. (The pad geometry quoted does match AGBM-02's Bucketmouse:VREG_TPS63802DLAR footprint, so only the body dimension is wrong.) (2) THE IN-USE SAVING IS UNSUPPORTED. MouseBiteLabs' wiki states verbatim: 'Note: All of the following measurements were performed with an AGBM-01. The AGBM-02 was not as thoroughly analyzed.' There is no measured in-use comparison. And the graph comparison does not survive re-reading: I rendered LTC3527 Fig. G05 (correctly identified - it is titled 'Efficiency vs Load Current and VIN for VOUT2 = 3.3V at 1.2MHz', traces 1.8/2.4/3 V) and read the 2.4 V trace at 200-212 mA as ~90-92%, not ~88%. TPS63802 Fig. 10-5 (VO = 3.3 V, MODE = Low, traces 2.5/3.6/4.2 V) at 0.212 A reads ~91%, which they got right. So the delta is ~0-1 point, not 3, and 26 mW collapses to roughly 0-9 mW. A 3-point difference read off two vendors' log-x graphs measured with different inductors is below the resolution of the method and cannot carry a milliwatt claim. (3) COST CLAIM IS BACKWARDS. TPS63802DLAR is $2.75 at qty 1 on Digi-Key (12,469 in stock); two per board is $5.50 against one LTC3527EUD#PBF at $1.81-4.52. Sourcing is genuinely better - LTC3527EUD#PBF is out of stock/backorder at Digi-Key - but the part cost goes up, not down. VOUT3 = 3.302 V is correct arithmetic and the NCV8164 keeps ample headroom (onsemi datasheet: 2.5 V option dropout 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA). Corrected: 29 mW at idle (measured, stands), in-use unproven and plausibly ~0-9 mW.

findings.title: L2 (the 3.3 V channel) 4.7 uH -> 3.3 uH in the same case cuts DCR 120 -> 78 mOhm and raises the Burst threshold ~40%; leave L1 alone
findings.current_part: L1 = L2 = Taiyo Yuden LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG (previous PN NRS3015T4R7MNGH): 4.7 uH +/-20%, DCR 0.12 Ohm typ / 0.144 Ohm max, Isat 1.02 A (dL = 30%), temperature-rise current 1.04 A (dT = 40 C), 3.0 x 3.0 x max 1.5 mm, wire-wound ferrite. Footprint Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering, pads 1.65 x 2.0 mm at +/-1.175 mm. Nearest neighbour to L1 is TP6 at 2.38 mm centre-to-centre, so there is no room for a 4x4 mm part.
findings.proposal: Taiyo Yuden LSXND3030QKT3R3MNG (previous PN NRS3015T3R3MNGH) for L2 only: 3.3 uH +/-20%, DCR 78 mOhm typ / 93.6 mOhm max, Isat 1.21 A max / 1.4 A typ, temperature-rise current 1.23 A max, same 3.0 x 3.0 x max 1.5 mm case, same series, same land. Note the saturation and thermal ratings are BETTER than the 4.7 uH part, not worse. Keep L1 (the 5 V channel) at 4.7 uH.
findings.benefit: Two effects. (1) DCR: at the typical in-use point (VOUT3 150 mA) dI_pp rises from 0.1154 to 0.6507/3.96 = 0.1643 A, so I_rms^2 goes 0.042823 to 0.043964; loss = 0.043964 x (0.5734 + 0.078) = 28.6 mW versus 0.042823 x 0.6934 = 29.7 mW, saving 1.1 mW. At the overclocked point (212 mA): 0.085575 x 0.6514 = 55.8 mW versus 58.6 mW, saving 2.8 mW. (2) The larger and less certain effect: the datasheet states "Raising the inductor value will lower the load current at which Burst Mode operation is entered", so dropping 4.7 -> 3.3 uH raises the leave-burst threshold by roughly 4.7/3.3 = 42%. My extrapolated 1.2 MHz threshold at VIN 2.45 V is ~30 mA; 42% takes it to ~43 mA. Stock VOUT3 idle is ~37 mA, so this could put the board back into Burst at idle and recover the ~6 mW that the 5 V channel is currently losing (finding ltc3527-shared-burst-decision). With the ClockxControl fitted, idle VOUT3 is ~49 mA and even 43 mA is not enough, so this lever only helps a board without the module — say so honestly. I quote only the DCR-certain part in benefit_mw.
findings.risk: I did NOT change L1. Doing so would be a net loss: the 5 V channel already runs 0.222 A p-p of ripple at 88 mA out and is in DCM at light backlight, where a smaller inductance increases RMS current more than it saves in DCR. The 42% burst-threshold scaling is my inference from a qualitative datasheet sentence; the published threshold curves are 2.2 MHz only, so treat the ~6 mW burst recovery as a hypothesis to measure, not a claim. Inductance tolerance is +/-20% on both parts, and 3.3 uH is the bottom of the datasheet's stated 1.2 MHz range ("Inductor values between 3.3uH and 4.7uH are suitable for most 1.2MHz applications"), so a -20% part is 2.64 uH, outside the recommended range — specify the M tolerance and accept that. Also verified NOT worth doing: Coilcraft XFL3012-472 is 171 mOhm max, Murata DFE322512F-4R7M is 157 mOhm, Taiyo Yuden's own metal-composite LCDND3030KKT4R7MM is 300 mOhm typ. In this envelope the installed 4.7 uH part is already near best-in-class; the only real gain is in dropping the inductance.
findings.verify_reason: The parts and the arithmetic are right. Taiyo Yuden's own pages confirm LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG (4.7 uH +/-20%, DCR 0.12 typ / 0.144 max, Isat 1.02 A max at dL=30%, temp-rise current 1.04 A at dT=40C, 3.0x3.0x max 1.5 mm, Mass Production Preferred) and LSXND3030QKT3R3MNG (3.3 uH +/-20%, DCR 78 typ / 93.6 max mOhm, Isat 1.21 A max / 1.4 typ, temp-rise 1.23 A max, same case, Mass Production Preferred) - and yes, the saturation and thermal ratings of the 3.3 uH part are BETTER, which is a genuinely non-obvious and correct observation. Same series, same land, drop-in confirmed. The DCR arithmetic reproduces to the digit: dI_pp 0.1154 -> 0.1643 A, I_rms^2 0.042823 -> 0.043964, loss 29.7 -> 28.6 mW (saving 1.1 mW) and 58.5 -> 55.7 mW overclocked (saving 2.8 mW). The datasheet quotes are real: 'Inductor values between 3.3uH and 4.7uH are suitable for most 1.2MHz applications' and 'Raising the inductor value will lower the load current at which Burst Mode operation is entered'. THE FATAL OMISSION: the finding quotes that second sentence but not the one directly before it in the Inductor Selection section - 'Larger values of inductance will allow slightly greater output current capability (and lower the Burst Mode threshold) by reducing the inductor ripple current.' Dropping L2 by 30% raises ripple 42% and therefore CUTS converter 2's maximum output current - on the exact channel that this same author's converter2-current-limit-vs-overclock finding says is already at its ceiling under the overclock. Quantified at VIN 2.0 V (the board's real floor, set by U3 = TPS3840DL20, VIT- = 2.0 V) against the 400 mA guaranteed-minimum limit: 4.7 uH gives Iout,max = (0.400 - 0.0711) x 0.5995 = 197 mA; 3.3 uH gives (0.400 - 0.1011) x 0.5995 = 179 mA. That is a 9% cut in worst-case headroom on the marginal rail, bought for 1.1-2.8 mW. The two findings contradict each other and this one does not acknowledge it. Also unverified: I did not independently check the Coilcraft XFL3012-472 (171 mOhm), Murata DFE322512F-4R7M (157 mOhm) or Taiyo Yuden LCDND3030KKT4R7MM (300 mOhm) figures used to argue the installed part is near best-in-class - treat those as unverified. Verdict: numbers correct, recommendation unsafe as written. Do this only in combination with moving VOUT3 to converter 1, or not at all.

findings.title: F1's 2 A Accu-Guard adds up to 80 mOhm in series with the whole board — up to 18 mW at max use — and it does not protect against reverse batteries anyway
findings.current_part: F1 = Kyocera AVX F0805B2R00FSTR, Accu-Guard SMD thin-film fuse. From the Accu-Guard II datasheet table: current rating 2.00 A, resistance 0.080 Ohm MAXIMUM (measured at 10% of rated current, 25 C), voltage drop 220 mV max at 1x rated current, fusing current within 5 s = 4.00 A, pre-arc I2t 0.030, 63 V. Board netlist: BT1+ -> F1 -> VBATT, so it carries every milliamp the board draws. NOTE the datasheet publishes only a maximum, not a typical, so the real installed resistance is somewhere at or below 80 mOhm.
findings.proposal: Same F0805B family, same 0805 land: F0805B2R50FW/STR (2.50 A, 0.060 Ohm max) or F0805B3R00FW/STR (3.00 A, 0.050 Ohm max). I am flagging this as a build option rather than recommending it, because the saving is bounded by a max-only spec and the protection cost is real.
findings.benefit: At the maximum measured in-use input current of 480 mA: worst-case loss now = 0.480^2 x 0.080 = 18.4 mW; with the 3 A part = 0.480^2 x 0.050 = 11.5 mW; saving up to 6.9 mW. At the overclocked 577 mA: up to 0.577^2 x 0.030 = 10.0 mW. Because only maxima are published, the true saving could be anywhere from ~0 (if the installed part measures well under 80 mOhm) to the numbers above.
