That is a bigger lever than anything in my domain, but it is an LDO/topology question, not a passives question.
findings.risk: The mounting-inductance figure is an estimate, so the 200 MHz impedance number is indicative rather than measured. If a build shows instability at 1.75x, the thing to instrument is VDD2 at TP18 with a short-ground-spring probe before adding capacitors - the likely culprits are the SRAM's missing local cap and the ECO-5 plane damage, not the CPU decoupling count. Also note U8's 350 mA minimum current limit: my estimated 117 mA of core current at 1.75x leaves headroom, but that estimate is derived from insideGadgets' system-level figure, not measured.
findings.verify_reason: Negative result survives, but the load current it is built on is not defensible and one inventory item is misplaced. VERIFIED from the NCV8164 datasheet: 'The device is designed to be stable with standard ceramics capacitors with values of 1 uF or greater' and 'does not require a minimum Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR) for the output capacitor'; Iq 30 uA typ / 40 uA max; dropout for the 2.5 V variant in TSOP-5 is 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA; Output Current Limit 350 mA min / 560 mA typ. All four numbers correct. LTC3527 FB reference is 1.20 V, so VDD3 = 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V - the LDO headroom figure of 0.836 V is right, and the '50 mA of extra core current costs 42 mW of heat' arithmetic checks. Placement claims verified exactly (see my sram verdict for the measured distances). All three margin checks reproduce: Ztarget = 0.125/0.0585 = 2.14 Ohm; Q = 0.117/7.34e6 = 15.94 nC; dV = 15.94e-9/4.37e-6 = 3.65 mV; |Z| = 2pi x 2e8 x 0.22e-9 = 0.277 Ohm. CORRECTIONS: (1) The 117 mA CPU core estimate is not defensible. 117 mA x 2.5 V = 292 mW of core alone, against a 134 mW stock-GBA idle and a 410-1175 mW whole-console in-use envelope; insideGadgets' 40-60 mA is explicitly system-level across all rails ('when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more'), not core-only. The error is in the safe direction - halving the current halves dV and doubles Ztarget - so the negative result holds, but the number should not be quoted as if it were a load figure. (2) The 'nine caps local to the CPU' count includes C8, which is at the SRAM 7-25 mm away and is the subject of a separate finding; eight caps and 4.28 uF is the correct local figure, which changes dV to 3.72 mV - immaterial. (3) C60's derated value: I digitised the same Murata GRM188R61E106KA73 curve and read 7.55 uF at 2.5 V against the finding's 7.39 uF; immaterial, and C60 is 33 mm away so it should not be in a CPU-decoupling tally at all. The recommendation - change nothing at U1, instrument TP18 before adding capacitors - is right.

findings.title: EM1/EM2/EM3/EM7 and RA1 sit on signal and accessory nets that carry essentially zero DC - their I2R loss is 0 mW
findings.current_part: EM1/EM2 = TDK ACM2520-801-3P-T002, 3-line common-mode choke, 800 Ohm at 100 MHz, rated current 150 mA, DC resistance 1.6 Ohm, SMD-6P 2.5 x 2.0 mm. EM3/EM7 = Bourns MH1608-601Y, 600 Ohm at 100 MHz +/-25 %, DC resistance 200 mOhm max, rated current 1 A, 0603 (1.6 x 0.8 x 0.8 mm). Nets, straight from the board file: EM1 filters /CPU/SO, /CPU/SI and /CPU/LGND; EM2 filters /CPU/SCK, /CPU/SD and /CPU/LGND - all six are AGB link-port serial lines and the link-port ground, each already in series with a 330 Ohm element of RA1. EM3 sits between VDD35 and Net-(P4-VDD35), i.e. it feeds only the link connector's VDD pin - I checked specifically that it is NOT in the cartridge supply path, because P1 pad 1 and pad C1 connect to VDD35 directly, upstream of EM3. EM7 sits between /~RESET and U1H's ~RESET input, a high-impedance logic input.
findings.proposal: Leave all of them alone. There is nothing to win.
findings.benefit: Zero, and that is the finding. With no link cable attached, all five parts carry no DC current at all: 0.144 W/A^2 x 0^2 = 0 mW. Even in the worst realistic case - a link accessory drawing 20 mA from VDD35 - the supply leg through EM3 dissipates 0.020^2 x 0.2 = 0.08 mW and the return leg through one ACM2520 winding dissipates 0.020^2 x 1.6 = 0.64 mW, both only while the accessory is plugged in. EM7 sees at most the 185 uA that R29's 18k pull-up sources into the reset net (3.336/18000), for 0.007 microwatts. RA1's 330 Ohm elements likewise carry only link-port signal current. Against a 170 mW idle and a 410-1175 mW in-use budget this is not a rounding error, it is exactly zero. The one thing worth noting rather than removing: because the ACM2520's third winding carries the link-port ground return at 1.6 Ohm, any future accessory drawing appreciable current through the EXT port would develop a real offset on LGND - 20 mA gives 32 mV. Not a problem for GBA link cables; would be for anything drawing hundreds of mA.
findings.risk: None from leaving them. If anyone were tempted to delete them to save cost, the cost is EMI compliance and ESD robustness on an exposed external connector, for no power benefit whatsoever.
findings.verify_reason: Both parts and every net claim check out. TDK ACM2520-801-3P-T002 confirmed on DigiKey: 3-line common mode choke, 800 Ohm @ 100 MHz, rated current 150 mA, DCR 1.6 Ohm max, 2.50 x 2.00 x 1.30 mm max, Active. Bourns MH1608-601Y confirmed: 600 Ohm @ 100 MHz, DCR 200 mOhm max, rated 1 A, 0603 (1608 Metric), Active. NETS VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY from the fork board, including the one that actually mattered: EM3 sits between VDD35 and Net-(P4-VDD35), and P1 pad 1 and pad C1 are both on VDD35 directly - so EM3 is genuinely NOT in the cartridge supply path, exactly as claimed. EM1 windings pair (1,6) GND/LGND, (2,5) RA1C/SI, (3,4) RA1D/SO; EM2 likewise on SCK/SD/LGND; EM7 between /~RESET and U1H's ~RESET. All arithmetic reproduces: 0.020^2 x 0.2 = 0.08 mW; 0.020^2 x 1.6 = 0.64 mW; 3.336/18000 = 185 uA and (185e-6)^2 x 0.2 = 6.8 nW; 0.020 x 1.6 = 32 mV of LGND offset. The RA1 elements likewise carry only pull-up current - RA1A sees 3.3/100.33k = 33 uA through 330 Ohm = 0.36 uW. Zero is zero and the finding says so. Two unverified details, neither material: the MH1608-601Y +/-25% impedance tolerance is not stated on the DigiKey page I opened, and DigiKey gives 1.00 mm max seated height rather than the 0.8 mm the finding quotes. The 'do not delete these for cost' warning is correct - they are the only EMI/ESD elements on an exposed external connector.

findings.title: CP2/CP3 audio coupling: a 250 mOhm drop-in exists, but the honest answer on audible improvement is no - except with 16 Ohm earbuds
findings.current_part: CP2/CP3 = TPSB107K010R0400, 100 uF 10 V case-B tantalum, ESR max 400 mOhm at 100 kHz, DCL max 10 uA. Topology: CP2 from U6 LOUT/BTL- to the jack's left contact with R20 1k to AGND; CP3 from U6 ROUT to the jack's right contact with R19 1k to AGND. DC bias across each is VAUD/2 = 1.25 V in the correct polarity, i.e. 12.5 % of rating - a properly applied polarized cap with plenty of margin, and crucially with NO meaningful DC-bias capacitance loss, which is the one place a tantalum beats a 1210 MLCC outright.
findings.proposal: If you want the lowest-ESR drop-in on the identical land, Kyocera AVX's TPS table lists TPSB107*006#0250 - case B, 100 uF, 6.3 V, ESR max 250 mOhm, 0.583 A rms at 25 C. 6.3 V is still 5x the 1.25 V applied bias, so the derating in voltage rating is safe here (it is NOT safe for CP1, which has zero DC bias - see cp1-reverse-bias-btl). Do not substitute a 100 uF MLCC at CP2/CP3: unlike CP1, these have a real DC bias, so a 6.3 V or 10 V 1210 X5R would lose a large fraction of its capacitance at 1.25 V and push the high-pass corner the wrong way.
findings.benefit: Be honest: essentially nothing audible. ESR path: 400 mOhm in series with a 32 Ohm headphone is 1.2 % of the load, worth 20*log10(32.4/32.25) = 0.04 dB. Going to 250 mOhm changes that to 0.02 dB. Nobody hears this. High-pass corner is the only thing that matters, and it is set by the capacitance, not the dielectric: the load is the headphone in parallel with R19/R20 1k, so 32 Ohm || 1k = 31.0 Ohm gives f(-3 dB) = 1/(2*pi*31.0*100e-6) = 51.3 Hz, which is fine; but 16 Ohm || 1k = 15.75 Ohm gives 101 Hz, which is an audible bass rolloff with low-impedance earbuds. The fix would be more capacitance, and here the answer is genuinely no: I walked the full Kyocera AVX TPS ratings table and case B tops out at 100 uF for any rating of 6.3 V or above (only the 2.5 V and 4 V blocks offer 150/220 uF in case B, and 2.5 V is too close to the 1.25 V bias to be sound practice). Going to 220 uF means case C (6.0 x 3.2 x 2.6 mm) which does not fit the 1210 land. So: the 101 Hz corner with 16 Ohm loads is a genuine limitation of this design, and there is no same-footprint part that fixes it.
findings.risk: Switching to the 6.3 V part halves the voltage margin on a rail whose only excursion is the 2.5 V VAUD supply - still 5x the applied bias, so low risk, but there is no real reward either. Recommendation: leave CP2/CP3 exactly as they are, and record the 16 Ohm corner as a known characteristic rather than chasing it.
findings.verify_reason: The recommendation (leave CP2/CP3 alone) is right; the key negative claim behind it is wrong. VERIFIED from the Kyocera AVX TPS ratings table, exact rows: TPSB107*010#0400 = case B, 100 uF, 10 V, DCL 10 uA, DF 8%, ESR 400 mOhm, 0.461 A rms @25C; TPSB107*006#0250 = case B, 100 uF, 6.3 V, DCL 6.3 uA, DF 10%, ESR 250 mOhm, 0.583 A rms @25C. Both exactly as claimed. Topology confirmed from the netlist (CP2 from LOUT/BTL- to jack pin 2 with R20 1k to AGND; CP3 from ROUT to jack pin 3 with R19 1k to AGND; DC bias VAUD/2 = 1.25 V in the correct sense). Corner arithmetic reproduces: 32||1k = 31.006 Ohm -> 51.3 Hz; 16||1k = 15.748 Ohm -> 101.1 Hz. The ESR dB figures reproduce (20log10(32.4/32.25) = 0.040 dB). CORRECTION: 'there is no same-footprint part that fixes it' is refuted by Kyocera AVX's own table, which lists TPSB157*004#0250 - case B, 150 uF, 4 V, DCL 6 uA, DF 10%, ESR max 250 mOhm, 0.583 A rms. At the 1.25 V applied bias that is 31% of rating, inside the conventional 50% tantalum derating, and it moves the 16 Ohm corner from 101 Hz to 1/(2pi x 15.748 x 150e-6) = 67 Hz - an audible improvement on a same-footprint drop-in. The finding's own survey missed it while asserting it had 'walked the full Kyocera AVX TPS ratings table'. The real objection to the 4 V part is different and better: at full SE output the node swings 1.25 V +/- ~1.26 Vpk (LM4853 SE into 32 Ohm is 25 mW at 2.7 V = 0.894 Vrms, scaling to ~1.26 Vpk), so peak applied reaches ~2.5 V = 63% of a 4 V rating, outside the 50% guideline. So the honest statement is 'a 150 uF case-B part exists and would fix the corner, but it trades away most of the voltage margin' - not 'nothing exists'. I could not confirm distributor stock for TPSB157*004#0250, so treat availability as unverified. Benefit correctly stated as 0 mW either way.

findings.title: C12's DC-bias deration shortens the U17 supervisor's power-up delay by 24 % versus the value in the schematic
findings.current_part: C12 = GRM188R61E106KA73J, 10 uF 25 V X5R 0603. Net: Net-(U17-VDD), fed from SW through R58 5.1k with R63 100k to GND, supplying U17 (TPS3840DL20). This is an RC delay element, not a bypass. At the divider ratio the node sits at 0.951 x SW, so roughly 2.3 V mid-discharge, where the digitised Murata curve gives about -24 % and an effective 7.6 uF.
findings.proposal: No part change. Either annotate the schematic with the effective value, or - if the delay actually matters for the power-sequencing behaviour - re-scale R58 so the intended time constant is met with the real capacitance rather than the marked one.
findings.benefit: No power saving; this is the one place on the board where DC-bias deration changes a behaviour rather than a margin, which is exactly the class of problem the reviewer asked about. Arithmetic: tau = (R58 || R63) x C = (5.1k x 100k / 105.1k) x C = 4.852k x C. With the marked 10 uF that is 48.5 ms; with the 7.6 uF the part actually delivers at 2.3 V it is 36.9 ms - 24 % faster than anyone reading the schematic would compute. Whether 12 ms matters depends on U17's role in the VOUT5/Q5 sequencing, which is outside my domain; the point is that the schematic's number is wrong by a quarter and nothing on the drawing says so.
findings.risk: None from flagging. If the delay is re-scaled via R58, note that the deration itself moves with battery voltage (the same cap is 7.54 uF at 2.4 V and about 8.5 uF at 1.8 V), so the delay is not constant across the discharge curve either.
findings.verify_reason: The deration is real and the RC algebra is right, but the deration number is off and the headline claim about it changing a BEHAVIOUR is not supported. VERIFIED: C12's schematic Source resolves to Murata GRM188R61E106KA73J - 10 uF +/-10%, 25 V, X5R, 0603, Active on DigiKey; the Murata datasheet confirms L 1.6+/-0.2, W 0.8+/-0.2, T 0.8+/-0.2, cap change rate +/-15.0%, -55 to 85 C. Topology confirmed from the netlist: R58 5.1k from SW to Net-(U17-VDD), R63 100k to GND, C12 on that node, U17 = TPS3840DL20. Node = SW x 100/105.1 = 0.9515 x SW; Thevenin R = 5.1k x 100k/105.1k = 4.852 kOhm; 4.852k x 10u = 48.5 ms. All correct. CORRECTION 1: I digitised Murata's own DC-bias chart for GRM188R61E106KA73 (gridlines located by pixel analysis) and read -21.9% at 2.3 V -> 7.81 uF, not -24% -> 7.6 uF. That gives tau = 37.9 ms, i.e. 22% faster than the marked value, not 24%. The finding's 7.54 uF at 2.4 V reads 7.68 uF on my digitisation and its ~8.5 uF at 1.8 V reads 8.60 uF - both close. CORRECTION 2, the substantive one: the finding bills this as 'the one place on the board where DC-bias deration changes a behaviour rather than a margin' while simultaneously admitting it never determined what U17 does ('outside my domain'). It does not. Tracing it: U17's output (pad 1) drives Net-(Q5B-G) on Q5 (NDC7002N), whose drain feeds U14 (MIC1553) and the R10/R65/R66 network that lights DL2, the red 150060RS75000 LED. With the TPS3840DL20's 2.0 V threshold and the 0.9515 divider, U17 trips at SW ~ 2.10 V. So the RC is a droop filter on a low-battery indicator, not a delay element in any power-sequencing path. An 11 ms change in the debounce of a battery-low LED is inconsequential, and the finding's own framing device ('nothing on the drawing says so' as a correctness issue) is therefore overstated. Keep it as a documentation nit at low priority; do not rescale R58.

findings.title: Negative result: the 0.1 uF, 1 uF, 15 pF and 3300 pF parts do not derate meaningfully - the small-signal decoupling is correctly specified throughout
findings.current_part: MPNs resolved from the schematics' own Source fields, which every one of these symbols carries: 0.1 uF = KEMET C0603C104K5RACTU, X7R 50 V 0603. 1 uF = KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU, X7R 16 V 0603. 15 pF (C40/C41, the LTC3527 feed-forward caps) = KEMET C0603C150J5GACTU, C0G/NP0 50 V +/-5 %. 3300 pF (C61/C80, the TPS22917 CT slew-rate caps) = KEMET C0603C332K5RACTU, X7R 50 V.
findings.proposal: No change. Report this so nobody spends money re-specifying parts that are already right.
findings.benefit: No power saving; this is the negative result that stops a pointless BOM churn. Digitised curves: a 1 uF 16 V X7R 0603 loses 3.2 % at 2.5 V (0.968 uF) and 12.5 % at 3.336 V (0.875 uF). A 0.1 uF X7R 0603 - and I deliberately used the 16 V curve, which is the pessimistic case, because the board's part is 50 V - reads +0.7 % at 2.5 V, 0.0 % at 3.336 V and -0.7 % at 5.014 V, i.e. flat. C0G has no voltage coefficient at all by construction, so the LTC3527's feed-forward compensation is stable, which matters because those two caps are inside the converter's feedback loop. The 3300 pF X7R 50 V parts sit at 5-7 % of rated voltage and follow the same flat behaviour as the 0.1 uF. The only two capacitor families on this board that derate hard are the 22 uF 0805s and the 10 uF 0603s, both covered in their own findings. The BOM is well chosen: 25 V dielectric for the bulk and 50 V X7R for the bypass on a 5 V board is more conservative than most hobbyist designs.
findings.risk: The 1 uF and 0.1 uF curves are from Murata parts of the same case size, dielectric class and (or lower) voltage rating, not from the KEMET parts actually specified - KEMET/Yageo publish their DC-bias data only through the KSIM web tool, which is JavaScript-rendered and could not be fetched. Same-class substitution is standard practice for this kind of estimate but it is a substitution, and it is why this finding is not at 0.9 confidence. The direction of the error is safe: the Murata 16 V curve bounds a KEMET 50 V part from the pessimistic side.
findings.verify_reason: I resolved every Source field in the schematics myself and opened each DigiKey page: 0.1 uF = KEMET C0603C104K5RACTU, X7R, 50 V, +/-10%, 0603, Active; 1 uF = KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU, X7R, 16 V, +/-10%, 0603, Active; 15 pF = KEMET C0603C150J5GACTU, C0G/NP0, 50 V, +/-5%, 0603, Active; 3300 pF = KEMET C0603C332K5RACTU, X7R, 50 V, +/-10%, 0603, Active. All four MPN identifications correct, all four in production. I then independently digitised Murata's own DC-bias chart for GRM188R71C105KA12 (the 1 uF 16 V X7R 0603 the finding substitutes) and read -2.8% at 2.5 V -> 0.972 uF and -11.7% at 3.336 V -> 0.883 uF, against the finding's -3.2%/0.968 uF and -12.5%/0.875 uF. Agreement within digitisation error, and the finding is the pessimistic side of my reading, which is the right direction for a margin claim. The 0.1 uF flatness assertion I did not verify curve-by-curve, but it is the expected behaviour of a low-CV 50 V X7R and the finding deliberately used the pessimistic 16 V curve, so the error direction is safe. The C0G point is structural, not empirical - NP0 has no voltage coefficient by construction - and it matters because C40/C41 sit inside the LTC3527's feedback path, which the datasheet's own feedforward recommendation (15 pF, verified verbatim) relies on. The Murata-for-KEMET substitution is disclosed and is the reason the finding is not higher confidence; that is the right call. Nothing to churn.

findings.title: Negative result: shrinking the output capacitors cannot recover the 29 mW idle gap to AGBM-02, because the board already idles above the Burst Mode threshold
findings.current_part: LTC3527 with MODE = GND (automatic Burst Mode) and FSEL = GND (1.2 MHz). Datasheet Iq is 12 uA in Burst Mode versus 500 uA typ / 900 uA max active, drawn from the higher of VOUT1/VOUT2. The Applications Information warns that "larger output capacitor values may cause this transition [out of Burst Mode] to occur at lighter loads", which is a genuine invitation to think that AGBM-01's 43 uF of nominal VOUT3 bulk is costing idle efficiency versus AGBM-02.
findings.proposal: Do not reduce COUT. The hypothesis is testable from the datasheet and it fails.
findings.benefit: Zero, and knowing it is zero is the point - this was the most plausible capacitor-side explanation for AGBM-01 idling 29 mW above AGBM-02 and 36 mW above a stock GBA, and it is wrong. The check: the datasheet's Burst Mode Threshold Current vs VIN curve for VOUT = 3.3 V shows enter-burst at roughly 14 mA and leave-burst at roughly 18 mA of load current at VIN = 2.4 V. The board's idle VOUT3 load is 170 mW x ~0.85 / 3.336 V = roughly 43 mA - about 2.5x above the leave-burst threshold. Channel 2 is therefore in fixed-frequency PWM at idle no matter what COUT is, so changing COUT cannot move the operating mode. Even if it could, the prize is small: the Iq difference is 500 - 12 = 488 uA drawn from a 5 V output, i.e. 2.4 mW at the output or about 2.9 mW at the battery, plus an unquantified switching-loss term. Channel 1 (VOUT5) is a different story - its idle load is only a few mA (the LED through R25 3.3k is 0.91 mA), which is below the roughly 30-38 mA burst threshold at VOUT = 5 V, so it is already in Burst Mode and already getting the 14 uA Iq the datasheet promises at VOUT = 5 V. Both channels are already in the best mode available to them. The 29 mW gap to AGBM-02 is a converter-topology difference (one dual boost with two 4.7 uH inductors versus two TPS63802 buck-boosts with 0.47 uH), not a capacitor selection difference, and no passive change on this board will close it.
findings.risk: None - the recommendation is to change nothing. The burst-threshold curves I read are labelled for 2.2 MHz operation while this board runs at 1.2 MHz (FSEL = GND), so the exact threshold on this board will differ; but it would have to be off by more than 2.5x in the wrong direction to change the conclusion, and lower switching frequency generally lowers, not raises, the burst threshold. My idle VOUT3 load figure also assumes ~85 % converter efficiency and that essentially all idle load is on channel 2, both stated estimates.
findings.verify_reason: The recommendation (do not reduce COUT) is correct and is if anything strengthened, but one of the two supporting claims is refuted by the same datasheet page the finding cites. VERIFIED VERBATIM from LTC3527 35271fc: 'Note that larger output capacitor values may cause this transition to occur at lighter loads.' Iq confirmed from the Electrical Characteristics table: Burst Mode 12 uA, Active 500 uA typ / 900 uA max. MODE=GND and FSEL=GND confirmed from the netlist, and the Burst Mode Threshold Current graphs (G13/G14/G15) really are labelled '2.2MHz OPERATION', which the finding correctly flags. The VOUT=3.3 V graph's load-current axis tops out at 25 mA, so a 14/18 mA enter/leave pair is a plausible reading. REFUTED CLAIM: 'Channel 1 (VOUT5) ... is already in Burst Mode and already getting the 14 uA Iq the datasheet promises at VOUT = 5 V. Both channels are already in the best mode available to them.' The datasheet says the opposite, twice: 'To realize the efficiency benefits of Burst Mode operation, both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition, if they are both enabled' and 'Once the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 have left Burst Mode operation and returned to normal operation, they will remain there until both output loads are reduced below the burst threshold current.' Since the finding's own estimate puts channel 2 at ~43 mA at idle, well above its threshold, the IC as a whole is in fixed-frequency 1.2 MHz PWM and channel 1 is held OUT of Burst Mode by channel 2. So the part is burning its 500 uA active Iq (~2.5 mW at the 5 V output, ~3 mW at the battery) plus continuous switching losses in both channels at idle - which is a real, quantified component of the 29 mW gap to AGBM-02, not the 'both channels already optimal' picture the finding paints. Also, the '14 uA Iq at VOUT = 5 V' figure does not exist in the datasheet; the only Burst Mode Iq given is 12 uA. Third point worth carrying forward: the datasheet attributes the ENTER-burst threshold to the inductor ('Raising the inductor value will lower the load current at which Burst Mode operation is entered'), not COUT - relevant because finding l1l2-dcr proposes changing L2. Conclusion unchanged: leave COUT alone; the gap is topological.

findings.title: VOUT3's bulk is 65 % of nominal after derating - which is still six times the LTC3527's stability minimum, so the rail carrying the overclock is fine
findings.current_part: VOUT3 at 3.336 V carries C42 (22 uF 25 V X5R 0805 -> 14.94 uF), C2 and C23 (10 uF 25 V X5R 0603 -> 6.11 uF each) and C22 (1 uF 16 V X7R 0603 -> 0.875 uF): 28.0 uF effective against 43 uF nominal. The converter's input cap C37 (10 uF 0603) sits at VCC, roughly 2.4 V mid-discharge, where it derates to 7.54 uF.
findings.proposal: No change. Recorded so the number exists in writing, because this is the rail the ClockxControl loads and it is the first thing anyone will suspect if the overclock misbehaves.
findings.benefit: No power saving. The margins: LTC3527 is specified stable with COUT >= 4.7 uF and recommends 4.7-10 uF, so 28.0 uF effective is 6x the floor - the 35 % capacitance loss to DC bias changes nothing about loop stability. On the input side the datasheet says "A 2.2 uF input capacitor is sufficient for most applications" and C37 delivers 7.54 uF, a 3.4x margin. Adding the overclock's 62 mA to VOUT3 raises the rail's load from roughly 43 mA at idle to roughly 150 mA; against the datasheet's Maximum Output Current vs VIN curve for converter 2 (roughly 300 mA at VIN = 2.4 V, VOUT = 3.3 V) that is comfortable at mid-discharge. The one thing worth watching is the low-battery end: the same curve falls to roughly 200 mA at VIN = 1.8 V, so an overclocked console with a bright backlight near the end of a set of alkalines is operating with about 25 % headroom on channel 2 rather than 100 %.
findings.risk: None from leaving it. The low-battery headroom note is derived by reading a datasheet graph and depends on my channel-split estimate; if the split is materially different from 40:60 the VOUT3 numbers move. Measuring current at TP16 would replace the estimate with a fact.
findings.verify_reason: I recomputed the derating from the Murata charts myself rather than accepting the figures. Digitising GRM21BR61E226ME44L at 3.336 V gives -32.2% -> 14.91 uF for C42 (finding 14.94); digitising GRM188R61E106KA73 at 3.336 V gives -36.8% -> 6.32 uF each for C2 and C23 (finding 6.11); GRM188R71C105KA12 at 3.336 V gives 0.883 uF for C22 (finding 0.875). Total 28.4 uF against the finding's 28.0 uF - the finding is 1.5% pessimistic, which is irrelevant against the floor. C37 at ~2.4 V reads 7.68 uF on my digitisation (finding 7.54). MARGINS VERIFIED VERBATIM from the LTC3527 datasheet: 'The internal loop compensation of the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 is designed to be stable with output capacitor values of 4.7uF or greater' - so 28 uF is 6x the floor and a 35% DC-bias loss changes nothing about the loop; and 'A 2.2uF input capacitor is sufficient for most applications', so C37 at 7.7 uF is a 3.5x margin. The VOUT3 = 3.336 V figure is independently confirmed by the datasheet's 1.20 V feedback reference and the R23/R55 divider. The converter-2 maximum-output-current reading (~300 mA at VIN 2.4 V, ~200 mA at VIN 1.8 V) comes from a datasheet graph and the 40:60 channel split is an estimate - both are explicitly disclosed, and the low-battery headroom note is the right thing to flag for an overclocked build. One loose number: 'adding the overclock's 62 mA ... raises the rail's load from roughly 43 mA at idle to roughly 150 mA' does not add up on its own terms (43 + 62 = 105) - the 150 mA presumably includes in-use rather than idle load, but it is not stated. Immaterial to the conclusion. Recommendation to change nothing is correct.

findings.title: DL1 power LED is an AlInGaP part at 0.93 mA burning 4.66 mW continuously; an InGaN green in the same 0603 pads at 0.12 mA is brighter and saves 5.05 mW at the battery
findings.current_part: DL1 = Wurth 150060VS75000, 0603 WL-SMCW, AlInGaP, bright green, 570 nm dominant; VF 2.0 V min / 2.4 V max at 20 mA; luminous intensity IV 12 mcd min / 40 mcd max at 20 mA; 140 deg viewing angle (https://www.we-online.com/components/products/datasheet/150060VS75000.pdf). Series resistor R25 = 3.3k (0603) from VOUT5; cathode to Q9A drain (Q9A on in the normal battery state, Rds(on) 1.7 ohm typ at Vgs=10 V, ~3 ohm at the 5 V gate drive here, so ~3 mV drop) (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/ndc7002n-d.pdf). The LED is lit the entire time the console is on, because VOUT5 is up whenever the boost runs.
findings.proposal: Replace DL1 with Wurth 150060GS75000 — same 0603 WL-SMCW family, same land pattern, InGaN green, 525 nm dominant, VF 3.2-3.5 V at 20 mA, IV 220 mcd min / 430 mcd max at 20 mA (https://www.we-online.com/components/products/datasheet/150060GS75000.pdf) — and change R25 from 3.3k to 22k (same 0603 pads). Cheaper alternative if you want to keep the existing LED: change R25 alone from 3.3k to 10k.
findings.benefit:
Today: I digitised the 150060VS75000 forward I-V curve from the datasheet's vector data (axis calibration 0-4.0 V x 0-35 mA; recovered points (0.106 mA, 1.801 V), (1.006 mA, 1.925 V), (2.006 mA, 1.964 V), (8.00 mA, 2.045 V), (20 mA, 2.09 V) — the last agrees with the datasheet's 2.0/2.4 V min/max spec). Solving I = (5.00 - VF(I) - 0.005)/3300 converges at I = 0.932 mA, VF = 1.92 V. Power from VOUT5 = 5.00 x 0.932 mA = 4.66 mW, of which only 1.79 mW is in the LED and 2.87 mW is heat in R25. At 80% boost efficiency that is 5.83 mW off the battery — 3.4% of the 170 mW idle, and the single largest item in this domain. Present brightness: 12-40 mcd x (0.932/20) = 0.56-1.86 mcd.
With 150060GS75000 + R25 = 22k: digitising that part's I-V curve the same way gives (0.106 mA, 2.251 V) and (1.006 mA, 2.638 V); solving I = (5.00 - VF(I))/22000 converges at I = 0.124 mA, VF = 2.28 V. Power from VOUT5 = 5.00 x 0.124 mA = 0.62 mW. Saving = 4.66 - 0.62 = 4.04 mW at VOUT5 = 5.05 mW at the battery at 80% boost efficiency (4.75 mW at 85%). Brightness = 220-430 mcd x (0.124/20) = 1.36-2.67 mcd, i.e. 2.4x brighter worst-case-to-worst-case and ~1.7x brighter mid-to-mid than today. Brighter AND 7.5x less power.
Resistor-only variant (keep DL1, R25 3.3k -> 10k): solving against the same curve gives I = 0.314 mA at VF = 1.86 V, 1.57 mW at VOUT5, saving 3.09 mW at VOUT5 = 3.86 mW at the battery, but brightness falls to 0.19-0.63 mcd (3x dimmer than today) — visible indoors, marginal in daylight.
findings.risk: 525 nm InGaN green is a visibly different, colder green than the 570 nm yellow-green of the existing part; purely cosmetic but it will not match a stock AGB. The InGaN VF (3.2-3.5 V at 20 mA, ~2.28 V at 0.12 mA) is much more temperature- and bin-dependent than AlInGaP, so the current through a 22k resistor varies more across parts; at 0.12 mA a +/-0.15 V VF spread moves the current +/-6%, which is immaterial for an indicator. If you go the resistor-only route the LED gets 3x dimmer, which some builders will dislike. No stability risk either way: DL1's cathode node /D1A also gates Q9B (the low-battery red-LED switch) through C68 10u, and reducing the DL1 current does not change that node's logic level — Q9A still pulls /D1A to ~0 in the normal state, and when Q9A turns off, /D1A is pulled to 5 V through R25 with essentially no current, so a 22k R25 works identically (it charges C68 in 220 ms instead of 33 ms, delaying the green-to-red changeover by ~0.2 s — cosmetic).
findings.verify_reason:
I fetched both Würth datasheets myself and confirmed every optical/electrical number verbatim. 150060VS75000: Chip Technology AlInGaP, Emitting Color Bright Green, λDom 570 nm, IV 12 min / 40 max mcd @ 20 mA, VF 2.0 min / 2.4 max V @ 20 mA, 140° viewing angle, 0603 WL-SMCW, STATUS 'Valid'. 150060GS75000: InGaN, Green, λDom 525 nm, IV 220/430 mcd @ 20 mA, VF 3.2/3.5 V @ 20 mA, 140°, 0603 WL-SMCW, 'Valid'. Page 1 of both PDFs carries the identical dimension and Recommended Land Pattern drawing (0.8 x 0.8 pads, 2.4 mm span), so the swap is a genuine drop-in on the LED_0603_1608Metric_Pad1.05x0.95mm_HandSolder pattern. I did NOT trust the finding's digitisation: I extracted the vector polyline for the 'Forward Current vs. Forward Voltage' graph on page 3 of each PDF with PyMuPDF and calibrated it against the axis label bounding boxes (0.0-4.0 V, 0-35 mA). VS curve: (0.081 mA, 1.800 V), (0.981, 1.924), (1.980, 1.963), (7.978, 2.044), (19.97, 2.099). GS curve: (0.081, 2.251), (0.981, 2.636), (19.97, 3.238) — matching the datasheet's 2.0/2.4 and 3.2/3.5 V @20 mA specs and matching the finding's claimed points to within its y-offset. The digitisation is honest.

Redone arithmetic. LTC3527 VFB verified as 1.176/1.20/1.224 V (Analog Devices 35271fc p.3), so VOUT5 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/560k) = 5.014 V, not 5.00. Solving I = (5.014 - VF(I) - IxRds(Q9A))/3300 against my digitised curve converges at I = 0.935 mA, VF = 1.922 V, P(VOUT5) = 4.68 mW (1.80 mW in the LED, 2.89 mW in R25). With the GS part and R25 = 22k: I = 0.1233 mA, VF = 2.297 V, P = 0.618 mW. Saving at the rail = 4.07 mW, matching the finding.

Correction to the battery conversion. Rather than assume 80%, I digitised the datasheet's own Figure G07 (Efficiency vs Load Current and VIN for VOUT1 = 5 V at 1.2 MHz; MODE=GND selects Automatic Burst Mode, FSEL=GND, verified U5 pin 3 = GND, pin 10 = GND from the netlist). The VIN = 2.4 V Burst curve reads 70.6% at 0.076 mA, 77.8% at 0.18 mA, 83.1% at 0.64 mA, 85.2% at 2.5 mA. VOUT5's total idle load sits in the 1-3 mA region, so the marginal efficiency is ~84%, not 80%. Saving at the battery = 4.07/0.84 = 4.8 mW, not 5.05 mW. Still the largest single item in this domain (2.8% of the 170 mW idle).

Four errors/omissions that do not overturn it. (1) 'Q9A Rds(on) ~3 ohm at the 5 V gate drive' is not in the NDC7002N datasheet — it specifies 1.6 ohm typ / 4 ohm max at VGS = 4.5 V, ID = 0.35 A and 1.7/2 ohm at VGS = 10 V; there is no interpolated 3 ohm figure. Immaterial (3 mV either way). (2) 'DL1's cathode node /D1A also gates Q9B through C68 10u' is wrong. From netmap: /D1A = {C68.1, DL1.1 (K), Q9.3 (G2), Q9.6 (D1)}. /D1A gates Q9B DIRECTLY; C68 is a shunt capacitor on that node, not in the gate path. (3) UNFLAGGED MARGIN RISK. Because the pull-up path for /D1A in the low-battery state is R25 in series with DL1, the high level at that node is VOUT5 - VF(DL1 at leakage current). Raising DL1's VF lowers Q9B's gate drive. Extrapolating my digitised slopes (0.105 V/decade for VS, 0.316 V/decade for GS) to the ~0.1-1 uA leakage load (Q9B IGSS 100 nA max, Q9A IDSS 1 uA max), /D1A reaches ~3.4-3.5 V today; with the GS part it lands between ~2.8 V (if the InGaN VF floors near its 0.08 mA value of 2.25 V) and ~3.4 V. Against Q9B's VGS(th) max of 2.5 V — a limit this same reviewer argues elsewhere is untrustworthy — the worst case leaves only ~0.3 V. Positive, but the finding did not check the one node its change actually perturbs. (4) The changeover delay is understated: integrating C68 = 10 uF against the falling LED current gives ~56 ms today and ~420 ms with 22k+InGaN (the finding's simple-RC 33/220 ms is about 2x low). Still cosmetic.

Finally, the brightness claim is not established: IV is extrapolated linearly 160x below the lowest plotted datasheet point (the IV-vs-IF graph on page 4 starts at 0-35 mA), and InGaN efficacy falls at very low current density. '2.4x brighter' should be stated as 'probably no dimmer, direction unverified'. The power saving is solid; the brightness claim is not.

findings.title: The Q1/Q3/Q10 brownout latch sits statically biased in the RUN state and burns 387 uA (0.93 mW) off VBATT; raising R15 and R16 from 10k to 100k cuts it to 81 uA
findings.current_part: Q1 = 2N3904 NPN SOT-23, hFE 40 min at IC = 0.1 mA, VCE = 1.0 V (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/2n3904-d.pdf). Q3 = 2N3906 PNP SOT-23, hFE 60 min at IC = 0.1 mA (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/2n3906-d.pdf). Q10 = NDC7002N dual N-ch in SuperSOT-6, pin assignment 1=G1, 2=S2, 3=G2, 4=D2, 5=S1, 6=D1 confirmed against the onsemi datasheet's pin-assignment graphic and against the KiCad symbol Transistor_FET:Q_Dual_NMOS_G1S2G2D2S1D1 used in the schematic (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/ndc7002n-d.pdf). Bias network as built: R12 100k (SW to Q1-C), R15 10k (Q1-C to Q3 base), R16 10k (Q10A-G to Q1 base), R17 100k (Q10A-G to GND).
findings.proposal: Change R15 from 10k to 100k and R16 from 10k to 100k (both existing 0603 pads, no other change). Optionally also R12 100k -> 470k. Do NOT take R12 to 1M: NDC7002N IDSS is spec'd 1 uA max (at VDS = 40 V, 25 C) and 500 uA at TJ = 125 C, and 1 uA through 1M would collapse the node.
findings.benefit:
Topology from the netlist: /EN is high in the run state (R11 1k pull-up from SW, R24 100k to GND, U3's open-drain RESET released), so Q10B (G=/EN pin3, S=GND pin2, D=Q1-C pin4) is ON, holding Q1-C at Vce(sat); that pulls Q3's base down through R15, turning Q3 ON, which pulls Q10A-G up to ~SW, which through R16 turns Q1 ON — a self-consistent, permanently-biased state, not a dormant one. Current at VBATT = 2.4 V, with Vbe(sat) = 0.65 V and Vce(sat) = 0.05 V: Ib(Q3) = (2.4-0.65-0.05)/10k = 170.0 uA; I(R17) = 2.35/100k = 23.5 uA; I(R16) = (2.35-0.65)/10k = 170.0 uA; Ic(Q3) = 193.5 uA; Ie(Q3) = 363.5 uA; I(R12) = 2.35/100k = 23.5 uA. Total from SW = 387.0 uA = 0.929 mW, straight off the battery with no conversion loss in between.
With R15 = R16 = 100k: Ib(Q3) = 1.70/100k = 17.0 uA; I(R16) = 1.70/100k = 17.0 uA; Ic(Q3) = 23.5 + 17.0 = 40.5 uA; Ie(Q3) = 57.5 uA; plus R12 23.5 uA = 81.0 uA = 0.194 mW. Saving 306 uA = 0.734 mW at the battery (0.43% of the 170 mW idle).
Saturation still holds with huge margin: Q3 forced beta = 40.5/17.0 = 2.4 (hFE min 60 at 0.1 mA), Q1 forced beta = (23.5 + 17.0)/17.0 = 2.4 (hFE min 40 at 0.1 mA). Re-checked at the worst-case operating point, VBATT = 2.0 V (just above U3's 2.0 V trip): Ib(Q3) = 13.0 uA, Ic(Q3) = 32.5 uA, forced beta 2.5 — still fine.
Secondary benefit: this network also dominates the post-brownout latched-off drain — see the en-pullup-scaling finding.
findings.risk: Regenerative turn-on gets slower: node capacitances here are a few pF, so 100k x ~10 pF = ~1 us versus a brownout event measured in milliseconds — no practical effect. The 100k values raise sensitivity to leakage: Q10's gate-body leakage is spec'd 100 nA max, which across R17 (unchanged at 100k) is 10 mV — fine. Do not also raise R17, and do not take R12 to 1M (see proposal). If a builder populates a hot-running board, 2N3904/2N3906 ICBO rises and the off-state margin at Q1-C shrinks; 470k is the safe upper bound for R12.
findings.verify_reason:
Topology re-traced from the fork netlist, not taken on trust. Net-(Q1-C) = {Q1.3 C, Q10.4 D2, R12.2, R15.2}; Net-(Q10A-G) = {Q3.3 C, Q10.1 G1, R16.1, R17.1}; Net-(Q1-B) = {Q1.1 B, R16.2}; Net-(Q3-B) = {Q3.1 B, R15.1}; /EN = {Q10.3 G2, Q10.5 S1, R11.2, R24.1, U3.1 RESET, U5.12 ~SHDN2}; SW = {Q3.2 E, R3.1, R11.1, R12.1, R58.1, SW1.2/3}. With the NDC7002N pin map (1=G1,2=S2,3=G2,4=D2,5=S1,6=D1), Q10B is G=/EN, S=GND, D=Q1-C, so with /EN high in RUN it is on and holds Q1-C low; that pulls Q3's base down through R15, Q3 pulls Q10A-G up to ~SW, and R16 turns Q1 on. The state IS statically biased, exactly as claimed — this is not a dormant network.

I redid the arithmetic at VBATT = 2.4 V and got the same answers: Ib(Q3) = (2.4-0.65-0.05)/10k = 170.0 uA; I(R17) = 2.35/100k = 23.5 uA; I(R16) = 1.70/10k = 170.0 uA; Ic(Q3) = 193.5 uA; Ie(Q3) = 363.5 uA; I(R12) = 23.5 uA; total from SW = 387.0 uA = 0.929 mW. With R15 = R16 = 100k: 17.0 + 23.5 + 17.0 -> Ic 40.5, Ie 57.5, plus R12 23.5 = 81.0 uA = 0.194 mW. Saving 306 uA = 0.734 mW, 0.43% of the 170 mW idle. Forced betas of 2.4 are far inside spec.

Datasheet checks. onsemi 2n3904-d Rev: hFE min 40 at IC = 0.1 mA, VCE = 1.0 V; VBE(sat) 0.65-0.85 V at IC = 10 mA; ICEX 50 nA max. onsemi 2n3906-d: hFE min 60 at IC = 0.1 mA, VCE = 1.0 V; VCE(sat) 0.25 V max at IC = 10 mA. Both numbers as claimed. NDC7002N IGSS 100 nA max at VGS = 20 V, IDSS 1 uA max at VDS = 40 V / 500 uA at TJ = 125 C — the finding's leakage caveats are right, and 'do not take R12 to 1M' is sound.

Two corrections. (1) SOURCING: both cited datasheets are for the TO-92 parts (2N3904 = TO-92 CASE 135AN/135AR; 2N3906 = TO-92 CASE 29 STYLE 1). The board's Q1/Q3 footprint is SOT-23, so the parts actually fitted are MMBT3904/MMBT3906 and the cited datasheets do not cover them. The die specs are equivalent so the conclusion survives, but the BOM values '2N3904'/'2N3906' against SOT-23 footprints are themselves a BOM inaccuracy worth flagging alongside the F1/PTC1/R3/R4/R64 mismatches. (2) VBE(sat) = 0.65 V is spec'd at IC = 10 mA; at the 17-170 uA operating here VBE is nearer 0.55-0.60 V, which raises every computed current by ~3-4%. The 0.734 mW saving is therefore slightly conservative, not optimistic. Drop-in on existing 0603 pads: confirmed, R15 and R16 are both R_0603_1608Metric_Boxed.

findings.title: R65 100k holds the MIC1553's CS pin down through Q5B and dissipates 250 uW at VOUT5 continuously for no reason; 1M does the same job
findings.current_part: R65 = 100k 0603 from VOUT5 to the Q5B drain node, which is also U14 pin 3 (CS). U14 = MIC1553, an IttyBitty CMOS RC 555-type astable oscillator in SOT-23-5; CS is 'Chip Select/Reset (Input): Active-high at >2/3 VS. Output off when low at <1/3 VS', and the part's inputs are described as 'Zero Leakage Trigger and Threshold Inputs' (https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/TCG/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/MIC1551-53-IttyBitty-RC-Type-555-Timer-Oscillator-DS20006985.pdf). In the normal (battery-OK) state U17's open-drain RESET is released, R66 100k pulls Q5B's gate to VOUT5, Q5B is on, and CS is held at ~0 V — so all of R65's current flows to ground through Q5B.
findings.proposal: Change R65 from 100k to 1M (same 0603 pad). No other change.
findings.benefit: Current through R65 today = 5.00 V / 100k = 50.0 uA, dissipating 5.00 x 50.0 uA = 250 uW at VOUT5, continuously, in the normal battery state. With R65 = 1M: 5.0 uA / 25 uW. Saving 225 uW at VOUT5 = 281 uW at the battery at 80% boost efficiency. The only requirement on R65 is that when U17 trips (battery below ~2.10 V) and Q5B turns off, R65 must pull CS above 2/3 VS = 3.33 V; with 1M and the MIC1553's spec'd zero-leakage input, even 100 nA of leakage would only cost 0.1 V.
findings.risk: 1M is a high-impedance node next to a 5 V rail on a hand-assembled board; flux residue or a fingerprint of a few hundred kohm across it would drag the CS-high level down and disable the low-battery blink. Clean the board. The MIC1553's CS leakage is described qualitatively ('zero leakage') rather than given a numeric max in the electrical table I read, so the 1M choice is bounded by that qualitative claim — 470k would be a more conservative compromise (10.6 uA, saving 197 uW at VOUT5).
findings.verify_reason:
Netlist verified: Net-(Q5B-D) = {Q5.4 D2, R65.2, U14.3 CS}; Net-(Q5B-G) = {Q5.3 G2, R66.2, U17.1 RESET}; R65 and R66 are 100k 0603 from VOUT5. In the battery-OK state U17's open-drain RESET is released, R66 holds Q5B's gate at 5.01 V, Q5B is on, CS sits at ~0 V and all of R65's current goes to ground. Arithmetic: 5.014/100k = 50.1 uA = 251 uW at VOUT5; with 1M, 5.0 uA / 25 uW; saving 226 uW at the rail. Battery conversion should use the datasheet-verified boost efficiency of ~84% (LTC3527 35271fc Figure G07, VOUT1 = 5 V, VIN = 2.4 V, Burst, 1-3 mA), not 80%: 226/0.84 = 269 uW, not 281 uW. Either way this is 0.16% of the 170 mW idle — genuinely rounding error, and the finding does not inflate it.

One correction from the Microchip datasheet I fetched (DS20006985A). The CS threshold is NOT a clean '2/3 VS'. The Electrical Characteristics 'Chip Select' row gives On at 50 min / 67 typ / 72 max %/VS and Off at 28 / 33 / 50 %/VS. So the guaranteed-on level is 0.72 x 5.014 = 3.61 V, not the 3.33 V the finding uses. With 1M and a bounded leakage this is still met with ~1.4 V of margin, so the conclusion holds — but the finding's stated requirement is the typical, not the guaranteed, threshold.

On leakage: the only numeric input-current spec in the table is 'Trigger and Threshold Current, max 50 nA at VS = 15 V' — it covers T/T, not CS, so the finding's caveat that the 1M choice rests on a qualitative claim is correct and correctly stated. Note that even 1 uA of CS leakage would only drop 1 V across 1M, leaving 4.0 V, still above the 3.61 V worst-case On threshold, so 1M has more headroom than the finding gives it credit for. The datasheet also says explicitly 'If unused, the CS input must be pulled up', confirming R65's role. Drop-in on the existing 0603 pad: confirmed.

findings.title: U10 and U17 sense the battery through low-value dividers that burn 86-241 uA; scaling both by 10x costs nothing and improves their transient filtering
findings.current_part: U10 and U17 are TPS3840DL20 (SOT-23-5 DBV): supply current 300 nA typical / 700 nA maximum, VDD operating range 1.5 V to 10 V, fixed threshold accuracy 1% typ / 1.5% max, hysteresis 100 mV typ for VIT- <= 3.0 V, and — important — the family offers fixed thresholds from 1.6 V to 4.9 V in 0.1 V steps (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3840.pdf). U10 senses SW through R3/R4 and U17 through R58/R63. NOTE the schematic and the PCB disagree on R3/R4 (see the bom-pcb-value-mismatch finding): schematic 5.1k/33k (divider ratio 0.8661, trip at SW = 2.31 V), PCB 1k/10k (ratio 0.9091, trip at SW = 2.20 V). R58/R63 = 5.1k/100k in both (ratio 0.9515, trip at SW = 2.10 V).
findings.proposal: Scale each divider up 10x, keeping the ratio exactly: R3 5.1k -> 51k with R4 33k -> 330k (ratio 330/381 = 0.8661, identical); R58 5.1k -> 51k with R63 100k -> 1M (ratio 1000/1051 = 0.9515, identical). All four are existing 0603 pads. If the built board carries the PCB values instead, R3 1k -> 10k and R4 10k -> 100k. Do NOT delete the dividers in favour of a direct-connect TPS3840DL23/DL21: the thresholds exist in the catalogue but TI's datasheet says non-standard voltages are 'sample upon request', and you would lose the RC filtering C10/C12 provide.
findings.benefit:
At VBATT = 2.4 V, with the schematic values: R3+R4 = 38.1k draws 63.0 uA = 151 uW; R58+R63 = 105.1k draws 22.8 uA = 55 uW. Total 85.8 uA = 206 uW straight off the battery. After 10x scaling: 6.3 uA + 2.3 uA = 8.6 uA = 21 uW. Saving 77.2 uA = 185 uW.
If the built board carries the PCB values, R3+R4 = 11k draws 218.2 uA = 524 uW and scaling to 10k/100k saves 196 uA = 471 uW; combined with R58/R63 the saving is 217 uA = 520 uW.
Bonus, not a cost: the RC corner improves. R58 x C12 (10 uF) goes from 51 ms to 510 ms and R3 x C10 (0.1 uF) from 0.51 ms to 5.1 ms, so both battery-gauge supervisors become an order of magnitude less likely to nuisance-trip on a speaker or backlight load transient.
Threshold error introduced: the supervisor's own IVDD flows through the top resistor. At 51k that is 300 nA x 51k = 15 mV typical (36 mV at the 700 nA max), which referred back to SW through the 0.8661 divider is 18 mV typical / 41 mV max — 0.75% typ / 1.8% max on a 2.31 V trip point. For a two-stage battery indicator that is irrelevant; if it were a safety trip it would not be.
findings.risk: The trip point shifts up by the 18-41 mV computed above, so the green-to-red changeover happens a fraction earlier. 1M and 330k nodes are leakage-sensitive on a hand-soldered board (same cleanliness caveat as R65). If you use 1% parts the ratio is preserved exactly; using 5% parts for R4/R63 would shift the trip point by up to 5%, which is worse than the Iq error you are trying to keep small — specify 1%.
findings.verify_reason:
Every TPS3840 number checked verbatim against the datasheet I fetched (SNVSB03E, rev May 2026): 'Wide operating voltage: 1.5V to 10V'; 'Nano supply current: 300nA (typical), 700nA (maximum)'; 'Threshold from 1.6V to 4.9V in 0.1V steps'; 'High accuracy: 1% (typical), 1.5% (maximum)'; VHYS 100 mV typ for VIT- = 1.6 V to 3.0 V; tSTRT 220 us typ / 350 us max; SOT23-5 (DBV). The 'sample upon request' caution is real — page 3 says 'Other voltages from Table 9-2 at the end of datasheet can be sample upon request'. All correct.

Netlist verified: Net-(U10-VDD) = {C10 0.1u, R3, R4, U10.2 VDD}; Net-(U17-VDD) = {C12 10u, R58, R63, U17.2 VDD}. Arithmetic redone: at 2.4 V, 2.4/38.1k = 63.0 uA = 151 uW and 2.4/105.1k = 22.8 uA = 55 uW, total 85.8 uA = 206 uW, going to 8.6 uA = 21 uW after 10x — saving 185 uW. Correct. PCB-value case: 2.4/11k = 218.2 uA = 524 uW, saving 471 uW; combined 520 uW. Correct. The IVDD-through-the-top-resistor error term is right: 700 nA x 51k = 36 mV, /0.8661 = 41 mV referred to SW. All four parts are R_0603_1608Metric_Boxed — drop-in confirmed.

What I would change. (1) The 'bonus, not a cost' framing on the RC is overstated. R58 x C12 = 51k x 10 uF gives tau = 510 ms, and U17's VDD must climb to VIT+ = 2.1 V from a 0.9515 x SW asymptote. At VBATT = 2.4 V that is 2.52 tau = 1.29 s versus 0.13 s today; at 3.0 V it is 0.68 s versus 68 ms. Through that whole window U17 holds RESET low, Q5B is off, R65 pulls CS high and the MIC1553 runs at 255 uA typ from VOUT5 at every power-on. I checked whether this is visible: it is not, because DL2's cathode is gated by Q9B whose gate is /D1A, which U10 (tau only 5.1 ms with C10 = 0.1 uF) pulls low within ~10 ms. So the cost is ~1.3 mW for ~0.6-1.2 s per power cycle, under 1 mJ — negligible, but it is a cost, not a bonus, and if the pack is already in the steady-red band the red LED will now blink for an extra ~1 s at switch-on. If that bothers you, drop C12 from 10 uF to 1 uF on the same 0603 pad when you raise R58. (2) Worth stating explicitly: with the schematic's 5.1k/33k, U10's VDD at VBATT = 2.4 V is 2.079 V, which is BELOW VIT+ = VIT- + VHYS = 2.1 V. So the 2.4 V operating point used as the reference throughout this whole review is already inside the 'red LED' band on a board built to the schematic. Worth knowing before quoting 2.4 V as 'normal'. (3) The saving is 0.185 mW only if the board is built to the schematic; if it carries the PCB's 1k/10k the number is 0.52 mW — a 2.8x difference that the bom-pcb-value-mismatch finding has to be resolved before this one can be sized.

findings.title: R11 = 1k makes the post-brownout latched-off state draw 2.87 mA (6.9 mW) forever until the switch is cycled; 10k plus the other changes cuts it to 0.33 mA
findings.current_part: R11 = 1k from SW to /EN, R24 = 100k from /EN to GND. /EN drives U5 pin 12 (~SHDN2), Q10 pin 3 (G2) and Q10 pin 5 (S1), and is pulled down by U3's open-drain RESET output. U3 = TPS3840DL20, open-drain active-low output requiring an external pull-up, IVDD 300 nA typ / 700 nA max (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3840.pdf). When VFILT falls below 2.0 V, U3 asserts RESET, /EN goes low, Q10A (G = Q10A-G held at ~SW by Q3, S = /EN now at 0) turns on and pulls ~MR low, which latches U3 asserted. The board then sits in that state indefinitely with SW1 still closed.
findings.proposal: Change R11 from 1k to 10k and R24 from 100k to 1M (existing 0603 pads, ratio preserved so the /EN high level is unchanged at 0.990 x SW).
findings.benefit:
Run-state saving is small: 2.4 V / 101k = 23.76 uA today versus 2.4 V / 1.01M = 2.38 uA, i.e. 21.4 uA = 51 uW.
The real number is the latched-off state. Today: R11 sinks 2.4 V / 1k = 2.40 mA into U3's open drain, plus the latch bias 387 uA (Q3 stays on — the latch holds through Q1/Q3/R16, it does not need Q10B), plus R12 23.5 uA, plus the two supervisor dividers 85.8 uA = 2.873 mA = 6.89 mW, drawn continuously from an already-flat pack until the user notices and moves SW1. With R11 = 10k plus the R15/R16 and divider changes above: 240 uA + 57.5 uA + 23.5 uA + 8.6 uA = 330 uA = 0.79 mW — an 8.7x reduction.
10k is still a strong pull-up here: the only DC loads on /EN are the LTC3527 ~SHDN2 input, Q10 pin 3's gate (100 nA max gate-body leakage per the NDC7002N datasheet -> 1 mV across 10k) and R24; and U3's open drain sinks 240 uA trivially.
findings.risk: The /EN rise time on power-up goes from ~20 ns to ~200 ns against a few tens of pF — irrelevant against the TPS3840's 220 us typical / 350 us maximum start-up delay. I could not fetch the LTC3527 datasheet, so I have NOT verified its ~SHDN2 input leakage or VIH; if that pin had, say, 1 uA of input leakage, a 10k pull-up would still only drop 10 mV, so the conclusion is robust, but the 1M R24 assumes the pin's leakage is well under a microamp. Verify against the LTC3527 datasheet before committing R24 = 1M; R11 = 10k with R24 left at 100k is the risk-free half of the change (/EN = 0.909 x SW, still far above any plausible VIH) and captures most of the latched-off benefit.
findings.verify_reason:
I fetched the LTC3527 datasheet the finding could not, and it closes the open question in the finding's favour. Analog Devices 35271fc, Electrical Characteristics p.3: 'SHDN1,2 Input High Voltage 0.88 V'; 'SHDN1,2 Input Low Voltage 0.35 V'; 'SHDN1,2 Input Current, VSHDN1,2 = 3.3V: 1 typ / 2 max uA'. So R24 = 1M is safe: with R11 = 10k / R24 = 1M at SW = 2.4 V, the open-circuit level is 2.376 V and the 2.1 uA of DC load (2 uA SHDN2 max + 100 nA Q10 gate) across the 9.90k Thevenin source drops only 21 mV, giving /EN = 2.355 V — 2.7x above the 0.88 V VIH. The finding's hedge was unnecessary; the conclusion is stronger than it claimed.

Netlist verified: /EN = {Q10.3 G2, Q10.5 S1, R11.2, R24.1, U3.1 RESET, U5.12 ~SHDN2}. Arithmetic redone. Run state: 2.4/101k = 23.76 uA -> 2.4/1.01M = 2.38 uA, saving 21.4 uA = 51 uW. Correct, and correctly labelled as small. Latched-off state: 2.4 mA through R11 into U3's open drain + 387 uA latch (which already contains R12's 23.5 uA) + 85.8 uA dividers = 2.873 mA = 6.89 mW. The printed total is right, but the itemisation double-lists R12 (2400 + 387 + 23.5 + 85.8 = 2896 uA, not 2873) — cosmetic. After the changes: 240 + 57.5 + 23.5 + 8.6 = 330 uA = 0.79 mW. 8.7x reduction confirmed.

Two supports the finding missed that make its case stronger. (a) TPS3840DL's VOL is specified 200 mV max at IOUT(sink) = 2 mA, and its Recommended Operating Conditions cap IRESET at 5 mA. With R11 = 1k the latched /EN low level is produced at 2.4-3.2 mA of sink — at or past the spec'd test point, and against U5's SHDN VIL of 0.35 V max that leaves only ~150 mV of margin. R11 = 10k drops it to 240-320 uA and restores the margin, so this is a stability improvement, not only an energy one. (b) Cross-finding caution: the 'risk-free half' (R11 = 10k, R24 left at 100k) moves /EN from 0.990 x SW to 0.909 x SW, which puts +168 mV of static VGS on Q10A instead of -26 mV. Harmless with NDC7002N (VGS(th) 1.0 V min) and still harmless with the 0.65 V-min FDC6301N proposed in the q10a finding — subthreshold current there is nA against the TPS3840's 100 kohm MR pull-up — but if you take both changes, take the R24 = 1M version so the ratio is preserved. All parts are R_0603_1608Metric_Boxed; drop-in confirmed.

findings.title: R3, R4 and R64 have different values in the schematic and in the PCB file — the low-battery trip point and the blink rate depend on which one you build
findings.current_part: Extracted directly from the KiCad files in this repo. Schematic (agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch): R3 = 5.1k, R4 = 33k, R64 = 200k. PCB (both agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb and the fork x/agbm-01-ram-desalvage/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb): R3 = 1k, R4 = 10k, R64 = 100k. This is the same class of defect as the already-known F1/PTC1 disagreement (schematic F0805B2R00FSTR / 0805L075SLYR versus PCB Value '0467001.NR' on both).
findings.proposal: Reconcile the two. The schematic is normally the source of truth in KiCad and the PCB Value fields look stale (they were never re-synced after a schematic value change), so I would take 5.1k/33k/200k as intended — but that is an inference, not something the files prove. Whichever you pick, run 'Update PCB from Schematic' with value updating enabled so the two agree, and correct the F1/PTC1 Value fields at the same time.
findings.benefit: Not an efficiency finding, but the numbers matter. R3/R4 sets U10's low-battery trip: 5.1k/33k gives a divider ratio of 33/38.1 = 0.8661, so the TPS3840DL20's 2.0 V threshold corresponds to VBATT = 2.31 V; 1k/10k gives 10/11 = 0.9091 and VBATT = 2.20 V. That is a 110 mV difference in where the power LED changes from green to red. The standing current differs too: 2.4/38.1k = 63.0 uA (151 uW) versus 2.4/11k = 218.2 uA (524 uW) — a 3.5x difference in a permanently-on battery load, which is why this matters to the efficiency inventory as well as to correctness. R64 with C44 1 uF sets the MIC1553 astable rate; for a 50% one-resistor-one-capacitor astable f ~ 1/(1.386 x R x C), giving 3.6 Hz at 200k and 7.2 Hz at 100k — the low-battery LED blinks at twice the rate depending on which value is fitted.
findings.risk: Nothing breaks either way — both value sets produce a working board. The risk is purely that a builder reading the PCB (or a fab reading a PCB-derived BOM) gets a different battery-warning threshold and blink rate from someone reading the schematic, and neither can tell they disagree. Cost to fix: zero.
findings.verify_reason:
I did not take this on trust — I parsed all 235 refdes out of agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch plus CPU/Audio/Display sub-sheets and out of agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb, and diffed the Value properties. Exactly six disagree, on both the stock PCB and the fork's AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb: F1 (sch F0805B2R00FSTR / pcb 0467001.NR), PTC1 (sch 0805L075SLYR / pcb 0467001.NR), R3 (5.1k / 1k), R4 (33k / 10k), R64 (200k / 100k), and TP22 (BATT / VAUD). The five the finding names are exactly right; the sixth it missed.

Electrical consequences re-derived. Divider ratios: 33/38.1 = 0.8661 -> TPS3840DL20 trip at SW = 2.309 V; 10/11 = 0.9091 -> 2.200 V. 109 mV apart, as claimed. Standing current 63.0 uA (151 uW) versus 218.2 uA (524 uW), a 3.46x difference. Correct.

Blink rate: I checked the astable formula against the MIC1553 datasheet rather than assuming. The datasheet's own Astable Timing Accuracy spec is 1717-2323 us for RA = RB = 10k, C = 0.1 uF, VS = 5V, which brackets the classic 555 result 0.693(RA+2RB)C = 2079 us — confirming real 1/3 and 2/3 comparators on the T/T pin, hence T = 2 RC ln2 = 1.386 RC for the single-resistor 50% configuration used here (R64 from OUT back to T/T, C44 1 uF to GND, verified from netmap: Net-(U14-T/T) = {C44.1, R64.2, U14.1}). f = 3.61 Hz at 200k and 7.22 Hz at 100k. Correct.

The proposal (reconcile, run Update PCB from Schematic with value updating, fix F1/PTC1) is right, but note that TP22 argues the PCB Values are not uniformly stale — at least one of the six is the PCB being right and the schematic being wrong. Whoever reconciles should check each of the six individually rather than bulk-pushing the schematic.
findings.correction: Six mismatches, not five: the finding missed TP22 (schematic Value 'BATT', PCB Value 'VAUD'). TP22 sits on the VAUD net, so the PCB label is the correct one and the schematic's 'BATT' is the misleading half — the opposite direction of trust from R3/R4/R64, which weakens the finding's 'the schematic is normally the source of truth' inference.

findings.title: Q10A must latch the brownout with only VBATT as its gate drive, but the NDC7002N's threshold is spec'd up to 2.5 V — a worst-case part will not latch
findings.current_part: NDC7002N dual N-channel, SuperSOT-6 / TSOT-23-6 (CASE 419BL): VGS(th) 1.0 V min / 1.9 V typ / 2.5 V max at VDS = VGS, ID = 250 uA; RDS(on) 1.7 ohm typ / 2 ohm max at VGS = 10 V, and 1.6 ohm typ / 4 ohm max at VGS = 4.5 V — there is NO on-resistance specification below VGS = 4.5 V (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/ndc7002n-d.pdf). Pin assignment 1=G1, 2=S2, 3=G2, 4=D2, 5=S1, 6=D1, confirmed against the datasheet pin-assignment graphic and the KiCad symbol name Q_Dual_NMOS_G1S2G2D2S1D1.
findings.proposal: Replace Q10 (and optionally Q2, Q5, Q7, Q9) with onsemi FDC6301N — identical SuperSOT-6 / TSOT-23-6 CASE 419BL package, and I verified the pin-assignment graphic is byte-identically placed in both datasheets (labels G1/S2/G2/D1/D2/S1 at the same page coordinates), so the pinout is the same. FDC6301N: VGS(th) 0.65 V min / 0.85 V typ / 1.5 V max; RDS(on) 3.8 ohm typ / 5 ohm max at VGS = 2.7 V and 3.1 ohm typ / 4 ohm max at VGS = 4.5 V; 25 V, 0.22 A continuous; VGSS rated -0.5 to +8 V (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/fdc6301n-d.pdf). Drop-in on the existing TSOT-23-6 land pattern.
findings.benefit:
Not a power saving — a reliability one. Q10A's job is to pull ~MR low when U3 asserts, latching the board off after a brownout. Its gate sits at Q10A-G ~ SW (held up by Q3) and its SOURCE is /EN, which is what goes to 0 V at the moment of the trip. So its turn-on VGS equals VBATT at the instant of the brownout — and the brownout happens when VFILT falls below the TPS3840DL20's 2.0 V threshold, i.e. VBATT ~ 2.0-2.1 V. Against a spec'd VGS(th) max of 2.5 V, a worst-case NDC7002N never turns on there and the latch never fires: U3 releases RESET as soon as the battery recovers, the LTC3527 restarts, the load pulls the pack down again, and the console can chatter on/off instead of staying down. With FDC6301N (1.5 V max threshold) there is at least 0.5 V of overdrive at the worst-case operating point.
Secondary: Q2 and Q7 are driven from U16's outputs on the 3.34 V VDD3 rail, so their VGS is 3.34 V — also inside the NDC7002N's 2.5 V max threshold band with only 0.84 V of overdrive, and in a region where the datasheet gives no RDS(on) number at all. Those FETs only pull logic lines, so a high on-resistance is tolerable, but they are equally unspecified.
findings.risk: FDC6301N is a much smaller die: 25 V / 0.22 A continuous versus 50 V / 0.51 A, and its gate rating is -0.5 to +8 V rather than +/-20 V. Every use on this board is at or below 5.0 V and at or below ~1 mA (the largest is Q9A carrying the 0.93 mA LED current, where 5 ohm gives a 5 mV drop), so both derations are irrelevant here — but if you reuse the same part elsewhere check that. Its higher RDS(on) (5 ohm max at 2.7 V versus NDC7002N's 2 ohm at 10 V) is a non-issue for the same reason. I have NOT observed the chatter failure mode on hardware; this is a datasheet-margin argument, so treat it as 'the spec does not guarantee it works', not 'it is broken'. Typical parts (1.9 V) do latch at 2.0-2.4 V.
findings.verify_reason:
All specs verified verbatim from the onsemi PDFs I fetched. NDC7002N (Rev 2, Dec 2021, no NRND note): TSOT23 6-Lead CASE 419BL, SUPERSOT-6; VGS(th) 1.0 / 1.9 / 2.5 V at VGS = VDS, ID = 250 uA (0.8 / 1.5 / 2.2 at TJ = 125 C); RDS(on) 1.7 typ / 2 max ohm at VGS = 10 V, ID = 0.51 A and 1.6 typ / 4 max ohm at VGS = 4.5 V, ID = 0.35 A — there is indeed NO spec below 4.5 V; VGSS 20 V; ID 0.51 A; VDS 50 V. FDC6301N (Rev 5, May 2023): same TSOT23 6-Lead SUPERSOT-6 CASE 419BL; VGS(th) 0.65 / 0.85 / 1.5 V at VDS = VGS, ID = 250 uA; RDS(on) 3.8 typ / 5 max ohm at VGS = 2.7 V, ID = 0.2 A and 3.1 typ / 4 max ohm at VGS = 4.5 V, ID = 0.4 A; VDSS 25 V; ID 0.22 A cont / 0.5 A pulsed; VGSS -0.5 to +8 V; IGSS 100 nA max; IDSS 1 uA max. Every number the finding quotes is correct. Production status independently checked: onsemi lists it Active and DigiKey shows 37,403 in stock, TSOT-23-6 / SuperSOT-6.

I verified the pinout claim independently rather than trusting it. Extracting the text spans from page 1 of both PDFs, the labels G1/S2/G2/D2/S1/D1 sit at byte-identical coordinates (D2 at 445.1,75.8; S1 at 434.4,82.2; D1 at 423.9,89.2; G2 at 477.5,110.3; S2 at 467.7,116.7; G1 at 457.7,121.8) in both documents, and the pin numbers are in the same relative arrangement. Pinout is 1=G1, 2=S2, 3=G2, 4=D2, 5=S1, 6=D1 in both, matching the KiCad symbol Q_Dual_NMOS_G1S2G2D2S1D1 and making the board netlist self-consistent. Drop-in on the existing TSOT-23-6 land pattern: confirmed.

The argument is stronger than the finding makes it, because it can be made quantitative and was not. The TPS3840 datasheet's Electrical Characteristics gives 'R MR, Manual reset internal pull-up resistance, 100 kOhm' and 'V MR_L, Manual reset logic low input, 600 mV' max. So to latch, Q10A must sink (2.0 - 0.6)/100k = 14 uA while holding ~MR under 600 mV — i.e. present under 43 kOhm. A worst-case 2.5 V-VGS(th) NDC7002N driven at VGS ~ 2.03 V is 0.47 V below its own 250 uA threshold point; at a 100-200 mV/decade subthreshold slope that is 5 nA to 1.1 uA, i.e. 13x to 3000x short of the 14 uA required. The latch demonstrably does not fire on the datasheet limits.

And it is worse than stated: /VFILT is a peak-hold of VBATT, because D2 (A = VBATT, K = /VFILT) blocks on the way down and R9 100k x C1 22 uF gives a 2.2 s decay. Q10A's gate drive is instantaneous SW, not VFILT, so at the moment VFILT crosses 2.0 V the instantaneous SW under load can be several hundred mV lower than the 2.0-2.1 V the finding assumes. Every FDC6301N use on this board stays inside -0.5/+8 V VGSS and 25 V VDS (worst gate is Q9A at VOUT5 = 5.014 V via R18; worst drain 5.014 V), so the derations really are irrelevant here. The one thing I will not certify is that the chatter has ever been observed — as the finding itself says, this is a datasheet-limit argument and a typical 1.9 V part latches fine.

findings.title: The three TPS22917 load switches cost 13-230 uW of conduction loss and 0.5 uA each — including the one carrying the ClockxControl — so no lower-Rds part is worth the swap
findings.current_part: TPS22917DBV, TSOT-23-6 (SOT-23 6-pin DBV), 1 V to 5.5 V, 2 A max continuous. On-resistance at IOUT = 200 mA: 80 mohm typ / 100 mohm max at VIN = 5 V (25 C), 90 mohm typ / 110 mohm max at VIN = 3.6 V (25 C, rising to 140 mohm max at 85 C), 120 mohm typ at 1.8 V. Quiescent current in the ON state 0.5 uA typ / 1.0 uA max (-40 to +85 C); shutdown 10 nA typ. ON pin VIH 1.0 V min, VIL 0.35 V max; ON-pin leakage +/-10 nA when enabled, with a 750 kohm smart pulldown only while VON <= VIL (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps22917.pdf).
findings.proposal: Leave all three as-is. I deliberately do not name a lower-Rds alternative, because the loss is not material and I would have to assert unverified numbers to do so.
findings.benefit:
U18 carries the whole VDD3 rail including the ClockxControl's 12 mA (the module's V+ lands on P1 pad S1 = VDD3, confirmed from the netlist). At VIN = VOUT3 = 3.34 V, RDS(on) is ~92 mohm typ (interpolating the 3.6 V figure). I2R at the plausible load range: 12 mA -> 1.10 mV drop, 13 uW; 30 mA -> 2.76 mV, 83 uW; 50 mA -> 4.60 mV, 230 uW; even 100 mA -> 9.2 mV, 920 uW. So replacing U18 with a perfect 0 mohm short would save at most ~0.1-0.2 mW at a realistic VDD3 load, against a 170 mW idle and a 40 mW ClockxControl overhead — rounding error.
U11 carries VDD5 to the screen (FFC pin 34 VSHA) and cart pad S2, at VIN = 5.0 V and RDS(on) 80 mohm typ: 20 mA -> 1.60 mV, 32 uW; 50 mA -> 4.00 mV, 200 uW; 100 mA -> 8.00 mV, 800 uW. Even bounding VDD5 at 100 mA (which would be 500 mW at 5 V — more than a third of the console's 1175 mW maximum), the switch loss is under 1 mW.
Quiescent side: 3 x 0.5 uA typ. U11 and U14's 5 V rail contribution is 2.5 uW; U12 and U18 on 3.34 V contribute 1.7 uW each. Total across all three: about 6 uW. Nothing.
The enable logic is also correct and worth confirming for the ClockxControl: U18's ON pin is /PG_2V5, which is U8's (the VDD2 LDO's) open-drain PGOOD pulled up by R8 100k to VDD2 = 2.5 V. TPS22917 VIH is 1.0 V min, so 2.5 V is comfortable, and the 750 kohm smart pulldown disconnects once VON exceeds VIH (2.5 x 750/850 = 2.21 V at the crossover, well above 1.0 V). Net effect: the ClockxControl only receives power after the CPU core rail VDD2 is good — correct sequencing for a module that drives the CPU's XIN.
findings.risk: None — this is a recommendation to change nothing. The one caveat is that I could not measure VDD3 or VDD5 current, so the loss figures are a bounded range rather than a single number; but even the top of the range (100 mA) does not make either switch worth replacing.
findings.verify_reason:
I fetched TI SLVSDW8B and checked every number. Package TSOT-23/SOT-23 6-pin DBV; VIN 1 to 5.5 V; IMAX 2 A. IQ,VIN enabled 0.5 typ / 1.0 max uA (-40 to +85 C), 1.2 uA to +125 C. ISD,VIN 10 nA typ / 100 nA max. RON at IOUT = 200 mA: VIN = 5 V, 80 typ / 100 max mOhm at 25 C rising to 140 max at 125 C; VIN = 3.6 V, 90 typ / 110 max at 25 C, 140 max at 85 C; features bullet gives 120 mOhm typ at 1.8 VIN. ON pin: Recommended Operating Conditions VIH 1 V min, VIL 0.35 V max; ION leakage +/-10 nA enabled; RPD 'Smart Pull Down Resistance, VON <= VIL, 750 kOhm typ' with Table 9-1 showing the pulldown Disconnected for VON >= VIH. Every figure the finding states is correct.

Arithmetic redone. Interpolating RON linearly between 90 mOhm at 3.6 V and 120 mOhm at 1.8 V gives 94 mOhm at VOUT3 = 3.336 V, not the finding's 92 — which moves the 12 mA loss from 13 uW to 13.5 uW. At 30 mA, 85 uW; at 50 mA, 235 uW; at 100 mA, 940 uW. U11 at 80 mOhm and 5.014 V: 32 uW at 20 mA, 200 uW at 50 mA, 800 uW at 100 mA. All within a few percent of the finding, and all far below anything worth a respin. Quiescent: 0.5 uA x 5.014 = 2.5 uW for U11, 0.5 uA x 3.336 = 1.67 uW each for U12 and U18, ~5.9 uW total. Correct.

Sequencing verified from the netlist: /PG_2V5 = {R8.2, TP30, U4.3 ~SHDN, U5.1 ~SHDN1, U8.4 PGOOD, U18.3 ON}; VDD3 = U18's output and carries P1 pad S1 where the ClockxControl's V+ lands. The finding's smart-pulldown crossover arithmetic (2.5 x 750/850 = 2.21 V) is right, but incomplete: /PG_2V5 also drives LTC3527 SHDN1, which draws 1 uA typ / 2 uA max (35271fc). Including that, the node sits at (2.5/100k - 2 uA)/(1/100k + 1/750k) = 2.03 V — still comfortably above VIH = 1 V, so the conclusion is unaffected. Two cosmetic slips: 'U11 and U14's 5 V rail contribution' names U14 (the MIC1553, not a load switch), and the RON figure is 94 not 92 mOhm. The recommendation to change nothing is correct and carries no risk.

findings.title: None of the three TPS3840 supervisors is redundant — they have three different trip points and three different jobs — but the entire low-battery-blink branch is optional and worth 0.36 mW plus 12 parts
findings.current_part: All three are TPS3840DL20: open-drain active-low RESET, 2.0 V fixed threshold, 300 nA typ / 700 nA max IVDD, 100 mV typ hysteresis, 220 us typ / 350 us max start-up delay, SOT-23-5 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3840.pdf). Reading the schematic: U3's VDD is /VFILT (VBATT through D2, bypassed for DC by R9 100k, held up by C1 22u) and its RESET drives /EN (LTC3527 ~SHDN2) with the Q1/Q3/Q10 latch on ~MR — that is the power-fail shutdown and latch. U10's VDD is SW divided by R3/R4 (0.8661 -> trips at VBATT 2.31 V with the schematic values) and its RESET gates Q9A, which switches the power LED from green DL1 to red DL2. U17's VDD is SW divided by R58/R63 (0.9515 -> trips at VBATT 2.10 V) and its RESET gates Q5B, which releases the MIC1553's CS and starts the red LED blinking. Three thresholds, three functions.
findings.proposal: Keep all three if you want the two-stage battery gauge. If you do not, the second stage is cleanly severable: depopulate U17, R58, R63, C12, R65, R66, U14, C44, R64, Q5, R10 and DL2 (12 parts) and the board keeps its brownout latch and its green/red changeover. No PCB change needed — it is purely a DNP list.
findings.benefit:
Always-on cost of the second (blink) stage, at VBATT = 2.4 V: R58+R63 divider 22.8 uA = 55 uW off the battery; R65 through Q5B 50.0 uA at 5.0 V = 250 uW at VOUT5 = 313 uW at the battery at 80% boost efficiency; U17's own IVDD 300 nA = 0.7 uW; U14 in shutdown <1 uA at 5 V = <5 uW at the rail. Total about 0.37 mW, i.e. 0.22% of the 170 mW idle. Removing it entirely is worth 0.37 mW; applying the R58/R63 and R65 changes proposed elsewhere in this review instead is worth 0.33 mW while keeping the feature — so deletion buys almost nothing beyond board space and 12 fewer placements. Report as an option, not a recommendation.
I also confirmed the two indicator supervisors cannot be collapsed into one part: they need two distinct trip points (2.31 V and 2.10 V) and the TPS3840 is a fixed-threshold device, so consolidation would require a dual comparator plus a reference, which would draw more than 600 nA and use more board area.
findings.risk: Deleting the blink stage removes the only warning the user gets between 2.31 V and the hard cutoff, which on a 2xAA alkaline pack is the last chunk of usable capacity — you would go from a solid red warning to an abrupt latched shutdown with no escalation. On a board whose whole selling point is battery life, that is a real usability loss for 0.37 mW. My recommendation is to keep the feature and take the resistor changes instead.
findings.verify_reason:
The core claim survives. TPS3840DL20 is a fixed-threshold part (thresholds 1.6-4.9 V in 0.1 V steps, DL = open-drain active-low, 300 nA typ / 700 nA max IDD, 100 mV hysteresis for VIT- <= 3.0 V, 220 us / 350 us start-up, SOT23-5 DBV — all verified from SNVSB03E), and the netlist confirms three genuinely different jobs: U3's VDD is /VFILT and its RESET drives /EN with the Q1/Q3/Q10 latch on ~MR; U10's VDD is SW/0.8661 and its RESET drives Net-(Q9A-G); U17's VDD is SW/0.9515 and its RESET drives Net-(Q5B-G). Three trip points, three functions, not redundant. Correct.

The cost arithmetic checks out: R58+R63 22.8 uA = 55 uW; R65 50.1 uA at 5.014 V = 251 uW at the rail = 299 uW at the battery at the datasheet-verified 84% (the finding used 80% and got 313 uW); U17 IDD 300 nA x 2.28 V = 0.7 uW; U14 in shutdown <1 uA x 5 V = <5 uW. Total ~0.36 mW, 0.21% of idle. Honestly small and honestly reported.

What is wrong is the severability list. From netmap: /DL2A = {DL2.2 A, Q5.6 D1, R10.2} and Net-(DL2-K) = {DL2.1 K, Q9.4 D2}, with Q9's pin 3 (G2, i.e. Q9B's gate) on /D1A. So DL2 is fed steadily by R10 from VOUT5 and is switched on by Q9B, whose gate is /D1A, which U10 — the FIRST stage — controls. The MIC1553/Q5A branch does nothing but chop an already-lit red LED to make it blink. Remove DL2 and R10 and you remove the steady red warning that the finding elsewhere says it is preserving. Ten parts, not twelve.

Also worth noting the finding's shutdown claim is confirmed from the datasheet I fetched: the MIC1553's running current is 255 uA typ / 315 uA max at VS = 5 V and shutdown is '<1 uA typical', so holding CS low really does save ~1.28 mW versus leaving it enabled. That part is right.
findings.correction: The 12-part DNP list is wrong: DL2 and R10 belong to the FIRST stage, not the second, and depopulating them deletes the steady red warning entirely — contradicting the finding's own claim that the board 'keeps ... its green/red changeover' and its own risk note about 'a solid red warning'. The correct severable list is 10 parts: U17, R58, R63, C12, R65, R66, U14, C44, R64, Q5. The 0.37 mW figure is unchanged, since neither DL2 nor R10 carries any standing current in the normal state.

findings.title: U16 SN74HC02 is a defensible choice at 3.34 V and should be left alone: SN74LVC02A is a verified pin-identical drop-in but is worse on the slow button edges, and the Schmitt SN74HC7002 is NOT pin-compatible
findings.current_part:
U16 = SN74HC02PWR, quad 2-input NOR, TSSOP-14 (PW), 5.00 x 4.40 mm. Verified pinout: 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3, 2Y=4, 2A=5, 2B=6, GND=7, 3A=8, 3B=9, 3Y=10, 4A=11, 4B=12, 4Y=13, VCC=14 — which matches the KiCad 74xx:74HC02 symbol and the board netlist exactly (outputs on 1/4/10/13 driving Q2A-G, Q2B-G, Q7A-G, Q7B-G; inputs on 2/5/9/12 from TP6/TP1/TP0/TP2 and on 3/6/8/11 all tied to /CPU/LRST). Operating range 2 V to 6 V; VIH spec'd only at VCC = 2 V (1.5 V), 4.5 V (3.15 V) and 6 V (4.2 V), i.e. 0.7 x VCC, so ~2.34 V at the 3.34 V VDD3 rail; ICC 2 uA typ / 20 uA max at VCC = 6 V; input transition rise/fall time tt max 500 ns at VCC = 4.5 V (1000 ns at 2 V) (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hc02.pdf).
Function on this board, read from the CPU sheet: U15 (SN74LVC1G332, 3-input OR) ORs TP3/TP8/TP9 (Start, R, L) to produce /CPU/LRST, which goes low only when all three are pressed; U16's four NOR gates then each combine /CPU/LRST with one more button — TP6 (D-pad Up) -> Q2A -> JP1-A (reset, but JP1 is a default-open jumper so this does nothing as shipped), TP1 (B) -> Q2B -> Display ZB, TP0 (A) -> Q7A -> Display ZA, TP2 (Select) -> Q7B -> TP12 (test point only, unused). It is the L+R+Start button-combo decoder for the IPS screen's mode-toggle lines.
findings.proposal: Leave U16 as SN74HC02PWR. Recording the two swaps a reviewer would naturally reach for, and why each fails: (a) SN74LVC02APWR IS a genuine pin-for-pin drop-in — I verified its Pin Functions table gives 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3 in the PW package, identical to HC02 — with VIH fixed at 2.0 V for VCC 2.7-3.6 V and ICC 10 uA max at 25 C (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lvc02a.pdf). But its input transition-rate requirement is far tighter than HC's, so on this board it is a downgrade, not an upgrade. (b) SN74HC7002PW is the quad 2-input NOR with Schmitt-trigger inputs in the same TSSOP-14 body — but its pinout is 1A=1, 1B=2, 1Y=3, 2A=4, 2B=5, 2Y=6, GND=7, 3Y=8, 3A=9, 3B=10, 4Y=11, 4A=12, 4B=13, VCC=14 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hc7002.pdf). That is the 7400-style arrangement, not the 7402-style one; every input and output moves. Fitting it needs a PCB revision.
findings.benefit:
There is no power to be had here, and I want to be explicit about that: HC02 draws 2 uA typ / 20 uA max, which at 3.34 V is 6.7 uW typ / 67 uW max. LVC02A is 10 uA max at 25 C but 40 uA max over the -40 to +125 C range — so the swap is not even reliably a saving. The value would be purely in noise margin (VIH 2.0 V fixed versus 0.7 x VCC = 2.34 V) and speed, neither of which this circuit needs: the inputs come from button lines that idle at the full VDD3 rail through the CPU's internal pull-ups, and from U15's rail-to-rail LVC output. Benefit is 0 mW.
The one thing that WOULD be a real upgrade — Schmitt inputs, for the reason in the slow-edge finding below — is unavailable without moving pins.
findings.risk: The risk here is the trap, not the change: someone reading 'HC part on a 3.3 V rail, swap it for LVC/AUP' would make the slow-edge behaviour worse, and someone reading 'use the Schmitt version' would order SN74HC7002PW, fit it to the existing footprint, and get four gates wired output-to-output against U15's output on /CPU/LRST. I verified both pinouts from the TI datasheets specifically because that is the failure this review is supposed to catch.
findings.verify_reason:
This is the finding I most wanted to break, because a wrong pinout claim here would cost a board. It holds exactly. From TI SCLS076G (SN74HC02, rev Dec 2020), Pin Functions table for D/DB/N/NS/PW/J/W: 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3, 2Y=4, 2A=5, 2B=6, GND=7, 3A=8, 3B=9, 3Y=10, 4A=11, 4B=12, 4Y=13, VCC=14. From TI SCLS033G (SN74HC7002, rev April 2021), Pin Functions table for D/N/PW: 1A=1, 1B=2, 1Y=3, 2A=4, 2B=5, 2Y=6, GND=7, 3Y=8, 3A=9, 3B=10, 4Y=11, 4A=12, 4B=13, VCC=14. Both quoted correctly; every input and output does move, and dropping an HC7002 onto the HC02 land pattern would put U16's outputs on pins 3/6/8/11 — which the netlist shows are all tied to /CPU/LRST, driven by U15's push-pull LVC output. That is exactly the destructive mistake the finding says it is guarding against, and the guard is correct. SN74HC7002PW is TSSOP-14 5.00 x 4.40 mm, same body, which is what makes the trap plausible.

SN74LVC02A (SCAS280T, rev Dec 2024): Pin Functions for D/DB/NS/PW/RGY/BQA gives 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3, 2Y=4, 2A=5 — pin-identical to HC02, as claimed. VIH 2 V and VIL 0.8 V for VCC = 2.7 V to 3.6 V. ICC 1 typ / 10 max uA at 25 C and -40 to 85 C, 40 uA max to 125 C. All correct.

HC02 numbers verified: VCC 2-6 V; VIH 1.5 / 3.15 / 4.2 V at 2 / 4.5 / 6 V (= 0.7 x VCC, so ~2.34 V at VDD3 = 3.336 V); ICC 2 typ / 20 max uA at VCC = 6 V; tt max 1000 / 500 / 400 ns at 2 / 4.5 / 6 V. Board netlist re-dumped and matches the finding's reading exactly: outputs 1/4/10/13 -> Q2A-G, Q2B-G, Q7A-G, Q7B-G; inputs 2/5/9/12 -> TP6/TP1/TP0/TP2; inputs 3/6/8/11 all on /CPU/LRST; VCC pin 14 on VDD3. U15's pins 1/3/6 are TP3/TP8/TP9 (Start/R/L) with pin 4 = /CPU/LRST — the 3-input OR that goes low only on L+R+Start.

One sub-claim I could NOT verify: 'its input transition-rate requirement is far tighter than HC's'. The current SN74LVC02A datasheet (SCAS280T) has no delta-t/delta-v row in its Recommended Operating Conditions at all — I read the table. The sibling SN74LVC1G332 does spec 10 ns/V at 3.3 V, so the claim is plausible for the family but is not supported by the datasheet the finding cites. Mark that sentence unverified.
