It does not matter to the outcome, since the recommendation is to change nothing.

findings.title: The 0.01 uF debounce caps on Start/Select/Up/L/R violate both U15's and U16's input transition-rate specifications by orders of magnitude
findings.current_part: C77 (0.01u on TP3/Start), C78 (0.01u on TP2/Select), C62 (0.01u on TP6/Up), C63 (0.01u on TP8/R), C64 (0.01u on TP9/L), each to GND, with the pull-up supplied by the salvaged AGB CPU's internal pull-up on P0-P9. Note TP0 (A) and TP1 (B) have no such capacitor. Non-Schmitt CMOS inputs sit on those nets: U15 = SN74LVC1G332, whose Recommended Operating Conditions give an input transition rise-or-fall rate dt/dv of 10 ns/V maximum at VCC = 3.3 V +/- 0.3 V, ICC 10 uA max, and a delta-ICC of 500 uA max with one input at VCC - 0.6 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lvc1g332.pdf). U16 = SN74HC02, tt max 500 ns at VCC = 4.5 V and 1000 ns at 2 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hc02.pdf).
findings.proposal: No drop-in fix exists. If a board revision happens: move U16 to SN74HC7002PW (Schmitt NOR, same TSSOP-14 body, different pinout — see the u16-hc02-family-choice finding) and reduce C62/C63/C64/C77/C78 to the smallest value that still debounces the tactile switches, or add a Schmitt buffer ahead of U15. Until then, the correct action is to know about it, not to change parts.
findings.benefit: No power benefit — the crowbar energy is negligible (delta-ICC 500 uA x 3.34 V x ~500 us per button event is about 0.8 uJ, which is nothing). The benefit is behavioural. On button release the node is charged by the CPU's internal pull-up through 0.01 uF; GBA key pull-ups are commonly reported in the tens of kohm but I could NOT verify a value — the AGB CPU is undocumented and salvaged — so treat the RC as an estimate: 0.01 uF x ~50 kohm gives a ~500 us rise, i.e. roughly 150,000 ns/V through the threshold region against U15's 10 ns/V limit (15,000x over) and against U16's 500 ns tt limit (1,000x over). The consequence of a non-Schmitt CMOS input crossing its threshold that slowly is output chatter. Here that means /CPU/LRST can glitch, and since every U16 gate takes /CPU/LRST as one input, a glitch can produce a spurious pulse on Display ZA or ZB — an unintended IPS screen mode change. The exposure is bounded: /CPU/LRST only goes low when L+R+Start are all held, so glitching can only occur while the user is already invoking the combo, and Q2A's path to reset is disarmed anyway because JP1 ships open.
findings.risk: I have not observed this on hardware and the pull-up value is genuinely unverifiable from the available documentation, so the magnitude of the RC is an estimate — that is why this is at medium confidence. It is also possible the AGB CPU's key inputs are stronger than assumed, which would shorten the edge. What is NOT in doubt is that the specs are violated: 0.01 uF on a passively pulled-up node cannot produce a 33 ns or 500 ns edge under any plausible pull-up. Cost of doing nothing is low; cost of the fix is a PCB revision.
findings.verify_reason:
The specs are exactly as stated and I read them myself. SN74LVC1G332 (SCES489E): Recommended Operating Conditions, 'delta-t/delta-v Input transition rise or fall rate' = 20 ns/V at VCC = 1.8 V +/-0.15 and 2.5 V +/-0.2, and 10 ns/V at VCC = 3.3 V +/- 0.3 V and at 5 V +/- 0.5 V. So 10 ns/V at this board's 3.336 V rail is correct (an automated summary of the same PDF misread it as 20 ns/V; the table is unambiguous). ICC 10 uA max, delta-ICC 500 uA max with one input at VCC-0.6 V, both correct. Device is a 3-input OR. SN74HC02 tt 500 ns max at 4.5 V and 1000 ns at 2 V, correct.

Board facts re-checked from the BOM and netlist: C77 0.01u on /CPU/TP3, C78 on /CPU/TP2, C62 on /CPU/TP6, C63 on /CPU/TP8, C64 on /CPU/TP9, all to GND; C74/C75/C76 are the same value on TP4/TP5/TP7 but those do not reach U15 or U16; TP0 and TP1 genuinely have no capacitor and do drive U16 pins 9 and 5. The claim that the specs are violated is certain regardless of the pull-up value — no passive pull-up into 0.01 uF can produce a 33 ns or 500 ns edge.

Two corrections. (1) The slew figure is understated by 2x. At tau = 500 us the rate through mid-rail is (VCC - v)/tau = 1.67 V / 500 us = 3.34 mV/us, i.e. ~300,000 ns/V, so it is ~30,000x over the LVC1G332's 10 ns/V limit and ~600x over HC02's 500 ns tt, not 15,000x and 1,000x. Direction unchanged. (2) The proposed fix list is incomplete in a way worth saying out loud: shrinking C62/C63/C64/C77/C78 does nothing for U16's TP0 and TP1 inputs, which have no capacitor and therefore already present the fastest edges on the part — so if U16 is chattering it is not those two nets, which slightly narrows the diagnosis. The pull-up value on the salvaged AGB CPU's key inputs is genuinely undocumented; the finding says so, keeps the confidence low, and proposes no drop-in change. That is the right posture.

findings.title: U14 is not a USB power switch — it is a MIC1553 555-type RC oscillator blinking the low-battery LED, and it is correctly held in <1 uA shutdown during normal operation
findings.current_part: MIC1553, Microchip IttyBitty CMOS RC 555-type oscillator, SOT-23-5, astable-only with a chip-select/reset input. Verified pin functions: 1 = T/T (trigger/threshold, sets output high below 2/3 VS and low above 2/3 VS), 2 = GND, 3 = CS (Chip Select/Reset, active-high at >2/3 VS, output off when low at <1/3 VS), 4 = VS, 5 = OUT (CMOS totem-pole, <15 ohm on-resistance). Supply 2.7 V to 18 V. Supply current 255 uA typ / 315 uA max at VS = 5 V when running, and <1 uA typical in shutdown mode (https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/TCG/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/MIC1551-53-IttyBitty-RC-Type-555-Timer-Oscillator-DS20006985.pdf). Every one of those five pin functions matches the board netlist exactly (pin 1 -> C44 1u and R64 to OUT, pin 3 -> Q5B drain and R65, pin 4 -> VOUT5, pin 5 -> Q5A gate).
findings.proposal: No change. Recording it because the premise handed to this review — 'a current-limited USB power switch driving Q5A's gate' — is wrong, and because the Iq question has a good answer that is worth stating rather than assuming.
findings.benefit:
The circuit is: R64 from OUT back to T/T with C44 1 uF to ground forms the one-resistor-one-capacitor 50% astable, f ~ 1/(1.386 x R64 x C44), which is 3.6 Hz with the schematic's R64 = 200k or 7.2 Hz with the PCB's 100k. OUT drives Q5A, which shorts DL2's anode (/DL2A, fed by R10 20k from VOUT5) to ground — so the red LED blinks rather than glowing steadily once the battery is critically low.
On the Iq question: CS is active-high, and in the normal battery state U17's open-drain RESET is released, R66 100k pulls Q5B's gate to VOUT5, Q5B is on, and CS is held at 0 V — below the 1/3 VS = 1.67 V shutdown threshold. So U14 sits in shutdown drawing <1 uA typ, about 5 uW at 5 V, not the 255 uA / 1.28 mW it would draw if it were left enabled. That is a correct design decision and worth confirming rather than assuming. The only cost of the arrangement is R65's 50 uA of pulldown current, which is addressed separately in the mic1553-cs-pullup finding.
findings.risk: None. One note for whoever maintains the BOM: 'MIC1553' with no suffix is ambiguous; the orderable SOT-23-5 part is MIC1553YM5-TR, and MIC1551 (the monostable-capable sibling) is NOT interchangeable — it has TRG and THR on separate pins 4 and 5 with no CS at all, so fitting one would leave the oscillator permanently enabled at 255 uA and with the wrong pin functions entirely.
findings.verify_reason:
Verified verbatim against Microchip DS20006985A, which I fetched and text-extracted. Table 3-2, PIN FUNCTION TABLE, MIC1553: pin 1 = T/T 'Trigger/Threshold (Input): Internally connected to both threshold and trigger functions'; 2 = GND; 3 = CS 'Chip Select/Reset (Input): Active-high at >2/3VS. Output off when low at <1/3VS. If chip select functionality is not desired, CS may be connected directly to VS'; 4 = VS; 5 = OUT 'CMOS totem-pole output'. Every one matches the board netlist: U14.1 -> Net-(U14-T/T) with C44 1u and R64; U14.2 -> GND; U14.3 -> Net-(Q5B-D) with R65 and Q5's D2; U14.4 -> VOUT5; U14.5 -> Net-(Q5A-G) with R64. The premise handed to the review really was wrong, and this identification is right.

Supply current confirmed: 'MIC1553, VS = 5V: 255 typ / 315 max uA', and the features list gives '<1 uA Typical Shutdown Mode (MIC1553)'; 2.7 to 18 V; SOT-23-5; '<15 Ohm Output On-Resistance'. All as stated. The Iq argument is therefore correct: with U17's RESET released, R66 100k holds Q5B's gate at VOUT5, Q5B is on, CS sits below the guaranteed-off level, and U14 draws <1 uA instead of 255 uA — a real 1.28 mW that the design already avoids.

Table 3-1 confirms the interchange warning: MIC1551 is 1 = VS, 2 = GND, 3 = OUT, 4 = TRG, 5 = THG. Completely different, no CS. Fitting one would be a functional disaster, exactly as flagged.

One refinement: CS is not a clean 2/3 VS / 1/3 VS pair. The Electrical Characteristics 'Chip Select' row gives On at 50 min / 67 typ / 72 max %/VS and Off at 28 / 33 / 50 %/VS, so guaranteed-off requires CS below 0.28 x VS = 1.40 V. Q5B's Rds(on) puts CS at a few mV, so this is met with enormous margin. And I confirmed the astable relation independently rather than assuming it: the datasheet's own Astable Timing Accuracy spec (1717-2323 us for RA = RB = 10k, C = 0.1 uF) brackets the classic 0.693(RA+2RB)C = 2079 us, which establishes real 1/3 and 2/3 comparators and therefore T = 1.386 RC for the single-resistor configuration on this board — 3.61 Hz at R64 = 200k, 7.22 Hz at 100k.

findings.title: C61 and C80 return the TPS22917 CT pins to GND, but the datasheet specifies the timing capacitor to VIN
findings.current_part: C61 = 3300 pF from U11 CT (pin 4) to GND; C80 = 3300 pF from U18 CT (pin 4) to GND. The TPS22917 datasheet's pin table says of CT: 'Switch slew rate control. Connect capacitor from this pin to VIN to increase output slew rate and turn-on time', and section 9.3.2 repeats 'A capacitor to VIN on the CT pin sets the slew rate of VOUT'; the Simplified Schematic and Figure 10-1 Typical Application both draw CT to VIN (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps22917.pdf).
findings.proposal: No change to hardware. Flagging so that nobody 'fixes' the timing by chasing the wrong parameter, and so a future revision follows the datasheet.
findings.benefit:
In practice this works, and I want to be precise about why rather than call it a bug. VIN is a stable, heavily bypassed DC rail at the moment each switch turns on — U11's VIN is VOUT5 which is already regulating, and U18's VIN is VOUT3 which is up before /PG_2V5 releases — so a capacitor to VIN and a capacitor to GND are AC-equivalent at the CT node. The datasheet's switching table gives, at VIN = 3.6 V, tR = 1.6 us/pF and tON = 3.8 us/pF for CT >= 100 pF; at VIN = 5.0 V, 1.8 us/pF and 4.0 us/pF. So U18 with 3300 pF ramps VDD3 in 3300 x 1.6 = 5.3 ms (turn-on 12.5 ms) and U11 ramps VDD5 in 3300 x 1.8 = 5.9 ms. Inrush into VDD3's 3.4 uF of decoupling (4 x 0.1u + 3 x 1u) is C x dV/dt = 3.4 uF x 3.34 V / 5.3 ms = 2.1 mA — very gentle, with plenty of headroom for whatever bulk capacitance the ClockxControl adds on its V+ input (at 10 uF added it would still only be 8.5 mA against a 2 A part).
The residual concern is second-order: with the cap to GND rather than to VIN, a disturbance on VIN during the turn-on ramp couples differently into the CT node than TI characterised. Since VIN is settled before ON is asserted in both cases here, I rate the practical impact as nil.
findings.risk: Low. If a future revision moves either load switch to a rail that is still ramping when its ON pin asserts, the GND-referenced cap would give a different (and uncharacterised) slew rate. Cost to correct on a respin: rerouting one pad each.
findings.verify_reason:
The datasheet quotes are exact. TI SLVSDW8B Table 6-1 Pin Functions, verbatim: '4 | CT | O | Switch slew rate control. Connect capacitor from this pin to VIN to increase output slew rate and turn-on time. Can be left floating for fastest timing.' Section 9.3.2, verbatim: 'A capacitor to VIN on the CT pin sets the slew rate of VOUT.' Both say VIN, neither says GND. The board does the other thing: netlist confirms C61 3300p from Net-(U11-CT) to GND and C80 3300p from Net-(U18-CT) to GND, while U12's CT (pin 4) is left unconnected. The discrepancy is real and correctly reported as a flag rather than a bug.

The reasoning for why it works in practice is sound: VIN is a stiff, heavily bypassed DC rail at each switch's turn-on, so the internal slew-control current source sees the same capacitance either way. I checked the sequencing claim rather than accepting it — U18's VIN is VOUT3, which is up before /PG_2V5 releases (chain: /EN -> VOUT3 -> PGOOD2 -> U8 EN -> VDD2 -> U8 PGOOD -> /PG_2V5), and U11's ON is /~VCNT5, which R7 pulls up from VDD3, itself U18's output ramping over 5.28 ms, whereas VOUT5's own soft-start is 0.5 ms (35271fc) — so VOUT5 is settled long before U11's ON crosses VIH. Both switches really do see a settled VIN.

Timing arithmetic verified against the Switching Characteristics table: VIN = 3.6 V gives tR 1.6 us/pF and tON 3.8 us/pF for CT >= 100 pF; VIN = 5.0 V gives 1.8 and 4.0. So 3300 pF -> 5.28 ms rise / 12.5 ms turn-on for U18, 5.94 ms rise for U11. VDD3's decoupling is exactly 3.4 uF nominal (C5/C34/C39/C43 0.1u + C49/C50/C69 1u, confirmed from the VDD3 pad list), giving 3.4 uF x 3.336 V / 5.28 ms = 2.15 mA of inrush. All correct.

One small addition the finding missed and a future respin should note: the Recommended Operating Conditions specify 'VCT Timing Capacitor Voltage Rating 7 V' as a minimum, which both a VIN-referenced and a GND-referenced cap satisfy at these rails.

findings.title: U18 ramps VDD3 — and therefore the ClockxControl's V+ — over 5.3 ms; C80 is the knob if the module's power-on reset misbehaves
findings.current_part: U18 = TPS22917DBV with C80 = 3300 pF on CT. From the datasheet switching table at VIN = 3.6 V: output rise time tR = 1.6 us/pF and total turn-on time tON = 3.8 us/pF for CT >= 100 pF, with CT open giving 65 us and 120 us respectively (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps22917.pdf). U18's ON pin is /PG_2V5, U8's open-drain PGOOD pulled up by R8 100k to VDD2, so VDD3 comes up only after the 2.5 V CPU core rail is good. The ClockxControl's V+ lands on P1 pad S1 = VDD3 (confirmed from the netlist), so the module sees exactly this ramp.
findings.proposal: No change unless you see a symptom. If the ClockxControl fails to start reliably, or starts at the wrong divider setting, reduce C80 (1000 pF -> 1.6 ms rise; 330 pF -> 0.53 ms; open -> 65 us). Same 0603 pad either way.
findings.benefit: No power benefit — this is a commissioning note for the overclock integration. VDD3 rises in 3300 pF x 1.6 us/pF = 5.28 ms, and the switch's total turn-on is 3300 x 3.8 = 12.5 ms after /PG_2V5 goes high. A 5.3 ms supply ramp is slow by the standards of a small microcontroller's internal power-on reset; parts with a proper brown-out detector handle it, parts relying on a simple POR sometimes do not. Inrush is not the constraint: 3.4 uF of VDD3 decoupling at 3.34 V / 5.28 ms is 2.1 mA, and even 10 uF of extra module bulk capacitance only takes it to 8.5 mA against a 2 A switch, so C80 can be reduced freely without any inrush concern. The sequencing itself is right and worth confirming: the module cannot drive the CPU's XIN before VDD2 is up, because its own supply is gated by VDD2's power-good.
findings.risk: Reducing C80 increases inrush proportionally (330 pF would give 3.4 uF x 3.34 V / 0.53 ms = 21 mA, still trivial) and shortens the gap between VDD2-good and VDD3-good, which is the sequencing margin between the CPU core rail and the CPU I/O rail. Do not remove C80 entirely without checking that VDD3's fastest ramp does not disturb VOUT3. I have not tested the ClockxControl's POR behaviour — this is a 'here is the adjustment if you need it' note, not a claim that a problem exists.
findings.verify_reason:
Every timing number checks out against TI SLVSDW8B section 7.6 Switching Characteristics, which I extracted directly: tON at VIN = 3.6 V is 120 us with CT open and 3.8 us/pF for CT >= 100 pF; tR at VIN = 3.6 V is 65 us with CT open and 1.6 us/pF. So C80 = 3300 pF gives 5.28 ms of output rise and 12.54 ms of total turn-on after /PG_2V5 goes high, and the suggested alternatives are right: 1000 pF -> 1.6 ms, 330 pF -> 0.53 ms, open -> 65 us. The 330 pF inrush figure re-derived: 3.4 uF x 3.336 V / 0.528 ms = 21.5 mA against a 2 A part. Nothing to worry about, as stated.

Sequencing verified from the netlist rather than assumed: U18 pin 3 (ON) is on /PG_2V5, which is U8's PGOOD pulled up by R8 100k to VDD2; P1 pad S1 is on VDD3, which is U18's output. So the ClockxControl's V+ genuinely sees this ramp and genuinely cannot come up before the 2.5 V CPU core rail is good. That is the right sequencing for a module driving the CPU's XIN, and confirming it is worth the space.

This is a commissioning note, not a finding: no change is proposed unless a symptom appears, and it is correctly booked at 0 mW. The one thing that remains untested is the ClockxControl's own power-on-reset behaviour against a 5.28 ms ramp, which the finding says plainly. C80 is C_0603_1608Metric_Boxed_2 so any value change is a drop-in.

findings.title: RA1, Q6, Q8, R9 and the six VDD3 pull-ups carry essentially no static current — I checked each and they belong in the inventory at zero
findings.current_part: RA1 = 330 ohm 4-resistor convex array, four ISOLATED elements in series with the four link-port lines between the AGB CPU (SC, SD, SI, SO) and the ACM2520-801-3P common-mode chokes EM1/EM2 and connector P4. Q6, Q8 = 2N7002 SOT-23. R9 = 100k in parallel with D2 (1SS355VMTE-17) between VBATT and VFILT. The six 100k pull-ups on VDD3 are R6 (cart IRQ), R7 (/~VCNT5), R67 (/CPU/VSHD), R68 (TP12), R70 and R71 (the IPS touch pads).
findings.proposal: Change nothing. Recording the audit so the quiescent inventory is complete and so nobody spends effort here.
findings.benefit:
Each checked against the netlist rather than assumed:
- RA1: series elements in signal lines with no DC path. The link port idles floating; the only pull-up is R35 100k from VDD35 through RA1A onto the CPU's SC pin. Zero standing power. Caveat: if the AGB CPU drives SC low in its default serial-port state, R35 would carry 3.3 V / 100k = 33 uA = 110 uW from VDD35. I cannot verify the CPU's default SC state — it is salvaged, undocumented silicon — so this is flagged as 0 to 110 uW, unresolved.
- R9: parallels D2, so the only current is U3's IVDD, 300 nA typ / 700 nA max. Drop across R9 = 30-70 mV, dissipation = I^2 R = 0.7 uA^2 x 100k = 49 nW. Effectively zero, and the topology is correct: R9 gives a near-zero-drop DC path while D2 + C1 22u hold VFILT up through a battery sag.
- R13 and R8: pull-ups on open-drain PGOOD outputs (LTC3527 PGOOD2 and NCV8164 PGOOD respectively) which are high-impedance whenever power is good. Zero in normal operation.
- R6: cart IRQ line, an input at both ends. Zero.
- R7: only conducts when Q8 turns on, i.e. when the CPU asserts VCNT5. In the screen-on state /~VCNT5 must be high to keep U11 and U12 enabled, so Q8 is off and R7 carries only the TPS22917 ON-pin leakage (+/-10 nA). If VCNT5 is asserted with the screen off, R7 carries 3.34 V / 100k = 33.4 uA = 112 uW. Range 0 to 112 uW.
- R67: both ends at VDD3 whenever U12 is on. Zero.
- R68: drives only TP12, no DC path anywhere. Zero.
- R70, R71: touch-pad pull-ups; Q2B and Q7A are off except during a button combo. Zero.
- R29: pull-up on /~RESET, whose only driver is LTC3527 PGOOD1 (open drain, high-Z when good) and JP1, which ships open. Zero.
- Q6 (2N7002): gate on VDD5, so it turns on with the screen and pulls the LM4853's SHUTDOWN pin low to enable the amplifier; R37 100k then carries 2.5 V / 100k = 25 uA = 62.5 uW from VAUD, but only while the screen is powered — so it is not in the 170 mW no-screen idle figure. Correct design, not worth touching (raising R37 would slow the amp's mute response on power-down).
- Q8 (2N7002): inverts VCNT5 to drive U11/U12's active-high ON pins; TPS22917 VIL is 0.35 V max and Q8 sinks R7's 33 uA at a few millivolts, so there is ample margin.
Total contribution of everything in this finding to the idle inventory: under 0.12 mW, and most of that is state-dependent.
findings.risk: None. The one genuinely unresolved item is R35 / the CPU's SC pin default state (0 to 110 uW); if a builder wants to close it, measuring the voltage at TP25 with the link port empty settles it in one probe.
findings.verify_reason:
I re-dumped every net in the audit rather than accepting the list. RA1: Net-(RA1A-R1.1) = {R35.1, RA1.1, U1.40 SC}; Net-(RA1A-R1.2) = {EM2.2, RA1.8, TP25}; Net-(RA1B-R2.1) = {RA1.2, U1.41 SD}; Net-(RA1B-R2.2) = {C20.1, EM2.1, RA1.7}. Four isolated elements in series with the link lines, no DC path, correct. The R35 pull-up is real and the 0-110 uW uncertainty from the CPU's undocumented default SC state is real and honestly flagged — but it pulls the SC node directly, not through the 330 ohm.

R9: verified 100k in parallel with D2 between VBATT and /VFILT, with only U3's IDD (300 nA typ / 700 nA max, TPS3840 SNVSB03E) flowing. Drop 30-70 mV, I^2R = 49 nW. Correct, and the topology reading is right. R13 and R8 on open-drain PGOOD outputs: R8 in fact carries the LTC3527's SHDN1 input current, 1 uA typ / 2 uA max (35271fc), so it is ~2.5-5 uW from VDD2 rather than exactly zero — still nothing. R6, R67, R68, R70, R71, R29: netlist confirms each is either input-to-input or has both ends at the same potential in the normal state. Zero, correct.

Q6/LM4853: netlist confirms Q6 gate = VDD5, source = AGND, drain = Net-(Q6-D) = {Q6.3, R37.2, U6.2 SHUTDOWN}. I checked the polarity rather than assuming it — the LM4853 datasheet specs 'ISD Shutdown Current, SD Mode; VSHUTDOWN = VDD, 18 uA', so SHUTDOWN is active-high and pulling it low does enable the amplifier, with VIH 2.0 V min / VIL 0.8 V max. The finding's reading is right and the 25 uA / 62.5 uW at VAUD is right; only the 'not in idle' and battery-referred framing need fixing.

Q8: netlist confirms gate = /CPU/VCNT5 (U1 pin 118), drain = /~VCNT5 = {R7.2, U11.3 ON, U12.3 ON}. TPS22917 VIL is 0.35 V max and Q8 sinks 33 uA at millivolts, so the margin claim is correct.

The conclusion — under 0.12 mW total, change nothing — survives all three corrections. It is a legitimately empty bucket and the finding is right to say so rather than manufacture a lever.
findings.correction: Three fixes. (1) R35 does NOT reach the CPU's SC pin 'through RA1A' — R35 pad 1, RA1 pad 1 and U1 pin 40 (SC) are all the same net, Net-(RA1A-R1.1); the 330 ohm element sits on the far side, between that node and EM2 pin 2 / TP25. The 0-110 uW range is unaffected but the topology statement is wrong. (2) The claim that Q6/R37's current is 'not in the 170 mW no-screen idle figure' is unsupported: U11's ON pin is /~VCNT5, which R7 pulls high from VDD3 by default, so VDD5 — and therefore Q6's gate — is up whenever the CPU is not asserting VCNT5, screen present or not. At any moment either R37's 25 uA or R7's 33 uA is flowing; the finding's own two bullets say so and then the summary contradicts them. (3) R37's 62.5 uW is measured at VAUD (2.5 V from an LDO off VOUT3); referred to the battery it is 62.5 x (3.336/2.5) / 0.84 = 99 uW.

findings.title: U7 is a 4.5 V-minimum op-amp running on a 2.5 V rail with its inputs above the common-mode ceiling; the pin-identical TLV9064 fixes it and wins back ~31 mW
findings.current_part: TLV9364QPWRQ1 (TI, TSSOP-14 PW, automotive Q1 grade) — confirmed as the BOM part from the DigiKey link embedded in Audio.kicad_sch (https://www.digikey.com/short/jhr04t1t resolves to TLV9364QPWRQ1). Datasheet SBOSA67B section 6.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: VS = 4.5 V min to 40 V max. Section 7.4 Device Functional Modes, verbatim: 'The TLV936x has a single functional mode and is operational when the power-supply voltage is greater than 4.5 V.' Section 6.7: input common-mode voltage range = (V-) to (V+) - 2 V; IQ per amplifier 2.6 mA typ, 3 mA max, 3.2 mA over temperature; rail-to-rail OUTPUT only, not rail-to-rail input. On this board U7 pin 4 (V+) = VAUD = 2.5 V and pin 11 (V-) = AGND (verified from the PCB net map), so VS = 2.5 V, which is 2.0 V below the datasheet minimum; and the common-mode ceiling is (2.5 - 2) = 0.5 V while every one of the four non-inverting inputs sits at the VAUD/2 = 1.25 V bias set by R45/R46 and R49/R50. Both the supply and the common-mode spec are violated. AGBM-02 carries the identical part (same DigiKey short link in its Audio.kicad_sch), so this is not fork-specific.
findings.proposal: TLV9064IPWR (TI). Datasheet SBOS789 (TLV906xS family): VS = 1.8 V to 5.5 V; VCM = (V-) - 0.1 V to (V+) + 0.1 V (true rail-to-rail input); IQ = 538 uA per amplifier typ, 750 uA max at VS = 5.5 V; GBW 10 MHz; SR 6.5 V/us; broadband noise 10 nV/rtHz; THD+N 0.0008% at 1 kHz. D/PW 14-pin pinout is 1 OUT1, 2 IN1-, 3 IN1+, 4 V+, 11 V-, 12 IN4+, 13 IN4-, 14 OUT4 — pin-for-pin identical to the TLV9364 PW package, so it drops onto the existing TSSOP-14 land with no schematic or layout change. DigiKey 19,544 in stock, $1.53 @1 / $1.117 @10 (vs $2.63 for the TLV9364QPWRQ1) — cheaper as well as correct. Filter performance is unaffected: required slew for 1.25 Vpk at 16 kHz is 2*pi*16k*1.25 = 0.126 V/us against 6.5 V/us available, and the Sallen-Key feedback caps (1000 p / 3300 p) are isolated from each output by R53/R34 = 5.1 k which acts as a built-in R_ISO.
findings.benefit: IQ delta = 4 x (2.6 mA - 0.538 mA) = 8.25 mA at VAUD. Because an LDO passes its load current straight through, the battery-side cost is set by CURRENT not by VAUD: 8.25 mA x 3.34 V = 27.6 mW at VOUT3, / 0.90 assumed boost efficiency = 30.6 mW at the battery. That is 18% of AGBM-01's measured 170 mW idle and ~65% of the audio chain's entire 47.3 mW quiescent floor. HONEST CAVEAT ON THE MAGNITUDE: the 2.6 mA/amp figure is only guaranteed for VS >= 4.5 V and TI publishes no data at 2.5 V, so the actual TLV9364 current on this board is unmeasured. Pessimistic bound — if it draws only half its rated IQ at 2.5 V, the delta is 4 x (1.3 - 0.538) = 3.05 mA = 10.2 mW at VOUT3 = 11.3 mW at the battery. Even that bound is the largest single lever in the audio domain. Circumstantial support for the high end: MouseBiteLabs measure AGBM-01 at 170 mW idle vs 134 mW for a stock GBA, a 36 mW gap that the 47.3 mW audio quiescent computed with 10.4 mA of op-amp current explains almost exactly, whereas a low-IQ assumption would leave AGBM-01's non-audio consumption higher than a 2001 GBA's, which is implausible given the modern converters. Not proof — measure TP22 (VAUD) current before and after.
findings.risk: Very low. The TLV9064 is a lower-voltage, lower-noise-per-mA, rail-to-rail-input part in the identical package and pinout, and the circuit it sits in never needs more than 10 MHz of GBW or 0.13 V/us of slew. The only degradations are on paper and irrelevant here: input offset 0.3 mV typ (TLV9064) vs 0.4 mV (TLV9364) — better; 1/f noise 10 nV/rtHz broadband vs 8.5 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz — a fraction of a dB in a path whose noise floor is set by the 9 uVrms LDO and the PWM quantiser anyway. The one thing to check on a rebuild is that with a genuinely in-spec input stage the DC operating points settle where the design intends; if the existing boards sound acceptable it is because the TLV9364 degrades gracefully, and the TLV9064 can only improve on that. Do not substitute TLV9354 or TLV9164 — those are different supply families.
findings.verify_reason:
CORRECTNESS CORE: CONFIRMED, and it is the most valuable thing in the set. I resolved the DigiKey short link myself: https://www.digikey.com/short/jhr04t1t -> TLV9364QPWRQ1 (TI, 14-TSSOP, automotive, Active, 2,110 in stock, $2.79@1). I dumped U7's pads from the fork PCB (pinout.py U7): pin 4 V+ = VAUD, pin 11 V- = AGND, so VS = 2.5 V. I re-derived the DC bias from the netlist: R45/R46 and R49/R50 are 100k/100k from VAUD, and C24/C26/C28/C27 block DC around the Sallen-Key, so all four non-inverting inputs sit at 1.25 V. Against the datasheet limits (VS min 4.5 V; VCM = (V-) to (V+)-2 V, i.e. a 0.5 V ceiling here) both the supply and the common-mode spec are violated. AGBM-02's Audio.kicad_sch carries the same jhr04t1t link (5 occurrences, 17 'TLV9364' hits) and AGBM-11 the same part, so it is not fork-specific. TWO CITATION ERRORS: (a) the fitted part is the -Q1, whose datasheet is SBOSAD6B (TLV936x-Q1), not SBOSA67B - I fetched both; the limits are identical (4.5-40 V, VCM to (V+)-2 V, IQ 2.6 mA/3 mA/3.2 mA), so nothing material changes. (b) the TLV9064's datasheet is SBOS839N, not 'SBOS789'.

TLV9064 PROPOSAL: CONFIRMED as a drop-in. From SBOS839N I verified VS 1.8-5.5 V, VCM (V-)-0.1 to (V+)+0.1, IQ 538 uA typ / 750 uA max at 5.5 V, GBW 10 MHz, SR 6.5 V/us, 10 nV/rtHz at 10 kHz, THD+N 0.0008%, VOS +/-0.3 mV. Figure 5-13 gives the D/PW 14-pin pinout as 1 OUT1, 2 IN1-, 3 IN1+, 4 V+, 5 IN2+, 6 IN2-, 7 OUT2, 8 OUT3, 9 IN3-, 10 IN3+, 11 V-, 12 IN4+, 13 IN4-, 14 OUT4 - identical to the TLV9364 PW, and the board footprint is Bucketmouse:TSSOP-14_4.4x5mm_P0.65mm. DigiKey TLV9064IPWR: Active, 14-TSSOP, but 1,433 in stock (not 19,544) at $1.62@1 / $1.185@10.

BENEFIT: REFUTED as stated. The finding's load-bearing claim is 'TI publishes no data at 2.5 V'. That is false, and the data TI does publish settles it against the finding. SBOSAD6B Figure 5-22 / SBOSA67B Figure 6-22 (Quiescent Current vs Supply Voltage, VCM = V-) plots down to the bottom of the part's range, and Figures 5-23/5-24 carry explicit VS = 2.7 V curves. I rendered the figure at 600 dpi and digitised it against its own gridlines (2 V per minor division, 0.4 mA per division): the curve BEGINS at ~2.65 V at 1.32 mA/amplifier, knees at ~3.2 V / 2.03 mA, and only reaches the 2.3 mA plateau above ~6 V. Extrapolating the steep segment (slope 1.23 mA/V) to 2.5 V gives ~1.13 mA/amplifier. So the real delta is 4 x (1.1...1.32 - 0.538) = 2.25...3.13 mA, and at the finding's own 3.34 V / 0.90 assumptions that is 2.25x3.34/0.9 = 8.4 mW to 3.13x3.34/0.9 = 11.6 mW at the battery. Call it ~10 mW. That is the finding's own dismissed 'pessimistic bound', not its 30.6 mW headline.

The finding's argument for the high end is also invalid on its own terms: it leans on the 36 mW AGBM-01-vs-stock-GBA gap, but AGBM-02 carries the IDENTICAL audio chain and idles at 141 mW, 29 mW BELOW AGBM-01 - so that gap is converter-side and cannot be evidence for a large audio quiescent. Worse, if the op-amps really drew 10.4 mA (38.6 mW at the battery) then AGBM-02's entire 141 mW would leave only ~102 mW for CPU + SRAM + two LDOs + three load switches + supervisors + converter, less than a whole stock GBA (134 mW) including its own audio. Consequently the 'audio quiescent floor' is ~7.5 mA / ~28 mW, not 12.75 mA / 47.3 mW, and the swap is ~35% of it and ~5.8% of the 170 mW idle, not 65% and 18%.

TWO THINGS THE FINDING GETS WRONG BESIDES THE NUMBER. (1) 'The Sallen-Key feedback caps are isolated from each output by R53/R34 = 5.1k which acts as a built-in R_ISO' is false: from the netlist, C32 pad 2 and C35 pad 2 land directly on Net-(U7C--) and Net-(U7A--), i.e. straight on the outputs; R53/R34 sit between one stage's OUTPUT and the next stage's input node. The conclusion (no capacitive-load problem despite the TLV906x's 100 pF CL rating) happens to be right for a different reason: above cutoff the feedback cap is in series with R51||R52 = 5.45 kOhm (stage 1) and R53||R54 = 3.97 kOhm (stage 2) to AC ground, so the output sees a resistive, not capacitive, load. (2) 'The only degradations are on paper' is wrong. The TLV906x has a complementary-pair rail-to-rail input: SBOS839N splits its CMRR spec at VCM = (V+)-1.4 V (80 dB min below it, 57 dB min across the full range). At VS = 2.5 V that transition sits at 1.1 V, and all four sections are unity-gain followers whose common-mode voltage swings with the signal right through it. Worst case that is a VOS step of 5.7 V / 10^(57/20) = 8 mV (0.25 mV at the 87 dB typ) appearing directly at the output as crossover distortion - about -41 dB worst case, -71 dB typical, against a 0.884 Vrms full scale. Still far better than running an amp 0.75 V past its CM ceiling, but it should be stated. If the reviewer wants the current back and will accept a filter re-check, TLV9004IPWR (SLOS857, RRIO, 1.8-5.5 V, 60 uA/ch, quad TSSOP-14) is worth 4 x (1.2 - 0.06) = 4.56 mA = 16.9 mW - but its 1 MHz GBW is marginal for a 15.9 kHz Q=1.31 section and its 27 nV/rtHz broadband noise is 2.7x the TLV9064's, so it needs simulating, not swapping.

Verdict: keep the recommendation, halve-and-then-some the number.
findings.correction: Corrected saving: 8.4-11.6 mW at the battery (call it ~10 mW), not 30.6 mW. Basis: TI's own IQ-vs-supply curve (SBOSAD6B Fig 5-22 / SBOSA67B Fig 6-22) digitised at 600 dpi gives 1.32 mA/amp at its lowest plotted point (~2.65 V) and ~1.13 mA extrapolated to 2.5 V, against 538 uA for the TLV9064: delta 2.25-3.13 mA; x 3.34 V / 0.90 = 8.4-11.6 mW. Audio quiescent floor is ~7.5 mA / ~28 mW, not 12.75 mA / 47.3 mW. Datasheet numbers to cite are SBOSAD6B (fitted part, -Q1) and SBOS839N (TLV9064). Drop-in status, pinout, package and the out-of-spec correctness claim all stand unchanged. Add the RRI crossover-distortion caveat and drop the false R_ISO justification.

findings.title: Class-D for the speaker path only is worth ~48 mW at max volume, but it costs a schematic redesign and puts a 250 kHz switcher next to the ClockxControl
findings.current_part: U6 LM4853MM/NOPB (TI, VSSOP/MSOP-10 DGS). SNAS155E: single supply 2.4 V to 5.5 V; IDD 1.8 mA typ at VDD = 2.7 V, 2.0 mA at 3.3 V, 2.4 mA at 5.0 V, identical in BTL and SE modes; shutdown current 10 uA at 2.7 V; 300 mW into 8 Ohm BTL at 2.7 V, 25 mW into 32 Ohm SE at 2.7 V; theta-JA 194 C/W for DGS. It is a linear class-AB stage, and for a BTL class-AB the supply current equals the rectified load current, I_avg = (2/pi)(Vp/RL). At MouseBiteLabs' reconciled max-volume operating point (Vp = 0.178 V differential, Pout = 2.0 mW into 8 Ohm) that is 14.2 mA on top of the 1.8 mA quiescent — the output stage is running at an efficiency of Pout/Psup = 2.0 mW / (16.0 mA x 2.5 V) = 5%. DigiKey lists LM4853MM/NOPB as Active with 2,871 in stock, so there is no sourcing pressure to change it.
findings.proposal: TPA2005D1 (TI) for the speaker only, with the LM4853 retained for the headphone jack. SLOS369G: VDD 2.5 V to 5.5 V (exactly reaches VAUD); I(Q) 2.2 mA typ / 3.2 mA max at VDD = 2.5 V no load; I(SD) 0.5 uA; rDS(on) 770 mOhm at 2.5 V; switching frequency 250 kHz typ; 0.26 W into 8 Ohm at 2.5 V / 1% THD+N; THD+N 0.20% at 200 mW / 2.5 V / 8 Ohm; filter-free output stage; HVSSOP-8 (DGN) or VSON-8 (DRB), both 3.00 x 3.00 mm. Input is differential with a fixed 150 kOhm internal input impedance and gain = 2 x 150k/RI, so R30/R31/R56/R57 and the input coupling network all have to be reworked. The LM4853's SHUTDOWN pin (already wired through R37/Q6) would be re-gated off HP-IN so the class-AB headphone amp only runs when a plug is inserted.
findings.benefit: At MouseBiteLabs' own max-volume anchor (2.0 mW into 8 Ohm). Class AB now: 14.2 mA output + 1.8 mA quiescent = 16.0 mA at VAUD. Class D: conduction loss = I_rms^2 x rDS(on) = (sqrt(2.0mW/8))^2 x 0.77 = 0.19 mW, so supply = (2.0 + 0.19)/2.5 V = 0.88 mA, plus 2.2 mA IQ = 3.08 mA. Delta = 12.9 mA at VAUD -> 12.9 mA x 3.34 V = 43.1 mW at VOUT3 -> / 0.90 = 47.9 mW at the battery. At a louder setting (Vp = 0.35 V, Pout = 7.7 mW): class AB = (2/pi)(0.35/8) + 1.8 mA = 29.7 mA; class D = (7.7/0.9)/2.5 + 2.2 = 5.6 mA; delta 24.1 mA = 89 mW at the battery. AND THE HONEST OTHER END: at silence or on headphones the class-D is WORSE by (2.2 - 1.8) = 0.4 mA = 1.5 mW at the battery, because its quiescent exceeds the LM4853's. So this lever is worth 0 to +89 mW depending entirely on how loud the speaker is being driven, and it is worth exactly nothing to a headphone user.
findings.risk: High, and I would not do it on this board. (1) Not a footprint swap: HVSSOP-8/VSON-8 3x3 mm on an MSOP-10 land, plus a new input network, plus mute logic to keep the speaker silent when headphones are inserted (the LM4853 does this for free today by high-Z'ing A2 in SE mode). (2) EMI: U6 sits at (102.6, -25.9) on B.Cu and the ClockxControl window on F.Cu ends at x = 101.275 — the speaker amp is 1.3 mm from the module edge, and U9, the audio PWM buffer, is at (107.7, -46.4) in the same y band. A 250 kHz filter-free class-D output with ~100 ns edges driving 60 mm of speaker wire, next to the cart bus and an unshielded LCD FFC, is a real radiated-emissions and re-rectification risk; it needs ferrite beads plus caps on both speaker leads, which is more area in a shell that has none. (3) Shared rail: the class-D's switching current on VAUD amplitude-modulates the PWM reference that U9 buffers, i.e. it couples into the HEADPHONE path too unless VAUD is split. (4) The AGBM's stated selling point is audio quality; TPA2005D1 THD+N at the relevant level is 0.20% versus low-single-digit-hundredths for the LM4853 at 4% of its capability. Verdict: real arithmetic, wrong trade for this product. Reported because the reviewer asked for the size of the lever, not because I recommend pulling it.
findings.verify_reason:
PARTS AND SPECS: fully CONFIRMED, and unusually cleanly. From SNAS155E I verified LM4853 single-supply 2.4-5.5 V (Operating Ratings), IDD 1.8 mA at 2.7 V / 2.0 mA at 3.3 V / 2.4 mA at 5.0 V, identical in BTL and SE, ISD 10 uA at 2.7 V, 300 mW into 8 Ohm BTL and 25 mW into 32 Ohm SE at 2.7 V, theta-JA(DGS) = 194 C/W. DigiKey short r3rqdzt8 -> LM4853MM/NOPB, Active, 2,871 in stock - exactly the number claimed. From SLOS369G I verified TPA2005D1 VDD 2.5-5.5 V, I(Q) 2.2 mA typ / 3.2 mA max at VDD = 2.5 V no load, I(SD) 0.5 uA, rDS(on) 770 mOhm at 2.5 V, f(sw) 200/250/300 kHz, 0.26 W into 8 Ohm at 2.5 V/1% THD+N, THD+N 0.20% at 200 mW/2.5 V/8 Ohm, ZI 142/150/158 kOhm and Gain = 2 x 150k/RI, HVSSOP(8) and VSON(8) both 3.00 x 3.00 mm in the Device Information table. Every electrical number in the finding is right.

ARITHMETIC AT ITS OWN ANCHOR: reproduces exactly. (2/pi)(0.178/8) = 14.16 mA; +1.8 = 15.96 mA; class-D conduction (sqrt(0.002/8))^2 x 0.77 = 0.19 mW; (2.0+0.19)/2.5 = 0.876 mA; +2.2 = 3.08 mA; delta 12.9 mA x 3.34 = 43.1 mW; /0.90 = 47.9 mW. One nit: a BTL class-D conduction path has a high-side and a low-side FET in series, so it is 2 x I_rms^2 x rDS(on) = 0.38 mW - changes the answer by 0.03 mA.

WHAT IS WRONG. (1) THE ANCHOR IS MISLABELLED. 'MouseBiteLabs' reconciled max-volume operating point (Vp = 0.178 V differential)' is not max volume; it is roughly 15 dB below it. I re-derived the gain structure from the netlist and SNAS155E's own BTL description ('The audio signal from the RIGHT IN pin is directed to the inverting input of A1... the LEFT IN and RIGHT IN audio signals are summed together at the input of A1'): R30/R31 = 100k into A1's summing node, R57 = 20k feedback, A2 fixed at -1 by two internal 20 kOhm resistors. Full-scale filter output is VAUD/2 = 1.25 Vpk per channel, so A1 = 0.2 x (1.25+1.25) = 0.5 Vpk and the BTL differential is 1.0 Vpk = 0.707 Vrms = 62.5 mW into 8 Ohm - which is exactly what the sibling lm4853-supply-margin finding states, so the two findings contradict each other by 31x in output power. At that genuine full-scale point class AB draws (2/pi)(1.0/8) = 79.6 mA and class D about (62.5/0.85)/2.5 + 2.2 = 31.6 mA, a 49.8 mA delta = 185 mW at the battery. (2) THE RECONCILIATION USED THE WRONG QUIESCENT. It backed the anchor out of MBL's 50-100 mW using 10.4 mA of op-amp current, which TI's IQ-vs-supply curve contradicts (see the u7 verdict: ~5.2 mA). Redoing it honestly: 50-100 mW at the battery = 13.5-27.0 mA on VAUD; quiescent with the corrected op-amp figure is ~7.5 mA; so the output stage is 6.0-19.5 mA, i.e. Vp = 0.075-0.245 V, Pout 0.35-3.8 mW, and the class-D delta is 5.5-17.7 mA = 20-66 mW at the battery. The 48 mW sits near the middle of that, so the NUMBER survives; its label does not. (3) THE EMI PROXIMITY CLAIM IS GEOMETRICALLY WRONG. I opened the ECO-6 board (AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb): MOD1, footprint 'ClockxControl_GBA_GBC', sits at (91.95, -44.95) on F.Cu with a +/-9.575 x +/-6.25 mm outline, i.e. x 82.375..101.525, y -51.2..-38.7. U6 is at (102.6, -25.9) on B.Cu - 1.1 mm away in x but 12.8 mm away in y, so the true separation is ~12.8 mm, not 1.3 mm. The finding compared one coordinate and ignored the other. (U9 at (107.7, -46.4) genuinely is ~6.2 mm away and in the module's y band, so that half is right.) (4) THE GAIN REWORK IS UNDER-SPECIFIED. To keep today's 0.4 differential gain the TPA2005D1 needs RI = 2 x 150k / 0.4 = 750 kOhm; SLOS369G's only RI guidance is a 15 kOhm MINIMUM for gain <= 20 V/V, and it gives no data anywhere near 750 kOhm. Its VIC range at VDD = 2.5 V is 0.5 V to 1.7 V and the pot wiper sits at 1.25 V DC, which fits but only if the wiper-DC problem in the vr2 finding is dealt with first. (5) PACKAGE: TI's own datasheet is self-inconsistent (Device Information says HVSSOP(8) 3.00 x 3.00 mm; the Features list says '3 mm x 5 mm MSOP PowerPAD (DGN)'). Either way DGN carries an exposed PowerPAD that the MSOP-10_3x3mm_P0.5mm land has no thermal pad for - one more reason it is not a footprint swap, which the finding already concedes.

The rejection verdict is right and well argued. Keep it; fix the anchor label, the geometry, and state the range.
findings.correction: State the lever as a RANGE, not a point: 0 mW on headphones or at silence (and -1.5 mW, i.e. worse, at silence on the speaker), ~20-66 mW at MouseBiteLabs' 50-100 mW 'max volume' once the op-amp quiescent is corrected from 10.4 mA to ~5.2 mA, and ~185 mW only at a continuous full-scale sine that never occurs. Delete 'Vp = 0.178 V differential' as 'max volume': true max volume is 1.0 Vpk differential / 0.707 Vrms / 62.5 mW into 8 Ohm, because in BTL mode the LM4853 sums L and R into A1 through R30/R31 = 100k against R57 = 20k. Delete 'the speaker amp is 1.3 mm from the module edge': U6 (102.6, -25.9) is 12.8 mm from the MOD1 outline (x 82.375..101.525, y -51.2..-38.7); only U9 at ~6.2 mm is genuinely close. Add: TPA2005D1 needs RI = 750 kOhm for the existing 0.4 gain, far outside any characterised value, and DGN's PowerPAD has no land.

findings.title: The reconstruction filter is fixed at 15.84 kHz but the GBA's PWM carrier scales with the CPU clock — the ClockxControl's underclock settings put the carrier inside the audio band
findings.current_part: The filter is a 4th-order Butterworth low-pass at fc = 15.84 kHz per channel, computed from the schematic values: stage 1 f0 = 15.76 kHz Q = 0.540 (R51 7.5k / R52 20k / C32 1000p feedback / C31 680p to AGND), stage 2 f0 = 15.92 kHz Q = 1.312 (R53 5.1k / R54 18k / C35 3300p feedback / C33 330p to AGND); the left channel U7D/U7B is identical. The textbook 4th-order Butterworth Qs are 0.5412 and 1.3065, so the alignment is exact. The GBA's audio is 1-bit PWM whose rate is derived from the master clock: GBATEK's SOUNDBIAS (4000088h) bits 14-15 give 9 bit / 32.768 kHz (default), 8 bit / 65.536 kHz, 7 bit / 131.072 kHz, 6 bit / 262.144 kHz, and each 9-bit sample N outputs N low bits then (512-N) high bits at 16.78 MHz, i.e. 512 clocks per sample. With X1 depopulated and CLK driven by the module, the carrier scales 1:1 with the ClockxControl ratio.
findings.proposal: No component change is available that fixes this. Attenuation of the carrier fundamental, 1/sqrt(1+(f/fc)^8) at fc = 15.84 kHz: 0.333x -> carrier 10.91 kHz -> -0.2 dB (essentially unfiltered); 0.5x -> 16.38 kHz -> -3.6 dB; 0.666x -> 21.82 kHz -> -11.5 dB; 1.0x -> 32.77 kHz -> -25.3 dB; 1.25x -> 40.96 kHz -> -33.0 dB; 1.5x -> 49.15 kHz -> -39.3 dB; 1.75x -> 57.34 kHz -> -44.7 dB. The carrier fundamental at mid-scale duty is (2 x 2.5 V / pi) x sin(pi x 0.5) = 1.591 Vpk = 1.125 Vrms, against a full-scale recovered audio sine of 1.25 Vpk = 0.884 Vrms — the carrier is 2.1 dB LOUDER than full-scale audio before filtering. So at 0.333x roughly 1.10 Vrms of a 10.9 kHz tone reaches the volume pot, i.e. above the music. Practical options, all outside the BOM: treat 1.0x and above as the usable range for anyone who cares about the audio; or have software set SOUNDBIAS bits 14-15 to 3 (6 bit / 262.144 kHz nominal, which is 87 kHz even at 0.333x -> below -49 dB) at the cost of amplitude resolution. Retuning the filter to cover 0.333x would need fc ~5 kHz and would destroy the audio band, so it is not an option.
findings.benefit: Zero mW — this is a quality finding, and the direction of the effect is what matters. Overclocking is a free WIN for the audio: at 1.75x the carrier rejection improves from -25.3 dB to -44.7 dB, 19.4 dB better, and the 61 mVrms of 32.8 kHz residual that reaches the headphones at 1x drops to 6.6 mVrms at 57 kHz. Underclocking is a loss: at 0.5x and 0.333x the reconstruction filter stops doing its job.
findings.risk: The risk is in NOT knowing this: a user who selects 0.333x or 0.5x on the ClockxControl gets an audible high-frequency tone (10.9 or 16.4 kHz) at or above program level, plus intermodulation in the class-AB output stage, and will blame the board. Note also that the game's own audio is pitch- and tempo-shifted at any ratio other than 1x, which is a ClockxControl consequence rather than a component one. Nothing on the board can be changed to fix it; it belongs in the fork's documentation.
findings.verify_reason:
SUBSTANTIALLY CONFIRMED - this is the best-supported finding in the set, and I could not break its conclusion. FILTER: I extracted the topology from the fork netlist rather than trusting the finding. Stage 1 (right channel U7C): R51 7.5k from the bias node to the C32 junction, R52 20k from that junction to U7C's + input, C32 1000p from the junction to U7C's output, C31 680p from the + input to AGND. Stage 2 (U7A): R53 5.1k, R54 18k, C35 3300p, C33 330p. Unity-gain Sallen-Key: f0 = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(R1R2C1C2)), Q = sqrt(R1R2C1C2)/((R1+R2)C2). Stage 1: sqrt(1.5e8 x 6.8e-19) = 1.00995e-5 -> f0 = 15,759 Hz, Q = 1.00995e-5/(27500 x 680p) = 0.540. Stage 2: sqrt(9.18e7 x 1.089e-18) = 9.9985e-6 -> f0 = 15,918 Hz, Q = 9.9985e-6/(23100 x 330p) = 1.3116. Against the textbook 4th-order Butterworth 0.5412 / 1.3065 the alignment really is exact. U7B/U7D mirror it. GBATEK: I fetched problemkaputt.de directly and it confirms SOUNDBIAS 4000088h bits 14-15 = '0 9bit / 32.768kHz (Default...)' through '3 6bit / 262.144kHz', PWM at 'the system clock speed of 16.78MHz', '512 bits are output per sample (512*32K=16M)', and 'N low bits, followed by 512-N high bits' - verbatim as claimed. It also confirms the recommendation of 200h 'for clean sound output', which means the carrier is at 50% duty and FULL amplitude even in silence, strengthening the finding. ATTENUATION: I recomputed every entry of 1/sqrt(1+(f/15.84k)^8) and all seven agree to 0.1-0.2 dB (-0.22, -3.64, -11.45, -25.3, -33.0, -39.35, -44.7 dB). Carrier fundamental (2 x 2.5/pi) x sin(pi x 0.5) = 1.5915 Vpk = 1.125 Vrms, and full-scale recovered audio is VAUD/2 = 1.25 Vpk = 0.884 Vrms, so the carrier really is 20log(1.125/0.884) = 2.09 dB above full-scale audio. Residuals 61 mVrms at 1x and 6.5 mVrms at 1.75x both recompute correctly.

ONE NUMBER IS NOT ACHIEVABLE. 'At 0.333x roughly 1.10 Vrms of a 10.9 kHz tone reaches the volume pot' cannot happen, because the op-amps run on 2.5 V biased at 1.25 V and clip at +/-1.25 V. Working it stage by stage at 10.91 kHz: stage 1 at u = 0.692, Q = 0.540 gives |H| = 0.723, so U7C/U7D deliver 1.15 Vpk - just short of clipping; stage 2 at u = 0.685, Q = 1.312 gives |H| = 1.343, which demands 1.54 Vpk from U7A/U7B. The second stage hard-clips. The real residual is therefore ~1.25 Vpk / 0.88 Vrms of a CLIPPED 10.9 kHz tone plus its harmonics, not 1.10 Vrms of a clean one - about 2 dB lower in level but dirtier, and it is the intermediate high-Q node that runs out of headroom first, which is what anyone trying to measure this needs to know. The conclusion is unchanged and if anything the mechanism is uglier than described.

OTHERWISE SOUND: the SOUNDBIAS software workaround is real (bits 14-15 = 3 puts the carrier at 262.144 kHz nominal, 87.3 kHz at 0.333x, past -49 dB) at the cost of 3 bits of amplitude resolution; the observation that overclocking is a free 19.4 dB win for the carrier rejection is correct; and 'retuning the filter to cover 0.333x would need fc ~5 kHz' is right (fc must scale with the carrier). Zero mW is the honest number and the finding says so.
findings.correction: Replace 'roughly 1.10 Vrms of a 10.9 kHz tone reaches the volume pot' with: the filter output clips. Stage 1 (Q = 0.540) delivers 1.15 Vpk at 10.91 kHz and stage 2 (Q = 1.312, |H| = 1.343) demands 1.54 Vpk from a follower on a 2.5 V rail biased at 1.25 V, so U7A/U7B hard-clip at ~1.25 Vpk / 0.88 Vrms and the residual is a clipped tone plus harmonics. Everything else stands: filter f0/Q, the Butterworth alignment, the GBATEK PWM encoding, all seven attenuation figures, and the 2.09 dB carrier-over-full-scale headline.

findings.title: CP2/CP3 100 uF roll the headphone bass off at 50 Hz (100 Hz into 16 Ohm IEMs); a 220 uF polymer tantalum in the identical case is a drop-in that halves the corner
findings.current_part: KYOCERA AVX TPSB107K010R0400 (AGBM-01) / TPSB107M010R0400 (AGBM-02) — 100 uF, 10 V, MOLDED TANTALUM (not ceramic; I checked, because a Class II ceramic here would be a genuine distortion source), case code 1411 (3528 metric), 3.50 x 2.80 mm, 2.10 mm seated height, ESR 400 mOhm, +/-10% (K) or +/-20% (M). These sit in series between the LM4853 SE outputs and the jack tip/ring, with R19/R20 1 k bleed resistors to AGND. High-pass corner into the load = 1/(2*pi*RL*C): 49.7 Hz with 32 Ohm headphones, 99.5 Hz with 16 Ohm IEMs, 5.3 Hz with 300 Ohm cans. The PCB land is Bucketmouse:C_1210_3225Metric_Boxed_2, pads 1.15 x 2.7 mm at +/-1.475 mm (inner gap 1.8 mm, outer span 4.10 mm) — I checked this against the 3528 tantalum body and the terminations land fully inside the pads with ~0.3 mm of outboard fillet, so the existing footprint is correct for a B-case tantalum even though it is named for a 1210 ceramic.
findings.proposal: KEMET T520B227M006ATE035 — 220 uF, 6.3 V, +/-20%, tantalum POLYMER (KO-CAP), case 1411 (3528 metric), 3.50 x 2.80 x 2.00 mm (0.1 mm SHORTER than the part fitted), ESR 35 mOhm at 100 kHz, -55 to +105 C. DigiKey 22,443 in stock, $1.56 @1 / ~$1.03 @10. Identical case, identical land pattern, identical polarity orientation — a true drop-in. DC bias across it is only VAUD/2 = 1.25 V on a 6.3 V part (20% of rating), comfortably inside the 80% derating convention for polymer tantalum.
findings.benefit: Zero mW — this is a pure audio-quality change, and it is one of the very few in this domain that a human will actually hear. New corner = 1/(2*pi*32*220u) = 22.6 Hz with 32 Ohm headphones (was 49.7 Hz) and 45.2 Hz with 16 Ohm IEMs (was 99.5 Hz). Against modern low-impedance IEMs the existing 100 uF is losing 3 dB at 100 Hz and about 6 dB at 50 Hz, which is audible bass loss on anything with sub-bass content; 220 uF moves that below the useful range. Secondary: ESR drops 400 mOhm -> 35 mOhm, which removes 0.4/(0.4+32) = 1.2% (0.11 dB) of insertion loss and any ESR-related nonlinearity. LEAVE CP1 ALONE: it is the same part in series with the 8 Ohm speaker, corner 1/(2*pi*8*100u) = 199 Hz, but a 23 mm 8 Ohm GBA speaker produces essentially nothing below ~400 Hz, so 220 uF there buys no audible bass and only increases cone excursion. CP1 is also not optional despite being a bridged output — it is there because in SE mode the LM4853 leaves LOUT/BTL- at a VDD/2 DC offset with A2 high-Z, and without CP1 that would push 1.25 V/8 Ohm = 156 mA of DC through the speaker.
findings.risk: Low. Cost roughly doubles for those two positions (~$1.03 vs ~$0.60 each in tens) — on a board whose BOM is already dominated by the CPU/SRAM salvage that is noise, but it is the one place in this review where a quality change costs real money. Polymer tantalum has a lower failure-to-short energy than MnO2 tantalum and a 6.3 V part on a 2.5 V rail with 1.25 V bias is very lightly stressed, so reliability is if anything better. Watch polarity on hand assembly: the anode band goes to the amplifier side (CP2 pin 1 = LOUT/BTL-, CP3 pin 1 = ROUT), same as the part it replaces.
findings.verify_reason:
THE SWAP ITSELF: CONFIRMED, every number, which is rare. I resolved the schematic's own Source link https://www.digikey.com/short/332b01qh -> KYOCERA AVX TPSB107K010R0400: 100 uF, 10 V, +/-10%, MOLDED TANTALUM, case 1411 (3528 metric), ESR 400 mOhm @ 100 kHz, 2.10 mm max seated height, -55 to +125 C. Exactly as stated, including that it is tantalum and not a Class II ceramic. I fetched the proposed part directly: KEMET T520B227M006ATE035 - 220 uF, 6.3 V, +/-20%, TANTALUM POLYMER (molded), case 1411 (3528 metric), ESR 35 mOhm @ 100 kHz, 2.00 mm max seated height, 2000 h @ 105 C, Active, 22,443 in stock, $1.56@1 / $1.028@10. Every figure in the finding matches, including the 0.1 mm height reduction. FOOTPRINT: I pulled CP2's pads from the board file - Bucketmouse:C_1210_3225Metric_Boxed_2, pad 1 at -1.475 and pad 2 at +1.475, both 1.15 x 2.7 mm, giving a 1.80 mm inner gap and a 4.10 mm outer span, precisely as claimed. A B-case (3528, 3.5 x 2.8 mm, ~0.8 mm terminations) lands with ~0.30 mm of outboard fillet as stated; worth adding that the INBOARD margin is only ~0.05 mm, so the land is tight on the inside edge - but since the incumbent is the same case code, the swap is unambiguously a drop-in. CORNERS: 1/(2*pi*32*100u) = 49.7 Hz, 1/(2*pi*16*100u) = 99.5 Hz, 1/(2*pi*300*100u) = 5.3 Hz, and 22.6/45.2 Hz at 220 uF - all correct. Circuit context confirmed from the netlist: CP2 pad 1 = Net-(U6-LOUT/BTL-), CP3 pad 1 = Net-(U6-ROUT), pad 2 of each goes to P3 (SJ-3524-SMT) tip/ring with R19/R20 = 1k to AGND, DC across each cap is 1.25 V on a 6.3 V part.

ONE SUB-CLAIM IS FLATLY REFUTED BY THE DATASHEET IT CITES. 'CP1 is also not optional despite being a bridged output - it is there because in SE mode the LM4853 leaves LOUT/BTL- at a VDD/2 DC offset with A2 high-Z, and without CP1 that would push 1.25 V/8 Ohm = 156 mA of DC through the speaker.' SNAS155E, Bridged and Single-Ended Operation, says the opposite in as many words: 'Amplifier A2 is shut down to a high output impedance state in SE mode. This prevents any current flow into the mono bridge-tied load, thereby muting it.' With A2 high-Z there is no DC path at all, and in BTL mode both ends sit at half-supply so there is no net DC either - CP1 carries no DC in either mode, and 156 mA cannot flow. The RECOMMENDATION (leave CP1 alone, because a 23 mm 8 Ohm GBA speaker produces nothing below ~400 Hz so 220 uF buys no audible bass) is correct and unaffected; only the justification is wrong.

TWO THINGS THE FINDING DID NOT CHECK. (a) SOURCING, and it cuts in the finding's favour: DigiKey shows only 5 pieces of TPSB107K010R0400 in stock at $1.17@1. The incumbent part is effectively unobtainable, which is a stronger argument for changing these two positions than the bass extension is. (b) Two side effects of doubling C: the turn-on charging time constant into a 32 Ohm load goes from 3.2 ms to 7.0 ms, lengthening the transient the LM4853's click-and-pop circuitry has to cover; and polymer tantalum (KO-CAP) is spec'd for materially higher DC leakage than MnO2 tantalum - UNVERIFIED, I did not fetch the KEMET T520 series leakage limit, and at 1.25 V bias on a 6.3 V part any leakage lands in R19/R20 = 1 kOhm so it is almost certainly harmless, but it should be looked up before committing.
findings.correction: Keep the swap exactly as specified - it verifies in full. Delete the CP1 justification: SNAS155E states 'Amplifier A2 is shut down to a high output impedance state in SE mode. This prevents any current flow into the mono bridge-tied load', so CP1 carries no DC in either mode and the 156 mA figure is impossible; leave CP1 alone for the stated speaker-bandwidth reason only. Add the real headline argument the finding missed: TPSB107K010R0400 is down to 5 pieces at DigiKey, so these two positions need re-sourcing regardless. Add two caveats: turn-on time constant into 32 Ohm goes 3.2 ms -> 7.0 ms, and polymer-tantalum DC leakage is spec'd looser than MnO2 (unverified, worth a datasheet check).

findings.title: Half the Sallen-Key capacitors are X7R and half are C0G — making the four X7R ones C0G removes up to 0.6 dB of Q-tolerance peaking for about 12 cents
findings.current_part: C24 and C32 = KEMET C0603C102K5RACTU, 1000 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603. C28 and C35 = KEMET C0603C332K5RACTU, 3300 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603. Their partners in the same filter sections are ALREADY C0G: C26/C31 = C0603C681J5GACTU (680 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%) and C27/C33 = C0603C331J5GACTU (330 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%). All part numbers read directly out of the DigiKey source links embedded in Audio.kicad_sch. The X7R parts are the Sallen-Key FEEDBACK capacitors, i.e. exactly the ones that set Q.
findings.proposal: C24/C32 -> KEMET C0603C102J5GACTU (1000 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%, 0603). C28/C35 -> KEMET C0603C332J5GACTU (3300 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%, 0603) — verified on DigiKey: 26,340 in stock, $0.41 @1, $0.157 @100. Same 0603 land, same voltage rating, no schematic change.
findings.benefit: Zero mW; a tolerance and repeatability fix, not a power one. For a unity-gain Sallen-Key, Q is proportional to sqrt(Cfb/Cgnd), so a +10% X7R feedback cap against a -5% C0G shunt cap scales Q by sqrt(1.10/0.95) = 1.076. On the high-Q section that takes Q from 1.312 to 1.412, and the section's peak gain Q/sqrt(1 - 1/(4Q^2)) from 1.419 (+3.04 dB) to 1.510 (+3.58 dB) — about 0.6 dB of extra passband peaking around 14 kHz, plus a comparable f0 shift. C0G's +/-5% and 30 ppm/C also remove the X7R temperature drift (+/-15% over the X7R range) that otherwise detunes the Butterworth alignment as the handheld warms up. BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT THIS IS NOT: I checked whether the X7R parts are a real distortion source and they are not. The AC voltage across a Sallen-Key feedback cap at frequency f is approximately (2*pi*f*R2*Cgnd) x Vout, which at 1 kHz for stage 1 is 2*pi*1000*20000*680p = 8.5% of the output, i.e. about 75 mVrms across a 50 V-rated part — 0.15% of its rating, where X7R's voltage coefficient is nil. So this change fixes a specification inconsistency and about half a dB of response ripple; nobody will hear it. The one unquantified residual is MLCC piezoelectricity — Class II dielectrics are microphonic, and these caps sit on B.Cu about 15 mm from a speaker in a plastic shell — but I have no measured figure for that and will not invent one.
findings.risk: None worth naming. C0G at these values in 0603 50 V is stocked in volume and costs the same order as X7R. The only thing to verify is that a C0G 3300 pF 0603 is physically available in the tolerance you order (J = +/-5% confirmed in stock; F = +/-1% also exists if you want a tighter alignment).
findings.verify_reason:
PARTS: CONFIRMED. I pulled the Source property out of Audio.kicad_sch myself and resolved the links: C24/C32 = https://www.digikey.com/short/377h8558 -> KEMET C0603C102K5RACTU, 1000 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603; C28/C35 = 3p3jj3wt -> C0603C332K5RACTU, 3300 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603; C26/C31 = jm5qjr7w -> C0603C681J5GACTU, 680 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%; C27/C33 use 5ptw22qq, which the finding reads as C0603C331J5GACTU (330 pF C0G) - consistent with the 330p schematic value and the C0G partner pattern. Q ALGEBRA: correct. At the 100-piece break the delta is ~$0.14 per 3300 pF position and ~$0.25-0.35 for all four positions; at qty 1 it is over $1. Still trivial against the board, but say the right number.

EVERYTHING ELSE STANDS, including the refusal to invent a piezoelectricity figure, which is the right call.
findings.correction: Benefit is ~0.27 dB of worst-case passband peaking removed, not ~0.6 dB: with both caps C0G +/-5% the worst-case Q ratio is still sqrt(1.05/0.95) = 1.0515, giving Q = 1.379 and a 3.25 dB peak against the nominal 3.04 dB. The change halves the tolerance-driven peaking rather than eliminating it; the removal of the X7R +/-15% tempco is the more durable half of the benefit. Cost delta is ~$0.25-0.35 for all four positions at the 100-piece break (C0G is ~6x the X7R price), not ~12 cents.

findings.title: The volume pot's track carries 1.25 V DC, which wastes 0.93 mW and makes turning the volume wheel produce an audible thump
findings.current_part: VR2 = Alps Alpine RK10J12R0A0B, 10 kOhm, dual gang (5 pins: ROUT/LOUT hot ends, LIN/RIN wipers, COM), from the DigiKey link in Audio.kicad_sch. Its COM (pin 5) goes to AGND, and its two hot ends (pins 1/2) are driven directly by the U7A and U7B outputs. Those outputs are DC-coupled followers whose inputs are biased at VAUD/2 = 1.25 V by R45/R46 and R49/R50, so both pot tracks sit with 1.25 V across them permanently, and the wiper DC voltage sweeps from 1.25 V at maximum volume to 0 V at minimum. The wipers feed C55/C56 (1 uF X7R, KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU, 16 V) and then R30/R31 (100 k) into the LM4853's inverting inputs, which are virtual grounds at the internal BYPASS half-supply.
findings.proposal: Move the DC block to the input side of the pot: insert two 1 uF caps between the U7A/U7B outputs and VR2 pins 1/2, keeping C55/C56 where they are. The pot track then sits at 0 V DC at every position, the wiper DC never moves, and the DC across C55/C56 is a constant 1.25 V. The new caps see 10 kOhm, giving a corner of 1/(2*pi*10k*1u) = 15.9 Hz, well below CP2/CP3's 22.6-49.7 Hz which dominates the low end anyway. Cost: two 0603 caps and the board area for them, in a region (x 100-127) that is already dense — hence needs-PCB-revision. PARTIAL DROP-IN ALTERNATIVE if you will not respin: change C55/C56 from 1 uF to 0.1 uF. The corner into R30/R31 = 100 k moves from 1.59 Hz to 15.9 Hz (still far below the output-cap corner, so no bandwidth is lost), and the thump's time constant drops from R*C = 0.1 s to 0.01 s. The step AMPLITUDE is unchanged; only its duration and energy fall by 10x, turning a thump into a click.
findings.benefit: Two separate effects, both small but real. (a) POWER: 2 tracks x 1.25 V / 10 kOhm = 250 uA of DC flowing continuously from the op-amp outputs through the pot to AGND, at every volume setting including zero. 250 uA x 3.34 V / 0.90 = 0.93 mW at the battery — 2% of the audio chain's quiescent, i.e. genuinely small, and I am reporting the number precisely so it can be dismissed. (b) QUALITY, which is the real point: because the wiper DC tracks the pot position, moving the volume wheel changes the DC across C55/C56 by up to 1.25 V, and that change has to charge through R30/R31 = 100 k with tau = 0.1 s. The resulting step at the LM4853 output is up to 1.25 V x (Rf/Ri = 0.2) = 0.25 V single-ended, or 0.5 V differential into the 8 Ohm speaker in BTL mode, decaying over ~0.1 s — an audible thump every time the volume is adjusted. The LM4853's click-and-pop suppression does not help here; it covers power-up and mode changes, not input-side DC transients.
findings.risk: Low technically, moderate practically. Adding the two caps needs board space in the densest corner of the layout and changes a net, so it cannot go into an existing build. The 0.1 uF drop-in alternative is free but is a judgement call: some people find a short click more objectionable than a slow thump, and it slightly raises the input-side corner (15.9 Hz, still inaudible against the 22.6-49.7 Hz output cap). Do NOT try to fix this by referencing VR2's COM to a half-supply node instead of AGND — at maximum volume the track carries up to 1.25 Vrms / 10 k = 125 uA of signal current per channel that would have to be sunk by that node, and there is no spare op-amp section (all four of U7 are used) and the LM4853's BYPASS pin is far too high-impedance to do it.
findings.verify_reason:

VR2 (Alps Alpine RK10J12R0A0B, confirmed via https://www.digikey.com/short/zh4rmq4h as 10 kOhm, Active, 2,648 in stock) has pad 1 'ROUT' -> Net-(U7A--), pad 2 'LOUT' -> Net-(U7B--), pads 3/4 the wipers -> /CPU/Audio/LIN and /CPU/Audio/RIN, pad 5 'COM' -> AGND. Net-(U7A--) and Net-(U7B--) are the OUTPUT nodes of the two final unity-gain followers (output tied to inverting input), so the pot's hot ends really are DC-coupled to the op-amp outputs, and the DC there really is 1.25 V, set by R45/R46 and R49/R50 (100k/100k from VAUD to AGND at C25-Pad2 and C29-Pad2) with C24/C26 and C28/C27 blocking DC around both Sallen-Key sections. (2) The RK10J12R0A0B is +/-30% tolerance, so the 250 uA is 190-360 uA and the power figure is 0.7-1.3 mW. Unverified sub-point: DigiKey's page does not state the gang count; the dual-gang assumption on which the 250 uA rests is inferred from the 5-pad symbol (two hot ends, two wipers, one COM) and the stereo function, not from a datasheet.

findings.title: The audio LDO is not the problem it looks like: raising VAUD saves nothing, merging it with VDD2 saves 0.11 mW, and a buck saves 7.9 mW at the cost of the rail that defines the audio
findings.current_part: U4 = NCV8164ASN250T1G (onsemi, TSOP-5/SOT-23-5), fixed 2.5 V. Verified from the datasheet: operating input 1.6 to 5.5 V; output accuracy +/-2% over load and temperature; quiescent current 30 uA typ; standby 0.1 uA; dropout for the 2.5 V variant 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA (113 mV typ for a 3.0 V variant); PSRR 83 dB at 100 Hz, 85 dB at 1 kHz, 80 dB at 10 kHz, 61 dB at 100 kHz; output noise 9 uVrms over 10 Hz to 100 kHz; 300 mA capability. U8, the CPU-core LDO, is the SAME part number producing the same 2.5 V from the same VOUT3. MouseBiteLabs describe the audio as fed from 'a roughly 75% efficient' supply, which is exactly 2.5/3.34 = 74.9%.
findings.proposal: No change. The reasoning, since the reviewer asked what sets 2.5 V and whether the extra LDO is the reason for the loss: (1) 2.5 V is floored by the LM4853's 2.4 V minimum supply and capped by VOUT3 minus the LDO dropout; it also sets the PWM full scale, since U9 buffers the CPU's PWM onto VAUD and therefore VAUD IS the audio DAC's reference voltage. (2) The extra LDO is not the reason for the 25% loss — VDD2 pays the identical 74.9% on the same VOUT3 through an identical NCV8164. Merging U4 into U8 would save only U4's own 30 uA = 0.11 mW at the battery and would put the CPU core's and SRAM's switching current directly onto the audio reference. (3) Raising VAUD to 3.0 V (feasible: 113 mV typ dropout from 3.34 V) improves the LDO's voltage efficiency from 74.9% to 89.8% and SAVES NOTHING, because an LDO passes its load current unchanged: the battery-side cost of a constant-current load is I x 3.34 V / eta_boost regardless of VAUD. It would actively cost power, because the bias networks scale as V/R (0.325 mA -> 0.39 mA) and the class-AB output-stage supply power is Vdd x (2/pi)(Vp/RL), which rises 20% for the same loudness. (4) Replacing U4 with a 2.5 V buck is the only arrangement that actually saves: P_VOUT3 falls from I x 3.34 V to I x 2.5/0.90 = I x 2.78 V, saving I x 0.56 V = 7.1 mW at VOUT3 (7.9 mW at the battery) at the 12.75 mA quiescent, proportionally more with signal.
findings.benefit: 7.9 mW at the battery at idle for the buck option, computed above (12.75 mA x 0.56 V / 0.90). Everything else in this analysis is 0 mW or negative. I am reporting it because 'the audio runs off a 75% efficient supply' invites exactly the wrong fix, and the arithmetic showing why is worth more than another part swap: the audio's battery cost is set by its CURRENT, not by the LDO's voltage ratio, which is precisely why the u7-tlv9364-out-of-spec finding above (an 8.25 mA current reduction) is worth four times more than replacing the LDO with a switcher.
findings.risk: The buck option is rejected, not recommended, and the reason is specific rather than general: VAUD is the full-scale reference for U9's PWM re-buffering, so any ripple on VAUD multiplies the audio signal directly — it is amplitude modulation, not additive noise, and it is not attenuated by anything downstream. The NCV8164's 85 dB at 1 kHz / 80 dB at 10 kHz PSRR and 9 uVrms output noise is what buys the AGBM's 'crystal clear audio' claim, and 9 uVrms against a 0.884 Vrms full scale is a -99.8 dB floor. A buck would also need an inductor in a shell that has no room and would sit near the ClockxControl window. Also worth knowing: the ClockxControl's extra 40-60 mA on VOUT3 raises the LTC3527's output ripple, but with 80 dB of LDO rejection at 10 kHz and the boost switching well above the audio band, that does not reach the audio — I checked and there is nothing to fix.
findings.verify_reason:
THE REASONING IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN THE SET AND IS CORRECT; ONE NUMBER IS WRONG. NCV8164 verified from the onsemi datasheet: operating input 1.6-5.5 V; output accuracy +/-2% over 0.1-300 mA and temperature; TSOP-5 dropout 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA for the 2.5 V option and 113 mV typ / 177 mV max for the 3.0 V option; IQ 30 uA typ / 40 uA max; PSRR 83/85/80/61 dB at 100 Hz / 1 kHz / 10 kHz / 100 kHz; output noise 9 uVrms over 10 Hz-100 kHz; 300 mA. TWO SPEC NITS: shutdown current is 0.01 uA typ / 1.5 uA max, not the 'standby 0.1 uA' quoted; and the PSRR and noise numbers are specified at VOUT(NOM) = 3.3 V, IOUT = 10 mA, not at 2.5 V, so quoting them for VAUD is optimistic by an unstated margin. From the netlist I confirmed U4 and U8 are both NCV8164ASN250T1G fed from VOUT3 (U4: pin 1 VOUT3, pin 5 VAUD; U8: pin 1 VOUT3, pin 5 VDD2), so the 'VDD2 pays the identical 74.9%' argument holds. 2.5/3.34 = 74.9%, matching MouseBiteLabs' 'roughly 75% efficient' quote. Merging U4 into U8 saves 30 uA x 3.34 / 0.90 = 0.111 mW - correct. The raising-VAUD analysis is correct and is the most useful paragraph here: an LDO passes its load current unchanged so the battery cost is I x 3.34 / eta regardless of VAUD, and going to 3.0 V would actively cost, because V/R bias currents scale up 20% and class-AB supply power Vdd x (2/pi)(Vp/RL) scales up 20% for the same loudness.

REVISED ON THE BUCK NUMBER. 7.9 mW rests entirely on 12.75 mA of VAUD quiescent, which in turn rests on 10.4 mA of TLV9364 current - and TI's own IQ-vs-supply curve (SBOSAD6B Fig 5-22, digitised: 1.32 mA/amp at its lowest plotted point ~2.65 V, ~1.13 mA extrapolated to 2.5 V) puts the op-amps at ~5.2 mA, giving a VAUD quiescent of ~7.5 mA. Redoing the finding's own arithmetic: 7.5 mA x (3.34 - 2.5/0.90) = 7.5 mA x 0.56 V = 4.2 mW at VOUT3, /0.90 = 4.7 mW at the battery, not 7.9 mW. Its closing claim that the U7 swap is 'worth four times more than replacing the LDO with a switcher' also shrinks: 9.8 mW vs 4.7 mW is 2.1x, not 4x - the ranking survives, the ratio does not.

ONE ARGUMENT IS INCOMPLETE. 'The ClockxControl's extra 40-60 mA on VOUT3 raises the LTC3527's output ripple, but with 80 dB of LDO rejection at 10 kHz and the boost switching well above the audio band, that does not reach the audio - I checked and there is nothing to fix.' The boost's SWITCHING frequency is not the whole story. From the netlist MODE = GND and FSEL = GND, and the LTC3527 datasheet says FSEL = 0 V gives 0.9/1.2/1.5 MHz and 'With the MODE pin low, the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 will automatically enter Burst Mode operation at light load'. In Burst Mode the BURST REPETITION rate varies with load and routinely falls inside the audio band, which is the classic mechanism for audible converter noise. The conclusion still survives - burst ripple sits at frequencies where the NCV8164's PSRR is at its best (83-85 dB), so tens of mV of VOUT3 ripple become sub-microvolt on VAUD - but it survives on the 100 Hz-1 kHz PSRR figure, not on the 80 dB @ 10 kHz figure the finding quoted, and the finding should say which mechanism it checked.

The rejection of the buck on the merits (VAUD is the full-scale reference for U9's re-buffered PWM, so ripple on it is multiplicative AM that nothing downstream attenuates; no room for an inductor) is correct and well argued.
findings.correction: Buck-instead-of-LDO saving is 4.7 mW at the battery, not 7.9 mW: the VAUD quiescent is ~7.5 mA, not 12.75 mA, once the TLV9364's IQ at 2.5 V is taken from TI's IQ-vs-supply curve (~1.2 mA/amp) instead of the 4.5 V-and-above 2.6 mA spec. 7.5 mA x 0.56 V = 4.2 mW at VOUT3, /0.90 = 4.7 mW. The U7 swap therefore beats it by 2.1x, not 4x. Fix two spec quotes: NCV8164 shutdown current is 0.01 uA typ (1.5 uA max), and its PSRR/noise numbers are specified at VOUT = 3.3 V, IOUT = 10 mA. Re-argue the boost-ripple dismissal on low-frequency PSRR (83-85 dB): MODE = GND enables Burst Mode, whose repetition rate - not the 1.2 MHz switching frequency - is what can land in the audio band.

findings.title: The LM4853 is running 50 mV above its absolute minimum supply and 200 mV below its lowest characterised point
findings.current_part: LM4853MM/NOPB, SNAS155E Operating Ratings: supply voltage 2.4 V <= VDD <= 5.5 V. The datasheet's Electrical Characteristics tables are given at 5.0 V, 3.3 V and 2.7 V only — there is no characterisation at 2.5 V. VAUD is 2.5 V nominal with +/-2% accuracy over load and temperature from the NCV8164, so the worst-case supply at the LM4853 is 2.45 V: 50 mV, or 2%, of margin to the absolute minimum operating rating, and 250 mV below the lowest voltage TI characterises. Extrapolating the datasheet trend (300 mW into 8 Ohm BTL and 25 mW into 32 Ohm SE at 2.7 V), the 2.5 V capability is roughly 250 mW BTL and 21 mW SE.
findings.proposal: Nothing to change, and I checked the alternatives before saying so. Raising VAUD costs power everywhere else (see vaud-rail-voltage-analysis). Replacing the LM4853 is impractical: its function set — mono BTL speaker plus stereo single-ended headphone plus automatic headphone-sense mode switching plus click-and-pop suppression, in a 10-pin 3 x 3 mm package — is unusual, and DigiKey lists LM4853MM/NOPB as Active with 2,871 in stock, so there is no sourcing pressure forcing the issue. What this finding is for is calibration: if a unit ever shows audio misbehaviour that tracks temperature or battery state, this 50 mV is where to look first, and TP22 (labelled BATT in the BOM but wired to VAUD) is the test point for it.
findings.benefit: 0 mW. The practical consequence is bounded and mild, because the gain structure keeps the amplifier nowhere near its limits: at maximum volume with full-scale content the BTL output needs 0.707 Vrms differential (62 mW into 8 Ohm) out of ~250 mW of capability, and the SE headphone output needs 0.177 Vrms (0.98 mW into 32 Ohm) out of ~21 mW. Thermally it is also fine: BTL worst-case internal dissipation is 4 x VDD^2/(2*pi^2*RL) = 4 x 6.25/(19.74 x 8) = 158 mW, which at the DGS package's 194 C/W is a 31 C rise.
findings.risk: The risk is silent, not catastrophic: below 2.4 V the part is simply unspecified, and the failure mode would be increased distortion or a failure to bias rather than damage. Because VAUD comes from a regulated LDO fed by a regulated boost, it does not sag with battery state until the LTC3527 itself drops out, so this is a component-tolerance stack-up risk (LDO at the -2% corner over temperature) rather than an end-of-battery risk.
findings.verify_reason:
I checked every number and found nothing wrong. SNAS155E Operating Ratings: 'Supply Voltage VDD 2.4V <= VDD <= 5.5V' - confirmed, and the Electrical Characteristics really are given at 5.0 V, 3.3 V and 2.7 V only, with no 2.5 V table. NCV8164 output accuracy is +/-2% over load and temperature (onsemi datasheet), so 2.5 V nominal gives 2.45 V worst case: 50 mV / 2% of margin to the absolute minimum, 250 mV below TI's lowest characterised supply, and the title's '200 mV below its lowest characterised point' is the nominal-to-nominal version of the same thing. The V-squared extrapolation checks: (2.5/2.7)^2 x 300 mW = 257 mW BTL ('roughly 250 mW') and x 25 mW = 21.4 mW SE ('roughly 21 mW').

I independently re-derived the gain structure rather than trusting it, and it comes out exactly right - which is notable because the sibling classd-speaker-amp finding contradicts it. From the netlist R30/R31 = 100k into U6 LIN/RIN, R57/R56 = 20k feedback, and SNAS155E's BTL description ('The audio signal from the RIGHT IN pin is directed to the inverting input of A1. As a result, the LEFT IN and RIGHT IN audio signals... are summed together at the input of A1. A2 is then activated with a closed-loop gain of AV = -1 fixed by two internal 20 kOhm resistors'). Full-scale filter output is VAUD/2 = 1.25 Vpk per channel, so A1 = 0.2 x (1.25 + 1.25) = 0.5 Vpk, differential = 1.0 Vpk = 0.707 Vrms, P = 0.707^2/8 = 62.5 mW into 8 Ohm - the finding's number to three figures. SE: 0.2 x 1.25 = 0.25 Vpk = 0.177 Vrms, P = 0.177^2/32 = 0.98 mW into 32 Ohm - also exact. So the amplifier really is running at ~25% of its 2.5 V BTL capability and ~5% of its SE capability, which is what makes the 50 mV of supply margin tolerable.

Thermal: PDMAX = 4 x VDD^2/(2*pi^2*RL) is SNAS155E's own Equation 3, not an invention; 4 x 6.25/(19.74 x 8) = 158 mW, x 194 C/W (theta-JA for DGS, confirmed in the Absolute Maximum Ratings table) = 30.7 C rise. It is worth saying explicitly that 158 mW is the theoretical maximum-dissipation point, which the 0.4 gain structure never reaches - but the finding already frames it as a bound.

Sourcing: DigiKey short r3rqdzt8 -> LM4853MM/NOPB, Active, 2,871 in stock, $2.92@1 - the stock figure is exactly as claimed. TP22: the BOM row reads Value 'BATT' but net VAUD, and pinout.py TP22 confirms its single pad is on VAUD - a genuine silkscreen/BOM inconsistency that deserves a correctness note of its own, and the finding is right that TP22 is where to measure this.

The reasoning that this is a component-tolerance stack-up risk rather than an end-of-battery risk (VAUD comes from a regulated LDO off a regulated boost) is correct. 0 mW, correctly stated.

findings.title: Replacing the crystal with the ClockxControl puts the module's clock jitter straight onto the audio PWM edges
findings.current_part: The GBA's audio is pulse-width modulation: per GBATEK, in the default 9-bit / 32.768 kHz mode each sample N (0-511) is emitted as N low bits followed by (512-N) high bits at 16.78 MHz, so the audio sample value is encoded purely as an EDGE POSITION within a 30.5 us frame, quantised in 59.6 ns steps. U9 (SN74LVC2G34, tpd 1.5 ns typ / 4.4 ns max at VCC = 2.5 V per SCES359J) faithfully re-times those edges onto VAUD. On the fork X1, C3 and C4 are depopulated and /CPU/CK1 is driven by the ClockxControl instead, so the timing reference for those edges is now whatever the module generates rather than a 4.194304 MHz crystal.
findings.proposal: No board change; a measurement to make. Because the full-scale pulse width is 512 x 59.6 ns = 30.5 us, an RMS edge jitter of dt translates to an amplitude error of dt / 30.5 us relative to full scale: 1 ns RMS gives a -89.6 dB noise floor, 5 ns gives -75.7 dB, 10 ns gives -69.7 dB. A crystal contributes picoseconds and is irrelevant; a PLL- or DDS-based clock module can contribute nanoseconds, and if its jitter is correlated (PLL reference spurs) it appears as discrete tones rather than a noise floor. If the audio floor is audibly worse with JP3 closed than with the crystal fitted, this is the mechanism.
findings.benefit: 0 mW.
