UNVERIFIED — I could not find a published jitter specification for the insideGadgets ClockxControl, so the 1/5/10 ns figures above are illustrative scalings of the transfer function, not a claim about the module. The transfer function itself (edge jitter -> amplitude error = dt/30.5 us) follows directly from the GBATEK-documented PWM encoding and is solid.
findings.risk: If real, it degrades the AGBM's headline audio quality specifically when the ClockxControl is engaged, which would be blamed on the audio chain rather than on the clock source. It costs nothing to check: compare the noise floor at TP115/TP114 (the CPU's L-OUT/R-OUT) or at the headphone jack with JP3 open (crystal) versus closed (module) at 1x.
findings.verify_reason:
THE PREMISE IS SOLID BUT THE TRANSFER FUNCTION IS THE WRONG ONE. Confirmed groundwork: GBATEK (fetched from problemkaputt.de) states the PWM runs at the 16.78 MHz system clock with 512 bits per sample and 'N low bits, followed by 512-N high bits', so the sample value really is encoded purely as an edge position in a 30.5 us frame quantised in 59.6 ns steps. U9 is SN74LVC2G34DBVR on VAUD (verified from the netlist: 1A/2A from /CPU/Audio/L-OUT and R-OUT, VCC = VAUD, GND = AGND). Its timing: SCES359J Switching Characteristics give tpd at VCC = 2.5 V +/- 0.2 V as 1.5 ns MIN / 4.4 ns MAX over -40 to +85 C - the finding calls 1.5 ns 'typ', but the datasheet publishes no typ for tpd, it is the minimum limit. Small mislabel, no consequence, since propagation delay is common-mode to both edges anyway.

THE ARITHMETIC AS STATED IS RIGHT: 1 ns / 30.5 us = 3.28e-5 = -89.7 dB; 5 ns = -75.7 dB; 10 ns = -69.7 dB. But that is the sensitivity to PULSE-WIDTH error, not to clock jitter, and the finding conflates them. The pulse width is an integer number of clock periods, so the width error is the accumulation of period jitter over the N <= 512 clocks that make up the pulse: for uncorrelated period jitter sigma_T the width error is sigma_T x sqrt(N), i.e. up to sqrt(512) = 22.6 x sigma_T at full scale, and for the correlated low-frequency jitter a PLL actually produces it tends toward N x sigma_T. So a module with 1 ns RMS PERIOD jitter does not land at -89.7 dB; it lands somewhere between -89.7 dB and roughly 27 dB worse. The stated scaling is defensible only if the input quantity is relabelled as RMS pulse-width error. Separately, the finding is right that a constant frequency error produces only pitch shift, since both the pulse and the 512-clock frame scale together - and it correctly attributes that to ClockxControl rather than to the board.

WHAT IT ADMITS AND SHOULD: no published jitter spec for the insideGadgets ClockxControl was found, so the 1/5/10 ns figures are illustrative. Self-assigned confidence 0.4 is honest.

ONE DOCUMENTATION GAP: the finding (and the context pack) state that X1, C3 and C4 are depopulated on the fork. That is the intended build, but it is not encoded in the board file - X1 (AGB-Crystal, /CPU/CK1 and Net-(C4-Pad1)), C3 (27p) and C4 (33p) all appear in the BOM with no (dnp yes) flag in AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb, while JP3 (pad 1 = /CPU/CK1, pad 2 = CXC_CLK) and MOD1 are excluded from BOM. Anyone building from the file as-is would fit the crystal and drive CK1 from two sources. That is worth flagging as a correctness item in its own right, and it is also the thing that makes the finding's proposed A/B test (JP3 open = crystal, closed = module) possible or not.

Kept as a flag, not a change. Revised for the transfer-function mislabel.
findings.correction: Relabel the input quantity: dt/30.5 us is the sensitivity to RMS PULSE-WIDTH error, not to clock edge jitter. Because the pulse is an integer number of clock periods, period jitter sigma_T accumulates over the N <= 512 clocks in the pulse - sigma_T x sqrt(512) = 22.6 x sigma_T for uncorrelated jitter, and closer to N x sigma_T for the correlated jitter a PLL produces - so 1 ns of module period jitter is worse than the quoted -89.7 dB by up to ~27 dB. Also: SCES359J's 1.5 ns at VCC = 2.5 V is the MIN limit, not a typ (no typ is published). Add the documentation defect: X1, C3 and C4 are not flagged dnp in AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb even though the build requires them depopulated.

findings.title: U8 (NCV8164, VDD2) has ~3.5x current margin and ~4x thermal margin at 1.75x — it is not the bottleneck
findings.current_part: U8 = NCV8164ASN250T1G, TSOP-5 (SOT-23-5 land), 2.5 V fixed, VIN = VOUT3 = 3.336 V. Verified from onsemi NCV8164/D rev.5: rated 300 mA; output current limit ICL 350 mA min / 560 mA typ at VOUT = 90 % VOUT(NOM); short-circuit current 580 mA; dropout for the 2.5 V variant in TSOP-5 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA; IQ 30 µA typ / 40 µA max at IOUT = 0; TSOP-5 thermal resistance RθJA = 158 °C/W (JEDEC 51.7 high-K board), RθJC(bot) 102 °C/W; TJ(max) 150 °C, datasheet recommends limiting TJ to 125 °C; thermal shutdown 165 °C; stable with any ceramic ≥ 1 µF with no minimum ESR and no stated maximum.
findings.proposal: No change. Keep U8 as fitted. The analysis: worst-case VDD2 draw at 1.75x is CPU core + SRAM = ~82 mA (see measured_anchors), i.e. 27 % of the 300 mA rating and 23 % of the 350 mA guaranteed current limit. If the true in-use I_VDD2 at 1x were double my estimate (94 mA rather than 47 mA), 1.75x would still only reach 165 mA and the part would still be inside its rating.
findings.benefit: Not an efficiency finding — this is the go/no-go answer. Current: I_VDD2(1.75x, game) = 1.75 × 47 mA = 82 mA vs a 300 mA rating and a 350 mA min current limit → 3.6x margin. Dropout: headroom is VOUT3 − VDD2 = 3.336 − 2.500 = 0.836 V; the 2.5 V part's dropout is 200 mV max at 300 mA, so at 82 mA (roughly proportional, ~55 mV) VOUT3 could sag to ~2.56 V before the LDO fell out of regulation — 780 mV of slack. Thermal, in a SOT-23-5: PD = (VIN − VOUT)·IOUT + VIN·IGND = 0.836 × 0.082 + 3.336 × 40 µA = 68.6 + 0.13 = 68.7 mW. ΔTj = 68.7 mW × 158 °C/W = 10.9 °C. Inside a sealed GBA shell take TA = 45 °C → Tj = 56 °C against a 125 °C recommended limit. At 1.75x idle (52.5 mA) it is PD = 43.9 mW, ΔTj = 6.9 °C. Even at the full 300 mA rating PD = 250.8 mW and ΔTj = 39.6 °C, so the part would still be inside spec at a 45 °C ambient. Output capacitance on VDD2 is ~14 µF nominal (C60 10 µF + 4×1 µF + 5×0.1 µF); the datasheet states stability with ceramics of '1 µF or greater' with no upper bound, so that is fine.
findings.risk: The residual risk is entirely in the I_VDD2 estimate, which is derived from the 170 mW idle figure and not measured. To close it, put a Fluke on TP18 (VDD2) — it is a plated test point — and read the current at 1x and at 1.75x with a game running. If I_VDD2 at 1.75x turns out above ~250 mA the picture changes, but nothing in the measured board power leaves room for that: 250 mA on VDD2 alone would be 625 mW, more than half the entire 1175 mW worst-case console power.
findings.verify_reason: Every NCV8164 number checks out against the onsemi datasheet (read the repo's cached ncv8164.pdf and independently confirmed the part on onsemi's product page, which lists NCV8164ASN250T1G as Active, 300 mA LDO). Verified line by line: 300 mA rating; ICL 350 mA min / 560 mA typ at VOUT = 90% VOUT(NOM); ISC 580 mA; dropout for the 2.5 V TSOP-5 variant 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA (the '110 mV' headline on p.1 is the 3.3 V variant, and the finding correctly did NOT use it); IQ 30 uA typ / 40 uA max at IOUT = 0; RthJA 158 C/W and RthJC(bot) 102 C/W for TSOP-5; TJ(max) 150 C with 'For reliable operation junction temperature should be limited to +125 C'; TSD 165 C; 'does not require a minimum ESR... stable with standard ceramics with values of 1 uF or greater'. Ordering table confirms ASN250T1G = 2.5 V, TSOP-5, with active output discharge, which drops on the BOM's SOT-23-5 land. Netlist independently confirms VDD2 carries only CPU core (U1 pins 44/65/115/117), SRAM (U2 pins 12/16/37), R8 100k, JP2 pad 2 and TP18 - so 'CPU core + SRAM' is the complete load. Arithmetic redone: PD = 0.836 x 0.082 = 68.55 mW, +0.13 mW ground term = 68.7 mW; 68.7 mW x 158 C/W = 10.9 C; at 300 mA PD = 250.8 mW, dTj = 39.6 C. All correct. Two nits that do not move the conclusion: (a) IQ 30/40 uA is specified at IOUT = 0 mA, and true ground current at 82 mA is higher, though for this PMOS topology still negligible against the 68.6 mW pass-element term; (b) the 47 mA I_VDD2 anchor is unmeasured and I would put its uncertainty nearer +/-50% than +/-20% - at 30 mA idle the LDO's 100 mW input is already 59% of the whole 170 mW idle board, which is high but not impossible. The conclusion is robust to all of that: even at 3x the assumed current the part is inside its 300 mA rating and its thermal limit.

findings.title: The constrained node is VOUT3, not the LDO: LTC3527 converter 2 (the 400 mA channel) carries all three logic rails while the 800 mA channel drives only the screen
findings.current_part: U5 = LTC3527, dual synchronous boost, QFN-16. Verified from ADI 35271fc: title 'Dual 800mA/400mA'; features 'Delivers 3.3V at 200mA/100mA from one Alkaline/NiMH Cell, or 3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells'; NMOS current limit SW1 = 800 mA (min, tested over temperature), NMOS current limit SW2 = 400 mA (min); NMOS/PMOS on-resistance SW1 0.30/0.40 Ω, SW2 0.50/0.60 Ω; MODE = Low is automatic Burst Mode, FSEL = Low is 1.2 MHz. On this board MODE and FSEL are both tied to GND, so it is 1.2 MHz auto-Burst. From the netlist: U5 pad 5 (VOUT1, converter 1) = VOUT5 → U11 → VDD5 → LCD FFC pin 34 (VSHA) and cart pad S2, nothing else. U5 pad 8 (VOUT2, converter 2) = VOUT3 → U8 (VDD2), U4 (VAUD) and U18 (VDD3). So the weaker channel carries CPU core, SRAM, all 3.3 V logic, the cartridge and the audio chain.
findings.proposal: No part change proposed — I checked the obvious one and it is wrong. Swapping the channel assignment (VOUT3 onto converter 1) looks attractive until you account for the screen: the measured spread between minimum and maximum brightness is 568→1175 mW at the battery, i.e. roughly 600 mW of backlight, which at 5.014 V is ~120–160 mA on VOUT5. Converter 1 at VIN 2.4 V is needed for that. The assignment as drawn is correct. What is actionable is documentation and a measurement: build sheet should state that a 1.75x build on 2×AA NiMH is operating converter 2 near its guaranteed limit at end of discharge, and TP16 (VOUT3) should be scoped for regulation loss under a worst-case load before anyone declares the mod stable. Raising L1/L2 above 4.7 µH would buy headroom (see benefit) but belongs to the passives reviewer and fights the LTC3527's internal compensation.
findings.benefit: Headroom arithmetic, guaranteed-silicon basis. Boost peak inductor current = Iin + ΔI/2, with Iin = Iout·VOUT/(η·VIN) and ΔI = VIN·D/(L·f), D = 1 − VIN/VOUT, L = 4.7 µH, f = 1.2 MHz, η = 0.9, VOUT = 3.336 V. At VIN = 2.4 V: D = 0.2805, ΔI = 119 mA, ΔI/2 = 60 mA, so Iin(max) = 400 − 60 = 340 mA and Iout(max) = 340 × 0.9 × 2.4/3.336 = 220 mA. At VIN = 2.0 V (the TPS3840DL20 cutoff): D = 0.4005, ΔI = 142 mA, Iin(max) = 329 mA, Iout(max) = 178 mA. At VIN = 3.2 V (fresh alkalines): 335 mA. This model reproduces the datasheet's own '3.3 V at 200 mA from two cells' headline, and the datasheet's Figure G11 (Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2) read off the VOUT = 3.3 V curve gives ~200 mA at 1.8 V, ~230 mA at 2.0 V, ~290 mA at 2.4 V — i.e. typical silicon is ~30 % above my min-spec numbers, as expected. Against that, my estimated VOUT3 draw at 1.75x: VDD2 82 mA + VAUD 15–40 mA + VDD3 (CPU I/O + logic + cart through VDD35) 37–60 mA + ClockxControl 12 mA = 146 mA typical to 194 mA worst case. So at 2.4 V there is 12–34 % margin on guaranteed silicon, and at the 2.0 V cutoff the worst case is over budget by ~10 %. Note the same worst case at 1x is ~147 mA, so the overclock is what consumes the last of the margin. Sizing L2 up from 4.7 µH to 10 µH would cut ΔI/2 from 60 to 28 mA and raise Iout(max) at 2.4 V from 220 to 241 mA (+10 %), at the cost of DCR and a part the LTC3527 is not compensated for.
findings.risk: Running converter 2 into current limit does not blow anything up — it drops out of regulation, VOUT3 sags, and VDD3 follows it directly (U18 is a switch, not a regulator). VDD2 rides it down until VOUT3 reaches ~2.56 V, so the CPU core survives longer than its I/O does; the symptom would be an I/O-level brown-out (cartridge read errors, then reset) near the end of the battery, at max volume, at max speed, under a demanding game — a combination that is hard to reproduce deliberately and easy to blame on the cart. My VOUT3 numbers are a build-up of estimates: the cartridge current in particular is unverified, and an Everdrive could plausibly be 30 mA or 80 mA. Confidence is set accordingly.
findings.verify_reason: The hardware facts are all correct and I reproduced them. LTC3527 datasheet (ADI 35271fc): title 'Dual 800mA/400mA, 1.2MHz/2.2MHz'; feature bullet 'Delivers 3.3V at 200mA/100mA from one Alkaline/NiMH Cell, or 3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells'; NMOS current limit SW1 800 mA / SW2 400 mA carrying the boldface-dot marker (guaranteed over -40..85 C) - and Figure G17 'Current Limit vs Temperature' shows CONVERTER1 ~1.2 A and CONVERTER2 ~0.61 A typical, which proves 800/400 are MIN not TYP; RDS(on) 0.30/0.40 (SW1) and 0.50/0.60 ohm (SW2); FB = 1.176/1.20/1.224 V, which is what makes VOUT3 = 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V and VOUT5 = 1.20 x 4.1786 = 5.014 V; FSEL = 0 V gives 1.2 MHz typ; MODE = Low is automatic Burst Mode. Netlist confirms U5 pad 3 (MODE) and pad 10 (FSEL) on GND, pad 5 (VOUT1) = VOUT5, pad 8 (VOUT2) = VOUT3, and that VOUT3 feeds U8, U4 and U18. The peak-current model is correct: D = 0.2805, dI = 2.4 x 0.2805 / (4.7u x 1.2M) = 119 mA, Iin(max) = 340 mA, Iout = 340 x 0.9 x 2.4/3.336 = 220 mA; at 2.0 V, 178 mA. Figure G11 exists and reads roughly as claimed. ADI lists LTC3527 as PRODUCTION. What does NOT survive is the load budget and therefore the risk claim.
findings.correction: Four corrections. (1) The load budget is internally inconsistent with the measured envelope. Taking the finding's own two estimates together - VOUT5 at 120-160 mA and VOUT3 at 146-147 mA at 1x - gives 602-802 mW + 487-490 mW = 1089-1292 mW delivered, i.e. 1238-1469 mW at the battery after the 88% boost, against a MEASURED maximum console power of 1175 mW. The worst case as constructed cannot happen. (2) '600 mW of backlight' over-attributes the 568->1175 mW spread: that spread also contains the audio (MouseBiteLabs' own figure, 50-100 mW at max volume) and the Everdrive-vs-OEM-cart delta. Backlight is more like 380-480 mW at the battery = 75-95 mA on VOUT5, which leaves 130-160 mA for VOUT3 at 1x - so the finding's VOUT3 number is roughly right but only because its VOUT5 number is wrong in the opposite direction. Net: 1x worst-case VOUT3 is somewhere in 105-160 mA and the wiki data cannot pin it down further. (3) Typical silicon is ~53% above min, not ~30%: Figure G17 puts converter 2's current limit at ~610 mA typ, which by the same model gives Iout(max) ~356 mA at VIN 2.4 V. The margin problem exists only for worst-case min-spec parts. (4) The '2.0 V cutoff, over budget by ~10%' case is at the TPS3840DL20's own threshold - I confirmed on TI's product page that the '20' suffix is a 2.0 V VIT-, and /EN from U3 gates U5 SHDN2 - so the console is milliseconds from shutting down anyway. Corrected statement: at 2.4 V converter 2 has roughly 25-40% margin on guaranteed silicon and about 2x on typical silicon; the guaranteed-limit budget only closes in the last moments of pack life. The actionable part (scope TP16 under worst case; document that a 1.75x build loads the weaker channel) stands. Two small factual slips: VOUT5 also feeds U14, R10, R18, R25, R65, R66, and VDD5 also feeds Q6's gate and R26 - not 'nothing else'.

findings.title: U8's 0.836 V drop is the single biggest recoverable loss the overclock creates — a buck on VDD2 wins back 21 mW at 1x and 49 mW at 1.75x
findings.current_part: U8 = NCV8164ASN250T1G, a linear regulator dropping VOUT3 3.336 V to VDD2 2.500 V. Its loss is exactly (VIN − VOUT) × IOUT + VIN × IGND; with IQ 30 µA typ (onsemi NCV8164/D) the ground-current term is 0.10 mW and can be ignored. So the loss is 0.836 V × I_VDD2, i.e. 25.1 % of every watt VDD2 consumes, unconditionally. Note this is not the audio LDO — MouseBiteLabs explicitly defends U4/VAUD as a deliberate noise-driven choice ('roughly 75 % efficient ... specifically for the audio'). U8 feeds the digital core and SRAM, where switching ripple is far less consequential.
findings.proposal: TPS62840DLC. Verified from TI SLVSEC6D (rev. D, March 2020): 'Input voltage range VIN from 1.8 V to 6.5 V', 'Output current up to 750 mA', '60-nA operating quiescent current', typical switching frequency 1.8 MHz, 16 output voltages selected by one resistor on VSET; the Device Comparison Table gives TPS62840DLC as '1.8 V to 3.3 V in 100-mV steps', and the RSET table lists 2.5 V for the DLC part at RSET = 11.5 kΩ nominal (E96, 11.04 k min / 11.96 k max). Package DLC = 8-pin SON, 1.5 × 2 mm — smaller than the NCV8164's SOT-23-5 land, but not on the same pads. External parts needed: a 2.2 µH inductor, and input/output ceramics — of which the board already has 43 µF nominal on VOUT3 (C42 22 µF + C2 10 µF + C23 10 µF + C22 1 µF) and ~14 µF on VDD2 (C60 + 4×1 µF + 5×0.1 µF), so realistically the only genuinely new part is the inductor. Precedent for a switcher on this rail: Zekfoo's AGZ GBA redesign states 'the 3.3V and 2.5V rails are generated by buck converters'.
findings.benefit: At the operating point that matters. TI's Figure 22 (Efficiency, Power Save Mode, VOUT = 1.8 V) shows the VIN = 3.6 V curve sitting at ~87–89 % from 10 mA to 100 mA; our conversion is 3.336 → 2.500 V, a gentler 0.75 duty ratio than 3.6 → 1.8, so ≥89 % is a conservative read. The exact 3.34 → 2.5 V curve is not published, so 89 % is an interpolation, not a datasheet point. Arithmetic, all at VOUT3 then referred to the battery at the boost's 88 %: (a) 1x, in use, I_VDD2 = 47 mA → LDO input 156.8 mW, loss 39.3 mW; buck output 117.5 mW, input 132.0 mW, loss 14.5 mW; saving 24.8 mW at VOUT3 = 28.2 mW at the battery. (b) 1x idle, I_VDD2 = 30 mA → LDO loss 25.1 mW, buck loss 9.3 mW, saving 15.8 mW = 18.0 mW at the battery, which is 10.6 % of the entire measured 170 mW idle figure and roughly half of AGBM-01's 36 mW idle gap to a stock GBA. (c) 1.75x idle, 52.5 mA → LDO loss 43.9 mW, buck loss 16.2 mW, saving 27.7 mW = 31.5 mW at the battery. (d) 1.75x in a game, 82 mA → LDO loss 68.6 mW, buck loss 25.3 mW, saving 43.3 mW = 49.2 mW at the battery. Against a total overclock cost of ~146 mW at the battery (module 45.5 mW + console ~100 mW), (d) recovers about a third of it. Second-order benefit: it also gives back 13 mA of VOUT3 current at the worst case, which is exactly the margin the previous finding says is running out.
findings.risk: This is the invasive one. It needs a schematic change (new part, new VSET resistor, an inductor, different pinout) and a PCB revision on a board with no free area — and the one component-free window on the front is now spoken for by the ClockxControl itself. It puts a 1.8 MHz switcher on the CPU core rail: with 11 decoupling caps already on VDD2 that should be fine, and AGZ does exactly this, but it is a change from a field-proven arrangement on an irreplaceable salvaged CPU. It also overlaps the passives/power-tree reviewer's territory — the same argument applies to the AGBM-01-vs-AGBM-02 converter question and should be resolved once, not twice. Sourcing: TPS62840DLC is a current TI part in a 1.5 × 2 mm SON, which is harder to hand-solder than a SOT-23-5 and is a real cost for a hobbyist build. My benefit numbers inherit the ±20 % uncertainty in I_VDD2 and the interpolated 89 % efficiency.
findings.verify_reason: The proposal as scoped is not buildable, for a reason the finding never mentions: U8's PGOOD pin is the board's master power sequencer, and the TPS62840 has no power-good output. I dumped the net: /PG_2V5 has six pads - U8 pad 4 (PGOOD, open-drain), R8 100k pull-up to VDD2, U4 pad 3 (SHDN of the VAUD LDO), U5 pad 1 (SHDN1, the 5 V screen boost), U18 pad 3 (ON, the VDD3 load switch), and TP30. So U8's power-good is what starts VDD3, VDD5 and VAUD. The TPS62840 pin list in SLVSEC6D is VIN, SW, GND, VSET, VOS, EN, STOP, MODE - no PG - and TI's product page confirms no power-good pin on any of the three packages. Drop a TPS62840 in for U8 and nothing downstream ever enables; the console does not boot. Everything else about the part checks out: SLVSEC6D rev D (June 2019, revised March 2020) gives VIN 1.8-6.5 V, up to 750 mA, 60 nA operating IQ, DLC = SON-8 1.5 x 2 mm, 16 output voltages via one VSET resistor, TPS62840 = 1.8-3.3 V in 100 mV steps, and the RSET table row 11.04k/11.5k/11.96k -> 2.5 V. TI lists it ACTIVE. The Zekfoo AGZ quote is accurate - I fetched the README and it says verbatim 'the 3.3V and 2.5V rails are generated by buck converters'. The NCV8164 loss model is right. The direction of the finding - a buck on VDD2 recovers a real, unconditional 25% of everything VDD2 consumes - is correct and is the largest single lever in this domain.
findings.correction: Three corrections. (1) SCOPE: 'realistically the only genuinely new part is the inductor' is false. You also need a supervisor to replace U8's PGOOD (a second TPS3840 plus its pull-up, since /PG_2V5 gates U4, U18 and U5 SHDN1), an RSET resistor, and a 1.5 x 2 mm SON-8 land - on a board whose one component-free window is now occupied by the ClockxControl. (2) EFFICIENCY BASIS IS WRONG BUT CONSERVATIVE: the claim that 'the exact 3.34 -> 2.5 V curve is not published' is incorrect - SLVSEC6D Figure 18 is 'Efficiency Power Save Mode, VOUT = 2.5 V, RSET = 11.5 kOhm' with VIN = 2.5/3.0/3.6/4.2/5.0/6.5 V curves; Figure 22 (VOUT = 1.8 V) was the wrong figure to interpolate from. Reading Figure 18 between the VIN = 3.0 V and 3.6 V curves at 30-100 mA gives ~91-93%, not 89%. (3) NUMBERS: redone at 93%: 1x idle (30 mA) LDO loss 25.1 mW vs buck loss 5.6 mW = 19.5 mW saved at VOUT3 = 22.2 mW at the battery; 1.75x in-game (82 mA) LDO 68.6 mW vs buck 15.4 mW = 53.2 mW = 60.5 mW at the battery. So the saving is LARGER than claimed, conditional on the unmeasured 30/47/82 mA anchors. Also flag: the headline '21 mW at 1x' matches neither of the finding's own 1x cases (18.0 mW idle, 28.2 mW in use). Unconsidered risks: a 1.8 MHz buck on VDD2 beating against the LTC3527's 1.2 MHz on VOUT3 gives a 600 kHz difference tone in a console whose designer went to the trouble of a dedicated LDO for the audio rail; and the LDO's 9 uVrms output noise is replaced by PFM ripple on the salvaged CPU's core rail.

findings.title: insideGadgets' 40–60 mA is a system-level figure with no rail attribution, no speed and no measurement point — and it is quoted identically for DMG, GBC and GBA
findings.current_part: insideGadgets' product page, verbatim and complete, is one sentence: 'Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more.' Grammatically 'it' is the console, not the module. There is no statement of where the current was measured, at what speed, with what cartridge or screen fitted, or on which rail. The same number is given for the DMG (whose firmware goes to 3x), the GBC (2x) and the GBA (1.75x) — three different CPUs on three different rails, which alone is enough to treat it as an order-of-magnitude figure. I fetched the page directly (WebFetch returns 403; a plain curl with a browser user-agent returns 200) rather than relying on a search snippet.
findings.proposal: Split it into the two rails it actually lands on, which the netlist settles unambiguously. (1) The module's own ~12 mA: V+ is specified as 'GBA SI', which is the pad silkscreened S1, and on all three AGBM variants P1 pad S1 is on net VDD3. So the module's 12 mA is on VDD3, switched by U18 off VOUT3. (2) The overclock's extra current is not the module's at all — it is the console's own dynamic power, which lives on VDD2 (CPU core pins 44/65/115/117 and SRAM pins 12/16/37) and on VDD3 (CPU I/O pins 1/103/124 plus the cartridge, which reaches the cart through the CPU's VDD35 pin). Both rails sit under VOUT3, so all of it is converter 2's problem. Nothing lands on VOUT5/VDD5 except through the screen.
findings.benefit: Reconciliation, which is the point of the finding. Module, at 1x: 12 mA × 3.335 V = 40.0 mW at VDD3; at the boost's 88 %, 45.5 mW at the battery = 19.0 mA at 2.4 V. That is +27 % on the measured 170 mW idle before a single clock is added. Overclock, from my own per-rail model: ΔI_VDD2 = 0.75 × 30 mA = 22.5 mA, which the LDO passes 1:1 to VOUT3 → 22.5 × 3.336 = 75.1 mW → 85.3 mW at the battery; plus VDD3 I/O dynamic ~3.6 mA → 12.0 mW → 13.6 mW; plus the clock net's own C·V²·f = 1.2 mW. Total ≈ 100 mW = 42 mA at 2.4 V, rising to ~63 mA if the in-use base is 1.5× idle. insideGadgets' 40–60 mA brackets that, which is the strongest evidence I have that the 30 mA VDD2 anchor is right. Whole-mod cost at 1.75x: 45.5 + 100 ≈ 146 mW idle-basis, ~195 mW in a demanding game. Consequences: idle goes 170 → 316 mW, i.e. past the 288 mW Funnyplaying GBA the AGBM is designed to beat; battery life at the measured extremes goes 15h15m → ~11h14m (410 → 556 mW) and 5h20m → ~4h34m (1175 → 1370 mW).
findings.risk: None — this is a flag, not a change. The risk is in *not* flagging it: 40–60 mA read as a per-rail number would suggest the VDD2 LDO is near its limit, which it is not, and would under-count what the boost has to supply, which is where the actual margin problem is. If anyone reuses insideGadgets' number, they should know it is a single un-conditioned sentence covering three consoles.
findings.verify_reason: The quotation is verbatim and complete - I read the captured product page and the sentence is exactly 'Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more.' It is one sentence, it covers all three consoles, and there is no measurement point, speed, cart or screen stated. The 'it too' construction does put the 40-60 mA on the console, in contrast to the module. The rail attribution is verified independently: insideGadgets' install list says 'Device V+ to GBA SI', the board silkscreens 'S1' at (95.85, -36.4) and (96.3, -36.0) beside the cart-slot pads, and P1 pad S1 is on net VDD3 on AGBM-01, AGBM-02 and AGBM-11 alike (I dumped all three board files). VDD2 carries CPU pins 44/65/115/117 and SRAM pins 12/16/37; VDD3 carries CPU pins 1 and 103 (pin 124 is ~FIQ pulled to VDD3, not a supply); VDD35 comes off CPU pin 38. All under VOUT3. Arithmetic all reproduces: 12 mA x 3.335 V = 40.0 mW, /0.88 = 45.5 mW = 19.0 mA at 2.4 V, 26.8% of 170 mW; 22.5 mA x 3.336 = 75.1 -> 85.3 mW; 41.7 mA at 2.4 V; battery life 410->556 mW gives 11h14m and 1175->1370 mW gives 4h34m. Two caveats worth carrying forward, neither fatal to the flag: (a) the finding says the source gives no measurement point, then silently reads the 12 mA as a current at V+ (3.335 V) while reading the 40-60 mA as a battery current - two different interpretations of two numbers in one sentence. If both are battery currents the module's own cost is 28.8 mW, not 45.5 mW. (b) 'Nothing lands on VOUT5/VDD5 except through the screen' is true as stated but is used to imply the screen's draw does not change; the GBA's LCD pixel clock scales with the system clock, so at 1.75x the panel's own consumption rises too. The headline claim - that 40-60 mA is an unattributed system-level number - is exactly right and is the single most useful correction in this set.

findings.title: ECO-6 has C4 and R41 the wrong way round: C4 is NOT dangling with the crystal removed — it is still on CK2 through R41, and it costs ~2 mW at 1.75x
findings.current_part: From the netlist: X1 pad 2, R41 pad 2 and C4 pad 1 all share net 'Net-(C4-Pad1)'; R41 pad 1 is /CPU/CK2; C4 pad 2 is GND. R41 = 2.2 k 0603, C4 = 33 p 0603, C3 = 27 p 0603 (CK1 to GND), R1 = 1.5 M (CK1 to CK2). The CPU symbol declares pin 113 CLK1 as an input and pin 114 CLK2 as an output — a textbook Pierce inverter. Depopulating X1 therefore removes the crystal from between C4 and CK1, but leaves C4 hanging on the CPU's still-driven XOUT pin through R41. ECO-6/README.md says 'C4 (33 p) — do not populate. Dangling once the crystal is gone' and 'R41 (2.2 k) ... ends up driving nothing'. Both statements are backwards: with X1 out, R41 is the part with a dead end on one side, and C4 is the part still being charged and discharged every clock edge.
findings.proposal: Keep the recommendation (depopulate X1, C3, C4) but fix the reason in the ECO text, and add the alternative: depopulating R41 *instead of* C4 achieves the same isolation with one part, since R41 is the only remaining path from C4 to CK2. Either way, note in the build sheet that leaving C4 fitted is not free. R1 (1.5 M) may stay as ECO-6 says — with CK1 driven, the feedback path carries at most 3.3 V/1.5 M = 2.2 µA.
findings.benefit: C3, on CK1, is charged by the module's output driver from VDD3: P = C·V²·f = 27 pF × 3.3² × 7.34 MHz = 2.16 mW at 1.75x (1.23 mW at 1x). This also confirms ECO-6's own figure — it quotes 0.37 mA at 4.19 MHz, and C·V·f = 27 pF × 3.3 V × 4.194 MHz = 0.374 mA, correct. C4, on CK2, is charged by the CPU's own XOUT driver through R41: the unloaded figure is 33 pF × 3.3² × 7.34 MHz = 2.64 mW, de-rated by the RC (τ = 2.2 k × 33 p = 72.6 ns against a 68.1 ns half-period at 7.34 MHz, so the cap only reaches ~61 % of the swing) to roughly 1.6–2.6 mW. Depopulating both is therefore worth ~4.3 mW on the 3.3 V domain at 1.75x → 4.9 mW at the battery, and ~2.4 mW → 2.8 mW at 1x. Small, but it is free, it was already planned, and it is one of only two genuine efficiency levers this domain has.
findings.risk: Almost none — depopulating is the mod's own requirement for X1 and is the obvious consequence for C3/C4. The one caveat is that I have assumed the AGB CPU's oscillator block runs from the 3.3 V domain; there is no public datasheet for the part. If XIN/XOUT are actually on VDD2 (2.5 V) the numbers scale by (2.5/3.3)² = 0.574, i.e. 2.5 mW rather than 4.3 mW at 1.75x. The RC de-rating on C4 is an approximation, not an exact integration.
findings.verify_reason: The correctness claim is right and I verified it directly from the netlist: net 'Net-(C4-Pad1)' has exactly three pads - C4 pad 1, R41 pad 2, X1 pad 2 - and R41 pad 1 is on /CPU/CK2 with C4 pad 2 on GND. So with X1 depopulated, C4 is still tied to the CPU's XOUT through R41, and R41 is the part with the dead end. The ECO README's bullets ('C4 ... Dangling once the crystal is gone', 'R41 ... ends up driving nothing') are backwards relative to the README's OWN ASCII diagram three lines above them, which draws the topology correctly. The C3 arithmetic is right: 27 pF x 3.3 V x 4.194 MHz = 0.374 mA reproduces the ECO's own quoted 0.37 mA, and 27 pF x 3.3^2 x 7.34 MHz = 2.16 mW. The magnitude is where it breaks.
findings.correction: C4's dissipation is over-stated by roughly 2x, and the finding's own risk-case correction is applied to the wrong capacitor. CPU pins 115 and 117 are VDD2 and pin 116 is GND, immediately adjacent to CLK1 (113) and CLK2 (114) - I dumped pins 100-128 to check - which is strong circumstantial evidence that the oscillator amplifier is on the 2.5 V core rail, not VDD3. That scales C4 (driven by the CPU's own XOUT) by (2.5/3.3)^2, but NOT C3, which is charged by the MODULE's output driver running from VDD3 = 3.335 V. The finding's risk paragraph scales both, which is wrong. Corrected at 1.75x: C3 = 2.16 mW on VDD3 -> 2.45 mW at the battery; C4 at a 2.5 V swing with the same RC derating = 33 pF x (0.609 x 2.5) x 2.5 x 7.34 MHz = 0.92 mW on VDD2, which is 0.37 mA drawn from VOUT3 through the LDO = 1.23 mW at VOUT3 -> 1.40 mW at the battery. Total ~3.85 mW at the battery at 1.75x (claimed 4.9), and ~2.3 mW at 1x (claimed 2.8). Additional unverified assumption the finding does not flag: whether the AGB CPU's oscillator inverter keeps driving XOUT at all once XIN is externally driven, and at what amplitude - there is no AGB CPU datasheet, and Pierce amplifiers are frequently amplitude-limited, so the true C4 cost could be well below 0.9 mW. The recommendation itself (fix the ECO prose; depopulating R41 instead of C4 achieves the same isolation with one part) is correct and free.

findings.title: The 67.5 mm B.Cu clock run is referenced to five different In2.Cu power islands in turn, and injects its return current into the LCD's own analogue rail for 32.6 mm of it
findings.current_part: Measured out of AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb. CXC_CLK is 73.5 mm total at 0.25 mm width: 6.0 mm on F.Cu, 67.5 mm on B.Cu, two F.Cu↔B.Cu vias at (47.45, −59.60) and (97.90, −38.60). The stackup in the board file is F.Cu / 0.100 mm prepreg / In1.Cu / 0.840 mm core / In2.Cu / 0.100 mm prepreg / B.Cu, so an F.Cu track is referenced to In1.Cu (which carries only GND and AGND zones) but a B.Cu track is referenced to In2.Cu, which carries GND, VDD2, VDD3, VDD35, VDD5, VOUT5, VAUD, VCC and /CPU/LGND zones. Sampling the B.Cu run at 0.25 mm intervals against the filled In2.Cu polygons: 32.6 mm sits over VDD5, 13.2 mm over VDD3, 8.8 mm over VDD35, 5.4 mm over no copper at all, 5.0 mm over VDD2 and only 2.4 mm over GND. The nearest GND via to either layer-change via is 2.44 mm and 2.47 mm away.
findings.proposal: Two options, in order of preference. (a) Re-reference: move as much of the run as possible onto F.Cu, where In1.Cu gives it a single continuous GND reference for its whole length. The router chose B.Cu because the cartridge keepout (which forbids pads and footprints but explicitly permits tracks) is empty; that is a routing convenience, not an electrical one. (b) If the run must stay on B.Cu, add 100 nF 0402/0603 stitching capacitors from the crossed rail to GND within ~2 mm of each In2.Cu boundary the run crosses, and add GND stitching vias adjacent to both layer-change vias so the return has a low-inductance hop between In1.Cu and In2.Cu. Either way, narrow the track from 0.25 mm to 0.15 mm while redrawing — it raises Z0 from 42 to 57 Ω and drops the run's capacitance from 10.9 to 7.8 pF, worth 0.25 mW at 1.75x, which is rounding error but free.
findings.benefit: Magnitude, honestly stated: the injected current is small but its spectral content is not. The run's capacitance to its reference is 0.148 pF/mm (Z0 = 42.0 Ω, εeff = 3.477, computed from the board's own stackup with εr 4.5), so the 32.6 mm over VDD5 presents 4.8 pF to the LCD's analogue rail. With a 3.3 V swing and an assumed 2 ns edge (dV/dt = 1.65 V/ns) that is 4.8 pF × 1.65 V/ns = 7.9 mA of peak displacement current into the VDD5 plane at every edge, twice per cycle; the time-average is only 4.8 pF × 3.3 V × 2 × 7.34 MHz = 0.23 mA, but the peak is what lands on the screen. VDD5 goes to exactly two places — P2 pin 34 (VSHA, the LCD's analogue supply) and cart pad S2 — so this is being coupled into the most display-sensitive rail on the board. That matters here specifically because insideGadgets already document screen trouble at speed: the FunnyPlaying laminated IPS 'fades to black' at 1.5x, and the OneChip IPS and GBC FP IPS are reported glitchy. I am not claiming the return path is the cause — but it is a mechanism the board is introducing that the field-proven flying-wire install does not have, and it costs nothing to avoid while the ECO is still on paper. Separately, the 5.4 mm stretch with no In2.Cu copper under it sees Z0 jump from 42 to 118 Ω (reference falls back to In1.Cu at 0.975 mm); electrically that is a 34 ps discontinuity and is irrelevant for timing, but it is 5.4 mm with nowhere local for the return to go.
findings.risk: The 2 ns edge is an assumption — insideGadgets publish no output characteristics for the module — and everything scales linearly with dV/dt, so a 5 ns edge cuts the peak to 3.2 mA. The coupling estimate assumes the In2.Cu island is the dominant return, which the 0.1 mm dielectric makes overwhelmingly likely. Option (a) may simply not be routable on a front side this congested; option (b) costs board area for capacitors in a band that is already tight, and the ECO has 0 new DRC violations today which any re-route has to preserve. This is a quality/EMI finding with no measurement behind it, hence the confidence.
findings.verify_reason: I re-measured everything from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb myself and it reproduces to within 0.1 mm. Net 238 CXC_CLK: 74 segments, 6.00 mm on F.Cu and 67.46 mm on B.Cu, total 73.46 mm, all at 0.25 mm width, with F/B vias at exactly (47.45, -59.60) and (97.90, -38.60). Stackup in the board file is exactly as stated: F.Cu / 0.100 prepreg / In1.Cu / 0.840 core / In2.Cu / 0.100 prepreg / B.Cu, FR4 epsilon_r 4.5. Zone enumeration confirms In1.Cu carries only GND and AGND, while In2.Cu carries VCC, VDD35, GND, VDD3, VDD2, VDD5, VOUT5, /CPU/LGND and VAUD. Sampling the B.Cu run at 0.05 mm against the 53 filled In2.Cu polygons gives VDD5 32.59 mm, VDD3 13.13 mm, VDD35 8.88 mm, no copper 5.48 mm, VDD2 5.02 mm, GND 2.37 mm - against the finding's 32.6/13.2/8.8/5.4/5.0/2.4. Nearest GND via to the two layer-change vias: 2.442 mm and 2.470 mm, matching the claimed 2.44/2.47. The transmission-line math is also right: Hammerstad with w/h = 2.5 gives eps_eff = 3.477 and Z0 = 42.05 ohm, C = sqrt(eps_eff)/(c*Z0) = 0.1478 pF/mm, 6.22 ps/mm; 32.6 mm x 0.148 = 4.82 pF; 4.82 pF x 1.65 V/ns = 7.9 mA peak; time-average 4.8 pF x 3.3 V x 2 x 7.34 MHz = 0.23 mA. Three notes that do not change the conclusion: (a) VDD5 has four pads not two - P2 pin 34 (VSHA), P1 pad S2, Q6's gate and R26 - but the LCD analogue supply is still the dominant one, so the substance holds; (b) Z0 is computed ignoring the 0.035 mm copper thickness, which would lower it to ~39 ohm and raise C to ~0.16 pF/mm, i.e. the coupling is if anything slightly worse than stated; (c) the 2 ns edge is an assumption with no vendor data behind it and everything scales linearly with it, which the finding says. This is a genuine, board-specific, correctly-measured layout finding and the proposed fixes cost nothing if taken during the re-route ECO-6 already schedules.

findings.title: CXC_CLK is an unterminated 42 Ω, 73.5 mm line into a capacitive far end — add a series-resistor land at TP83 so overshoot into the salvaged CPU's XIN can be clamped
findings.current_part: CXC_CLK as routed: 73.5 mm of 0.25 mm track 0.1 mm over a plane. From the board's stackup, Hammerstad gives εeff = 3.477, Z0 = 42.0 Ω, 6.22 ps/mm — so one-way delay is 457 ps and the round trip is 914 ps. The far end is the CPU's XIN (U1 pin 113, declared 'CLK1 input' in the schematic symbol) plus the existing 22.9 mm of CK1 copper (3.4 pF) with C3 depopulated, so a capacitive load of roughly 8–9 pF including an assumed 5 pF of CPU input. There is no series element anywhere on the net — the only components on CK1 are R1 1.5 M to CK2 and, on a crystal build, X1/C3. The module's output impedance and edge rate are not published by insideGadgets.
findings.proposal: Add a 0603 land in series with CXC_CLK immediately adjacent to TP83 (the CLK wire pad at 97.900, −37.950), i.e. at the source end of the board's run — the wire from the module's CLK pad to TP83 is only 3.8 mm, so a resistor there really is at the source. Populate 0 Ω by default so the board is electrically identical to today's ECO, and specify in the build sheet: scope CK1 at TP80 with the module fitted and running at 1.75x; if the positive peak exceeds VDD3 + 0.3 V, fit 22–33 Ω. Source-series termination is the correct topology here because the driver is at one end and the only load is at the other.
findings.benefit: Stability, not power. The rule of thumb is that a line needs termination when the driver's rise time is shorter than twice the one-way delay, which here is 914 ps. If the module's edge is faster than that, the line behaves as a transmission line: with an assumed 15 Ω CMOS driver into 42 Ω the initial step is 3.3 × 42/(42+15) = 2.43 V, which doubles at the open/capacitive far end to 4.86 V — 1.56 V above VDD3, enough to forward-bias the CPU's input ESD clamp on an irreplaceable salvaged part. Adding Rs = 27 Ω makes the source impedance 42 Ω, the initial step 1.65 V, and the far-end sum exactly 3.3 V with no overshoot. The RC cost of doing so is negligible: 33 Ω into the line's 10.9 pF plus ~8 pF of load gives τ = 0.63 ns and a 10–90 % time of ~1.4 ns, against a 136 ns period at 7.34 MHz. Worth noting the board's route is capacitively *worse* than the stock install it replaces: 10.9 pF of PCB run against roughly 2.5–5 pF for 40–60 mm of flying wire (~0.5–1 pF/cm in air), so the on-board version costs about 0.5–0.7 mW more at 1.75x and presents a lower-impedance, more reflective line.
findings.risk: The whole case rests on an unpublished parameter — if the module's driver is slow (say 5 ns) or already has an internal series resistor, the line is electrically short and the resistor does nothing. That is precisely why the proposal is a 0 Ω land plus a measurement, not a specified value: the downside of the land is one 0603 footprint and a solder joint, the downside of getting it wrong is a damaged CPU that cannot be bought. The counter-evidence is that the stock 40–60 mm flying-wire install is field-proven and would have a *higher* line impedance (~100–150 Ω for a wire over a board) and therefore a larger initial step — which suggests either the driver is slow or people are living with overshoot they have never looked at.
findings.verify_reason: The line parameters are right (73.46 mm verified, 0.25 mm width verified, stackup verified, Z0 = 42.05 ohm and 6.22 ps/mm from Hammerstad on the board's own dielectric, so 457 ps one-way / 914 ps round trip). CK1's existing copper is 22.91 mm, matching the claimed 22.9 mm / 3.4 pF. The net has no series element: /CPU/CK1 carries only C3, R1, TP80, U1 pin 113 and X1 pad 1. The tr < 2*Td rule is stated correctly. But the finding does not survive as written on three specific points, and its own counter-evidence is decisive.
findings.correction: (1) THE PROPOSED LOCATION DOES NOT FIT. I pulled the pad geometry: TP83 is at (97.900, -37.950) and TP84 at (99.450, -37.950) - 1.550 mm apart, which is exactly this board's own 0603 land pitch (C_0603_1608Metric_Boxed_2 pads sit at +/-0.775 mm, e.g. C7). There is therefore no room for a series part between them. P1 pad S1 is 2.93 mm away to the NNW and the MOD1 body edge is 1.0 mm south at y = -38.95, and the module lies flat on the board so nothing can sit under it. The resistor has to go about 2 mm WEST of TP83 (centre no further east than x = 95.9 to keep 0.2 mm off TP83's pad), where the band between the cart pads and the module is clear. That is still electrically at the source and does not change the argument, but the ECO text has to say so. (2) THE OVERSHOOT FIGURE IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT A PREDICTION. The far end is 8-9 pF, not an open: tau = Z0*CL = 42 x 8.5 pF = 357 ps against a 457 ps one-way delay, so the reflection is rounded and does not fully double - 4.86 V is the open-circuit limit, and the real peak with a fast driver would be meaningfully lower. (3) THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION NAMES THE WRONG RAIL. CPU pins 115/117 are VDD2 and 116 is GND, immediately flanking CLK1/CLK2 at 113/114, which says the oscillator block is on the 2.5 V domain. If so the clamp reference is VDD2 + 0.3 = 2.8 V, and the module - specified by insideGadgets to run from S1 = VDD3 = 3.335 V - is already over it at DC in the vendor's own field-proven configuration. Telling a builder to scope against VDD3 + 0.3 V will find nothing. (4) The finding's own counter-evidence is the strongest argument against acting: a 40-60 mm flying wire has Z0 ~100-150 ohm, so the field-proven install produces a LARGER initial step than this board's 42 ohm run. On this axis the board is strictly better than the installation insideGadgets validate. Corrected recommendation: scope CK1 at TP80 (an existing test point, no board change) at 1.75x against VDD2 + 0.3 V before declaring the mod stable; do not spend a PCB revision on a 0603 land whose value is entirely conditional on an unpublished driver parameter.

findings.title: 33.3 mm of the clock run sits 0.25 mm from /CPU/TP9 on B.Cu — checked, and it is benign because TP9 is AC-grounded by C64
findings.current_part: Measured from the ECO board file: sampling CXC_CLK at 0.1 mm intervals and taking the edge-to-edge gap to the nearest same-layer track of each other net, 33.3 mm of the 73.5 mm run has a /CPU/TP9 track within 0.5 mm, with a minimum gap of 0.250 mm. GND is the only other net within 0.5 mm and only for 2.7 mm. This is an artefact of the ECO's own maze router, which routed CXC_CLK and the three button nets together through the same B.Cu corridor in the cartridge keepout. TP9's own network on this board is R44 15 Ω in series from SW2, C64 0.01 µF directly from /CPU/TP9 to GND, plus U15 pin 6 (SN74LVC1G332 input) and the CPU.
findings.proposal: No change required, but when the 169 maze-router segments are redrawn by hand (which ECO-6 §6.3 already flags as a cosmetic to-do), pull the clock away from TP9 to ≥0.5 mm at no routing cost. Do not spend a re-route on this alone.
findings.benefit: The numbers say leave it. For two 0.25 mm coplanar tracks 0.25 mm apart over a plane only 0.1 mm below, the plane takes almost all the field: mutual capacitance is on the order of 1–3 % of the line's self-capacitance, so Cm ≈ 0.02 × 0.148 pF/mm × 33.3 mm ≈ 0.1 pF (an estimate from the geometry, not a datasheet figure). At an assumed 1.65 V/ns edge that injects Cm·dV/dt ≈ 0.17 mA into TP9. C64's 0.01 µF presents 1/(2π × 7.34 MHz × 10 nF) = 2.2 Ω at the fundamental and far less at the edge's spectral content, so the disturbance at the CPU end is well under a millivolt; even at the module end, where the node looks like the 42 Ω trace, it is ~7 mV. Against a logic threshold of order 1.5 V that is 200x of margin. Coupling in the reverse direction is a non-issue: TP9 is a DC button line that only changes when a finger moves.
findings.risk: None from leaving it. The estimate of Cm is a geometric approximation rather than a field solve, so it could be out by 2–3x and the conclusion would not change. The one thing this does *not* cover is coupling to nets on other layers directly above or below the run, which is the return-path finding, not this one.
findings.verify_reason: I re-ran the proximity scan independently. Sampling net 238's B.Cu run at 0.1 mm and taking edge-to-edge gaps to every other same-layer track: /CPU/TP9 is within 0.5 mm for 31.99 mm with a minimum gap of 0.250 mm; GND for 2.68 mm at 0.249 mm; and one more the finding missed, /~{VCNT5}, for 0.48 mm at 0.488 mm, which is immaterial. The finding says 33.3 mm and 0.250 mm - the gap is exact, the length is 4% long, plausibly a sampling-interval or edge-definition difference, and nothing turns on it. TP9's network is confirmed from the BOM and netlist: R44 15 ohm in series from SW2, C64 0.01 uF from /CPU/TP9 to GND, plus U15 (SN74LVC1G332) pin 6 and the CPU. The impedance arithmetic checks: 1/(2*pi*7.34 MHz*10 nF) = 2.17 ohm, and 0.17 mA into 42 ohm = 7.1 mV at the module end, against a logic threshold of order 1.5 V. The mutual-capacitance figure is explicitly labelled a geometric estimate rather than a datasheet or field-solver number, and the finding correctly says a 2-3x error would not change the answer. Honest no-change flag; the 'redraw it away for free during the maze-router cleanup ECO-6 already schedules' advice is right.

findings.title: No decoupling capacitor at the module's V+/V− pads — and TP84/TP85 happen to sit 1.55 mm apart, which is an 0603 land
findings.current_part: From ECO-6 §6.5, TP84 (V+, net VDD3) is at (99.450, −37.950) and TP85 (V−, GND) at (101.000, −37.950), ø1.2 mm pads. There is no capacitor between them and none anywhere near the module: the nearest VDD3 bypass caps (C5, C34, C39, C43, C49, C50, C69) are all in the CPU corner. VDD3 reaches TP84 through 7.0 mm of track and 2 vias from P1 pad S1, then 5.9 mm of user-supplied wire to the module. TPS22917 Rds(on) is 90 mΩ typ / 110 mΩ max at VIN = 3.6 V, 200 mA, 25 °C (TI SLVSDS4).
findings.proposal: Add an 0603 capacitor footprint bridging TP84 and TP85. The KiCad C_0603_1608Metric land has its pads 1.575 mm centre-to-centre; TP84 and TP85 are 1.550 mm apart, so the geometry already almost is one — a 0.1 µF X7R (and, if there is room, a 1 µF alongside) drops straight in, and on the board as it stands today a capacitor can be tack-soldered across the two existing pads by hand without any board change at all. Do this at the same time as any other edit; it does not justify a spin on its own.
findings.benefit: Transient, not average. The module's driver has to charge the board's clock capacitance every edge: 73.5 mm of run at 0.148 pF/mm = 10.9 pF, plus the existing CK1 copper 22.9 mm = 3.4 pF, plus the 3.8 mm wire ≈ 0.4 pF, plus an assumed 5 pF of CPU input ≈ 20 pF total. At an assumed 2 ns edge that is 20 pF × 1.65 V/ns = 33 mA of peak supply current at every transition, 14.7 million times a second at 1.75x. The feed inductance is roughly 5.9 nH (wire, ~1 nH/mm) + 1.8 nH (7.0 mm of 42 Ω track, L = Z0·√εeff/c = 0.261 nH/mm) + ~2.4 nH (two full-stack vias) ≈ 10 nH, so L·di/dt = 10 nH × 33 mA/2 ns = 165 mV of droop on the module's own V+ at each edge, which is jitter on the clock it is generating. A 0.1 µF within 2 mm of the module's pads removes essentially all of it. Average power is unaffected — this buys clock quality, not milliwatts.
findings.risk: Honestly: the field-proven stock install is *worse* than this and works. It uses 40–60 mm of flying wire, i.e. roughly 50 nH, which by the same arithmetic would be ~800 mV — so either the module already carries substantial local decoupling or its edges are much slower than 2 ns. Either explanation means this is a nice-to-have. What tilts it is that the board route triples the capacitive load on the driver compared with the flying-wire install (20 pF vs ~8 pF), so the peak current this board asks for is genuinely larger than the one insideGadgets validated. Both the 2 ns edge and the 5 pF CPU input are unverified assumptions.
findings.verify_reason: The geometry and the part data check out, and the geometric coincidence is actually better than claimed. From the board file, TP84 is at (99.450, -37.950) and TP85 at (101.000, -37.950), both 1.2 mm SMD circles, 1.550 mm apart - and this board's own 0603 land (C_0603_1608Metric_Boxed_2, e.g. C7) has pads at +/-0.775 mm, i.e. 1.550 mm pitch exactly, not the 1.575 mm of the stock KiCad library part the finding quotes. So the two test points already ARE an 0603 land. I also confirmed the decoupling claim: the nearest VDD3 bypass capacitor to TP84 is C69 at 43.6 mm, and the rest are 47-74 mm away, all in the CPU corner. TPS22917 RON verified from TI SLVSDS4: 90 mOhm typ / 110 mOhm max at VIN = 3.6 V, IOUT = 200 mA, 25 C (140 mOhm max over -40..+85 C, which the finding does not quote and which is the number that actually applies inside a sealed shell - still only 20 uW at 12 mA). The problem is the inductance model.
findings.correction: The claim that a 0.1 uF at TP84/TP85 'removes essentially all of' the 165 mV droop is wrong, because the model counts only the V+ side of the loop. The finding's 10 nH is 5.9 nH (V+ wire) + 1.8 nH (7.0 mm VDD3 track) + 2.4 nH (2 vias). It omits the return entirely: the module's V- reaches GND through a 4.7 mm wire to TP85 plus 4.6 mm of track and one via (ECO-6 section 6.5's own routing table). The real supply loop is therefore ~15-17 nH, and a capacitor bridging TP84/TP85 shorts out only the board-side portion (~6-7 nH), leaving the module's own two wires - 5.9 + 4.7 = 10.6 mm, roughly 8-10 nH - permanently in series between the capacitor and the module's pins. On the finding's own 20 pF / 2 ns / 33 mA assumptions that takes the droop from about 280 mV to about 165 mV: a ~40% improvement, not an elimination. The only way to remove the rest is a capacitor on the module itself, which is not this board's to change. Second, practical: TP84 and TP85 are the wire-solder targets for V+ and V-, so a capacitor on those two pads competes with the wires for the same 1.2 mm lands - workable by hand, but it should be called out. Third, both load inputs (2 ns edge, 5 pF CPU input) are unverified, as the finding says. Verdict stands as a cheap nice-to-have with no mW value; the claimed transient benefit should be halved.

findings.title: VDD3 is the correct rail for the module — U18's pass element costs 13 µW at 12 mA, and every alternative is worse
findings.current_part: U18 = TPS22917DBV load switch, SOT-23-6, VOUT3 → VDD3, enabled by /PG_2V5. Verified from TI SLVSDS4: input operating range 1 V to 5.5 V, maximum continuous current 2 A, ON-resistance 90 mΩ typ / 110 mΩ max at VIN = 3.6 V and IOUT = 200 mA and 25 °C (80/100 mΩ at 5 V, 120/150 mΩ at 1.8 V), quiescent current 0.5 µA typ enabled, shutdown 10 nA, θJA 183 °C/W in DBV. The module's V+ lands on P1 pad S1, which the netlist puts on VDD3 on AGBM-01, -02 and -11 alike.
findings.proposal: No change. Keep V+ on VDD3 via P1 pad S1 / TP84, exactly as insideGadgets specify and as ECO-6 has drawn it. The alternatives, checked: VOUT3 directly (bypassing U18) saves the switch's loss but gives up the property that the module powers down with the console — and the loss it saves is 13 µW. VDD5 (5.014 V) would make the module dissipate 51 % more for the same load current if it regulates internally, and there is no evidence it needs more than 3.3 V on a GBA. VBATT is upstream of SW1, so tapping it would give the module a permanent standby drain on the pack and would present it with 1.8–3.2 V, below any plausible minimum. There is no pre-boost rail that survives the power switch, so there is no way to avoid paying boost efficiency on the module's current.
findings.benefit: Quantified so the reviewer can stop wondering about it. Through U18 at 12 mA: V drop = 12 mA × 0.090 Ω = 1.08 mV (1.32 mV at the 110 mΩ max), so VDD3 = 3.3349 V, and the dissipation is I²R = 0.012² × 0.090 = 13 µW — five thousand times smaller than the module's own consumption and utterly invisible against a 170 mW idle board. The chain cost that actually matters is the boost: 12 mA × 3.335 V = 40.0 mW at the rail, /0.88 = 45.5 mW at the battery = 19.0 mA at 2.4 V. That is the irreducible price of fitting the module, and no rail choice available on this board changes it by more than a few tens of microwatts. One consequence worth noting: at 43 mA of idle VOUT3 current the LTC3527's converter 2 is already well past its Burst-Mode threshold (datasheet Figure G14 puts it around 15–18 mA for VOUT = 3.3 V at VIN 2.4 V), so adding the module does not change the converter's operating mode and there is no mode-related saving to chase.
findings.risk: One genuine unknown: the module's supply range and whether it has an internal regulator are not published. The only evidence is circumstantial and comes from the install instructions themselves — GBA V+ goes to S1 (3.3 V), while the GBC instruction is 'Device V+ to VCC pad' and the DMG instruction is 'Device V+ to Capacitor +', both 5 V domains. A part specified across 3.3 V and 5 V hosts must either be a wide-Vdd design or carry its own regulator. Since 3.3 V is the vendor's own GBA answer, this is not a risk to act on, but it is unverified.
findings.verify_reason: Every number verified. TI SLVSDS4 (TPS22917x): 'Input operating voltage range (VIN): 1 V to 5.5 V', 'Maximum continuous current (IMAX): 2 A', ON-resistance table gives 90 mOhm typ / 110 mOhm max at VIN = 3.6 V, IOUT = 200 mA, 25 C (80/100 at 5 V, 120/150 at 1.8 V, exactly as the finding states), IQ 0.5 uA typ enabled, shutdown 10 nA typ. Netlist confirms U18 sits VOUT3 -> VDD3 with ON = /PG_2V5, and P1 pad S1 is on VDD3 in all three MouseBiteLabs board files (I dumped AGBM-01, AGBM-02 and AGBM-11 and the VDD35/VDD3 topology is byte-identical across them). Arithmetic redone: 12 mA x 0.090 = 1.08 mV, I^2R = 12.96 uW; 12 mA x 3.335 V = 40.0 mW, /0.88 = 45.5 mW = 19.0 mA at 2.4 V. The rejection of every alternative rail is correct - VOUT3 direct loses the power-down coupling for 13 uW, VDD5 is 5.014 V for no reason, and VBATT is upstream of SW1 at 1.8-3.2 V. Two minor corrections that change nothing: over -40..+85 C the switch's max RON is 140 mOhm, so 20 uW rather than 13 uW; and the Burst-Mode threshold read-off cites LTC3527 Figure G14, which is labelled '2.2MHz OPERATION' while this board ties FSEL to GND for 1.2 MHz - the threshold at 1.2 MHz is lower still, so the conclusion (43 mA of idle VOUT3 current is far past the burst threshold, no mode-related saving to chase) holds either way. The one genuinely unverified item - the module's supply range and whether it regulates internally - is correctly flagged and does not need action, since 3.3 V is the vendor's own GBA answer.

findings.title: U2 (CY62157EV30LL-45) is comfortable at 1.75x: 2.3x timing margin, valid at 2.5 V, and only +0.7 to +2.4 mA of extra VDD2 current
findings.current_part: U2 on the ECO-5 fork is a CY62157EV30LL-45ZXI, 8 Mbit (512K × 16) async SRAM. Verified from Infineon 38-05445 rev *S: 'Wide voltage range: 2.20 V to 3.60 V'; Operating Range table gives Industrial/Automotive-A as −40 to +85 °C at 2.2 V to 3.6 V; Product Portfolio lists VCC min 2.2 / typ 3.0 / max 3.6 with 45 ns speed; ICC at f = 1 MHz is 6 mA typ / 7 mA max, and at f = fmax = 1/tRC is 18 mA typ / 25 mA max; ISB2 standby 2 µA typ / 8 µA max. Critically, the Switching Characteristics table is headed 'Over the Operating Range', so the 45 ns access time is guaranteed at 2.5 V, not only at the 3.0 V typical. On this board its VCC pins (12, 16, 37) are on VDD2 = 2.500 V.
findings.proposal: No change. This is one place where the ECO-5 de-salvage is a straight win over a salvaged original AGB WRAM, and the ClockxControl makes it more of one.
findings.benefit: Timing: the GBA service manual confirms the CPU multiplies the crystal by 4 in GBA mode, so 7.34 MHz in gives a 29.36 MHz core. A 3-cycle 16-bit EWRAM access is therefore 102 ns against the part's 45 ns rating — 2.3x margin, versus 4.0x at stock 16.78 MHz. Current: ICC is essentially linear in address-toggle rate between the two datasheet points, ICC ≈ 6 + 0.566·(f − 1) mA (typ) or 7 + 0.849·(f − 1) mA (max), for f in MHz. Bounding the access rate: 100 % EWRAM utilisation at stock is 16.78/3 = 5.59 M accesses/s → ICC 8.6 mA typ; at 1.75x it is 9.79 M/s → 11.0 mA typ (14.5 mA max-spec). So the absolute worst case the overclock adds on the SRAM's account is +2.4 mA on VDD2, and at a realistic ~30 % EWRAM duty it is +0.7 mA. Either way it is a small fraction of the ~22 mA that the CPU core adds, and it does not move the LDO analysis. Referred to the battery, the SRAM's worst-case increment is 2.4 mA × 3.336 V / 0.88 = 9.1 mW.
findings.risk: None from leaving it. Two caveats on the numbers: the linear ICC-vs-frequency interpolation between 1 MHz and fmax is my construction, not a datasheet curve (the datasheet gives only the two endpoints); and the EWRAM access model assumes the GBA's default 2-wait-state 16-bit external bus, which games can and do change. Neither changes the conclusion, because even the datasheet's own fmax figure of 25 mA max is small against the VDD2 budget.
findings.verify_reason: Every datasheet number verified against Infineon 38-05445. Features: 'High speed: 45 ns', 'Wide voltage range: 2.20 V to 3.60 V'. Operating Range table: CY62157EV30LL Industrial/Automotive-A, -40 C to +85 C, VCC 2.2 V to 3.6 V. Product Portfolio: Operating ICC at f = 1 MHz is 6 mA typ / 7 mA max, at f = fmax = 1/tRC is 18 mA typ / 25 mA max; ISB2 2 uA typ / 8 uA max. Critically, I confirmed the load-bearing claim myself: both the Electrical Characteristics table and the Switching Characteristics table are headed 'Over the Operating Range', so the 45 ns bin is guaranteed down to 2.2 V, not only at the 3.0 V typical. Part status: CY62157EV30LL-45ZXI is listed in Production at Infineon/DigiKey, 48-TSOP I, 45 ns. ECO-5's own write-up names CY62157EV30LL-45ZXI(T), matching. Netlist confirms U2 VCC pins 12/16/37 on VDD2. Arithmetic reproduces exactly: linear fit (18-6)/(22.22-1) = 0.5655 mA/MHz; 5.59 M accesses/s -> 8.60 mA, 9.79 M/s -> 10.97 mA, delta 2.37 mA; 2.4 mA x 3.336 / 0.88 = 9.1 mW; timing 3/29.36 MHz = 102 ns vs 45 ns = 2.27x, and 3/16.78 MHz = 179 ns = 3.98x. One conservatism the finding did not claim credit for: the ICC test condition is 'VCC = VCCmax', i.e. 3.6 V, while this rail is 2.5 V, so the real dynamic current is roughly 30% lower than the numbers used - the +0.7 to +2.4 mA increment is an over-estimate, which only strengthens the conclusion. The linear ICC interpolation and the EWRAM duty-cycle model are correctly flagged as the author's own constructions.

findings.title: JP3 is the right call, but the stub it isolates is ~11 pF and ~58 ppm, not the ~5 pF and ~40 ppm ECO-6 states
findings.current_part: ECO-6 §6.5 justifies JP3 by saying an ungated CK1 run would be 'roughly 5 pF of added load (about 40 ppm of frequency error) plus a 73 mm antenna'. Computing it from the board's actual stackup instead: a 0.25 mm track 0.1 mm over a plane has εeff = 3.477 and Z0 = 42.0 Ω, giving C = √εeff/(c·Z0) = 0.148 pF/mm. The 73.5 mm run is therefore 10.9 pF, about twice the ECO's estimate. With JP3 open, only the 5.0 mm from CK1 to JP3 pad 1 remains, i.e. 0.74 pF.
findings.proposal: No design change — JP3 stays exactly as drawn, default-open. Correct the number in the ECO text, because it is the number the design decision rests on and it is understated by 2x in the conservative direction.
findings.benefit: Pull calculation, for a 4.194304 MHz crystal with the board's C3 = 27 p / C4 = 33 p load network and assumed C0 = 3 pF, C1 = 15 fF (typical for a fundamental-mode 4 MHz crystal; the AGB part has no published datasheet, so this is an assumption). Nominal CL = (27 × 33)/(27 + 33) = 14.85 pF. Ungated, +10.9 pF on the XIN side takes CL to 17.64 pF, ΔCL = 2.79 pF, and Δf/f = −C1·ΔCL/(2(C0+CL)²) ≈ −58 ppm. Gated, the 0.74 pF residual gives ΔCL = 0.22 pF and Δf/f ≈ −5 ppm. So JP3 turns a 58 ppm pull into a 5 ppm one, and a 73 mm antenna on the oscillator's high-impedance node into a 5 mm stub. The ECO's conclusion is right and now has the right magnitude behind it. Zero power implication either way — this is about not breaking crystal builds.
findings.risk: None. The crystal constants C0 and C1 are assumed, so the ppm figures could be off by a factor of two in either direction; the capacitance figure is computed from the board file and the stackup and is solid. The practical instruction is unchanged: leave JP3 open unless the module is fitted.
findings.verify_reason: The capacitance correction is solid and I reproduced it from the board file rather than from the finding. The stackup block in AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb gives F.Cu / 0.100 mm prepreg / In1.Cu / 0.840 mm core / In2.Cu / 0.100 mm prepreg / B.Cu with epsilon_r 4.5; Hammerstad for a 0.25 mm track over 0.1 mm gives eps_eff = 3.477 and Z0 = 42.05 ohm, hence C = sqrt(eps_eff)/(c*Z0) = 0.1478 pF/mm. I measured net 238 at 73.46 mm, so 10.86 pF - twice ECO-6 section 6.5's stated 'roughly 5 pF'. The JP3 residual is 5.0 mm to pad 1, i.e. 0.74 pF, matching. JP3 exists on the board as a two-pad open jumper at (45.000, -64.200), pads 1.05 mm at 1.3 mm pitch, exactly as documented. The pull arithmetic is self-consistent: CL = 27*33/60 = 14.85 pF nominal, 17.64 pF loaded, dCL = 2.79 pF; I get 49-66 ppm depending on whether the loaded or unloaded CL goes in the denominator of -C1*dCL/(2*(C0+CL)^2), so the quoted 58 ppm sits in the middle of that range, and 5 ppm gated is right. The C0 = 3 pF / C1 = 15 fF crystal constants are assumptions - there is no AGB crystal datasheet - and the finding says so explicitly, so the ppm figures carry a factor-of-two band while the capacitance figure does not. No design change, JP3 stays default-open, and the ECO text should be corrected. Low value, but correct.

findings.title: What the overclock asks of VDD2 decoupling: the bulk is fine, the requirement moves from 16.8 to 29.4 MHz, and the burden is entirely on the ceramics' ESL
findings.current_part: VDD2 carries C60 10 µF 0603, C45–C48 4 × 1 µF 0603, and C8/C15/C16/C52/C53 5 × 0.1 µF 0603 — 14.5 µF nominal across 10 parts, plus the LDO. The NCV8164 datasheet states the part is 'stable with standard ceramics capacitors with values of 1 µF or greater' and does not impose a maximum or a minimum ESR, so the count is not a stability problem for U8.
findings.proposal: No change requested from this domain — this is the requirement statement the passives reviewer should size against, so the two audits do not contradict each other. (1) Bulk: unchanged and comfortable. (2) High frequency: the CPU's core-current spectrum moves from a 16.78 MHz fundamental to 29.36 MHz, and the current amplitude rises 1.75x, so the useful decoupling is whatever is still capacitive at ~30 MHz and above. Every 0603 on this rail is above its self-resonance well before 30 MHz, so above SRF the network's impedance is set purely by mounted inductance and the number of parts in parallel, not by capacitance. The right lever is therefore more, shorter-loop parts (and 0402 rather than 0603 where a footprint can be changed), not more microfarads. (3) The 10 µF 0603 (C60) should be checked for DC bias derating at 2.5 V — that is a passives-audit item but it is the one part carrying the bulk transient budget.
findings.benefit: Sizing arithmetic. Charge drawn per clock cycle at 1.75x with I_VDD2 = 82 mA: Q = I/f = 82 mA / 29.36 MHz = 2.8 nC. Against even a heavily derated 5 µF of effective bulk that is ΔV = Q/C = 0.56 mV, so the low-frequency side is a non-issue — the rail cannot droop meaningfully between clock edges. The LDO contributes nothing at these frequencies: its PSRR is specified at 61 dB at 100 kHz and falling, and its loop bandwidth is orders of magnitude below 30 MHz, so 100 % of the cycle-by-cycle charge comes from the ceramics. Setting a target: to hold the rail within 25 mV (1 % of 2.5 V) against a 1.75x-scaled transient of, say, 50 mA of AC content, the network needs ≤0.5 Ω at 30 MHz, which ten parallel 0603s clear with a large margin even taken as pure inductors. So the existing array is adequate; the point of the finding is that the *reason* it is adequate changes at 1.75x, from capacitance to parallelism.
findings.risk: I have deliberately not quoted a self-resonant frequency or an ESL for any specific 0603, because I could not verify one from a manufacturer datasheet and the whole review depends on not inventing datasheet numbers. That means my '≤0.5 Ω at 30 MHz' claim is a target rather than a verified achievement — the passives reviewer should confirm it against the actual MPNs with a manufacturer impedance curve. The transient AC amplitude (50 mA) is an assumption; nothing in the measured board power constrains it.
findings.verify_reason: The conclusion - no change needed, the array is adequate, and the reason it is adequate shifts from capacitance to parallelism at 29.4 MHz - is right, and the parts inventory is right: the netlist confirms 10 capacitors on VDD2 (C60 10 uF, C45-C48 1 uF, C8/C15/C16/C52/C53 0.1 uF, all 0603) plus U8, totalling 14.5 uF nominal. The NCV8164 stability statement is verbatim correct ('does not require a minimum Equivalent Series Resistance... designed to be stable with standard ceramics capacitors with values of 1 uF or greater'). The charge arithmetic reproduces: 82 mA / 29.36 MHz = 2.79 nC, and 2.79 nC / 5 uF = 0.56 mV.
findings.correction: Two corrections. (1) The 61 dB PSRR figure is specified for VOUT(NOM) = 3.3 V at IOUT = 10 mA, f = 100 kHz - it is the 3.3 V variant's number, not the 2.5 V part fitted here, and it is a 10 mA condition. The qualitative point (the LDO contributes nothing at 30 MHz) is unaffected, but the number should not be quoted as if it applied to U8 at 82 mA. (2) The finding asserts as fact that 'every 0603 on this rail is above its self-resonance well before 30 MHz' in the same breath as refusing to quote any SRF or ESL because it could not verify one. That statement happens to be true for this mix - with a typical ~1 nH mounted inductance, 0.1 uF resonates near 16 MHz, 1 uF near 5 MHz and 10 uF near 1.6 MHz - but as written it is an unverified parameter claim presented as established, which is exactly what the finding elsewhere refuses to do. Either verify it against the actual MPNs or mark it as an estimate. The '50 mA of AC content' and the resulting '<=0.5 ohm at 30 MHz' target are assumptions with no anchor in the measured data, which the finding does concede. Net: keep the requirement statement, drop the two unsupported specifics, and hand the SRF question to the passives audit as the finding suggests.

findings.title: VDD35 has no driver anywhere in the netlist, so the cartridge's supply path — and therefore where the overclock's cart current is billed — cannot be traced from the design files
findings.current_part: Every pad on VDD35 is a load, a bypass or a connector: C6/C7/C17 (0.1 µF), C51 (1 µF), EM3 pad 1 (MH1608-601Y ferrite, whose other side goes to the link port's VDD via P4 pin 1), P1 pin 1 and pad C1 (cartridge VDD), R2 10 k to /CPU/RES, R35 100 k, and U1 pin 38. The CPU symbol declares pin 38 as 'VDD35', pin type power_in. There is no regulator, load switch, ferrite-from-another-rail or zero-ohm link feeding this net on AGBM-01, and grepping the schematics finds VDD35 only as power symbols inside the CPU sheet. The board is field-proven, so it evidently works — which means either the AGB CPU sources the cartridge rail internally out of pin 38 (in which case the symbol's power_in type is wrong and KiCad ERC should be reporting a power net with no driver), or the rail is fed from somewhere I have not found.
findings.proposal: No change to the copper. Two things to do: (a) run ERC on the schematic and see whether it flags VDD35, and if the CPU really does source it, change pin 38's type to power_out or add a PWR_FLAG so the check is meaningful; (b) resolve where the cartridge current is actually billed before anyone relies on the VOUT3 budget above.
findings.benefit: This is not a saving, it is the largest single source of uncertainty in my VOUT3 headroom finding. If VDD35 is generated inside the CPU from VDD3, then every milliamp a cartridge draws lands on VDD3 → U18 → VOUT3 → converter 2, and the cart is one of the three big consumers competing for the ~220 mA that channel can guarantee at 2.4 V. If it comes from somewhere else, the VOUT3 budget improves by however much the cart draws — plausibly 30–60 mA for an Everdrive, which is 15–27 % of converter 2's guaranteed capability and is the difference between the worst case being comfortable and being over budget. Since a 1.75x build is precisely the configuration that pushes converter 2, this needs to be settled with a meter on TP16 rather than reasoned about.
findings.risk: There is a real chance this is simply a symbol-typing artefact of MouseBiteLabs' AGB-CPU library part rather than a design issue — the board demonstrably works and stock GBAs have always fed the cartridge through the CPU. Reporting it because the instruction is to flag things that look wrong even when they are not upgrades, and because in this case the ambiguity propagates into a real margin calculation. No action beyond a meter and an ERC run is warranted.
findings.verify_reason: The observation is factually correct and I reproduced it. Every VDD35 pad is a load, bypass or connector: C6/C7/C17 0.1 uF, C51 1 uF, EM3 pad 1 (MH1608-601Y, other side to P4 pin 1), P1 pin 1 and pad C1, R2 10k, R35 100k, U1 pin 38. The schematic declares pin 38 'VDD35' as pin type power_in. And the situation is identical in all three MouseBiteLabs designs - I dumped AGBM-01, AGBM-02 and AGBM-11 and got exactly the same ten-pad VDD35 net in each - all three of which are field-proven, so the AGB CPU does source the cartridge rail out of pin 38. Two things to correct.
findings.correction: (1) The ERC angle is broader and weaker than stated: there is no PWR_FLAG anywhere in the project (I grepped all four schematic files - zero hits), so KiCad ERC would flag every power net whose only driver is a connector or a power_in pin, not VDD35 specifically. This is a project-wide convention, not a VDD35 defect. (2) The consequential claim does not survive. The finding calls this 'the largest single source of uncertainty in my VOUT3 headroom finding' and says that if VDD35 came from somewhere else the VOUT3 budget would improve by 30-60 mA. There is nowhere else. The AGB CPU has exactly two supply rails on this board - VDD3 (pins 1 and 103; pin 124 is ~FIQ pulled up to VDD3, not a supply) and VDD2 (pins 44/65/115/117 at 2.5 V) - and the cartridge rail is 3.3 V, so it can only be derived internally from VDD3, which is fed from VOUT3 through U18. Cartridge current is unambiguously billed to converter 2, and no measurement can change that; only its magnitude is unknown. Corrected action: drop item (b) entirely, keep item (a) as a cosmetic ERC nit, and measure the cart's draw at TP16 because you want the number, not because the path is in doubt.

findings.title: ECO-5 fork: RAM VCC (U2 pin 37) sits on an isolated VDD2 island - the RAM has no supply
findings.current_part: AGB-SRAM / CY62157EV30LL on the ECO-5 extended U2 footprint, F.Cu. Pin 37 (VCC) has three pads at (95.10,-58.05), (98.97,-58.05) and (100.31,-58.05), joined by an F.Cu track (98.9575,-58.05)->(95.10,-58.05). They land on an isolated F.Cu VDD2 zone island of 6.89 mm2, bbox x[99.0,101.8] y[-58.9,-54.7]. Verified from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb and from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb: there is no VDD2 via anywhere with x > 93 in either file, and no VDD2 track leaves that island. The stock AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb has VDD2 vias at (100.8,-56.6) and (100.8,-55.2) which tie that island to the In2 VDD2 plane; the fork deleted both (via-set diff stock vs fork: removed (100.3,-53.3) GND, (101.0,-61.25) GND, (100.8,-62.15) Net-(Q5B-G), (100.8,-56.6) VDD2, (100.8,-55.2) VDD2; nothing added). Separately, C8 (0.1u, the pin-37 decoupler) was relocated to (103.0,-64.9); its VDD2 pad at (102.22,-64.90) sits over the F.Cu GND pour with no VDD2 copper touching it, and the three stock F.Cu tracks that fed it were deleted.
findings.proposal: No part change. Restore two 0.3 mm vias in the F.Cu VDD2 island at approximately (100.8,-56.6) and (100.8,-55.2) - the exact stock coordinates - to reconnect it to the In2 VDD2 plane (which extends to x=101.8 at that y, verified by plane profiling), and route C8's VDD2 pad back to that island. Then re-pour In2. The fork's own README lists this as deliberately left for the interactive router; that is accurate but it means the board as committed will not boot.
findings.benefit: Not an energy finding. Without it the RAM's VCC pin 37 is open: I_VDD2 through that pin is 0 mA and the chip is powered only through pins 12/16 (which ARE connected - the F.Cu VDD2 zone x[74.3,86.0] reaches them and vias at (83.227,-56.074) and (83.4,-45.9) tie it to the In2 plane, verified). On the original GBA SRAM pins 12/16/37 are all VCC, so the part may partially work and behave erratically; on the CY62157 the pin-37 open removes one of the two VCC pins.
findings.risk: Zero risk to fix. Not fixing it: the board is unbuildable or intermittently unstable, and the failure mode (a floating supply pin on a salvaged/expensive RAM) is exactly the kind that looks like a bad solder joint. Note also the F.Cu VDD2 island only extends to x=101.8 while the In2 VDD2 plane ends at x=101.8 too - the vias must land inside both, which (100.8,-55.2)/(100.8,-56.6) do.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced every geometric claim from the raw .kicad_pcb files with my own parsers. (1) Via-set diff stock vs fork: exactly 5 vias removed — (100.3,-53.3) GND, (101.0,-61.25) GND, (100.8,-62.15) Net-(Q5B-G), (100.8,-56.6) VDD2, (100.8,-55.2) VDD2 — and none added. Exact match. (2) VDD2 via census: stock 16, ECO-5 fork 14, ECO-6 CXC 12 (the CXC additionally drops (84.4,-45.9) and (85.4,-45.9)); no VDD2 via with x>93 in either derived file. Confirmed. (3) U2 pin 37 has three F.Cu pads at (95.100,-58.050), (98.968,-58.050), (100.310,-58.050) — exact. (4) VDD2 has only 21 track segments in the fork; the only ones near pin 37 are F.Cu (98.957,-58.050)->(95.100,-58.050) and a 0.015 mm stub. Nothing bridges x=86 to x=95, so the pin-37 group is isolated from the 59.68 mm2 F.Cu VDD2 zone x[74.34,86.00] that serves pins 12/16. (5) The isolated F.Cu VDD2 island is 6.89 mm2, x[98.97,101.80] y[-58.92,-54.70] — exact. (6) Point-in-polygon: both (100.8,-56.6) and (100.8,-55.2) lie inside BOTH the F.Cu island and the 468.04 mm2 In2 VDD2 plane, so the proposed via positions are valid. (7) Pins 12/16 at (81.31,-58.05)/(81.31,-56.05) are inside the 59.68 mm2 F.Cu zone, and vias (83.227,-56.074) and (83.4,-45.9) tie it to In2 — verified by point sampling. (8) C8 is at (103.0,-64.9) with its VDD2 pad at (102.225,-64.900). (9) The fork README does say the VDD2 feed to U2 pin 37 and the ground-via re-stitching are 'deliberately left for the interactive router' and warns 'Do not send this to a board house without finishing the items'. Nothing here survives challenge — the finding is correct as written.
findings.correction: None material. One nuance the finding does not state: the zone fill data is byte-identical across agbm01, the ECO-5 fork and the ECO-6 CXC file — the fork never re-poured — so the 6.89 mm2 island geometry is the stale stock fill. On a re-pour KiCad would most likely delete the orphan island outright, which does not change the conclusion (pin 37 open) but does change what the reader will see on screen.

findings.title: ECO-5 fork: a signal via removal has open-circuited Net-(Q5B-G) - the battery-low LED control
findings.current_part: Net-(Q5B-G) connects U17 (TPS3840DL20 supervisor) pad 1 /RESET at (103.04,-54.25) to Q5 (NDC7002N) pad 3 at (102.36,-62.15) and R66 (100k pull-up to VOUT5) pad 2 at (99.42,-62.10). The route is: B.Cu from U17 to (104.3819,-53.3), via at (104.38,-53.30), then 10.56 mm of trace ON THE In1.Cu GROUND PLANE LAYER from (104.3819,-53.3) to (100.8,-62.15), then a via at (100.8,-62.15) back to B.Cu for Q5 and R66. The fork deleted the via at (100.8,-62.15) (confirmed by via-set diff against agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb; both files still contain the In1.Cu segments and the (104.38,-53.30) via).
findings.proposal: Restore the 0.7/0.3 mm via at (100.8,-62.15) on net Net-(Q5B-G). While there, consider re-routing this net off In1.Cu entirely - it is one of 314.1 mm of signal routing that the design puts on the In1 ground plane, each mm of which is a slot in the return path.
findings.benefit: Not an energy finding. As drawn, U17's /RESET output cannot pull Q5B's gate down; R66 holds the gate at VOUT5 so Q5B is permanently on and the low-battery (red) LED indication is broken. This is not mentioned in the fork's README, which lists only five GND stitching vias.
findings.risk: Zero risk to fix. The wider point is that this net is routed inside the GND plane, so any future edit near U2 can silently break it again - moving it to B.Cu removes that trap.
findings.verify_reason: Verified independently.
