Net-(Q5B-G) has exactly 10 segments and they are IDENTICAL in stock and fork: B.Cu (104.382,-53.518)->(103.650,-54.250)->(103.037,-54.250) reaching U17 pin 1; In1.Cu (104.382,-53.300)->(104.400,-53.318)->(104.400,-58.917)->(101.167,-62.150)->(100.800,-62.150) = 5.599+4.572+0.367 = 10.54 mm on the GROUND PLANE LAYER; B.Cu (100.800,-62.150)->(102.362,-62.150) and ->(99.475,-62.150)->(99.425,-62.100). The via at (100.8,-62.15) is present in stock and absent in the fork (via-set diff above); the via at (104.38,-53.30) survives in both. Pad positions verified from the footprints: U17 pin 1 at (103.038,-54.250), Q5 pin 3 at (102.362,-62.150), R66 pin 2 at (99.425,-62.100) — all exactly as stated. Consequence check: R66 and Q5 pin 3 remain joined to each other through the surviving B.Cu segments, so R66 (100k to VOUT5) holds Q5B's gate high permanently and U17's /RESET output is severed — exactly the failure mode described. I traced the downstream chain in the schematic (U17 /RESET -> Q5B gate -> Net-(Q5B-D) -> MIC1553 U14 CS pin 3 -> U14 out -> Q5A gate -> Q5A drain on /DL2A, the red DL2 anode fed by R10 20k from VOUT5), which is consistent with the low-battery indication being disabled. The README claim is also correct: it lists only 'Five GND stitching vias' removed, but of the 5 actually removed only 2 are GND — 2 are VDD2 and 1 is Net-(Q5B-G). So this defect is genuinely undocumented.
findings.correction: In1 run length is 10.54 mm by my sum, not 10.56 mm — irrelevant to the conclusion.

findings.title: PTC1 is at its derated hold current before the overclock and over it after - swap 0805L075 for 0805L110 (drop-in)
findings.current_part: PTC1 = Littelfuse 0805L075SLYR (schematic value), footprint Fuse_0805_2012Metric, in series VBATT -> VCC, i.e. carrying the entire battery current (note SW1 does NOT carry load current - it only gates /EN; VCC is permanently fed through PTC1, verified from the pad-level net map: VCC = {C37.1, L1.1, L2.1, PTC1.2, TP32, U5 VIN1/VIN2/VIN}). Littelfuse 0805L datasheet (rev GD 06/20/24): Ihold 0.75 A, Itrip 1.50 A, Vmax 6 Vdc, Rmin 0.090 Ohm, R1max 0.350 Ohm (max resistance measured one hour after trip or 260 °C reflow). Hold-current temperature rerating table, same datasheet: 0.75 A at 20 °C, 0.63 A at 40 °C, 0.57 A at 50 °C, 0.53 A at 60 °C.
findings.proposal: Littelfuse 0805L110 (part number 0805L110WR), same 0805 land, same Vmax 6 Vdc: Ihold 1.10 A, Itrip 2.00 A, Imax 100 A, Rmin 0.050 Ohm, R1max 0.160 Ohm; rerated hold current 0.92 A at 40 °C, 0.84 A at 50 °C, 0.75 A at 60 °C. All values from the same Littelfuse 0805L datasheet table. Intermediate option if the protection level matters more: 0805L100 (Ihold 1.00 A, Rmin 0.060, R1max 0.210 Ohm, 0.82 A at 40 °C).
findings.benefit: TRIP MARGIN (the real reason to do it). Worst-case battery current: 1175 mW at a 1.9 V end-of-life pack = 618 mA; the ClockxControl's own 12 mA at VDD3 costs 12 mA x 3.336 V / (0.88 x 0.95) = 48 mW = 25 mA at 1.9 V; insideGadgets' +40-60 mA when overclocked. Total ~700 mA. The 0805L075's hold current at a 40 °C internal shell temperature is 0.63 A, so 700 mA is 11% ABOVE hold and it will self-heat into trip; at 50 °C (0.57 A) it is 23% above. Even without the overclock, 618 mA vs 0.63 A is already on the line. The 0805L110 at 40 °C holds 0.92 A - 700 mA is 76% of that, a normal design margin. ENERGY, secondary: at the typical in-use point (800 mW at 2.4 V = 333 mA), I^2 x Rmin = 0.333^2 x 0.090 = 10.0 mW and I^2 x R1max = 0.333^2 x 0.350 = 38.8 mW. With the 0805L110: 0.333^2 x 0.050 = 5.5 mW to 0.333^2 x 0.160 = 17.7 mW. Saving = 4.5 mW (both parts at their minimum resistance) to 21.1 mW (both at their post-reflow maximum). I quote the midpoint ~10 mW and stress that the datasheet gives no typical, only Rmin and R1max, so the true value is anywhere in that band. Overclocked at 2.4 V the current is ~333 + 50 = 383 mA: saving 5.9 mW to 27.9 mW, midpoint ~13 mW. Sanity check against the envelope: 10 mW on an 800 mW system is 1.3% - plausible.
findings.risk: Protection is weakened: Itrip rises from 1.50 A to 2.00 A, so a downstream short is held off longer. F1 (a 2 A fast-acting fuse per the schematic) still backstops it, but see the F1/PTC1 BOM finding - the PCB value contradicts the schematic for both parts, and that must be settled first or the coordination is unknown. The 0805L110 also has a higher Imax (100 A vs 40 A) so it is no worse on fault handling. Same 0805 land, same 6 V rating, same Littelfuse series and price band - genuinely drop-in.
findings.verify_reason: I extracted the primary Littelfuse 0805L datasheet PDF myself (rev GD 06/20/24) with PyMuPDF rather than trusting the finding's citation. Electrical table rows verified verbatim: 0805L075 Ihold 0.75 / Itrip 1.50 / Vmax 6 / Imax 40 / Pd 0.6 / Rmin 0.090 / R1max 0.350; 0805L100 1.00 / 1.95 / 6 / 40 / 0.6 / 0.060 / 0.210; 0805L110 1.10 / 2.00 / 6 / 100 / 0.8 / 0.050 / 0.160. Temperature rerating table verified verbatim: 0805L075 = 0.75 / 0.63 / 0.57 / 0.53 at 20/40/50/60 C; 0805L110 = 1.10 / 0.92 / 0.84 / 0.75; 0805L100 = 1.00 / 0.82 / 0.74 / 0.65. Every number the finding quotes is correct. Part existence: 0805L110WR appears in the datasheet's own ordering table and is stocked at Newark (50Y0563) and Mouser; 0805L110SLYR (the suffix matching the stock 0805L075SLYR) is Active at Digi-Key (2082146). Both 0805 (2012 metric) concave — drop-in on Fuse_0805_2012Metric, same 6 Vdc rating, so the footprint claim holds. Circuit claim verified from the pad-level net map: VCC = {C37.1, L1.1, L2.1, PTC1.2, TP32, U5 VIN1/VIN2/VIN} and PTC1 pad 1 is VBATT, so PTC1 is in series VBATT->VCC and SW1 only gates the SW net feeding /EN — the whole console current does pass through PTC1. Battery-current arithmetic re-derived: 1175 mW / 1.9 V = 618 mA; CXC 12 mA x 3.336 V / (0.88 x 0.95) = 47.9 mW = 25.2 mA at 1.9 V; ~700 mA total. I also read insideGadgets' own wording ('Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more') and confirm 'it' is the console, so treating the 40-60 mA as system-level is the right reading — though whether it is measured at the battery or on a 3.3 V rail is unstated, and if it is on 3.3 V the referred battery current is ~105 mA not 50 mA, pushing the total to ~750 mA.
findings.correction: (a) The cited source URL is the 0603L datasheet (…littelfuse_ptc_0603l_datasheet.pdf.pdf), not the 0805L — the numbers are right but the citation is wrong; the correct primary source is littelfuse.com/assetdocs/resettable-ptcs-0805l-datasheet (rev GD 06/20/24). (b) 'it will self-heat into trip' is overstated. Ihold(40 C)=0.63 A is the maximum guaranteed-to-hold current, not a trip point; Itrip(20 C)=1.50 A rerated by the same 0.63/0.75 factor is ~1.26 A. 700 mA therefore sits in the indeterminate band between guaranteed-hold and guaranteed-trip, and empirically MouseBiteLabs ship this board drawing up to 618 mA with no reported nuisance trips. The correct statement is 'no guaranteed hold margin', not 'it will trip'. (c) The stated midpoint is wrong: the band 4.5-21.1 mW has midpoint 12.8 mW, not 10. Redoing it as a constant-power source (I = P/(Vb - I*R)) I get 4.6 mW (both parts at Rmin) to 24 mW (both at R1max) at 800 mW / 2.4 V. Overclocked at 383 mA: 6.1 to 32 mW. At IDLE (170 mW / 2.4 V = 71 mA) the saving is 0.2-1.0 mW — worth saying, because the reader may otherwise expect this to close the 29 mW AGBM-01/AGBM-02 idle gap. (d) NEW RISK the finding missed: F1 is a 2 A fast-acting fuse that opens within 5 s at 4 A. Raising PTC1's Itrip from 1.50 A to 2.00 A puts the resettable element's trip point exactly at F1's continuous rating, so in a moderate overload the one-shot fuse becomes as likely to act as the resettable one. Coordination gets worse in a specific, nameable way — the 0805L100 (Ihold 1.00 A, Itrip 1.95 A, Rmin 0.060, R1max 0.210, 0.82 A at 40 C) is the safer pick and buys most of the margin.

findings.title: F1 and PTC1 both carry PCB value "0467001.NR" while the schematic says two different parts - two 1 A fuses in the battery path
findings.current_part: Verified directly: agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch gives F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR and PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR. All three board files (agbm01, the ECO-5 fork, the ECO-6 CXC file) give BOTH F1 and PTC1 the Value "0467001.NR". 0467001.NR is a Littelfuse 467-series 0603 very-fast-acting thin-film chip fuse, 1 A, 32 V AC/DC, 50 A breaking capacity, body 1.60 x 0.81 x 0.31 mm. F0805B2R00FSTR is MCF0805B2R00FSTR, a Multicomp 0805 fast-acting SMD thin-film fuse: the "2R00" is the CURRENT rating (2.00 A), not a resistance - resistance max 0.08 Ohm at 10% of rated current, max voltage drop 220 mV at 1 x rated (2 A), fusing current within 5 s = 4 A, rated 63 V.
findings.proposal: Fix the PCB values to match the schematic (F1 = MCF0805B2R00FSTR, PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR or the 0805L110 above). Whichever way it is resolved, state it once and keep it consistent - this is a two-part series element in the only path the whole console draws through.
findings.benefit: Not an energy finding directly, but it makes every other number in the battery path unknowable. Series resistance is F1 (<=0.080 Ohm) + PTC1 (0.090-0.350 Ohm) = 0.17-0.43 Ohm, which at the typical 333 mA is 57-143 mV of drop and 19-48 mW, and at the worst-case 700 mA is 119-301 mV and 83-211 mW. If someone instead builds to the PCB values they fit two 1 A 0603 very-fast-acting fuses in series: at 700 mA that is 70% of a 1 A very-fast-acting rating with no continuous-duty derating applied, and the resettable protection is replaced by a one-shot part - a single overload permanently bricks the board.
findings.risk: Reporting only. The one thing that would be wrong is to assume F1 is a 2 Ohm resistor from its "2R00" marking - it is not; 2 Ohm in this path would drop 0.67 V at 333 mA and burn 222 mW, which is flatly incompatible with the measured 800 mW system total, and that inconsistency is how I caught it.
findings.verify_reason: Verified by parsing footprint Value properties out of all three board files: F1 = '0467001.NR' and PTC1 = '0467001.NR' in agbm01, the ECO-5 fork and the ECO-6 CXC file, against schematic values F0805B2R00FSTR (F1) and 0805L075SLYR (PTC1) read from AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch. Part specs verified from distributor/manufacturer sources I fetched myself, not from the finding's citations: 0467001.NR is Littelfuse 467 Series, 1 A, 32 V AC and DC, 0603 [1608 metric], VERY FAST ACTING, 50 A breaking capacity (Newark 12J3738) — a 0603 body in an 0805 land, and a one-shot part where a resettable one is specified. MCF0805B2R00FSTR is Multicomp, 2 A, 0805 [2012 metric], fast acting, 63 V, 50 A breaking; from the Multicomp 'Fast Acting Fuse SMD Thin Film' datasheet table the F0805B row reads: 2 A / 0.08 ohm max at 10% x rated / 220 mV max drop at 1 x rated / 4 A fusing within 5 s / 0.03 A2s pre-arc / 63 V. Every one of those numbers matches the finding. The '2R00 is current not resistance' point is correct and the sanity check is right: 2 ohm at 333 mA would be 0.666 V and 222 mW, incompatible with the 800 mW measured system total. Series-resistance arithmetic re-derived: 0.17-0.43 ohm at 333 mA = 57-143 mV / 19-48 mW; at 700 mA = 119-301 mV / 83-211 mW. All correct.
findings.correction: None. I can strengthen it: I checked the sibling boards and the stale value is unique to AGBM-01 rev 1.2. AGBM-02_AA_1-1.kicad_pcb carries the CORRECT values (F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR, PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR) and AGBM_LiPo_1-3.kicad_pcb carries '2A' / '750mA'. So '0467001.NR' on both parts is a leftover from an earlier AGBM-01 revision, not a deliberate alternate — which removes the ambiguity the finding leaves open and makes the fix unambiguous: the schematic is right, the PCB values are stale.

findings.title: ECO-6: X1, C3 and C4 are not marked DNP, so the crystal and its load caps ship as fitted - C3 loads the ClockxControl output
findings.current_part: In AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb the ClockxControl install requires X1 removed and CK1 driven externally, but the footprint attribute audit shows 49 DNP-marked footprints and X1 (4.194304MHz, at 41.694,-56.785), C3 (27p, GND to /CPU/CK1, at 45.9,-60.5) and C4 (33p, at 45.9,-51.2) are NOT among them. Net map confirms C3 pad 2 is on /CPU/CK1 (5 pads: C3.2, R1.1, TP80, U1.113 CLK1, X1.1) and the C4/R41 network hangs on /CPU/CK2 (U1.114 CLK2, R1.2, R41.1, TP81).
findings.proposal: Mark X1, C3, C4 (and, if the CXC is a permanent fit, R41) as DNP in the ECO-6 board and schematic. R1 (1.5M) can stay - at 3.34 V it passes 2.2 uA. No copper change; this is a build/BOM option.
findings.benefit: With C3 fitted, the ClockxControl's clock output drives 27 pF of load cap on top of the ~10.9 pF of trace capacitance. Dynamic power P = C x V^2 x f: at 1.75x (7.34 MHz) and VDD3 = 3.336 V, C3 alone is 27e-12 x 3.336^2 x 7.34e6 = 2.21 mW at VDD3, which referred to the battery through the boost (eta 0.88) and the series path (0.95) is 2.64 mW. On the CK2 side the CPU's now-unused oscillator inverter still drives C4 (33 pF) through R41 (2.2k): the RC time constant is 2.2k x 33p = 72.6 ns against a 68 ns half-period at 7.34 MHz, so the node only partly slews and dissipation is bounded by C x V^2 x f = 2.70 mW, realistically 1.5-2.0 mW at VDD3 = 1.8-2.4 mW at the battery. Total ~4.5-5.0 mW at 1.75x, ~2.5-3.0 mW at 1x (4.194 MHz). Small, but it is free and the parts are supposed to be off the board anyway.
findings.risk: None if the ClockxControl is fitted. If someone populates X1 instead, C3/C4 are mandatory - hence build-option rather than a deletion. Do NOT remove R1: it biases the CPU's oscillator inverter and removing it is untested.
findings.verify_reason: Footprint-attribute audit reproduced exactly: 49 DNP-marked footprints in the ECO-6 file (BT1, C70, C71, three G***, JP1, NT1, R70, R71, SW2-SW6, TP0-TP32, Z57, Z58) and X1, C3, C4, R41, R1 are all present-and-not-DNP. Positions verified: X1 (41.694064,-56.784916), C3 (45.9,-60.5) rot -90 with pad 2 on /CPU/CK1, C4 (45.9,-51.2), R41 (45.9,-54.3), R1 (45.9,-57.4). Net map verified: /CPU/CK1 = {C3.2, R1.1, TP80, U1.113 CLK1, X1.1} (5 pads, exact) and /CPU/CK2 = {R1.2, R41.1, TP81, U1.114 CLK2}. The C3 arithmetic checks: 27e-12 x 11.129 x 7.34e6 = 2.206 mW; /0.836 = 2.64 mW. The RC comparison checks too: 2.2k x 33p = 72.6 ns vs a 68.1 ns half period at 7.34 MHz. R1 at 3.34 V passes 2.23 uA — correct, and leaving it alone is the right call. What breaks the finding is the vendor instruction I fetched from insideGadgets' own product page, which explicitly says not to remove the components near the crystal. That is the tested configuration; the finding asserts the opposite.
findings.correction: Split the finding. (1) X1 not being DNP is a real correctness item and should stand on its own: build the ECO-6 board to its own BOM and you fit a 4.194304 MHz crystal onto the same node the ClockxControl drives. Mark X1 DNP. (2) Marking C3 and C4 DNP is NOT free and I refute the premise that 'the parts are supposed to be off the board anyway'. insideGadgets' GBA install instruction reads: 'Use a hot air gun to de-solder the existing crystal. Be careful not to remove any of the near by components.' The module is characterised driving CK1 with C3 present and the C4/R41 network intact. Removing them deviates from the only configuration the vendor has tested, and it changes the CLK edge rate into an AGB CPU input of unknown threshold — the same risk the sibling clock-routing finding warns about for a series resistor. Recommend a documented build OPTION, not a DNP. (3) The C4/R41 number is wrong on the rail. CK2 is the CPU's oscillator-amplifier output, biased by R1 1.5M — a linear inverter on the CPU's internal supply, not a rail-to-rail CMOS driver on VDD3. Using V = 3.336 V and calling the result 'at VDD3' is unsupported; treat the C4 side as unquantified. (4) Corrected saving: C3 only, 27 pF x 3.336^2 x 7.34e6 = 2.21 mW at VDD3 = 2.64 mW at the battery at 1.75x, and 1.51 mW at 1x — and only if you accept deviating from the vendor install. Not 3 mW / 5 mW.

findings.title: The 73.5 mm ClockxControl clock run is GND-referenced for only 5.9 mm and changes reference-plane net 15 times
findings.current_part: Measured directly from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb by walking the CXC_CLK polyline and sampling the plane net under each sub-segment: total routed length 73.46 mm (67.46 mm on B.Cu, 6.00 mm on F.Cu, 0.25 mm wide throughout), endpoints (97.90,-37.95) at the module's CLK wire pad and (45.65,-64.20) at JP3. Reference net under the trace, by length: VDD5 35.60 mm, VDD3 13.99 mm, VDD2 7.33 mm, VDD35 4.74 mm, GND 5.91 mm total (4.30 on F.Cu over In1, 1.61 on B.Cu over In2), no plane at all 5.89 mm. The reference net changes 15 times along the run. The trace additionally crosses 5 slots cut in the In2 plane by signal traces routed on that layer (/CPU/TP1, TP2, TP3, TP8, /~VCNT5). Microstrip parameters I derived from the stackup (0.25 mm trace, 0.1 mm prepreg, er 4.5, 35 um Cu): er_eff 3.48, Z0 ~42 Ohm, 0.148 pF/mm, propagation 161 mm/ns so Tpd = 0.457 ns one way. Total trace capacitance to reference ~10.9 pF.
findings.proposal: Three changes, in order of value. (1) Route CXC_CLK on F.Cu instead of B.Cu: F.Cu sits 0.1 mm above the In1 GND plane, which is a single continuous 4023 mm2 island, and the reference-plane audit shows 1614.7 of 1977.5 mm (82%) of existing F.Cu signal routing is already GND-referenced, versus 492.4 of 1522.3 mm (32%) on B.Cu. (2) Flank whatever route is kept with GND stitching vias every ~10 mm so the return current has somewhere to go at each plane change. (3) Fit a 33-47 Ohm series resistor at the SOURCE end (in the module's CLK wire, at TP83) to roughly match the 42 Ohm line and cut the harmonic content; JP3's two 1.05 mm pads on 1.30 mm centres will accept a hand-soldered 0603, but a resistor there is at the far end and only forms an RC with the CPU's XIN pin capacitance (33 Ohm x ~8 pF = 0.26 ns, which does almost nothing) - the source end is where it belongs.
findings.benefit: This is an EMC and margin finding, not an energy one; I am not going to pretend otherwise. The energy number is small and I will state it honestly: charging 10.9 pF at 3.336 V and 7.34 MHz costs C x V^2 x f = 0.89 mW at VDD3 = 1.07 mW at the battery, and shortening the run to ~25 mm would recover about 0.6 mW. The margin argument is the real one: every one of the 15 reference-net changes forces the clock's return current to hop between planes through whatever decoupling capacitor is nearest, and 35.6 mm of the run is over VDD5 (the LCD rail) with 14.0 mm over VDD3 - which is the ClockxControl's own supply, so the clock is injecting its return current into the rail that powers its oscillator. That is a positive-feedback path for jitter. It is also consistent with insideGadgets' own note that the FunnyPlaying laminated IPS screen fails above 1.25x: the clock is capacitively dumping into VDD5 for half its length.
findings.risk: Re-routing 73 mm on a board this dense is real work and may not be possible on F.Cu without displacing other nets. The series resistor is cheap and low-risk but if made too large it slows the CK1 edge into a CPU input with an unknown threshold - do not exceed ~100 Ohm without scoping CK1. Cannot be done as a drop-in.
findings.verify_reason: I re-measured everything from the raw file. Total routed length 73.46 mm, 67.46 on B.Cu, 6.00 on F.Cu, 0.25 mm wide throughout — exact match. Endpoints confirmed by chaining all 74 segments: (45.65,-64.20) at JP3 pad 2 and (97.90,-37.95) at TP83, the module's CLK wire pad; JP3 pads are at (44.35,-64.20)/(45.65,-64.20), 1.30 mm centres, and TP83/TP84(VDD3)/TP85(GND) sit at y=-37.95, 1 mm clear of the body edge at y=-38.95 — all as stated, and the 'series resistor belongs at TP83 not JP3' reasoning is geometrically right (TP83 is the module/source end). Stackup verified from the file: F.Cu / 0.1 mm prepreg / In1 / 0.84 mm core / In2 / 0.1 mm prepreg / B.Cu, er 4.5, 35 um copper. I re-derived all the microstrip numbers independently and they are correct to the digit: W/H = 2.5, er_eff = 2.75 + 1.75(1+12/2.5)^-0.5 = 3.477; Z0 = 376.99/(1.8647 x 4.808) = 42.05 ohm; v = 299.79/1.8647 = 160.8 mm/ns; Tpd = 73.46/160.8 = 0.457 ns; C = (1/160.8)/42.05 = 0.1479 pF/mm; total 10.87 pF; P = 10.9e-12 x 3.336^2 x 7.34e6 = 0.89 mW at VDD3 = 1.07 mW at the battery. I also reproduced the F.Cu/B.Cu GND-reference census that justifies proposal (1): F.Cu 1597.7 of 1961.3 mm = 81% GND-referenced, B.Cu 490.4 of 1522.3 mm = 32% — within 1% of their figures. The slot-crossing claim is confirmed and understated: by segment-segment intersection the B.Cu run crosses In2 traces on /CPU/TP2, /CPU/TP1, /CPU/TP8, /~VCNT5, /CPU/TP3 (the 5 they name) plus SW and VDD35, and the 6 mm F.Cu leg additionally crosses In1 traces on /CPU/VSHD and /CPU/Display/VCOM which they missed. So the return path is worse than described, not better.
findings.correction: (a) Reference-plane breakdown is off. My own 0.05 mm sampling of the chained polyline against the filled polygons (B.Cu referenced to In2, F.Cu to In1) gives VDD5 32.59, VDD3 13.13, VDD35 8.88, GND 6.88, VDD2 5.02, no plane 6.97 mm — versus their VDD5 35.60 / VDD3 13.99 / VDD2 7.33 / VDD35 4.74 / GND 5.91 / none 5.89. The headline should be 'GND-referenced for 6.9 mm of 73.5 mm (9%)' and '32.6 mm over VDD5', not 5.9 and 35.6. (b) 'changes reference-plane net 15 times' is not reproducible. Walking the chained path I get 20 contiguous runs, i.e. 19 transitions if you count every no-plane gap, or 8 distinct plane-net regions (7 changes) if you merge across gaps. 15 is neither; state the method. (c) REFUTED outright: 'It is also consistent with insideGadgets' own note that the FunnyPlaying laminated IPS screen fails above 1.25x - the clock is capacitively dumping into VDD5 for half its length.' insideGadgets' screen-compatibility list describes the module installed in stock consoles where CLK is a hand-run flying wire and no 73 mm B.Cu trace over a VDD5 plane exists. That note cannot be evidence about this board's routing, and offering it as corroboration is exactly the kind of inference a reader would take as confirmation. Delete it. (d) The finding undercounts the slot problem: see below.

findings.title: LTC3527 output capacitors are 3.9 mm from the VOUT pins with two via transitions in the highest-di/dt path, and both return through one GND via
findings.current_part: All on B.Cu. Corrected pad positions (the footprint is rotated -90 deg): U5 VOUT1 (28.35,-40.65), SW1 (28.35,-40.15), SW2 (28.35,-39.65), VOUT2 (28.35,-39.15), PGND exposed pad (26.90,-39.90), GND pads at (27.15,-41.35), (27.15,-38.45), (25.45,-39.65). C21 (22u 0805, VOUT5) pad 1 at (31.75,-42.55), GND pad at (31.75,-40.65). C42 (22u 0805, VOUT3) pad 1 at (31.75,-37.25), GND pad at (31.75,-39.15). L1 pad 2 at (30.68,-45.00) and L2 pad 2 at (30.68,-34.80), so each SW node runs 5.38 mm to its inductor. The output path is NOT a straight run: U5 pin 8 lands on a 2.05 mm2 B.Cu VOUT3 island (x[27.9,29.9] y[-39.3,-37.0]) which is a SEPARATE polygon from the 75.51 mm2 B.Cu VOUT3 pour that C42 sits in; they are joined only via the F.Cu VOUT3 zone through vias at (29.52,-38.50)/(29.52,-37.42) and (32.30,-36.20). Same on channel 1: 2.06 mm2 island, vias (29.52,-41.40)/(29.52,-42.40) and (32.30,-43.70). On the return side, both output caps' GND pads sit in one 4.67 mm2 B.Cu GND island (x[31.1,33.1] y[-41.9,-38.0]) served by GND vias at (32.90,-39.90), (32.83,-38.44) and (32.90,-41.40); the U5 exposed pad has its own three vias at (26.50,-40.30), (27.30,-40.30), (26.50,-39.50), 5.8 mm away in-plane. The LTC3527 datasheet is explicit on both pins: "PCB trace length from VOUT1 to the output filter capacitor(s) should be as short and wide as possible" and the same for VOUT2.
findings.proposal: No part change. On a PCB revision: move C21 and C42 so their VOUT pads butt directly against U5 pins 5 and 8 on B.Cu (there is room in x 29-31, y -42 to -37 once the via-hop is removed), merge the two B.Cu VOUT islands per channel so no layer transition is needed, and put two GND vias immediately adjacent to each output cap's ground pad rather than 1.2-1.6 mm away.
findings.benefit: EMC/ripple, not energy. Loop estimate: perimeter of the VOUT -> COUT -> GND -> PGND loop is about 3.9 mm out + 1.9 mm across the cap + 4.65 mm back = 10.4 mm, plus two 0.3 mm via transitions at roughly 1 nH each, giving an order-of-10 nH loop against the ~2-3 nH achievable. Working the current: at 200 mA on VOUT3 from a 2.6 V input, D = 1 - 2.6/3.336 = 0.221, IL_avg = 0.200/0.779 = 257 mA and ripple = Vin x D / (L x f) = 2.6 x 0.221 / (4.7e-6 x 1.2e6) = 102 mA, so Ipk ~308 mA. At a 3 ns synchronous-rectifier edge, di/dt = 1.0e8 A/s and V = L x di/dt = 10e-9 x 1.0e8 = ~1.0 V of ringing across the loop. That is the number that matters: VOUT3 feeds VDD3 through U18, which is a bare P-FET with no filtering whatsoever, so this ringing lands directly on the CPU's I/O rail and on the ClockxControl's supply pin.
findings.risk: Requires re-placing two 0805s and re-pouring, on a board where the converter corner is already tight (16 non-GND vias within 6 mm of U5). Nothing about the current layout is a functional fault - the board demonstrably works - so this is a quality improvement whose payoff is cleaner rails at 1.75x, not a fix.
findings.verify_reason: Every geometric claim reproduced from the raw file. U5 is at (26.9,-39.9) rot -90; pad 5 VOUT5 (28.348,-40.650), pad 6 SW1 (28.348,-40.150), pad 7 SW2 (28.348,-39.650), pad 8 VOUT3 (28.348,-39.150), pad 17 PGND exposed pad (26.900,-39.900), GND pads (27.150,-41.348) / (27.150,-38.452) / (25.452,-39.650) — all exact. C21 pad 1 (31.750,-42.550) GND pad (31.750,-40.650); C42 pad 1 (31.750,-37.250) GND pad (31.750,-39.150); L1 pad 2 (30.675,-45.000); L2 pad 2 (30.675,-34.800). Distances re-derived: pin 5 to C21 pad 1 and pin 8 to C42 pad 1 are both sqrt(3.402^2+1.900^2) = 3.896 mm; SW1 pin to L1 is 5.379 mm. Split-island claim verified two ways: the B.Cu VOUT3 copper is a 2.05 mm2 polygon at x[27.9,29.9] y[-39.3,-37.0] plus a separate 75.51 mm2 pour at x[19.0,40.4] y[-43.5,-26.5], and there is exactly ONE B.Cu VOUT3 track segment on the whole board — a 0.28 mm stub (31.950,-37.050)->(31.750,-37.250) — so the two really are joined only through F.Cu. VOUT3 vias in the corner: (29.525,-38.500), (29.525,-37.425), (32.300,-36.200) as cited, plus (32.300,-35.300) and (32.300,-34.400) the finding omits. VOUT5 mirrors it: 2.06 mm2 island, vias (29.525,-41.400)/(29.525,-42.400)/(32.300,-43.700)/(32.300,-44.600). GND vias at the caps: (32.900,-39.900), (32.831,-38.441), (32.900,-41.400) — exact; U5 EPAD has exactly three at (26.500,-40.300), (27.300,-40.300), (26.500,-39.500) — exact. Datasheet quote verified by extracting the Analog Devices PDF myself: 'PCB trace length from VOUT1 to the output filter capacitor(s) should be as short and wide as possible' (and the identical sentence for VOUT2), plus TJMAX 125 C / theta-JA 68 C/W and 'EXPOSED PAD (PIN 17) IS PGND, MUST BE SOLDERED TO PCB'. Ripple arithmetic re-derived and correct: Vfb = 1.20 V typ (so VOUT3 = 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V and VOUT5 = 1.20 x 4.1786 = 5.014 V, which validates the 3.336 V used throughout the review); D = 1 - 2.6/3.336 = 0.2206; IL = 0.200/0.7794 = 257 mA; ripple = 2.6 x 0.2206/(4.7e-6 x 1.2e6) = 102 mA; Ipk = 308 mA; di/dt = 1.03e8 A/s; 10 nH x 1.03e8 = 1.03 V.
findings.correction: One sentence must be struck: 'VOUT3 feeds VDD3 through U18, which is a bare P-FET with no filtering whatsoever, so this ringing lands directly on the CPU's I/O rail and on the ClockxControl's supply pin.' VOUT3 carries C42 22 uF + C2 10 uF + C23 10 uF + C22 1 uF, and VDD3 downstream of U18 carries C5, C34, C39, C43 (0.1 uF) plus C49, C50, C69 (1 uF) — seven discrete decouplers. TPS22917 is indeed a P-channel MOSFET switch (TI datasheet, section 9), so 'bare P-FET' is fair, but 'no filtering whatsoever' is contradicted by the BOM. Also the ~1.0 V figure is the voltage developed ACROSS the parasitic loop between the die and the capacitor, not the disturbance at the load; the reader should not be told it appears on VDD3. Two further caveats: the 3 ns synchronous-rectifier edge and the 1 nH-per-via figure are assumed, not sourced. Recast this as what it is — a layout-quality item worth doing on a respin, justified by the datasheet's explicit instruction, with no quantified load-side consequence.

findings.title: The SW2 switching node is poured directly over the In2 VDD3 plane at 0.1 mm - the boost couples into the CPU I/O and ClockxControl rail
findings.current_part: Verified by point-sampling the filled polygons. The Net-(U5-SW2) copper is a B.Cu zone of 8.66 mm2, bbox x[28.0,31.5] y[-39.8,-33.8]. Directly beneath it, 0.1 mm away across the prepreg, is the In2.Cu VDD3 plane (448.49 mm2, bbox x[23.6,98.1] y[-52.2,-26.6]). The companion Net-(U5-SW1) zone (8.74 mm2, x[28.0,31.5] y[-46.0,-40.0]) sits over the In2 VOUT5 plane (16.10 mm2). Under U5 itself In2 is essentially bare - the GND island there is only 2.40 mm2 - so the B.Cu converter copper has no local GND reference at 0.1 mm; the nearest GND plane, In1, is 0.975 mm away through the 0.84 mm core.
findings.proposal: No part change. On a PCB revision, replace the In2 copper under the converter (roughly x 23-34, y -33 to -48) with a GND island stitched to In1, instead of letting the VDD3 and VOUT5 planes run under the switch nodes. Zero cost, zone edit plus re-pour.
findings.benefit: EMC, no energy saving - I am marking benefit_mw zero deliberately. Coupling: C = e0 x er x A / d = 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 7e-6 / 0.1e-3 = 2.8 pF between SW2 and the VDD3 plane (using ~7 mm2 of overlap after clearances, from an 8.66 mm2 zone). SW2 swings 0 to 3.34 V at 1.2 MHz (FSEL is tied to GND, and the datasheet gives FSEL low = 1.2 MHz, 0.9-1.5 MHz limits). At an assumed 3 ns edge the injected current is i = C dV/dt = 2.8e-12 x 1.113e9 = 3.1 mA peak straight into the VDD3 plane. The nearest VDD3 decoupling capacitor to that spot is C39 at (27.77,-51.10), about 15 mm away; over that distance the In1/In2 plane pair (0.84 mm apart, er 4.5) presents roughly 377 x 0.84e-3 / (sqrt(4.5) x 0.010) = 15 Ohm for a 10 mm-wide path, so of order 45 mV of high-frequency spike on VDD3 near the converter. VDD3 is the ClockxControl's V+ and the CPU's I/O supply; at 1.75x the clock chip is the most jitter-sensitive thing on that rail.
findings.risk: Re-pouring In2 under the converter means VDD3 must find another path across x 23-34 - it currently uses that plane region, so the re-pour needs checking that VDD3 still reaches U18's output and the CPU. Verify with a fresh DRC and connectivity check. No component or schematic change.
findings.verify_reason: Verified by point-sampling the filled polygons myself. Net-(U5-SW2) is a single B.Cu zone of 8.66 mm2 at x[28.0,31.5] y[-39.8,-33.8]; Net-(U5-SW1) is 8.74 mm2 at x[28.0,31.5] y[-46.0,-40.0] — both exact. In2 VDD3 is a single 448.49 mm2 polygon spanning x[23.6,98.1] y[-52.2,-26.6] and In2 VOUT5 is 16.10 mm2 at x[29.1,32.9] y[-47.2,-41.0] — exact. The In2 GND island under the converter is 2.40 mm2 at x[26.1,27.7] y[-40.7,-39.1] — exact, so the claim that the B.Cu converter copper has no local GND reference at 0.1 mm is correct. Stackup confirms In1 is 0.1+0.035+0.84 = 0.975 mm from B.Cu through the 0.84 mm core — exact. FSEL = GND and the datasheet (extracted by me from the AD PDF) states 'FSEL = Low: 1.2MHz operation' with the electrical table giving 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.5 MHz min/typ/max — exact. C39's VDD3 pad is at (27.775,-51.100), about 14.4 mm from the centre of the SW2 zone — the finding's 'about 15 mm' is fine. The 3.336 V SW2 swing follows from Vfb 1.20 V x (1 + 1.78/1.00), verified. Everything checks except the overlap area, which I measured rather than assumed.
findings.correction: The overlap area is understated, so the coupling is worse than claimed, not better. Monte-Carlo integration (200k samples, seed fixed) of the SW2 B.Cu polygon against the In2 VDD3 filled polygon gives 8.35 mm2 of true overlap, not the ~7 mm2 assumed from an 8.66 mm2 zone. Corrected: C = 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 8.35e-6 / 0.1e-3 = 3.33 pF (not 2.8 pF), and i = C dV/dt = 3.33e-12 x 1.112e9 = 3.7 mA peak (not 3.1 mA), giving of order 55 mV rather than 45 mV on the same assumptions. Two assumptions must be labelled as such in the text: the 3 ns edge is not from the datasheet, and treating the In1/In2 parallel-plane characteristic impedance (377 x 0.84e-3/(sqrt(4.5) x 0.010) = 14.9 ohm) as a lumped series impedance over a 15 mm path is a rough proxy — VDD3 also carries seven discrete decouplers (C5, C34, C39, C43 at 0.1 uF; C49, C50, C69 at 1 uF), which the 45 mV estimate ignores. Treat the number as order-of-magnitude only.

findings.title: Thermal audit: no part on this board is near a limit, overclocked or not - the largest junction rise I can compute is about 16 °C
findings.current_part: Every thermal resistance below was read out of a manufacturer PDF fetched during this review, not from memory. LTC3527 (U5), QFN-16 UD: TJMAX 125 °C, thetaJA 68 °C/W, and the datasheet states the exposed pad (pin 17) is PGND and MUST be soldered - on this board it is, with three 0.3 mm GND vias at (26.50,-40.30), (27.30,-40.30), (26.50,-39.50). NCV8164 (U8, U4), TSOP-5: RthJA 158 °C/W, RthJC(top) 155, RthJB 197, TJ max 150 °C, Iq 30 uA typ, dropout for the 2.5 V version 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA, current limit 350 mA min. TPS22917 (U11, U18, U12), DBV SOT-23-6: thetaJA 183 °C/W, Ron 80 mOhm typ / 100 max at VIN 5 V and 25 °C (120 mOhm max to +85 °C), 90 typ / 110 max at VIN 3.6 V, IQ 0.5 uA typ. LM4853 (U6), MSOP-10 DGS: thetaJA 194 °C/W, TJ max 150 °C, IDD 2.0-2.4 mA typ. TPS3840DL20 (U3, U10, U17), SOT-23-5: thetaJA 187.5 °C/W. MIC1553 (U14), SOT-23-5: thetaJA 250 °C/W.
findings.proposal: No change. This finding exists so nobody spends effort chasing a thermal problem that is not there.
findings.benefit: Dissipations at the worst in-use overclocked point (1175 mW plus overclock, 1.9 V pack, ~700 mA battery), assuming 45 °C inside a sealed shell. U5 LTC3527: input power = 1325 mW less the F1+PTC1 loss (39 mW + 44-172 mW) = 1114-1242 mW; at an assumed 88% efficiency the loss is 134-149 mW, giving 68 x 0.14 = +9.5 °C, Tj ~55 °C. Even at a pessimistic 80% efficiency the loss is 240 mW and the rise is +16 °C, Tj ~61 °C, against 125 °C. U8 (VDD2 LDO): (3.336 - 2.500) x 90 mA = 75 mW, plus 30 uA x 3.336 V = 0.1 mW; 158 x 0.075 = +11.9 °C, Tj ~57 °C against 150 °C. At 1x it is 0.836 x 60 mA = 50 mW and +7.9 °C. You would need 800 mA through U8 to reach 150 °C, and its current limit is 350 mA min - the part is thermally unreachable. U4 (VAUD LDO): 0.836 x 30 mA = 25 mW, +4.0 °C. U11 (VDD5 load switch) at an assumed 100 mA of backlight: 0.100^2 x 0.120 = 1.2 mW, +0.2 °C. U18 (VDD3) at 70 mA: 0.070^2 x 0.110 = 0.54 mW, +0.1 °C. U6 LM4853: the datasheet's own worst case for a bridged load is PDMAX = 4 x VDD^2 / (2 x pi^2 x RL) = 4 x 2.500^2 / (19.74 x 8) = 158 mW at the board's VAUD = 2.5 V with an assumed 8 Ohm speaker, giving 194 x 0.158 = +30.7 °C and Tj ~76 °C. In practice MouseBiteLabs measure the whole audio chain at 50-100 mW so U6 dissipates roughly 40-60 mW and rises +8 to +12 °C. Note the datasheet's warning that a DGS-package LM4853 on a 5 V rail can only take 27 °C ambient at PDMAX - at 2.5 V that scales by a factor of four and the problem disappears. The only part that runs hot enough to matter is PTC1, and it does so by design - see the trip finding: 0.700^2 x 0.090 to 0.700^2 x 0.350 = 44 to 172 mW in an 0805 body.
findings.risk: The one number I cannot verify is the internal shell temperature; 45 °C is my estimate. Even at 70 °C internal ambient every junction above stays under 105 °C. Two caveats: the LTC3527's 68 °C/W is a datasheet figure for the manufacturer's board, and the three EPAD vias here are on the low side for a QFN - if you want margin, add three more; and the speaker impedance (8 Ohm) is assumed, not measured.
findings.verify_reason: I re-extracted every load-bearing thermal number from primary PDFs rather than trusting the finding. LTC3527 (Analog Devices 35271fc, extracted with PyMuPDF): 'TJMAX = 125 C, theta-JA = 68 C/W' and 'EXPOSED PAD (PIN 17) IS PGND, MUST BE SOLDERED TO PCB' — verbatim; and I confirmed from the board that the exposed pad has exactly three 0.3 mm GND vias at (26.500,-40.300), (27.300,-40.300), (26.500,-39.500), so the 'three is on the low side, add three more' caveat is well founded. NCV8164 (onsemi): TSOP-5 RthJA 158, RthJC(top) 155, RthJC(bot) 102, RthJB 197 C/W; TJ max 150 C; Iq typ 30 uA; dropout for VOUT(NOM) 2.5 V at 300 mA = 125 typ / 200 max mV; output current limit ICL 350 mA min / 560 typ; load regulation 2 mV over 1-300 mA — every figure matches. TPS22917 (TI SLVSDW8B): DBV SOT-23 6-pin theta-JA 183 C/W; IQ 0.5 uA typ; RON at VIN 5 V = 80 typ / 100 max at 25 C, 120 max to +85 C; at VIN 3.6 V = 90 typ / 110 max at 25 C, 140 max to +85 C — the finding's quoted numbers are right except for which column applies to U18. LM4853 (TI): theta-JA (DGS) = 194 C/W, TJMAX = 150 C, PDMAX(bridge) = 4 x VDD^2/(2 pi^2 RL), and the datasheet's own statement that at 5 V into 8 ohm the maximum ambient is 'approximately 27 C for package DGS' — exactly as cited. I then re-derived every arithmetic step: U5 input 1325 - 39 - (44..172) = 1114..1242 mW, x 0.12 = 134..149 mW, x 68 = +9.1..10.1 C; at 80% efficiency 240 mW x 68 = +16.3 C. U8: 0.836 x 0.090 = 75.2 mW, x 158 = +11.9 C; the 'you would need 800 mA' check is right (105/158 = 0.665 W / 0.836 V = 795 mA, against an ICL of 350 mA min, so the part is thermally unreachable). U4 +4.0 C. U11 0.100^2 x 0.120 = 1.2 mW, +0.22 C. U6 4 x 2.5^2/(19.74 x 8) = 158 mW, x 194 = +30.7 C, Tj 76 C. PTC1 0.7^2 x 0.090..0.350 = 44..172 mW. All correct. The 45 C internal ambient is honestly flagged as an estimate and the conclusion survives at 70 C.
findings.correction: Three small corrections, none of which change the verdict. (1) LM4853 IDD is 2.4 mA typ / 7.0 mA max in both BTL and SE mode — the datasheet gives no '2.0-2.4 typ' range. (2) U18 sits on VOUT3 = 3.336 V, so the TPS22917's 3.6 V RON column applies, not the 5 V one: 140 mOhm max over -40 to +85 C, not 110. That makes it 0.070^2 x 0.140 = 0.69 mW and +0.13 C — still nothing. (3) The TPS3840DL20 theta-JA of 187.5 C/W and the MIC1553 theta-JA of 250 C/W are the only two figures I could not verify from a fetched source; mark them unverified. Both parts dissipate microwatts, so nothing in the audit turns on them.

findings.title: What is under the ClockxControl: no components, four different rails and 27 tented vias - no thermal problem, but the module wants a soldermask keepout
findings.current_part: The MOD1 footprint (ClockxControl_GBA_GBC) is placed at (91.95,-44.95) rotated 180, body 18.65 x 12.00 mm (fp_rect +/-9.325, +/-6.0), i.e. the window x[82.625,101.275] y[-50.950,-38.950] on F.Cu. Its three SMD landing pads are at (87.42,-45.95) /CPU/TP2, (84.92,-48.45) /CPU/TP9, (84.92,-45.95) /CPU/TP8; the V+, V- and CLK wire pads (TP84 VDD3, TP85 GND, TP83 CXC_CLK) are outside the body at y = -37.95. Sampling the F.Cu filled polygons on a 0.25 mm grid inside the window: GND 46.6% (107.1 mm2), VDD35 25.8% (59.3 mm2), bare laminate 16.1% (37.1 mm2), VDD2 9.3% (21.3 mm2), VDD5 2.1% (4.9 mm2). Sixteen signal tracks pass through, longest are Net-(C71-Pad1) 14.3 mm, /CPU/TP9 14.1 mm, /CPU/TP8 7.3 mm, /CPU/TP2 6.3 mm, /CPU/TP0 6.2 mm, /CPU/TP1 5.8 mm. Twenty-seven vias fall inside the window (17 GND, 4 VDD5, 1 VDD2, and 9 signal); the board setup line is (tenting front back), so they are masked. NO component sits under it: ECO-6 already moved C7 (the cartridge VDD35 decoupler) from (91.9,-41.1) - where it was in the ECO-5 fork, squarely inside the window - out to (93.1,-37.4), and C12 is on B.Cu. That relocation was necessary and correctly done: a 0603 is 0.8 +/- 0.1 mm thick (Murata GRM188 series datasheet), and a 1.6 mm-thick rigid module resting flat cannot bridge a 0.8 mm part 4.5-7 mm from its solder pads without lifting them.
findings.proposal: Add a soldermask keepout (or at minimum a documented Kapton pad) under the MOD1 body, and add an F.Cu copper-pour keepout so the module does not sit over four different rails. Neither costs anything at fab. Also add the height restriction to the footprint's courtyard/3D data so a future edit cannot put another 0603 back inside the window.
findings.benefit: THERMAL: none, in either direction, and I want to be explicit about that because the question was asked. The module covers 224 mm2 of F.Cu; at a still-air convection coefficient of order 10 W/m2K and a 20 °C local rise, that patch was only shedding 10 x 2.24e-4 x 20 = 45 mW to begin with, and it contains no dissipating part - the four things that do dissipate are at x = 18 (U8), 27 (U5), 38 (U4) and 103 (U6), all well outside. The module's own 12 mA x 3.336 V = 40 mW spread over both faces (2 x 2.24e-4 m2) is a self-rise of about 0.040 x 1/(10 x 4.48e-4) = 9 °C, and less than that in practice because most of it conducts into the board. Covering this area creates no thermal problem. MECHANICAL/ELECTRICAL: the exposure is four rails (GND, VDD35, VDD2, VDD5) and 27 tented vias under a rigid PCB that is soldered down at three points on one side. Tenting a 0.3 mm drill with LPI mask is normally reliable but is not a guarantee, and VDD35 to GND is a short that kills the CPU's internal regulator.
findings.risk: None to add the keepouts. The residual risk if nothing is done is a mask defect or via tenting failure shorting VDD35, VDD2 or VDD5 to GND under a part you cannot inspect once it is fitted.
findings.verify_reason: Verified against the raw file. MOD1 footprint 'ClockxControl_GBA_GBC' is at (91.95,-44.95) rotated 180 with fp_rect (start -9.325 -6) i.e. 18.65 x 12.00 mm, giving the window x[82.625,101.275] y[-50.950,-38.950] = 223.8 mm2 — exact. Board setup line '(tenting front back)' is present at line 107 — exact. F.Cu composition by 0.25 mm grid sampling of the filled polygons: GND 47.5% / 106.8 mm2, VDD35 26.1% / 58.8, bare 16.4% / 36.9, VDD2 8.6% / 19.2, VDD5 1.4% / 3.2 — within 0.5 percentage points of their figures everywhere, so four different rails do run under the module. C7 relocation confirmed: (91.9,-41.1) in the ECO-5 fork (inside the window) moved to (93.1,-37.4) in ECO-6 (outside, y = -37.4 vs the -38.95 edge); C12 is at (100.6,-48.8) with both pads on B.Cu, so it is under the window in XY but on the far side of the board — exactly as stated. 0603 body thickness of 0.8 mm confirmed for the Murata GRM188 series, so the mechanical argument for having moved C7 is sound. Thermal arithmetic re-derived and correct: 10 W/m2K x 2.24e-4 m2 x 20 K = 45 mW of convection lost, and 0.040 W / (10 x 4.48e-4) = 8.9 C self-rise. The dissipating parts are indeed all outside the window (U8 x=18.4, U5 x=26.9, U4 x=37.9, U6 x=102.6 y=-25.9). Recommendations cost nothing at fab and are sound.
findings.correction: The via breakdown is wrong and does not even self-consistently sum. The finding says '27 vias fall inside the window (17 GND, 4 VDD5, 1 VDD2, and 9 signal)' — that is 31, not 27. My count inside x[82.625,101.275] y[-50.950,-38.950] is 27 vias split 12 GND, 4 VDD5, 1 VDD2 and 10 signal (/CPU/TP0, TP1, TP9, ~OE_RAM, MD_0, MD_1, MD_2, MD_8, MD_9, MD_10). Correct the split; the total, the tenting state and the conclusion are all fine. Everything else stands.

findings.title: VDD2 layout verdict: DC drop is under 1 mV and is a non-issue; the plane pair contributes 22 pF of decoupling, so the discrete caps do all the work
findings.current_part: VDD2 leaves U8 pad 5 at (19.35,-31.44) on B.Cu, crosses a 17.66 mm2 B.Cu pour, and reaches the In2 VDD2 plane through a SINGLE via at (19.20,-32.70) (14 VDD2 vias exist on the whole board; the others are at the load ends). The In2 VDD2 plane is one contiguous island of 468.04 mm2 spanning x[17.7,101.8] y[-63.2,-31.9]. I profiled its width every 0.5 mm and integrated R = 0.491 mOhm/sq x dx / w(x): from the U8 via to U1's core pins at x = 74.3 the resistance is 7.36 mOhm; out to U2's furthest pin-37 pad at x = 100.3 it is 10.43 mOhm. The narrowest neck is 1.3 mm wide at x = 58.0-58.5, under the CPU. U1's four core pins are 44 (74.34,-49.62), 65 (72.34,-61.52), 115 (51.84,-53.62), 117 (51.84,-52.62); each has a 0.1 uF within 2.4-3.7 mm (pin 117 to C45 2.46 mm, pin 115 to C47 2.58 mm, pin 44 to C15 2.62 mm, pin 65 to C16 2.39 mm) plus a 1 uF alongside. C60 (10 uF) is the bulk cap at (19.17,-33.80), 3.5 mm from U8.
findings.proposal: No change to VDD2's routing. Two small things worth doing on a revision: add a second via at U8's output so the whole core rail does not depend on one 0.3 mm barrel, and see the separate finding about restoring the RAM's decoupling.
findings.benefit: Quantified so it can be dismissed: at the estimated 90 mA of VDD2 current at 1.75x, the plane drop to the CPU core pins is 0.090 x 7.36 mOhm = 0.66 mV, and to the RAM 0.94 mV; adding the single via (0.88 mOhm) and the B.Cu pour brings the total under 1.0 mV. For scale, the NCV8164's own load regulation is 2 mV from 1 mA to 300 mA. Current density in the 1.3 mm neck at 90 mA is 1.98 A/mm2, more than 20x inside any IPC-2152 internal-layer limit. The DC path is not a lever and no copper change will win anything here. The AC picture is different but also bounded: the In1(GND)/In2(VDD2) plane pair is separated by the 0.84 mm core, giving C = 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 468e-6 / 0.84e-3 = 22.2 pF, whose impedance at 100 MHz is 72 Ohm - useless. All VDD2 decoupling is therefore discrete: 10 uF + 4 x 1 uF + 5 x 0.1 uF nominal. On the stackup generally: putting the 0.84 mm core between In1 and In2 and the 0.1 mm prepregs against the outer layers is the RIGHT trade for this board, because it puts the busiest signal layer (F.Cu, 1977.5 mm of signal routing) 0.1 mm from a continuous GND plane - and the audit shows 1614.7 mm of that, 82%, is genuinely GND-referenced. The price is paid on B.Cu, where only 492.4 of 1522.3 mm (32%) is GND-referenced and the rest runs over VDD2 (365.6 mm), VDD3 (203.5), VAUD (193.1) or nothing (200.0). Most of the VDD2-referenced B.Cu routing is the CPU-to-RAM MD bus, which is legitimately a VDD2-domain signal, so that part is fine.
findings.risk: None - this is a report of a measurement, not a change.
findings.verify_reason: I parsed every VDD2 via out of the fork file (14 total, matching their count) and point-tested each against the filled polygons. Four sit in the U8 pour, not one — that is the refutation. Everything else I checked holds: the In2 VDD2 plane is a single contiguous 468.04 mm2 island spanning x[17.72,101.80] y[-63.25,-31.92] (exact); the B.Cu VDD2 pour is 17.66 mm2 (exact); U8 pad 5 VDD2 is at (19.350,-31.438) (they said 19.35,-31.44); C60's VDD2 pad is at (19.175,-33.800), 3.5 mm from U8 (exact). Sheet resistance re-derived: 1.72e-8/35e-6 = 4.91e-4 ohm/sq = 0.491 mOhm/sq — correct for 35 um copper, which the stackup confirms. Plane-pair capacitance re-derived: 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 468e-6/0.84e-3 = 22.2 pF, |Z| at 100 MHz = 1/(2 pi x 1e8 x 22.2e-12) = 71.7 ohm — correct, so the 'plane pair is useless as decoupling, the discretes do all the work' conclusion stands. Current density 0.090/(1.3 x 0.035) = 1.98 A/mm2 — correct. NCV8164 load regulation of 2 mV from 1 mA to 300 mA verified from the onsemi datasheet, so the '0.66 mV is 3x smaller than the regulator's own load regulation' scaling argument is fair. The decoupling distances are right: C45 pad to U1 pin 117, C47 to pin 115, C15 to pin 44, C16 to pin 65 all land in the 2.4-3.7 mm band. The stackup commentary is also correct and I independently reproduced the census it rests on (F.Cu 1597.7/1961.3 = 81% GND-referenced, B.Cu 490.4/1522.3 = 32%, with VDD2 367.0, VDD3 203.0, VAUD 192.3 and 200.8 mm unreferenced).
findings.correction: The central factual claim is wrong and the resulting recommendation must be withdrawn. 'VDD2 leaves U8 pad 5 ... and reaches the In2 VDD2 plane through a SINGLE via at (19.20,-32.70) (14 VDD2 vias exist on the whole board; the others are at the load ends)' is false. There are FOUR full through-vias (F.Cu-to-B.Cu, 0.7/0.3 mm, net VDD2) at (19.20,-32.70), (19.15,-35.00), (20.20,-35.00) and (18.60,-35.90). I point-tested all four: every one lies inside BOTH the 17.66 mm2 B.Cu VDD2 pour at x[14.84,21.60] y[-36.42,-31.31] — which is the pour U8 pad 5 at (19.350,-31.438) sits in — and the 468.04 mm2 In2 VDD2 plane. So the core rail already has four parallel barrels within about 4 mm of the LDO output, and the proposal 'add a second via at U8's output so the whole core rail does not depend on one 0.3 mm barrel' should be deleted. Adding the four vias in parallel also makes the DC case even stronger than the finding's own number: via resistance drops to ~0.22 mOhm and the total drop falls further below 1 mV. The rest of the finding survives intact.

findings.title: ECO-5 moved C8 7.2 mm away from the RAM's VCC pin, leaving U2 with no local VDD2 decoupling - worst possible change for 1.75x
findings.current_part: In the stock board C8 (0.1 uF) sits adjacent to U2 pin 37 with F.Cu tracks at (100.081,-58.525)->(100.081,-56.9), (100.349,-58.525)->(100.8,-58.525) and (100.8,-58.525)->(100.081,-58.525). The fork deleted all three and relocated C8 to (103.0,-64.9), 7.2 mm from the nearest pin-37 pad at (100.31,-58.05) - and, per the separate correctness finding, left its VDD2 terminal unconnected. The nearest CONNECTED VDD2 capacitor to U2 is then C46 (1 uF) at (78.70,-48.48), 8.0 mm from pin 16 at (81.31,-56.05) and about 20 mm from the pin-37 pads. There are also only 4 GND vias within 10 mm of U2's centre, against 72 within 13 mm of U1.
findings.proposal: Restore a 0.1 uF within 1.5-2 mm of U2 pin 37 (the stock position was right) and add a second within 2 mm of pins 12/16. Add 3-4 GND stitching vias inside the U2 footprint area. All of this is copper and placement, no new parts beyond what the BOM already has.
findings.benefit: Estimated with stated assumptions: the CPU-RAM MD bus is 16 lines, each loaded by roughly 2.2 pF of trace (0.148 pF/mm x ~15 mm) plus ~5 pF of pin capacitance at each end, so about 12 pF per line, 192 pF total. A full 16-bit transition at 2.5 V moves 480 pC; delivered over a 2 ns edge that is 240 mA of peak supply current the RAM must pull from somewhere. With the nearest capacitor 8 mm away across a plane the path inductance is of order 4 nH, giving dV = L x di/dt = 4e-9 x 0.240/2e-9 = 0.48 V of droop on a 2.5 V rail. With a 0.1 uF at 1.5 mm (roughly 1 nH) it is 0.12 V. At 1.75x these events happen 1.75x as often, so the rail has 43% less time to recover between them. This is the single most likely cause of an overclocked build being unstable specifically after the ECO-5 change. Not an energy finding.
findings.risk: The 12 pF/line and 2 ns edge are estimates - I have no AGB CPU datasheet - so treat the 0.48 V as an order-of-magnitude figure, not a measurement. But the direction is not in doubt: removing a decoupling capacitor from beside a 16-bit SRAM's supply pin and then clocking it 75% faster is the wrong way round.
findings.verify_reason: Placement change verified: stock C8 at (100.8,-59.3) rot 90 with its VDD2 pad about 0.9 mm from the pin-37 pad at (100.31,-58.05), and the three stock F.Cu ties around (100.081,-58.525)/(100.349,-58.525)/(100.800,-58.525) are absent from the fork's VDD2 segment list, which I dumped in full (21 segments, none in that region). Fork C8 at (103.0,-64.9), VDD2 pad (102.225,-64.900) — dx 1.915, dy 6.850, distance 7.11 mm. Nearest connected VDD2 capacitor verified by exhaustive distance search over all VDD2 caps: C46 pad (78.700,-48.475) is 8.01 mm from pin 16 (81.310,-56.050) and 19.0 mm from the pin-37 pad at (95.100,-58.050) — matching 'about 20 mm'. Droop arithmetic re-derived and internally consistent: 16 lines x ~12 pF = 192 pF, 192 pF x 2.5 V = 480 pC, 480 pC / 2 ns = 240 mA, 4 nH x 0.240/2e-9 = 0.48 V; with 1 nH, 0.12 V. The via counts are where it fails — I ran the count four ways (footprint origin and pad-bounding-box centre, at r=10 and r=13 mm) and could not reproduce 72 for GND under any of them, but 74 for all-nets at r=13 reproduces it immediately.
findings.correction: (a) The via comparison is an apples-to-oranges error and must be corrected. 'only 4 GND vias within 10 mm of U2's centre, against 72 within 13 mm of U1' — I count 3 GND vias within 10 mm of U2's footprint origin (88.0,-57.8) and 14 GND vias within 13 mm of U1's origin (63.09,-53.12). The number 72 is close to the count of ALL vias of ALL nets within 13 mm of U1, which is 74. So the comparison as written contrasts a GND count against a total count and inflates the asymmetry by ~5x. There IS a real asymmetry (3 vs 14 GND vias, for a part half the size), but state it correctly. (b) Distance is 7.11 mm from C8's relocated VDD2 pad (102.225,-64.900) to the nearest pin-37 pad (100.310,-58.050), not 7.2 mm. (c) The 0.48 V droop is weaker than presented for reasons beyond the stated estimate error: pins 12/16 sit inside a 59.68 mm2 F.Cu VDD2 POUR, not a trace, so the inductance to C46 is well under the generic 4 nH assumed for an 8 mm path; and VDD2 carries 10 uF + 4 x 1 uF + 5 x 0.1 uF in total. (d) The ranking 'the single most likely cause of an overclocked build being unstable specifically after the ECO-5 change' cannot stand, because in the fork as committed U2 pin 37 has no supply at all (the sibling correctness finding) — an open VCC pin outranks degraded decoupling. Keep the recommendation (restore a 0.1 uF within 1.5-2 mm of pin 37, add stitching); drop the ranking and fix the via numbers.

findings.title: Grounding verdict: the GND/AGND split is done correctly - single-point tie at NT1, no signal crosses it, and the whole analog block sits inside the island
findings.current_part: NT1 is a KiCad net tie (Bucketmouse:NetTie-2_SMD_Pad0.5mm) at (36.4,-33.0) on F.Cu, marked DNP and exclude_from_bom, with net_tie_pad_groups "1, 2". It is real copper, not a placeholder: the footprint carries an fp_poly on F.Cu from (-0.5,-0.25) to (0.5,0.25) bridging pad 1 (GND, at 35.90,-33.00) and pad 2 (AGND, at 36.90,-33.00). That bar is 1.0 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, 35 um thick = 2 squares = 0.98 mOhm. The In1 layer carries one 4023.38 mm2 GND island and one 1001.16 mm2 AGND island (both single, contiguous polygons - verified by counting filled_polygon groups); the AGND island occupies the top-right audio corner and reaches NT1 through a neck along y ~ -33 that runs from x = 37.0 to x = 121.5. NT1 is placed exactly on that boundary. Three AGND vias sit within 3 mm of the AGND pad, at (37.25,-33.75), (38.10,-33.25), (39.25,-33.25). All the analog parts fall inside the island: U6 (102.6,-25.9), U7 (115.1,-29.8), U9 (107.7,-46.4), VR2 (117.86,-11.54), P3 (105.65,-5.95), SP1 (126.685,-27.9). Separately, /CPU/LGND is a third ground with 40.45 mm2 on B.Cu and 40.47 mm2 on In2; its only pads are EM1.6, EM2.4 and P4 pins 6/7/8, so it reaches board GND ONLY through one winding of each common-mode choke (ACM2520-801-3P-T002, DCR 1.6 Ohm per line, rated current 150 mA) - two windings in parallel, about 0.8 Ohm.
findings.proposal: Keep the split; it is doing what it should. Two small drop-in improvements: (1) add one GND via right at NT1 pad 1 - the nearest GND via today is at (33.70,-31.20), 2.83 mm away, so the tie's GND side runs 2.83 mm on F.Cu (about 0.7 mOhm but roughly 2 nH) before reaching the plane stack; (2) decide deliberately whether /CPU/LGND should have a DC path to GND other than 0.8 Ohm of choke winding, because as drawn an ESD strike on the link connector shell has nowhere to go except through those windings.
findings.benefit: The split is verified correct, which is worth stating: I swept every F.Cu signal trace at 0.25 mm intervals against the In1 filled polygons and found ZERO crossings of the GND/AGND boundary, so no signal has a broken return path across the split. Loading: the LM4853 is bridge-tied, so the speaker current returns into the amplifier's own AGND, not across NT1; likewise the headphone return enters P3 pad 1 (AGND) and closes locally with U6 a few mm away. Only U6's DC supply current traverses NT1 - at 2.0-2.4 mA of quiescent IDD (LM4853 datasheet) plus the average draw of a 50-100 mW audio stage, call it up to 30 mA, the 0.98 mOhm bar drops 29 uV. That is a well-executed single-point analog ground. No energy in it either way.
findings.risk: The via at NT1 costs nothing. Changing the LGND arrangement is a design decision, not a defect - I am flagging it, not asserting it is wrong; MouseBiteLabs may have chosen the choke-only path deliberately to keep cable-borne noise out of board GND.
findings.verify_reason: Almost everything else verified exactly from the raw file. NT1 is at (36.4,-33.0) on F.Cu with attrs 'exclude_from_pos_files exclude_from_bom allow_missing_courtyard dnp' and 'net_tie_pad_groups "1, 2"'; the fp_poly is on F.Cu with vertices (-0.5,-0.25),(0.5,-0.25),(0.5,0.25),(-0.5,0.25), i.e. 1.0 x 0.5 mm — 2 squares x 0.491 mOhm/sq = 0.98 mOhm, correct. Pads at (35.900,-33.000) GND and (36.900,-33.000) AGND — exact. In1 carries exactly one 4023.38 mm2 GND polygon and one 1001.16 mm2 AGND polygon (I counted filled_polygon groups myself) — exact to two decimals. Nearest GND via to NT1 pad 1 is at (33.700,-31.200), 2.84 mm away — they said 2.83; nearest AGND vias are (37.250,-33.750) at 0.83 mm, (38.100,-33.250) at 1.23 mm, (39.250,-33.250) at 2.36 mm — exactly the three cited. Analog part positions all confirmed: U6 (102.6,-25.9), U7 (115.1,-29.8), U9 (107.7,-46.4), VR2 (117.86,-11.54), P3 (105.65,-5.95), SP1 (126.685,-27.9). /CPU/LGND has exactly five pads — EM1.6, EM2.4, P4.6, P4.7, P4.8 — so it genuinely reaches board GND only through choke windings. LM4853 IDD is 2.4 mA typ / 7.0 mA max (the finding's '2.0-2.4 mA' is imprecise); 30 mA x 0.98 mOhm = 29 uV checks. ACM2520-801-3P-T002 verified at 800 ohm/100 MHz, 150 mA, 1.6 ohm DCR max, 2.50 x 2.00 x 1.20 mm.
findings.correction: (a) 'I swept every F.Cu signal trace at 0.25 mm intervals against the In1 filled polygons and found ZERO crossings of the GND/AGND boundary' is false. Sweeping at 0.1 mm and allowing for the clearance gap between the islands, exactly ONE F.Cu signal segment spans the boundary: Net-(C71-Pad1) from (97.818,-34.596) to (97.818,-33.245), 1.35 mm long, crossing at about y = -33 where the split runs. In practice it is harmless — Net-(C71-Pad1) is the display TOUCH2 sense node, pulled up through R71 (100k) with Z58 ('100p or 0 ohm') and 27 pF of C71 on it, so it is quasi-static — but an absolute 'ZERO' claim that a reader would rely on is wrong, and if Z58 is stuffed as 0 ohm this node carries /CPU/Display/ZA. (b) The category is wrong: 'quality / drop-in' but the proposal is to add a GND via at NT1 pad 1, which is a PCB revision, not a drop-in. (c) The '0.8 ohm through two windings' figure for /CPU/LGND rests on reading the TDK 1.6 ohm DCR spec as per-line; neither the TDK product page nor the Digi-Key listing states per-line explicitly, so treat the LGND path as 0.8-1.6 ohm and mark it uncertain.

findings.title: Explicitly checked: neither ferrite bead forms the bead-plus-ceramic resonance, and the link-port chokes are damped by their series resistors
findings.current_part: EM3 and EM7 are Bourns MH1608-601Y, 0603 ferrite beads: 600 Ohm +/- 25% at 100 MHz, 1 A rated, 0.2 Ohm max DCR. EM3 is in series between the VDD35 rail and the link connector's VDD pin - net map confirms Net-(P4-VDD35) has exactly two pads, EM3 pad 2 and P4 pin 1, with NO capacitor. EM7 is in series between /~RESET and Net-(U1H-~RESET), which again has exactly two pads, EM7 pad 2 and U1 pin 125, with no capacitor. EM1/EM2 are TDK ACM2520-801-3P-T002 3-line common-mode chokes: 800 Ohm at 100 MHz, 150 mA rated, 1.6 Ohm DCR per line. On the board side of the chokes each link line passes through RA1 (4 x 330 Ohm array); three of the four have a 100 pF shunt (C18 on Net-(RA1C-R3.2), C19 on Net-(RA1D-R4.2), C20 on Net-(RA1B-R2.2)).
findings.proposal: No change on the resonance question. See the separate finding about the missing fourth 100 pF.
findings.benefit: The classic mistake asked about is NOT present, and here is the arithmetic rather than an assertion. For a resonance you need the bead's inductance working against a capacitor on its far side; both beads have an open-ended far side. Even taking the crudest inductance estimate from the impedance spec, L ~ Z/(2 pi f) = 600/(2 pi x 1e8) = 0.95 uH, and pairing it with the CPU pin's own ~5 pF, f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(0.95e-6 x 5e-12)) = 73 MHz - at which frequency the bead is almost entirely resistive (that is what a 600 Ohm at 100 MHz part is), so Q is far below 1 and there is nothing to peak. On the link chokes, the differential leakage inductance is typically a few percent of the common-mode 1.27 uH (= 800/(2 pi x 1e8)), so take 50 nH against the 100 pF shunt: f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(50e-9 x 100e-12)) = 2.25 MHz, characteristic impedance sqrt(L/C) = 22.4 Ohm, and with RA1's 330 Ohm in series Q = 22.4/330 = 0.068 - heavily overdamped. No peaking anywhere. Also worth stating: VDD35 is not fed by any regulator on this board - the pad-level net map shows its ten pads are C6, C7, C17, C51, EM3.1, P1 pin 1, P1 pad C1, R2.1, R35.2 and U1 pin 38, with no source - so it is generated inside the salvaged AGB CPU and feeds the cartridge. At 1.75x the cartridge bus toggles 75% faster and draws that much more from a regulator whose limit is undocumented; the only board-side lever is bulk capacitance, and VDD35 currently has 3 x 0.1 uF + 1 x 1 uF = 1.3 uF nominal, with C17 stranded at (85.22,-67.00), far from both U1 pin 38 (72.34,-45.22) and the cart pins.
findings.risk: None. If anyone wants to act on the VDD35 observation, adding bulk there is a PCB revision and is speculative until someone actually scopes VDD35 at 1.75x with a cartridge inserted - I would not change it on the strength of this analysis alone.
findings.verify_reason: Net topology verified exactly from the pad-level map I regenerated myself: Net-(P4-VDD35) has exactly two pads, EM3.2 and P4.1 (VDD35 pin of the link connector), with no capacitor; Net-(U1H-~RESET) has exactly two pads, EM7.2 and U1.125, with no capacitor. VDD35 has exactly the ten pads listed (C6, C7, C17, C51, EM3.1, P1.1, P1.C1, R2.1, R35.2, U1.38) and no regulator among them — so the claim that VDD35 is generated inside the salvaged CPU and that its only board-side lever is bulk capacitance holds, as does 3 x 0.1 uF + 1 x 1 uF = 1.3 uF. C17's position at (85.22,-67.00) puts it far from both U1 pin 38 and the cart pins, as stated. Part specs verified from sources I fetched: Bourns MH1608-601Y is 600 ohm +/-25% at 100 MHz, 1 A, 0.2 ohm max DCR, 0603 [1608 metric]; TDK ACM2520-801-3P-T002 is 800 ohm at 100 MHz, 150 mA rated, 1.6 ohm DCR max, 3 lines. Bead math re-derived and correct: L ~ 600/(2 pi x 1e8) = 0.955 uH as a crude upper bound; with 5 pF, f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(0.955e-6 x 5e-12)) = 72.9 MHz, at which a 600-ohm-at-100-MHz part is predominantly resistive so Q << 1. The RA1 shunt topology is confirmed (see the link-filter finding). The honesty of the finding is good; only the one frequency is wrong.
findings.correction: One arithmetic error, non-load-bearing but it must be fixed because the reader will check it. '50 nH against the 100 pF shunt: f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(50e-9 x 100e-12)) = 2.25 MHz' is wrong by a factor of 32. 1/(2 pi sqrt(5.0e-18)) = 71.2 MHz. The 2.25 MHz figure corresponds to 50 uH, not 50 nH. The companion numbers ARE computed from 50 nH and are right — sqrt(L/C) = sqrt(500) = 22.4 ohm, Q = 22.4/330 = 0.068 — so the conclusion (heavily overdamped, nothing to peak) is unaffected; only the frequency is wrong, and correcting it to 71 MHz actually puts the notional resonance in the band the ferrites are there to damp, which is worth saying rather than burying. Second, smaller point: 'both beads have an open-ended far side' is right, but EM7's NEAR side carries C30 (1 uF) on /~RESET, so the reader should not conclude there is no capacitor anywhere near EM7.

findings.title: Only three of the four link-port lines get the 100 pF shunt - SCK is unfiltered and unbalances the common-mode choke
findings.current_part: Each of the four link lines passes through RA1 (330 Ohm array) then a common-mode choke winding. Net map: Net-(RA1B-R2.2) has C20 (100p) and EM2 pad 1; Net-(RA1C-R3.2) has C18 (100p) and EM1 pad 2; Net-(RA1D-R4.2) has C19 (100p) and EM1 pad 3. But Net-(RA1A-R1.2) - which goes to EM2 pad 2 and out to P4 pin 5 (SCK) - has NO shunt capacitor; it carries RA1 pad 8 and TP25 (the "SCK" test point) instead. There is no footprint for a fourth capacitor.
findings.proposal: On a PCB revision, add a fourth 100 pF (0603) from Net-(RA1A-R1.2) to GND alongside C18/C19/C20, giving all four lines the same 330 Ohm / 100 pF network (corner frequency 1/(2 pi x 330 x 100e-12) = 4.82 MHz, comfortably above the GBA link's fastest 2 Mbit/s mode). Keep TP25.
findings.benefit: EMC only, and modest. A common-mode choke rejects common-mode current in proportion to how well matched the two lines through it are. On EM2, one line (SD) sees 330 Ohm into 100 pF and the other (SCK) sees 330 Ohm into an open, so the two windings terminate into different impedances and the choke converts common-mode to differential and back. The unfiltered line is also the clock, which is the line with the most harmonic energy and the one that runs to an external cable acting as an antenna. I am not going to put a dB number on it without a chamber measurement.
findings.risk: Low, but it may be deliberate: SCK is the one line where a 4.8 MHz corner could matter if anyone ever pushes the link port hard, and it is the line with the test point. If the intent was to preserve SCK edges, leave it and note the reason in the schematic. Needs a PCB revision either way - there is no spare pad.
findings.verify_reason: Verified directly from the pad-level net map I regenerated. Net-(RA1A-R1.2) has exactly three pads — EM2.2, RA1.8 (the R1.2 end of the array) and TP25, the 'SCK' test point — and NO capacitor. The other three link lines each carry a 100 pF: Net-(RA1B-R2.2) = {C20.1, EM2.1, RA1.7}, Net-(RA1C-R3.2) = {C18.1, EM1.2, RA1.6}, Net-(RA1D-R4.2) = {C19.1, EM1.3, RA1.5}. So on EM2 one winding terminates into 330 ohm + 100 pF and the other into 330 ohm + an open, exactly as described, and the unfiltered one is SCK going to P4 pin 5. I searched the BOM for any unpopulated fourth capacitor footprint on that net and found none. Corner frequency re-derived: 1/(2 pi x 330 x 100e-12) = 4.823 MHz — correct. RA1 is confirmed as a 4 x 330 ohm R_Array_Convex_4x0603. Choke part verified (ACM2520-801-3P-T002, 800 ohm at 100 MHz, 150 mA, 1.6 ohm DCR). The mode-conversion argument for a mismatched common-mode choke is standard and correctly applied here; there is nothing in it I can refute.
findings.correction: None. The finding is correctly scoped, correctly categorised as needing a PCB revision (there is no spare pad), and honest about the fact that it will not put a dB number on the benefit and that the omission may be deliberate. The 0.6 confidence is appropriate. One thing I would add rather than correct: the reason to leave it alone is stronger than the finding allows. The GBA's fastest link mode is 2 Mbit/s, so a 4.82 MHz corner is only about 2.4x the bit rate — that is tight enough on the clock line that preserving SCK edges is a plausible deliberate choice, not merely a possible one.

findings.title: 314 mm of signal routing is cut through the In1 GND plane and 408 mm through In2 - the buses happen to miss it, but the ClockxControl clock does not
findings.current_part: Routing census over all three board files (identical on the plane layers): In1.Cu carries 314.1 mm of signal trace and 36.8 mm of power trace; In2.Cu carries 408.4 mm of signal and 79.0 mm of power. The biggest offenders are the button lines - /CPU/TP8 124.51 mm on In2, /CPU/TP2 81.53 mm on In2 and 38.66 mm on In1, /CPU/TP3 49.35 mm on In2, /CPU/TP5 37.97 mm on In1, /CPU/TP7 34.92 mm on In1, /CPU/VSHD 30.95 mm on In1 - plus Net-(Q5B-G) 10.56 mm on In1 (see the open-circuit finding). At 0.25 mm trace plus 0.2 mm clearance each side, that is roughly 0.65 mm x 314 mm = 204 mm2 of slot cut into a 5024 mm2 In1 pour, about 4%.
findings.proposal: On any respin, pull signal routing off In1 entirely and off In2 wherever it crosses a fast net's return path. Where that is not possible, at least keep the slots away from the clock and bus regions.
findings.benefit: I tested the actual consequence rather than assuming it, and the result is mixed. GOOD: I checked every F.Cu CPU-to-RAM and CPU-to-cart bus segment (MD, MA, PHI, ~RD, ~WE_RAM, ~OE_RAM) against every In1 signal slot and found ZERO crossings - the buses never have to detour around a slot in their reference plane, which is why the board works well at stock speed. BAD: in the ECO-6 file the CXC_CLK trace on B.Cu crosses 5 slots cut into In2 by /CPU/TP1, TP2, TP3, TP8 and /~VCNT5. That is on top of the 15 reference-net changes already counted in the clock-routing finding, so the 7.34 MHz clock is the one net on the board whose return path is comprehensively broken.
findings.risk: Re-routing plane-layer traces on a board this dense is a substantial respin, and the button lines that are on the planes are DC-slow so there is no urgency for their own sake - the case is entirely about the slots they leave behind. Fixing just the 5 slots the clock crosses is far cheaper than a general cleanup, and is subsumed by moving CXC_CLK to F.Cu.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the routing census from scratch with my own parser and got In1.Cu 314.1 mm signal / 36.8 mm power and In2.Cu 408.4 mm signal / 79.0 mm power — identical to the finding's figures to one decimal, and identical across all three board files as claimed. The named offenders reproduce exactly too: /CPU/TP8 124.51 mm on In2, /CPU/TP2 81.53 on In2 and 38.66 on In1, /CPU/TP3 49.35 on In2, /CPU/TP5 37.97 on In1, /CPU/TP7 34.92 on In1, /CPU/VSHD 30.95 on In1, and Net-(Q5B-G) 10.54 on In1. The 'GOOD' claim is the one most worth attacking and it survives: I intersected every F.Cu bus segment (MD, MA, PHI, ~RD, ~WE, ~OE — 394 segments) against every In1 signal segment (204 segments) and found ZERO intersections, and I extended the test to B.Cu (139 bus segments) against In2 signal segments and also found zero. So the buses genuinely never detour around a slot in their reference plane. The 'BAD' claim also survives and is understated: by segment intersection the ECO-6 CXC_CLK B.Cu run crosses In2 traces on /CPU/TP2 (47.80,-58.78), /CPU/TP1 (47.83,-58.16), /CPU/TP8 (48.12,-57.83), /~VCNT5 (48.80,-57.05) and /CPU/TP3 (49.55,-55.00) — the five named — PLUS In2 power traces SW (49.75,-49.27) and VDD35 (88.80,-38.20), and the 6 mm F.Cu leg additionally crosses In1 traces on /CPU/VSHD (46.65,-63.20) and /CPU/Display/VCOM (46.20,-63.65). Nine crossings, not five.
findings.correction: Two immaterial nits. (1) The F.Cu signal total is given as 1977.5 mm; I get 1961.3 mm in the stock file (0.8% apart, a power/signal net-classification difference — my B.Cu figure of 1522.3 mm matches theirs to the digit). (2) The '5024 mm2 In1 pour' is the sum of two separate islands: the GND island is 4023.38 mm2 and the AGND island 1001.16 mm2 (4 percent slot fraction is computed against the wrong denominator if only the GND island matters — against 4023 mm2 it is 5.1 percent, which strengthens rather than weakens the point). Neither changes anything. If anything the finding UNDERSTATES the problem: the clock crosses more slots than it claims (see below).
